about: One row per test, written BEFORE the test runs (the style guide: NO TEST RUNS WITHOUT ITS ROW ON THE TESTS PAGE). The dashboard's Tests page shows every row. The pause runners and the ability scheduler refuse a job whose row is missing or incomplete. Every text field follows the style guide MECHANISM, NEVER METAPHOR and ONE WORD PER THING; .agent/hooks/worklog_time_check.py checks this file on every write. Created Oct 2, 2026 5:08 PM PDT.

fields.id: exactly the pause job's name, or the ability scheduler's task name
fields.title: a short plain name, at most 8 words
fields.question: one plain question the result answers
fields.why: the decision that depends on the answer

fields.steps: list: the exact procedure, in order
fields.measures: list: each measured quantity, its unit, and the two ends of its scale
fields.pass_line_basis: why that line: the measurement or arithmetic behind it, with its source file
fields.cost: {training_stopped: true|false, memory_gb: number, where: 'training pause' | 'beside training' | 'offline'}
fields.result_source: {file: path of the result file, keys: the keys read from it}

fields.decision: null until decided, then the decision taken, in plain words

rows.title: Whole-body hierarchy causal test over 0.25 s holds
rows.question: When only one body part's code is changed and the decoded command is held for 5 model steps, does that part's actual movement follow the movement the hold hierarchy predicted for it?
rows.why: No production switch reads these counts: the driver writes them as reported only, because the live shadow learns one-model-step examples. They are read beside the queued planner comparison, whose primary latent arm is this same hold hierarchy. That comparison selects commands by the hierarchy's predicted end-of-hold positions; this test measures, part by part, whether those predictions match the body's actual movement over the same 0.25 s. Row timing: the test started at 3:05 PM PDT Oct 2, before the rule that every test has its row first; this row was written after it started. At 5:12 PM PDT bodies 1 and 4 of the 4 test bodies had finished.
inputs: Production checkpoint Saved/mimo_bridge/experiments/H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41s_1146_resume_20261001_213502/checkpoints/ckpt_step_455800 (read only) and its saved episode worlds.
Bodies 1, 4, 5 and 7. Body 7 is held out of the hierarchy's training rows.

The hold hierarchy D:/UEMA_latent_body/full_body_20261001/digit_cmd/hold_fit/hierarchy.pt: 24 parts that own the 26 body handles, fitted offline on 30,464 recorded 5-model-step holds of bodies 0-6, with the digit setting on (each finger part computes its predicted movement from its decoded command, not from its code).

Code range: the hierarchy's encoder applied to the last 2,000 rows of D:/UEMA_latent_body/full_body_20261001/hold_split/train.jsonl. Per part this gives the mean code and the 95th percentile of the encoder's own Mahalanobis distances.
Settings: 16 codes per part, 3 warm-up model steps, random seed 0, centre code = the mean real code, trial codes taken from real encoded rows.
steps: Copy the hierarchy file and load it. Load the checkpoint. Encode the 2,000 rows and measure each part's code range.
Per body: build a fresh world from the checkpoint's episode, run 3 warm-up model steps, save a physics snapshot.
Hold command: every handle keeps its current target for 5 model steps from the snapshot. Record the end pose.

Per part (24 parts): take 16 codes, the part's mean code first, then 15 codes the encoder produced for real rows inside the part's range. The roots stay at their mean codes; only this part's code changes.
Decode each code top-down into handle targets (the command: 26 handles x 9 numbers). Handles the part does not own keep the hold command's targets.

Restore the snapshot and hold that command for 5 model steps (25 physics steps of 10 ms), physics only, rendering the last physics step of each model step so the eye reflex acts as in training. Read the change of the part's handles from start to end.
Run the mean code a second time from the snapshot (the repeat).
For the first part of each body, run the mean code once more with the model observing every model step. Record the largest bone difference against the physics-only run.

Grade each part: correlate, over the 16 codes, the predicted 5-model-step displacement with the actual one, each coordinate centred over codes. Repeat with 200 random re-pairings of predictions and outcomes.
Count controllable parts per part kind. Write the verdict beside the one-model-step test's counts.
measures: Spread (cm): mean distance between each code's actual displacement and the mean code's. 0 = every code moves the part the same way; larger = the code changes the movement.
Repeat (cm): distance between two runs of the mean code. 0 = exact physical replay.
Match: correlation over the 16 codes between predicted and actual displacement. -1 = the part moves opposite to the prediction, 0 = no relation, 1 = it moves where predicted for every code.
Chance line: the 95th percentile of the same correlation over the 200 re-pairings.
Head, eyes and feet are graded on turn instead of displacement: rotation in radians, with the same spread, repeat, match and chance line.
Controllable parts per kind: 0 to 8 for paired kinds (2 sides x 4 bodies), 0 to 4 for single parts.
Execution check: largest bone difference between physics-only and observed execution. 0 = observing does not change the physics.
rows.pass_line: Per part: controllable when spread is above repeat and match is above its chance line. No overall pass line: the counts are reported only.
rows.pass_line_basis: A part whose predictions have no relation to its movement crosses its chance line in 5 of 100 tests. The driver declares the hold counts reported only, because the live shadow learns one-model-step examples (docs/gain_of_function_v4/coordinator/latent_full_body_2026-10-01.py, hold causal step; Source/Python/mimo_bridge/tools/latent_body_intervention.py).

cost.where: training pause

rows.on_pass: The counts per part kind are written into this row beside the one-model-step counts. No production switch changes. The queued planner comparison runs next with this hold hierarchy as its primary latent arm.
rows.on_fail: There is no overall fail. A part kind with few controllable parts is recorded here as one whose hold predictions do not match its movement. If the result does not record trial codes from real encoded rows, the driver stops without a verdict. The planner comparison still runs: its gate is the hold fit's held-out loss line, which passed.

rows.title: Whole-body hierarchy against current planner, recorded goals
rows.question: From the same saved starts, do commands selected with the whole-body latent hierarchy's predictions end nearer recorded goal poses after 0.25 s than the commands of the production planner's direct and synergy searches?
rows.why: It measures whether the latent body hierarchy, which commands no live body today, selects reaching commands better than the production planner. Per goal, a pass is the measured evidence for developing the hierarchy as a command selector; a fail or an undecided goal keeps the production planner as the only command selector. No production file or switch reads this result.
inputs: Production checkpoint ckpt_step_455800 of the same run (read only), its saved episode worlds, and its two planner searches: direct search and search through the learned synergy.

Primary latent arm: D:/UEMA_latent_body/full_body_20261001/digit_cmd/hold_fit/hierarchy.pt, which predicts the change over the whole 0.25 s hold. Its held-out hold prediction error was 0.323 against 1.089 for predicting no movement (0 = perfect prediction).

Second latent arm, reported only: D:/UEMA_latent_body/full_body_20261001/digit_cmd/fit/hierarchy.pt, which predicts one model step. Its step is stretched over the hold by measured per-handle factors, 3.09 for the pelvis to 4.24 for the wrist. In its own causal test it moved the arms as predicted on 2 of 8 arms.
Goal source: D:/UEMA_latent_body/full_body_20261001/hold_split/witness_bank.pt, every recorded 5-model-step hold of every body (start pose, command, end pose).
Goals: left wrist (world), left and right index fingers (relative to their own wrist), left foot (world), both upper arms (world).
Starts: bodies 0-6 after 1 and 21 warm-up model steps (14 starts) and held-out body 7 after 1, 11, 21, 31, 41, 51, 61 and 71 warm-up model steps (8 starts): 22 starts.
Search settings: 256 candidate root codes per latent search, taken from 2,000 real encoded held-out rows, with the encoder's mean code as candidate 0; 8 recorded candidates per start; random seed 0.
steps: Load both hierarchies. Measure each one's code range on 2,000 held-out rows. Record each side's training exposure; the run refuses to start without it.
Per start: build a fresh world, run the production policy for the warm-up model steps, read the decision state, save a physics snapshot.
Execute the production policy's own command (the controller arm) for 0.25 s (25 physics steps), twice. An unequal replay stops the job.

Goal candidates: the 8 recorded holds of the same body with the nearest start (handle positions relative to the pelvis plus velocity x 0.25 s, root mean square, cm; pelvis up direction within 30 degrees). Carry each recorded command to the current pelvis pose; radius, strength and the eyes stay the controller's. Execute each twice from the snapshot.

Admission: the goal is the first candidate, in nearness rank, whose endpoint lies at least the separation line from the controller's endpoint: 2.4 cm for the left wrist, 0.30 cm for an index finger relative to its wrist, 0.60 cm for the left foot, 0.47 cm for the upper arms. A start with no such candidate is recorded as not admitted.

Per admitted goal pose, compute each arm's command. Direct and synergy: the production planner's two searches toward the goal pose, gaze held. Latent: for each of 256 candidate root codes, the hierarchy's predicted handle positions at the end of the hold; the code with the lowest mean squared distance to the goal is decoded into handle targets. Latent one-model-step: the same with the stretched step. Witness: the goal's own recorded command.
Execute every arm's command for 0.25 s from the snapshot, twice. The witness must end 0 cm from its goal.
Count wins per goal and the held-out signs per start. Write the result file; the driver writes its verdict file with the lines, admitted counts, code sampling and both sides' training exposure.
measures: Goal error (cm): root mean square distance of the goal handles from the goal pose after 0.25 s, in the goal's frame. 0 = on the goal (the witness command scores 0); the controller's own command scores at least the separation line.
Gap closed: 1 minus the arm's error divided by the controller's error. 1 = reached the goal, 0 = no nearer than the controller's own command, below 0 = farther.
Wins per goal: admitted starts on which the primary latent arm's error is below both planners' errors, out of the admitted starts (0 to 22).

Held-out sign per start of body 7: the mean over that start's admitted goals of (planner error minus latent error) divided by the controller error. A win when above 0; 0 to 8 wins against each planner.
Admitted starts per goal: 0 to 22. Goals the planners could have commanded exactly (within 1.8 cm per coordinate and 11 degrees of the controller's command) are counted separately.
Training exposure: the production model trained on 455,800 model steps x 8 bodies = 3,646,400 observed model steps; the hold hierarchy on 304,640 presentations of 30,464 recorded holds.
rows.pass_line: Per goal: at least 10 admitted starts, and the primary latent arm's error is below both planners' errors on at least the sign-test number of starts (16 of 22 when all 22 are admitted), with a positive mean gain over each planner. Held-out body 7: at least 5 admitted starts, and wins against each planner on at least the sign-test number of starts (7 of 8).
rows.pass_line_basis: The sign-test number is the smallest win count whose one-sided probability under chance (each start won with probability 1/2) is below 0.05: 16 of 22 has probability 0.026, 7 of 8 has 0.035. Reachability: every admitted goal was reached by an executed command from the same start (the witness, 0 cm). The planners can request at most 1.8 cm per coordinate and 11 degrees away from the controller's command, which moved their wrist endpoint 0.37-0.97 cm on Sep 30. On recorded rows, 600 of 600 starts per goal had a candidate beyond every separation line (Source/Python/mimo_bridge/tools/latent_body_compare.py; docs/gain_of_function_v4/agents/latent_compare_design_2026-10-01.md).

cost.where: training pause

rows.on_pass: The goals on which the hierarchy's commands beat both planners are written into this row with their wins, gap closed and the count of goals inside the planners' region. If the wins come only from goals outside that region, the result measures the planners' 1.8 cm and 11 degree limit, not their search; the next test then restricts goals to witness commands inside the region.
rows.on_fail: The production planner remains the only command selector and the hierarchy stays a shadow that commands nothing. A goal with fewer than 10 admitted starts is reported as not decided, and its recorded separations set the next declaration. If neither gate had passed, the driver would write a skip file instead of running; the hold fit's held-out line passed, so the comparison runs.

values: Finished 10:54 PM PDT; primary arm the 5-model-step (hold) hierarchy; result in D:/UEMA_latent_body/full_body_20261001/digit_cmd/compare_verdict.json.

Distance from the goal after one 250 ms command, mean over admitted starts (0 cm = the goal, the witness command's own endpoint): left index finger, hierarchy 0.31 cm against the planners' 0.62 and 0.59 cm and the controller's 0.55 cm; it closed a median 45 of 100 of the gap where the planners closed -19 and -8 of 100. This goal passed (hierarchy better than both planners).
Right index finger: hierarchy 0.36 cm against 0.47 and 0.49 cm (median gap closed 43 of 100), but its wins over both planners did not reach the 14 of 19 needed.

Left wrist: hierarchy 3.30 cm, planners 3.22 and 3.36 cm, controller 3.64 cm. Upper arms: hierarchy 1.00 cm, planners 1.00 and 1.03 cm. Left foot: hierarchy 1.49 cm, planners 1.27 and 1.34 cm, controller 1.18 cm. None passed.
Held-out body (body 7): failed its line.

Every admitted goal lay outside the planners' search region (inside_planner_region 0 for all five goals): the production planners could not have issued the witness command, while the hierarchy's candidates are not bounded the same way.

rows.decision: The hierarchy stays a shadow that commands nothing. Recorded for the plan: it reaches finger goals better than both planners (left index passed, right index 0.36 against 0.47 cm without enough wins), and the planners' search region excludes every witness goal, so a planner whose region is too small cannot be judged on these goals.

rows.title: Whole-body hierarchy offline fit with the digit setting
rows.question: Fitted on recorded rows with each finger's predicted movement computed from its decoded command, does the whole-body hierarchy meet its offline lines on held-out body 7?
rows.why: Four of its lines (held-out prediction, arm control, finger carry, index direction) gate the shadow switch together with the causal test's no-regression line. The prepared switch moves the in-training shadow to this fit only when all five pass.
inputs: Recorded rows of the in-training shadow, D:/UEMA_latent_body/seg41/trajectory.jsonl, split on Oct 1 into D:/UEMA_latent_body/full_body_20261001/split: 152,474 training rows of bodies 0-6 and 21,782 held-out rows of body 7, checked equal to the Sep 30 refit's rows.

Configuration: the split's configuration plus the digit setting (each finger part computes its predicted movement from its decoded command, not from its code), written to D:/UEMA_latent_body/full_body_20261001/digit_cmd/config.json.
Budget: 4,764 optimizer updates of 64 rows, 2 passes over the rows, shuffle buffer of 4,096 rows: the budget of the fit without the digit setting.

Readings: 1,000 held-out rows (the first 3,000 rows of body 7, every third). Per row and part, 16 trial codes: the mean code and 15 codes the encoder gave other held-out rows inside the 95th-percentile code range. These decide the lines. Box codes (each code dimension drawn within 2 standard deviations) are read and reported.
The fit without the digit setting, D:/UEMA_latent_body/full_body_20261001/fit/hierarchy.pt, read on the same rows and codes as the before.
No production checkpoint and no world; CPU only.
steps: Reuse the Oct 1 split and check its rows against the Sep 30 refit's.
Write the configuration with the digit setting. Refuse a configuration that already routes other part groups.
Fit the hierarchy: 4,764 updates of 64 rows, saving every 200 updates.
Read every part on the 1,000 held-out rows three times: this fit with encoded codes, this fit with box codes, the fit without the setting with encoded codes.
Compute the offline lines and write the fit verdict with the code sampling used and the before lines.
measures: Held-out future loss: error of the predicted one-model-step change on body 7 rows, in the hierarchy's scaled units. 0 = perfect; the 'nothing moves' guess on the same rows reads 1.079.

Arm control, per arm: correlation over the arm part's trial codes between the wrist movement the hand part predicts and the wrist target the hand part decodes, median over rows. 0 = no relation, 1 = they always agree.

Finger carry, per finger: R squared of a linear read-out from the finger part's code to its wrist's one-model-step world displacement. 0 = the code holds none of the arm's movement, 1 = it holds all of it.

Direction, per finger: correlation over 16 trial codes between the finger's predicted movement and its decoded command offset, median over rows. 0 = no relation, 1 = the predicted movement always points where the command points.

Command miss, reported per part: median distance between the command decoded from the row's own code and the recorded command, divided by the miss of 'command zero' (the handle's current place or pose). 0 = exact, 1 = no better than command zero.
rows.pass_line: Held-out future loss below the 'nothing moves' loss; arm control above 0.4 on both arms; finger carry R squared below 0.2 on all 10 fingers; index direction above 0.3 on both index fingers. Reported, not gating: thumb, middle and ring direction above 0.3, little finger above 0.15, command miss below half of command zero.
rows.pass_line_basis: Arm control 0.4: a small CPU fit of the whole-body design read 0.51 / 0.59, and the Sep 30 refit, whose arms were controllable 8 of 8 in the causal test, read 0.73 / 0.65. Carry 0.2: the Sep 30 refit's index carry read 0.62 / 0.47 and its index fingers failed the causal test; the index repair read -0.04 / 0.02 and passed. Direction 0.3: the index repair read above it and its index fingers were controllable 5 of 8. Row-sampling noise of every reading: at most 0.011 (docs/gain_of_function_v4/coordinator/latent_full_body_2026-10-01.py, LINES and LINE_NOTES; docs/gain_of_function_v4/agents/latent_code_range_2026-10-01.md).

rows.on_pass: The four gating lines join the causal test's no-regression line. When all five pass, the causal verdict marks this fit for the shadow switch.
rows.on_fail: The causal verdict cannot mark this fit for the shadow switch. The switch refuses and the in-training shadow keeps its current hierarchy.

values: Held-out future loss 0.162 against 1.079 for 'nothing moves' (0 = perfect): the fit removes 85 of every 100 parts of the no-movement error. Passed. The fit without the digit setting read 0.162.

Arm control: left arm 0.73, right arm 0.39, against the 0.4 line (0 = no relation, 1 = always agree). Failed: the right arm is 0.012 below the line, against a row-sampling noise of at most 0.011. The fit without the digit setting read 0.72 / 0.66 on the same codes.
With box codes the same fit read 0.80 / 0.45 and would pass; the line is decided on encoded codes.

Index direction 0.92 / 0.93 against the 0.3 line (1 = the predicted movement always points where the command points). Passed. The other 8 fingers read 0.81-0.92 against their 0.3 or 0.15 lines; without the digit setting the 10 fingers read 0.44-0.72.
Command miss, reported: 22 of 24 parts below half of command zero; the trunk read 0.79 and the head 0.68 (0 = exact, 1 = no better than command zero).
The job ran 3,518 s, from 12:32 AM to 1:31 AM PDT Oct 2, with training stopped.

The prepared shadow switch refuses while the causal verdict reads false, so the in-training shadow keeps its current hierarchy.

rows.why: Its line gates the planner comparison's primary arm. When it passes, the comparison uses this hold hierarchy, scored on its own 0.25 s prediction; otherwise the comparison falls back to the one-model-step fit or is skipped.
inputs: The hold split of Oct 1, D:/UEMA_latent_body/full_body_20261001/hold_split: the same recorded rows cut into complete holds of one command over 5 model steps, 30,464 training holds of bodies 0-6 and 4,352 held-out holds of body 7. It also holds the witness bank, the comparison's goal source.
Configuration: the hold split's configuration plus the digit setting, written to D:/UEMA_latent_body/full_body_20261001/digit_cmd/hold_config.json.

No production checkpoint and no world; CPU only.

Write the configuration with the digit setting.
Fit 4,760 updates of 64 holds, saving every 200 updates.
Read every part on held-out holds with encoded trial codes (reported).
Compare the held-out hold future loss with the 'nothing moves' loss. Write the hold fit verdict with the fit's training exposure.

rows.title: Whole-body hierarchy causal test, one model step
rows.question: When only one body part's code is changed and the decoded command runs for one model step, does that part's actual movement follow the movement the hierarchy predicted, for each of the 24 parts?
rows.why: Its no-regression line gates the shadow switch. The in-training shadow moves to this whole-body fit only when arms are controllable on 8 of 8, hands on at least 7 of 8 and index fingers on at least 5 of 8, together with the fit's four offline lines.
inputs: Production checkpoint ckpt_step_455800 of run H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41s_1146_resume_20261001_213502 (read only) and its saved episode worlds; bodies 1, 4, 5 and 7, body 7 held out of the hierarchy's training rows.
The one-model-step hierarchy D:/UEMA_latent_body/full_body_20261001/digit_cmd/fit/hierarchy.pt: 4,764 updates, digit setting on.
Code range from the hierarchy's encoder on the last 2,000 rows of D:/UEMA_latent_body/full_body_20261001/split/train.jsonl.
16 codes per part, 3 warm-up model steps, random seed 0, centre code = the mean real code, trial codes from real encoded rows.
Before references: the Sep 30 refit's causal counts (arms 8 of 8, hands 6 of 8, index fingers 1 of 8) and the index repair's (arms 6 of 8, hands 7 of 8, index fingers 5 of 8).
steps: Copy and load the hierarchy, load the checkpoint, encode the 2,000 rows and measure each part's code range.
Per body: build a fresh world, run 3 warm-up model steps, save a physics snapshot, and run the hold command for one model step.
Per part (24 parts): 16 codes, the mean code then 15 encoded codes inside the range. Only this part's code changes; the roots stay at their mean codes.
Decode each code into handle targets (the command: 26 handles x 9 numbers). The eyes receive their decoded eye command. Run one model step from the snapshot and read the part's change.
Run the mean code a second time (the repeat).
Grade: correlation over the 16 codes between predicted and actual displacement (head, eyes and feet: turn), against 200 random re-pairings.
Count per part kind, combine with the fit's offline lines, and write the verdict. Its shadow-adoption flag is true only when the fit's four gating lines and the no-regression line pass.
measures: Spread (cm): mean distance between each code's actual displacement and the mean code's. 0 = every code moves the part the same way.
Repeat (cm): distance between two runs of the mean code. 0 = exact physical replay.
Match: correlation over the 16 codes between predicted and actual displacement. -1 = opposite to the prediction, 0 = no relation, 1 = moves where predicted for every code.
Chance line: the 95th percentile of the same correlation over 200 random re-pairings.
Head, eyes and feet are graded on turn: rotation in radians, with the same readings.
Controllable parts per kind: 0 to 8 for paired kinds, 0 to 4 for single parts.
rows.pass_line: Per part: controllable when spread is above repeat and match is above its chance line. No regression (gating): arms 8 of 8, hands at least 7 of 8, index fingers at least 5 of 8. New parts (reported, each with its own line): thumbs, middle and ring fingers 5 of 8 each, little fingers 4 of 8, thighs 6 of 8, feet 5 of 8, calves 4 of 8, eyes, chest, trunk and head 2 of 4 each.
rows.pass_line_basis: Arms 8 of 8 is the Sep 30 refit's count, set as the coordinator's line; hands 7 and index fingers 5 are the index repair's counts. New-part lines follow each part's recorded one-model-step follow of its own command (correlation: thighs 0.43-0.50, feet 0.53-0.58, calves 0.38-0.42) and its small-fit direction reading. A single part tested on 4 bodies reaches 2 of 4 by chance with probability 0.014 under the 5-in-100 shuffle line (docs/gain_of_function_v4/coordinator/latent_full_body_2026-10-01.py, LINES and LINE_NOTES).

cost.where: training pause

rows.on_pass: The prepared shadow switch may move the in-training shadow to this fit in a training pause; it also checks that no trainer runs and that the eye convention matches.
rows.on_fail: The prepared shadow switch refuses and the in-training shadow keeps its current hierarchy. Each failed new-part line names its next test in the verdict.

values: Arms: 2 of 8 controllable against the line of 8 of 8. Failed. The Sep 30 refit had 8 of 8 and the index repair 6 of 8.

Every arm moved with its code (spread 0.20-0.44 cm against a repeat of 0 cm), but on 6 of 8 arms the match between predicted and actual displacement was below its chance line; body 1's left arm read -0.19 against a chance line of 0.27.

inputs: The pause's checkpoint ckpt_step_455800 of run H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41s_1146_resume_20261001_213502.

steps: Start the trainer from the checkpoint on the graphics card, as the only trainer on the machine. Run 1,000 model steps of training (455,800 to 456,800): one stats report every 100 model steps, one checkpoint at the end.
Every 30 s read the stats. A non-finite step writes snapshot_and_stop.
From the 5 reports covering model steps 456,301-456,800 (800 transitions each), compute V, G and the own-command advantage.
Compute the noise margins from those 5 reports.

measures: V: vision's next-model-step prediction error divided by the error of predicting that the picture stays the same, pooled over the 5 reports. 0 = exact, 1 = no better than an unchanged picture.

Own-command advantage: 1 minus (vision error with the copy and this body's command) divided by (vision error with another body's command). 0 = no better than another body's command, 1 = the copy leaves no vision error.
Noise margins: m_V = 2 x standard deviation of (each report's V / mean V - 1) / square root of 5, a relative margin; m_G = 2 x standard deviation of each report's G / square root of 5.
rows.pass_line: No pass line of its own. It must finish 1,000 model steps with a final checkpoint, no non-finite step, stats that say the chain trains the copy, and at least 2 complete reports in the window for the margins.
rows.pass_line_basis: Arm A is the measurement baseline; the trial's lines are judged on arm B against it (docs/gain_of_function_v4/gaze_copy_chain_trial_2026-10-01.py docstring, declared 10:52 PM PDT Oct 1; docs/gain_of_function_v4/agents/gaze_copy_detach_2026-10-01.md section 6).

rows.title: Which lessons push the vision offset outward
rows.question: On the newest checkpoint, which training lesson's optimizer step moves vision's shared prediction offset outward, is that push each update's own draw, and would folding the memory bias out of the vision head's values cut the largest per-update push to a third?
rows.why: Rules declared Sep 25 tie each answer to a repair decision. LEVER met licenses qualifying the prepared repair (the vision head's attention values read without the memory bias). PULL naming a lesson makes that lesson's route into the head the repair target. NOISE met with LEVER not met points to a repair that normalises the head's attention output before its MLP.
inputs: Checkpoint ckpt_step_455800 with its saved AdamW state and its episode companion (saved live transitions and replay windows).
Two sets of saved model steps: the live transitions, and 64 windows of production's replay draw.
Parameters read: the vision head's attention (148,800 numbers), its MLP with the revived rows (111,552), the gaze copy's layers (52,288).
Production constants read from the checkpoint: learning rate 0.0003, core clip factor 0.0079, vision next-frame weight 1.59, imagination weight 0.5.
steps: Load the checkpoint on the CPU: one model, nothing trained, no file written but the result.
Build the two sets. Per set, the offset is the mean residual of the vision prediction (base head plus gaze copy) over the set's model steps; read its direction.

Per lesson (the live next-frame lesson on the live transitions, replay's on the draw, the imagination chain on the saved histories): take its gradient on the three parameter groups and turn it into the step the saved AdamW state gives it alone: -0.0003 x clip factor x gradient / (square root of the saved running mean of squared gradients + eps).
Apply the step, read the change of the prediction's shared part on each set, undo the step. s = that change's component along the set's offset direction (above 0 = the step grows the offset).
NOISE: repeat the live lesson's step from each body's model steps alone and read s on the draw's offset.

LEVER: L = 0.0003 x the sum over the parameters of |d s / d parameter| on both sets pooled, for the head as it is (A) and with the fold (the vision head's values read without the memory bias, its constant moved into the attention's output bias), per parameter group.
Judge the three rules on the one checkpoint read and write the result file.
measures: s per lesson and set, in the prediction's units along the offset. Above 0 = grows the offset. Scale: the offset's own length is 0.235 on the draw and 0.635 on the live transitions.
NOISE ratio: standard deviation of the 8 per-body s values divided by the absolute value of their mean.
L_fold / L_A: 1 = the fold cuts nothing of the largest per-update push, 0 = it removes all of it. Beside it, each group's share of L_A (0 to 1).
rows.pass_line: PULL names a lesson when its s on the other set is above 0 and it carries at least half of the positive s of the three lessons, at two thirds of the checkpoints read (1 of 1 here). NOISE is met when the per-body spread is at least 3 times the absolute value of the mean. LEVER is met when L_fold is at most L_A / 3 and the attention carries at least half of L_A.
rows.pass_line_basis: Declared 7:08-7:14 PM PDT Sep 25, before any run. LEVER's third: the offset is renewed by these kicks, so a third of the kick is a ninth of the offset's squared error, which would take the vision ratio from its median 1.47 to about 1.05, the pre-deploy level 1.03-1.07 (docs/gain_of_function_v4/agents/vision_regression.md, NEXT 2; docs/gain_of_function_v4/vision_head_pulls.py docstring).

rows.on_pass: LEVER met: qualify the prepared repair. PULL naming a lesson: that lesson's route into the head becomes the repair target, declared then.
rows.on_fail: LEVER not met: the prepared repair is not licensed and stays unmerged. No lesson named: the record reads 'no lesson pushes it'.

values: PULL named the imagination chain. Its step moved the draw's offset outward by 0.039 along it, 17 in 100 parts of the offset's length 0.235. The live lesson's step moved the draw's offset inward by 0.0135 (6 in 100 parts), and replay's step moved the live transitions' offset inward by 0.0055 (1 in 100 parts of 0.635).
On the live transitions the imagination step moved the offset inward by 0.062 (10 in 100 parts of its length): the rule reads it on the draw.
NOISE not met: the 8 per-body live steps read -0.032 to +0.004 along the draw's offset; their spread is 0.83 times the absolute value of their mean, against the line of 3.
LEVER not met: the fold leaves 0.985 of the lever (line: at most 0.333), and the attention carries 0.015 of it (line: at least 0.5). The gaze copy's layers carry 0.79 of the lever and the MLP 0.19.
It ran 134 s, from 3:22 AM to 3:24 AM PDT Oct 2, with training stopped; one checkpoint was read, so 'two thirds of the checkpoints' is 1 of 1.

rows.decision: By the rules declared Sep 25: the prepared repair (the vision head's values without the memory bias) is not licensed and stays unmerged. The imagination chain is the named lesson. The gaze copy trial in the same pause removed the chain's gradient from the copy's layers, which carry 0.79 of the lever; under that switch the vision head's attention and MLP still receive the chain's gradient.

rows.title: Planner repair rerun: forecaster-only training arm
rows.question: Trained for 3,000 model steps beside production's configuration, does the grounded wellness forecast learn the change of the five wellness terms over a held command, and does its forecast depend on the body's own command?
rows.why: This arm is the forecaster-only configuration. Its live lines and the probe of its final checkpoint decide whether the forecaster's two production constants (its difference scale and its tie band) are set. Its checkpoint after 1,125 model steps is the matched control for the body copy's credit.
inputs: The pause's checkpoint ckpt_step_455800; production's own launch command and seed, read from Saved/mimo_bridge/training_continuation.json (read only); the latent body shadow and the observer recorder off.
Forecaster in shadow mode (it learns and changes nothing the learner does); body copy off.

The forecaster (version 3): a network 128 numbers wide that reads the forward model's latent on the raw-token route, every handle's asked change, and the start's five grounded wellness terms and three skin numbers, each standardised by its running mean and spread. It outputs each term's change at the next model step and averaged over the command's tenure of 5 model steps.
Code of branch fix/planner_fix_v2-2026-10-01 (worktree C:/Users/bhart/Documents/UEMA_wt/planner_fix).
steps: Run 3,000 model steps of training (455,800 to 458,800) on the graphics card as the only trainer, one stats report every 100 model steps.
At model step 456,900 write a snapshot command; the mid checkpoint lands at 456,925.
Once the mid checkpoint is on disk, read the kill line over model steps 456,301-456,900. A miss writes snapshot_and_stop and the final probe is skipped.
From model steps 456,301-456,800, per sense (tactile, proprioception), compute the body copy's noise margin: 2 x standard deviation of (window error / mean error - 1) / square root of 5.
At model step 458,800 read the live pass line over model steps 457,801-458,800.
Write the arm record and keep the checkpoints under D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/planner_repair_trial/rerun_2026-10-01/runs/off.
measures: Explained share per 100-model-step window: 1 minus (forecast error of the tenure-long change of the five-term sum) / (error of predicting no change). 1 = exact, 0 = no better than no change, below 0 = worse than no change.
Shuffled share: the same with another body's command at the same model step.
Command-specific share = explained share minus shuffled share. 0 = the own command adds nothing; it exceeds 1 when the forecast with another body's command is worse than predicting no change.
Noise margins for tactile and proprioception, relative to each sense's mean next-model-step error.
rows.pass_line: Kill line (model steps 456,301-456,900): mean explained share above 2 x standard deviation / square root of the window count (6). Live pass line (model steps 457,801-458,800): command-specific share mean above 2 x standard deviation / square root of 10, and above 0 in at least 9 of 10 windows (one-sided sign test probability below 0.05). The live pass line is necessary, not sufficient: the probe's judge decides.

rows.title: Forecaster judged on real candidate outcomes
rows.question: After 3,000 model steps of learning, does the forecaster's predicted difference between candidate commands from one saved start match the real difference in the five wellness terms over the command's tenure, enough to separate candidates?
rows.why: The decisive forecaster line. A pass, together with the live line, sets the forecast's difference scale and tie band, after which the score-mode adoption comparison can run. A fail keeps the forecaster out of production.
inputs: The copy-off arm's final checkpoint ckpt_step_458800 with its forecaster, and its saved episode worlds.
8 bodies x 2 saved planning decisions = 16 starts; the second start of each body 10 model steps after the first.
Per start, 5 candidate commands: the chosen command, hold, reflex, and two perturbations at the babble's size of 0.05; plus 2 perturbations at 2 times and 2 at 4 times that size (9 candidates).
The forecaster scored on the production scorer's own route: each candidate's transition from the decision's raw tokens.
steps: Load on the CPU with learning off; hash the weights and the repair's learned parts.
Per start: restore the snapshot at a planning decision. For each candidate compute the forecast five-term change (tenure-long and at the next model step).
Execute each candidate for its tenure (5 model steps) from the same snapshot, twice; the replays must be bit-identical. Record the grounded five terms at each model step.

Judge: split the bodies into even and odd halves. On one half fit the difference scale (grounded difference regressed through zero on forecast difference) and the pair band (90th percentile of |scale x forecast difference - grounded difference|). On the other half a pair is decided when |scale x forecast difference| exceeds the band. Swap the halves and pool.
Count decided pairs right and wrong, decided starts, and the bodies whose slope is above 0; exact one-sided sign tests.
Check the hashes are unchanged and write the result.
measures: Slope sign per body: bodies whose sum of (forecast difference x grounded difference) is above 0, out of 8.
Decided pairs: pairs separated beyond the band, and how many have forecast and grounded differences of the same sign.
Sign agreement: share of the 160 candidate pairs whose forecast and grounded differences have the same sign. 50 in 100 = a coin, 100 in 100 = always right.
Grounded wellness: the five-term sum on its 0-to-5 scale; tenure-long gaps between two candidates measured earlier at a median of 0.014.
rows.pass_line: Slope above 0 in at least 7 of 8 bodies (sign test probability below 0.05); at least 5 decided pairs on the judged body halves; decided pairs and decided starts each right by an exact one-sided sign test with probability below 0.05.
rows.pass_line_basis: Five decided pairs is the smallest count that can pass (5 of 5 right has probability 1/32). Reachability on the saved outcomes of checkpoint 437,125: a forecast carrying 0.3 of each start's between-candidate difference with noise 0.002 per term passes in 18 of 20 noise draws; information-free and sign-reversed forecasts never pass (docs/gain_of_function_v4/agents/planner_repair_2026-09-30.md section 6; planner_repair_judge.py).

rows.title: Caused change: measurement arm, 1,000 model steps
rows.question: On the live model, with the flags still deciding every goal, how large is each sense's caused change (own-command agreement minus swapped-command agreement), and how often do each sense's evidence gate and its null gate open?
rows.why: It provides the readings that set the caused-change floor constant and decide which senses may pay under caused mode; the operator then chooses the channel's weight.
inputs: The pause's checkpoint; production's own command and seed (Saved/mimo_bridge/training_continuation.json, read only) with the consequence switch at measure; the latent body shadow and the observer recorder off; this branch's code.

Every model step, per body and sense: change = token now minus token a model step ago; own agreement and swapped agreement of the predicted changes with it; advantage = own minus swapped. A second swapped forward with two other bodies' commands gives the null.
Per sense gate: one reading per control model step (every 7th), open above 3 standard errors over 32 readings, close below 1.

Each report's caused-change block records per sense the advantage, agreements, caused and changed shares, gate and null gate open shares, the repeat line, habituation, the would-be pay, and the channel value's spread with every gate open; and the cost.

Write arm.json and copy the stats.

Gate and null gate open shares: 0 to 1 of the window's control readings.
Value spread with every gate open: standard deviation of the value's successive changes divided by the square root of 2.

inputs: The saved eight-world episode of ckpt_step_455800; each body restored to its saved state as training restores it on resume; the caregiver's event list replaced by a counter.

The learner's own commands as the world recorder stored them (authors: planner, self choice, acting snapshot, reflex, reflex noise), each a whole command with its hold and its eye command at each model step.
8 bodies, 2,500 model steps each, 8 worker processes, vision as in the run.
steps: Extract the saved worlds; per body build the world from production's body settings, restore it and check it field by field.

Collect the body's recorded commands. Re-anchor each: keep each handle's displacement and turn from where the command began and ask for them again from the handle's current pose; the eye row, radius, strength, mask and hand joint goal stay as recorded.

Play the commands in a random permutation (a new one each pass), each held as many model steps as in production, 5 physics steps of 10 ms per model step, the eyes rendered at each model step's last physics step.
Record with the world recorder, run the same detectors, and write the per-capability summary.
measures: B06 rate: arm-into-view events per body-model-step. An event is a hand entering the eye's view while its palm moved at least 0.10 m/s in the preceding 0.25 s and the head turned at most 10 degrees.
Reference points: production's own record reads 538 events in 499,869 body-model-steps (1.08 per 1,000); random commands from checkpoint 415,075 read 93 in 20,000 (4.65 per 1,000).

Verdict 'the commands keep the hands down' when this replay's whole interval lies below M; 'gaze and timing' when it lies above M; 'no verdict' when the interval contains M. Declared 5:46 PM PDT Oct 2, 2026, before any run.
rows.pass_line_basis: Reachability, from the rates on record: the learner's whole-run rate is 538 events in 499,869 body-model-steps, 1.08 per 1,000 (Saved/mimo_bridge/observer/H84_fresh_drivers_20260918/development.json); random commands from checkpoint 415,075 read 93 in 20,000, 4.65 per 1,000 (Saved/mimo_bridge/observer/baselines/74302686aba93fca/random_orders.json). rows.title: Reachable body goals: planners against the controller
rows.question: From saved starts in all eight worlds, does the production planner's direct search or its learned-synergy search end nearer reference body goals after 0.25 s than the controller's own command?
rows.why: It measures whether planning toward a physical goal beats the controller's own command: the evidence for the planner's hand and body control and for the synergy's adoption comparison. A change of its line state triggers this test and the planner-candidate test at the next saved window.
inputs: The newest production checkpoint at the scheduled step (first 380,500, then every 12,000 model steps, or earlier on a trigger), its saved eight-world episode and its learned synergy.

Goal suite hand_and_body, 5 goals per body: finger curl, finger extension, a left-wrist reach, a supported trunk turn and a left-elbow flex. Each goal is the observed end pose of a reference command executed from the same saved start; the body references change the controller's request by at most 1.8 cm per coordinate and 11 degrees, the planners' own search region.
Triggers: commits to its declared code files, a change of production's flags, and a change of the line state of this test or of the hand-following test.
steps: Load the checkpoint frozen (learning off, weights hashed before and after) with its saved worlds.

Per body (8) and goal (5), from the same saved start: the controller's own command, the planner's direct hand-space search toward the goal pose, and the planner's search through the learned synergy; strength and gaze are shared inside the searches.
Execute each command for 0.25 s (25 physics steps of 10 ms) through the real moving-wrist path from the restored snapshot; each replay must be exact.
Score each end pose against the goal, average each body's goals, and take a paired bootstrap over the 8 bodies (10,000 draws) of arm error minus controller error.
measures: Physical goal error: mean over the goal's handles of (position error / 1.8 cm) squared plus (turn error / 11 degrees) squared. 0 = on the goal; 1 = one planner-region step of 1.8 cm or 11 degrees away.
Wrist goal error (cm) and hand joint error (degrees), reported.
Arm minus controller per body, its 95% paired interval, and the bodies where the arm is better (0 to 8).

rows.title: Planner candidates: predicted against executed outcomes
rows.question: From saved planning events, do the planner's candidate commands differ in predicted and actual outcome, which stage loses the difference, and does selecting by predicted wellness 150 ms ahead give better actual wellness than selecting 50 ms ahead?
rows.why: Its captured share is the planner-side reading of the forward model: how much of the real difference between two executed candidates' next tokens the predicted difference matches. Production's tie count cannot give this reading, because a tie is a predicted difference inside the evaluator's own error band, and that band has been wider than the candidates' predicted spread in every report window since Sep 23 (1,174 of 1,174, median 12.6 times the spread; docs/gain_of_function_v4/agents/hold_loss_history_2026-10-02.json). The test also locates which stage loses the difference (forward model, evaluator or planner) and tests whether a deeper lookahead makes a better physical decision. A change of its line state, of the body-goals line, a commit to its declared code or a flag change triggers it.
inputs: The newest production checkpoint at the scheduled step (first 399,050, then every 12,000 model steps, or earlier on a trigger) and its saved eight-world episode.
16 starts (8 bodies x 2, 10 model steps apart), each a planning event of the checkpoint's own behaviour.
Per start 5 candidate commands: the planner's chosen command, hold, the controller's own proposal, and two perturbations of the chosen command at the babble's size, seeded as production seeds them.

The probe script at version planner_candidates_v3 (Oct 2, 2026). Its SHA-256 is written into the declaration, every per-start row, status.json, the result and the summary, and the Development page labels each round by its first 8 characters. Earlier rounds: 1467b636 (version 1) at 399,100; b5cbb3be (version 2) at 408,450 to 414,200; 7819ad7a (version 2) at 415,325 to 450,525.
steps: Predict every candidate before anything moves, on the planner's route and on the learning route, held 1, 2 and 3 model steps, every depth reading the decision's achieved pose: every sense's token, the evaluator's five wellness terms, the goal distance. These predictions are used for the route check against the production planning record, for the planner's ranks and for the depth comparison's selections, because a planner at the decision has no later pose.
Execute each candidate from the identical restored snapshot for its tenure of 5 model steps; replay each branch; the two physical traces must be bit-identical.
After every model step read the raw tokens, the grounded wellness terms, the evaluator on the actual tokens, the next-model-step prediction error and the pose.

Restore the snapshot and predict again from the same states, depth 2 reading each candidate's own achieved pose after 1 executed model step and depth 3 its pose after 2. Depth 1 reads the decision's pose and must reproduce the first pass to within 1e-6 per token number, else the probe stops. The token-space shares are taken on these executed-pose predictions; the decision-pose shares of depths 2 and 3 are kept beside them.

Per sense and depth, sum the real difference between candidates (mean over the 192 token numbers of the squared difference of their real tokens) over all pairs, and sum its float32 floor over the same pairs (per pair, the mean over the numbers of (192 x the float32 grid step at that number) squared). At or below the floor the sense's captured share reads not measurable.
Split the evaluator's error on a candidate difference into the forward model's part and the evaluator's part; per stage take the transfer slope with a 95% interval over whole bodies.
Select candidates by predicted wellness at 50 ms and at 150 ms and compare the two selections' actual wellness over the tenure, paired over the starts.
measures: Transfer slopes: 1 = the stage passes the whole between-candidate difference on, 0 = none of it.

Captured share of the between-candidate token difference, on the executed-pose predictions: 0 = foresaw none, 1 = all, below 0 = the opposite direction. It reads not measurable when the real difference is within the token's float32 floor. In the nine earlier rounds vestibular's real difference was 2 to 19 grid steps per number against a floor of 192, and the other senses' was 270,000 grid steps or more.

Executed pose shift: per depth 2 and 3 and per candidate, the mean distance (cm, over the handles) between the pose the branch reached and the decision's pose. 0 = the decision's pose was still right.
Depth difference: actual wellness over the tenure of the 150 ms selection minus the 50 ms selection, on the 0-to-5 wellness sum.
Ranking: candidate pairs out of 100 that the forecast ranks as the outcomes rank (50 = chance, 80 to 90 = a ranking a planner can use).
rows.pass_line: Passed when the command selected by predicted wellness at 150 ms beats the one selected at 50 ms in actual grounded wellness averaged over the command's tenure, with the 95% interval over bodies above 0.
rows.pass_line_basis: docs/gain_of_function_v4/probe_planner_candidates.py, DECISION_RULES depth_claim, declared before measurement; the scheduler reads the result's passed flag (Source/Python/mimo_bridge/tools/ability_rechecks.py, declared_line).

rows.title: Own-command read-outs: collect every hold phase
rows.question: With no training, from checkpoint 455,800's saved worlds, what do the delayed next-model-step lesson's predictions read at every model step of a 5-model-step hold, with the body's own command and three swapped commands, under the production bf16 path, with the prediction heads in fp32, and with the persistent memory's constant subtracted from the heads' input?
rows.why: Both read-outs the own-command analysis of Oct 2 calls decisive are computed from this job's records: a reading that rises under fp32 or with the constant subtracted makes centring the prediction heads' input the repair; a motor token near its shuffled control makes the motor encoder or a direct command input the repair; neither leaves the contrast-loss route. The live audit grades only the hold's fifth model step; no record holds the first four.
inputs: Checkpoint ckpt_step_455800 of run H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41s_1146_resume_20261001_213502 (read only), its args.json, and its eight-body episode companion (970,668,506 bytes on D:, read only).

Production's model code: branch fix/own_command_readouts-2026-10-02 adds only this script, its tests and the jobs file; its model files (Source/Python/lem, mimo_bridge/lem_model.py, train_mimo.py) equal production's commits 06223f2df and 54f8db1ae, whose model code equals the checkpoint's commit 66c51897e.
The probe harness (mimo_bridge/tools/gof_probe_harness.py Session): one body at a time on the CPU with 8 threads, learning off, the run's babble of 0.05 and its planner.

The persistent memory's constant per slot, read as the motor-input fold of Sep 27 reads it (lem/model/motor_input_fold.effective_constant: the readout's ordinary bias times the return's factor): 107 to 268 per number on the vision, tactile, proprioception and motor slots at model step 455,800 (own-command analysis); the job records the values it used.
steps: Write declaration.json (the rules, the counts and their arithmetic) before anything is measured. Check the memory guard: 19 GB needed, 6 GB reserve.

Build the model on the CPU from the run's args.json and load the checkpoint once. Refuse a checkpoint step other than 455,800, a build without the delayed next-model-step lesson, or --self-state perceive. Hash every parameter and freeze it.

Load the episode companion once. For each body 0 to 7: restore its saved world, context, memory and histories (Session); one first model step; then 250 transitions. A transition is Session.policy_act (a new command from the model's output when the policy index is a multiple of 5, else the held one; the eyes follow the gaze output at every model step) followed by Session.observe (one LemLite.step with learning off).

During each observe, a forward pre-hook on the forward model keeps the inputs of the step's first forward call, the lesson's: the 5 sense tokens of model step t, the motor token with the executed command A_t, the context of the 127 model steps before t, and the memory's bias of model step t. Kept beside them: A_t (26 handles x 9 numbers), the achieved pose of t, the model's own lesson prediction and the raw tokens of model step t+1. The captured motor token must equal the motor encoder's output for [achieved pose of t, A_t] within 0.0001, else the job stops.

Phase of each transition = the policy index of model step t mod 5 (0 = A_t latched at t, the hold's first model step; 4 = its last). Check: the held rows of the command (every row but the eyes' and the hand path's wrist and finger rows) change only into phase 0.

Per step index, the 8 bodies as one batch and four commands: own (A_t); absolute roll (the previous body's A_t, the live audit's control); size-matched (the previous body's A_t as a change from its own pose applied to this body's pose, contact_head.shuffled_order); noise (A_t plus Gaussian noise of one standard deviation per command column over all executed commands, quaternions renormalised, seed 20261002). Check: every swapped command differs from the own one for every body.

Per command: the motor encoder, the transformer and the prediction heads with the gaze copy on the bf16 grid (every matrix product's inputs and output rounded to bf16, layer_norm and softmax in fp32, the card's autocast policy; emulated because this CPU ran a batch-8 transformer pass in 8.2 s under bf16 against 0.19 s in fp32); the same transformer output into the heads in fp32; and the heads in fp32 on that output minus the memory's constant (check: the input equals the output minus the constant to 1e-5 of the constant's size). The own command also with everything in fp32.

Route check: the all-fp32 own-command prediction must equal the model's own lesson prediction within 0.001 per number. Emulation check on the first batch: the grid's and fp32's mean deviation from true CPU bf16 autocast, over the predictions' spread across the bodies.

Per transition and sense: the mean squared error of every prediction against the raw next token; the offset_subtracted_mean_matched form (the offset_subtracted predictions minus, per sense, their mean difference from the heads_fp32 predictions over all transitions and the four commands); the features READ-OUT 2 reads; the heads' attention weights. Check the parameters' hash unchanged. Write transitions.npz and collect.json.
measures: Prediction error per transition, sense, command and condition: mean over the 192 numbers of (prediction minus raw next token) squared, token units squared. 0 = exact; the no-change error (the current token as the prediction) is kept beside it.
Route check: largest absolute difference between the read-out's fp32 own-command prediction and the model's own lesson prediction, token units. 0 = the same computation.
Emulation check: mean absolute deviation from true bf16 autocast over the predictions' spread across the 8 bodies, for the grid and for fp32. 0 = identical to autocast.
Counts: 8 bodies x 250 transitions = 2,000; 400 per hold phase (350 without body 2).
rows.pass_line: Completes with: the route check within 0.001 per number for every sense, the phase-label check passed, the captured motor token within 0.0001 of the encoder's output, every swap applied, the constant subtracted, the parameters' hash unchanged, and 2,000 transitions written.
rows.pass_line_basis: The route check compares one computation done twice (the model's batch of 1 against the read-out's batch of 8, both fp32): on the tests' fake-session fixture its largest difference was below 0.0001; 0.001 is the planner probe's route tolerance (docs/gain_of_function_v4/probe_planner_candidates.py, ROUTE_TOLERANCE). The grid's fidelity: on the tests' fixtures it matched true CPU bf16 autocast to 0 on standalone batches and to 0.0003 to 0.19 of the bodies' spread on the fake-session batch, where fp32 sat 0.27 to 1.02 away (test_own_command_readouts.py).

rows.title: READ-OUT 1: own-command reading per hold phase
rows.question: At each of the 5 model steps of a hold, does the main route's prediction with the body's own command beat the prediction with another body's size-matched command, under the production bf16 path, with the prediction heads in fp32, and with the memory's constant subtracted from the heads' input?
rows.why: It applies the centring rule: a reading that rises above its noise in fp32 or with the constant subtracted, at any phase, makes centring the prediction heads' input the repair (the decision job). It also gives the production path's reading at the hold's first four model steps for the first time; the live audit grades only the fifth.
inputs: transitions.npz from own_command_readouts_collect: per transition the body, the phase, which senses count, the prediction errors (4 conditions x 4 commands x 5 senses), the no-change errors, the token sizes and the vestibular tokens.
collect.json: the route and phase-label checks; the job refuses when either failed.
steps: Refuse unless collect's route check and phase-label check passed.
Two pools: all 8 bodies, and bodies 0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 (the decision pool; body 2 left out by the operator's decision of Sep 25).

Per pool, phase (0 to 4, and all phases together) and sense: a transition counts for a sense when its input and its next token are both real readings; the sense is measurable at that phase when the root mean square of the real next-token change is at least 1 part in a million of the token's root mean square.
Per swapped command and condition: reading = 1 - (sum of own-command errors) / (sum of swapped-command errors) over that phase's transitions.

Interval: 95 in 100 from 2,000 draws of a two-level bootstrap (bodies drawn with replacement, then each drawn body's transitions of that phase drawn with replacement). Every condition uses the same draws, so condition minus production bf16 is a paired difference with its own standard error.
Command shift share per condition: square root of (sum of squared own-minus-swapped prediction differences) / (sum of squared own-prediction changes from the current token).
Judge the centring rule on the decision pool and the size-matched swap; record each comparison it read. Write readout1_phases.json.
measures: Own-command reading per sense, phase, swapped command and condition: 0 = the command makes no difference to the prediction error, 1 = the own command leaves no error, below 0 = the swapped command predicts better (reported as counts per 100).
Paired difference, condition minus production bf16, on the same scale.
Command shift share: 0 = swapping the command leaves the prediction where it was, 1 = it moves it as far as the whole predicted change.
Vestibular token variation over the window per body: root mean square of the token's departure from its mean, over its root mean square; 0 = the token never changes.
Beside it: the phase-4 reading with the absolute roll on the bf16 path against the live audit's 44 windows (vision 13 of 100 pooled; proprioception, tactile and audio within 1 of 10,000 of 0).
rows.pass_line: Read on the size_matched swap, pooled over bodies 0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 (body 2 left out by the operator's decision of Sep 25), for each of vision, tactile, audio and proprioception whose real next-token change is measurable at that phase, at each of the 5 hold phases, under heads_fp32, offset_subtracted and offset_subtracted_mean_matched: MET when the condition's own-command reading AND its paired difference from the production_bf16 reading on the same transitions are each above z times their bootstrap standard error, where z is the one-sided normal line for 5 in 100 shared over the comparisons made (at most 4 senses x 5 phases x 3 forms = 60, z = 3.14). Met by any one: the repair is centring the prediction heads' input.
rows.pass_line_basis: Declared before the run (RULES in the script). Reachability: 8 bodies x 250 transitions = 400 transitions a phase, 350 in the decision pool. From the live audit's window spread (40 transitions a window), the standard error at 350 is 0.000164 for proprioception, 0.000626 for audio, 1.76e-06 for tactile and 0.0268 for vision, so the smallest rise the rule can declare (z = 3.14 times it) is 0.00052, 0.002, 5.5e-06 and 0.084 of the reading's 0-to-1 scale. H71's pooled proprioception reading of 0.08 is 155 times proprioception's line, so a dependence of H71's size at any phase is declared; today's live reading at phase 4 (proprioception -0.00007) is not. The plain offset_subtracted form is expected to read near 0 by construction: the heads' output without the constant leaves their trained range (in lem/model/persistent_memory.py, moving every constant 2 in 100 of the way raised vision's error by a factor of about 3,400); the mean-matched form removes the vector that shift adds to every command alike. Source of the spreads: Saved/mimo_bridge/experiments/H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41s_1146_resume_20261001_213502/replay_training_stats.jsonl, prediction_audit, 44 windows of 40 transitions (one of 24), model steps 451,500 to 455,800.

rows.title: READ-OUT 2: does the motor token carry the command
rows.question: Can a linear read-out fitted on other bodies recover the executed command, and its change from the achieved pose, from today's motor token, from the transformer's output at the motor slot, and from each prediction head's input?
rows.why: It applies the motor-token rule: a motor token near its shuffled control makes the motor encoder or a direct command input the repair (the decision job). The other features show where between the motor token and the heads the command is lost.
inputs: transitions.npz from own_command_readouts_collect: per transition the executed command (26 handles x 9), the achieved pose (26 x 10) and the features: the motor encoder's input position columns (26 x 6, the positive control) and its whole input (26 x 19), the motor token (192), the transformer's final LayerNorm output at the motor slot (192), the 6 tokens the heads attend over in fp32 and rounded to bf16 (1,152 each), and each of the 5 heads' attention outputs under the 3 computed conditions (192 each).
collect.json: the route check; the job refuses when it failed.
steps: Refuse unless collect's route check passed.

Targets: for the 25 body handles the command's position (cm), orientation (unit quaternion, w at least 0), radius and strength; the eye command's azimuth and elevation (radians); the asked position change (command position minus achieved position, cm) and the asked turn (rotation vector from the achieved to the commanded orientation, degrees).

Per feature: leave one body out. On the other bodies the features are standardised and the targets centred; lambda is chosen per target group from 15 values (0.01 to 100,000) by an inner leave-one-body-out; the held-out body is predicted; R^2 = 1 - sum of squared errors / sum of squares about the training mean, pooled over the held-out bodies and the group's columns.

Control: the same with the targets' rows permuted: 100 permutations for the motor token on the decision pool, lambda chosen again in each; 20 for every other feature, reusing the real fit's lambdas (reported only).
Two pools as in READ-OUT 1: the decision pool without body 2, and all bodies. Judge the motor-token rule on the decision pool. Write readout2_motor_token.json.
measures: Held-out R^2 per feature and target group: 0 = predicts nothing beyond the training mean, 1 = exact, below 0 = worse than the training mean.
The permuted control's median, 97.5th percentile and largest value per feature and group.
The positive control's R^2 on the asked position change.
rows.pass_line: The motor token's held-out R^2 for the asked position change or the asked turn (the 25 body handles pooled, bodies 0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7, each held out in turn) above both the 97.5th percentile of the same R^2 over 100 row permutations of the targets (5 in 100 shared over the two groups) and 0.04, one handle's share of the 25 pooled handles: the motor token carries the command. rows.title: Vestibular repair measured on the graphics card
rows.question: On checkpoint 455,800's saved model steps, in the graphics card's bf16, does dividing the vestibular encoder's last layer by 4,096 leave every token and prediction exactly as it was, does learning then spread the token, which mode does that license, and what does the revived token add to the other senses' prediction errors?
rows.why: Its MODE is the mode the two-arm trial's repair arm runs (both arms refuse without it), its EM reading is half of the trial's line (a), and its expected_rise is the declared cost the kill-line watcher needs before a deploy from 455,800 (the watcher refuses a cost read at another step). The Sep 26 result on 415,075 is 40,725 updates older and cannot serve.
inputs: Checkpoint ckpt_step_455800 (Saved/mimo_bridge/experiments/H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41s_1146_resume_20261001_213502/checkpoints/ckpt_step_455800, read only): weights, optimizer state (the encoder's Adam running averages), runtime state, and its episode companion (970,668,506 bytes on D:): the delayed next-model-step lesson's saved model step for all 8 bodies (raw inputs, a context of 127 model steps, mask, tokens, memory bias) and the replay ring's stored vestibular tokens. Its receipt records no switch; the last layer's bias has the spread 74,425 of every checkpoint since Sep 23.
For RV: the saved model steps of the two checkpoints before it in the run, 454,483 and 452,933 (companions 959,966,167 and 944,837,532 bytes).
For OT: the 8 newest clusters of saved model steps since 382,800 whose checkpoints lie within 1,000 model steps: 28 saved model steps from 410,400 to 450,525, 20,768 MB of companions.
Then the five checkpoints across the dead period read on Sep 26: 402,150, 392,950, 380,550, 359,875 and 347,791 (D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_recordings/H84_checkpoint_archive).
Settings: `--updates 200 --mode rescale_restart --device cuda:0 --moments 3 --ot-clusters 8`.
steps: Per checkpoint, one model at a time on the graphics card: build it with the trainer's builder from the run's args.json and load weights and optimizer state; nothing trains production or writes a checkpoint.

EM: run the delayed lesson's forward pass on the saved model step (the 8 bodies' vestibular tokens, the core's output at every position and at its newest step, every prediction head) in float32 and in bf16 under autocast; divide the last layer's weight and bias by the largest power of two that keeps the bias spread at or above 9.16 (4,096); run the forward pass again; record each block's largest absolute change and compare the replay ring's stored vestibular tokens bit for bit. EM32: the encoder in float32 against production's bf16.

LS: from the divided state, train the vestibular encoder alone for 200 Adam updates on the 8 bodies' saved inputs, arms A (not divided), R, RR, R8 and CORE (the whole next-model-step lesson through the real core and heads) in float32 and A, RR, CORE and CORE32 in bf16; read the token's spread between the 8 bodies after 1, 10, 50, 100 and 200 updates.

MODE: rescale_restart when bf16 RR or CORE spreads the token to at least 0.05 and 1,000 times arm A after 100 updates with RR's largest hidden-layer step within 4.0 learning rates; else rescale_restart_fp32 when CORE32 does and EM32 is within its line; then none unless OT and the cost were read on that mode's arm.

RV: on both deploy arms, how far each other sense's prediction head moves when the revived token replaces the dead one, as a share of that sense's typical change per model step, over 3 saved model steps; expected_rise = per other sense, the mean over the 3 saved model steps of the largest of its context-form rises.

OT: each deploy arm's revived encoder applied to each cluster's saved inputs; body 0's token's standard deviation over the cluster's saved model steps, averaged over the 192 numbers, scaled to the collapse watch by the live senses' ratio (kappa).
Write vestibular_encoder_repair_card.json after every stage and every arm.
measures: EM change: the largest absolute change of each block, in token units; 0.0 = the same number; the script's line 2e-5 x max(1, largest value / 16).
LS spread: the standard deviation of the vestibular token across the 8 bodies, root mean square over its 192 numbers; 0 = every body gets the same token; the live senses read 0.15 to 0.53.
OT: body 0's predicted collapse watch; 0 = the same token over the cluster; the live senses read 0.22 to 0.65 before Sep 23; the dead-token line K2 = 9.42e-5.
RV: the expected rise of each other sense's next-model-step error ratio (the ratio: 0 = exact, 1 = no better than predicting no change).
MODE: rescale_restart, rescale_restart_fp32 or none, and whether the card's reading licensed it.

For the trial's line (a) the EM blocks of 455,800 must read exactly 0.0 in float32 and bf16.

Reachability, from this job on 415,075 and the five spanning checkpoints on Sep 26 (Saved/gof_takeover_20260924/repair/vestibular_encoder_repair/vestibular_encoder_repair_card.json): EM read exactly 0.0 on every block in float32 and bf16 at all 6; bf16 CORE spread the token between the bodies to 0.070-0.088 after 100 updates against arm A's 0.0; OT's lowest predicted collapse watch was 0.011, 117 times K2's line; MODE rescale_restart, licensed by the card. Prediction reading (improvement_over_persistence: 1 = exact next token, 0 = no better than predicting no change) and own-command reading (improvement_over_shuffled: 0 = this body's command predicts no better than another body's), with the sensitivity.
Each other sense's next-model-step error ratio (next_frame_norm.ratio): 0 = exact, 1 = no better than predicting no change.

inputs: The control arm's finished record (its checkpoint and its stats) and the same production command and seed, folders replaced, the latent body shadow and the observer recorder off.

steps: Check the control's finished record and the card's licence; without them, record why and stop before training.

Start the trainer from the checkpoint with the repair on. rows.title: Motor encoder: where the asked change is lost
rows.question: With the motor encoder's weights of checkpoint 455,800 and the 2,000 recorded encoder inputs, at which stage does a linear read-out fitted on other bodies stop recovering the asked position change and the asked turn: each handle's own per-handle network output, the pooled vector before the output LayerNorm, or the token; and how is each pooling head's attention weight spread over the 26 handles?
rows.why: The declared rule of the own-command read-outs selected a repair of the motor encoder or a direct command input (row own_command_readouts_decision). The repair's design depends on where the asked change is lost. Lost inside each handle's per-handle network: the asked change has to be given to the encoder as an explicit input. Kept per handle and lost at the pooling: a path that every handle reaches would be enough.
inputs: transitions.npz of the own-command read-outs (D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/own_command_readouts/2026-10-02, read only): 2,000 recorded transitions of checkpoint 455,800 (8 bodies x 250 model steps); used here: the motor encoder's input (26 handles x 19 numbers: the achieved pose's 10 numbers with positions divided by 200 cm, then the executed command's 9 numbers with positions divided by 200 cm), the command in cm, the achieved pose, the body number and the recorded motor token (192 numbers).

model.safetensors of ckpt_step_455800 of run H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41s_1146_resume_20261001_213502 (read only): only the 24 tensors of the motor encoder (encoder_registry.encoders.motor) and the 5 tensors of the liveness repair's all-element path for the motor pool (liveness_repair.paths.motor), read one by one on the CPU. No other weight is read, no model beyond the motor encoder module is built, no world, no trainer.
The run's args.json (the encoder's sizes: 2 attention layers of 4 heads, 4 pooling heads, width 192, no biases, a learned vector per handle).
The regression code of read-out 2 (LoboRidge, target_groups, bf16_grid of docs/gain_of_function_v4/own_command_readouts.py at commit a334a8f90), loaded with git show.
steps: Check that each recorded input row equals [achieved pose, command with positions divided by 200 cm] to 1e-6.

Compute the encoder's forward pass in float32, keeping every stage: each handle's per-handle network output (19 -> 192 -> 192, one handle at a time), the backbone output after the 2 attention layers, the pooling attention's output and its weights per head, the all-element path's 19 numbers per handle and its output, their sum (the pooled vector), and the token (LayerNorm of the pooled vector without gain or bias).

Route check: compute the token again on the read-out's bf16 grid in batches of 8 rows in the recorded sequence and compare it with the recorded motor token; stop without readings when the largest difference exceeds 0.02 per number.

Per body handle (25) and stage (the handle's 19 input numbers, its per-handle network output, its backbone output, its 19 numbers inside the all-element path): ridge regression to that handle's asked position change (3 numbers, cm) and asked turn (3 numbers, degrees), one body held out in turn, lambda chosen by an inner leave-one-body-out, on bodies 0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7; held-out R^2 per handle and pooled over the 25 handles as summed squared error over summed squares; control: 20 row permutations of the targets with the real fit's lambdas. A control input for the turn: the command's orientation relative to the achieved one as a quaternion (4 numbers).

Pooled stages, the 25 handles' 75 + 75 target numbers together, on the same bodies and on all 8: all 26 per-handle outputs side by side (4,992 numbers), the pooling attention's output, the all-element path's 494 numbers and its output, the pooled vector, the token and the recorded token.

Attention: per pooling head over the 2,000 inputs, the mean largest weight, the handle that holds it most often and in what share of inputs, and the spread; the same spread for the backbone's two attention layers.

First layer: for each position axis the cosine between the per-handle network's weights on the achieved position and on the command position, the size of the part that multiplies their difference and of the part that multiplies their sum, and the share of each hidden unit's input variance that comes from the command columns and from the asked position change.
Write stages.json.
measures: Held-out R^2 per stage and target group: 0 = the read-out predicts nothing beyond the training mean, 1 = exact, below 0 = worse than the training mean; beside each the permuted control's median and 97.5th percentile. Read-out 2's size line is 0.04, one handle's share of the 25 pooled handles.

Largest attention weight per pooling head: 1/26 = 0.038 = even weight on all 26 handles, 1 = all weight on one handle. Spread: entropy of the weights over log 26; 0 = all weight on one handle, 1 = even.
Route check: largest absolute difference between the recomputed and the recorded token, in token units (a token's numbers have root mean square 1); 0 = the same computation.

First-layer shares: variance of that part of a hidden unit's input over the recorded handle rows, over the variance of the unit's whole input, averaged over the 192 units; 0 = that part never changes the unit's input, 1 = it is the whole input's variation.
Sizes over the recorded rows: the asked position change in cm and the asked turn in degrees (root mean square per axis), the spread of the absolute positions in cm.
rows.pass_line: No pass line of its own: it is a measurement. It completes when the route check passes (the token recomputed on the bf16 grid within 0.02 per number of the recorded motor token on all 2,000 inputs) and the positive control holds (the per-handle read-out of the asked position change from the handle's own 19 input numbers at R^2 0.9 or more, pooled over the 25 handles).
rows.pass_line_basis: The route check repeats one computation (the read-out's collect job computed the recorded token with the same weights on the same grid in the same batches), so its expected difference is 0; a token number has root mean square 1 after the LayerNorm, so 0.02 is 2 of 100 of a number's typical size, while a wrongly rebuilt encoder moves the token by tenths: the all-element path alone is 42 of 100 of the pooling attention's output in size (stats record of model step 455,800, liveness.token_read.motor.path_size_share). The positive control: a handle's asked position change is an exact linear function of its own input row (200 x (command position / 200 cm - achieved position / 200 cm)); read-out 2 read 0.9996 for it from all handles' position columns together (D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/own_command_readouts/2026-10-02/readout2_motor_token.json).
