rows.title: Motor encoder: sizes and one-handle sensitivity
rows.question: On the same weights and recorded inputs as row motor_encoder_asked_change_stages_455800: how large is each stage of the motor encoder and the pooled vector its output LayerNorm divides; does a read-out fitted on the same bodies (one block of 50 model steps held out) recover the asked change where the read-out with a body held out does not; and how far does the token move when one handle's command moves 10 cm or turns 20 degrees, against a control that moves the handle's pose and command together?
rows.why: The first job read the pooled vector at about 10,000 per number and the per-handle read-outs below 0 on a held-out body. The repair's design needs three more readings: the size the output LayerNorm divides by (it sets how large an added path's output has to be before the token moves), whether the asked change is absent or only tied to each body's own places (time-held-out against body-held-out), and whether the token responds to one handle's command at all (the liveness rule's one-input-at-a-time check).
inputs: The inputs of row motor_encoder_asked_change_stages_455800: transitions.npz of the own-command read-outs (2,000 recorded transitions of checkpoint 455,800) and the 29 tensors of the motor encoder and of the liveness repair's all-element path for the motor pool, read from ckpt_step_455800 on the CPU. No other weight, no world, no trainer.
The regression code of read-out 2 at commit a334a8f90, loaded with git show.
steps: Route check as in the first job: the token recomputed on the bf16 grid against the recorded motor token, largest difference at most 0.02 per number; stop without readings above it.

Sizes, float32, all 2,000 rows: the root mean square per number of the first layer's input to its GELU, each handle's per-handle network output, the learned vector per handle, each attention layer's attention output, feed-forward output and running sum, the pooling attention's query, keys, values and output, the all-element path's 19 numbers and output, and the pooled vector; the standard deviation of each row's pooled vector over its 192 numbers (the size the output LayerNorm divides by); the bf16 grid step at each pooled number over that standard deviation; per pooling head the gap between the largest and second largest logit over the 26 handles; the root mean square of every weight tensor.

One-handle sensitivity on every 10th row (200 rows), one handle at a time (26): (1) the handle's command position moved 10 cm in a random direction; (2) its command orientation turned 20 degrees about a random axis; (3) the control: its achieved position and its command position moved 10 cm together, so the asked change stays. Per change: the root mean square over the token's 192 numbers of (token after - token before), and whether any pooling head's largest weight moved to another handle. Beside them: the same token change between consecutive recorded model steps of one body, and between two recorded rows drawn at random.

Time-held-out read-out on bodies 0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7: the ridge read-out of the first job with 5 blocks of 50 consecutive model steps as the held-out groups (every body is in the training rows), for the same per-handle stages and for the pooling attention's output, the all-element path's 494 numbers and output, the pooled vector and the token; control: 20 row permutations.
Write mechanism.json.
measures: Sizes: root mean square per number, in the stage's own units (the input row's positions are cm / 200; a token number has root mean square 1). The LayerNorm's divisor: the row's standard deviation over the pooled vector's 192 numbers.
bf16 grid step over the row's standard deviation: 0 = no rounding of the pooled vector, 1 = one rounding step as large as the token's whole spread.
Logit gap per pooling head: 0 = two handles share the head's weight evenly; a gap of g leaves the second handle at most exp(-g) of the first's weight.
Token change: 0 = the token did not move; 1.41 = as far as two unrelated tokens of root mean square 1.
Time-held-out R^2: 0 = predicts nothing beyond the training mean, 1 = exact, below 0 = worse than the training mean.
rows.pass_line: No pass line of its own: it is a measurement. It completes when the route check passes (largest difference at most 0.02 per number; the first job read 0).
rows.pass_line_basis: The route check is the first job's (row motor_encoder_asked_change_stages_455800: the recomputed token equalled the recorded one exactly on all 2,000 rows).

cost.where: training pause
cost.basis: Run directly by the agent on the CPU while training is stopped; the card is hidden from the process. The first job peaked at 4.16 GiB of private memory against its declared 3 (stages.json peak_private_commit_gib): its largest regression read 4,992 numbers per row. This job leaves that regression out; its largest reads 494 numbers per row with 25 decompositions of at most 1,400 x 494 float64 (5.5 MB each). Time: the first job took 438 s, 237 s of it in the 4,992-number regression on two pools.

rows.on_pass: The readings go into this row and into the agent record (section 1). The LayerNorm's divisor sets the unit of the new path's output in the design; the time-held-out read-out says whether the per-handle outputs hold the asked change in a form tied to each body; the sensitivity says whether today's token responds to one handle's command.
rows.on_fail: A failed route check stops the script before any reading; the rebuild is corrected and the job run again into a new folder.

values: Route check passed (largest difference 0 on all 2,000 inputs). File: D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/motor_encoder_asked_change/2026-10-03/mechanism_455800/mechanism.json. Peak private memory 2.81 GiB, run time 98 s.

Sizes, root mean square per number: each handle's per-handle network output 1.5; the running sum after the first attention layer 302 and after the second 378 (the attention layers add outputs of 126 to 208 and the feed-forward layers 169 to 196 to it); the pooling attention's keys 4,010, its values 2,100 and its output 9,568; the all-element path's output 3,786; the pooled vector 9,972. The output LayerNorm divides each row by its standard deviation over the 192 numbers: mean 9,846, between 6,947 and 17,333.

Pooling attention logits: the gap between a head's largest and second largest logit over the 26 handles has a median of 2,202 to 21,091 (a gap of 20 already leaves the second handle 2 parts in a thousand million of the first's weight); in at most 45 of every 10,000 inputs is the gap under 1.
bf16 rounding of the pooled vector: one grid step is 0.45 of 100 of the row's standard deviation on average and at most 3.1 of 100.

One handle's command changed, token change as the root mean square over its 192 numbers (0 = the token did not move; 1.41 = as far as two unrelated tokens): command position moved 10 cm, median 0.0013; command orientation turned 20 degrees, median 0.0049; the control, the handle's achieved position and command position moved 10 cm together so that the asked change stays, median 0.0012. Between consecutive model steps of one body the token changes by 0.45, between two recorded rows at random by 0.83.

In 15 of every 100 position changes and 23 of every 100 turns the change moved a pooling head's whole weight to another handle; then the token changed by 0.15 to 0.16, otherwise by 0.0003 (position) and 0.0010 (turn).

Asked position change, read-out fitted and tested on the same 7 bodies with one block of 50 model steps held out (0 = predicts nothing, 1 = exact): from each handle's own input numbers 1.000; from its per-handle network output 0.754 (every one of the 25 handles at 0.62 or more); from its backbone output 0.185; from its 19 numbers inside the all-element path 0.067; from the all-element path's 494 numbers together 0.091 and its output 0.055; from the pooling attention's output 0.014; from the pooled vector 0.033; from the token 0.037.
Asked turn on the same read-out: from each handle's own input numbers 0.26; from its per-handle network output 0.43; from its backbone output 0.08; from the token 0.013.

rows.decision: Where the asked change is lost: each handle's per-handle network output still holds the asked position change for bodies the read-out was fitted on (75 of 100) but not in a form that carries over to another body (below 0); the two attention layers then add outputs about 200 times that output's size, and the backbone output holds 19 of 100; the pooling attention reads one handle per head, and the pooled vector and the token hold 3 to 4 of 100. The token moves as far when a handle's pose and command move together as when the command moves alone, so it follows the command's absolute place, not the asked change. The design (the record's section 2): the asked change computed per handle from the encoder's own input row, a path with its own weights for every handle, added to the pooled vector in units of the row's standard deviation (about 9,846), so that one unit of the path's output is one unit of the token before its final LayerNorm.

rows.title: Asked-change path: unit tests, planted defects, lockstep
rows.question: Does the code of branch fix/motor_encoder_asked_change-2026-10-03 do what its design says on a small CPU learner: with --motor-asked-change off, train bit for bit as the code the branch was cut from; with it on, leave the tokens, the predictions, the loss and the other weights' update unchanged at the switch; give every handle's asked change its own input columns; present the same command form at every call site of the motor encoder; load checkpoints both ways; and does each unit test catch the defect it guards against?
rows.why: The trial's arms and any later switch in production rest on these properties. They are checked on a small learner on the CPU before a graphics card run is spent on them.
inputs: The working tree of branch fix/motor_encoder_asked_change-2026-10-03 (worktree C:/Users/bhart/Documents/UEMA_wt/motor_encoder): lem/model/motor_asked_change.py, the changed mimo_bridge/lem_model.py and train_mimo.py, the test file and its fixture.
The code the branch was cut from (git merge-base with production's branch, e022cae26), taken with git archive into a temporary folder.

A small learner built by train_mimo.build_learner from H84's own learner flags at width 32 with 3 bodies, driven on seeded synthetic frames (mimo_bridge/tests/motor_asked_change_fixture.py). No checkpoint of production, no world, no graphics card.
steps: Unit tests: pytest on mimo_bridge/tests/test_motor_asked_change.py (24 tests) and test_motor_asked_change_trial.py (13 tests of the trial driver's pure parts), one thread.

Planted defects (docs/gain_of_function_v4/motor_encoder_asked_change/planted_defects.py): the source is copied once; the path's tests run on the clean copy; then each of 36 defects is planted by one exact text substitution, the tests named for it run, and the file is put back.

Lockstep (docs/gain_of_function_v4/motor_encoder_asked_change/lockstep.py): the base code and the branch's code each drive the same small learner for 120 model steps with the flag absent from the launch line, with dead units planted so that the liveness repair revives units during the run; a third run has the flag on. Every model step records the loss, the gradient norm, hashes of the command, the tokens, the predictions and the random streams, and every 10 model steps one hash over every weight and Adam state.
One process at a time, each held to the RAM and commit limits of motor_encoder_asked_change_registry.py; no process is started with under 8 GB of commit room. Write cpu_checks_result.json.
measures: Unit tests passed, of 37.
Planted defects caught, of 36: a defect is caught when at least one of the tests run on it fails.

Lockstep, base against branch with the flag absent: the first model step at which any recorded value differs (none = the two codes trained the same numbers at all 120 model steps) and whether the final hash over all weights is equal.
Lockstep, branch with the flag on against off: the first model step with a differing value, beside the first model step before which the path's output layer had moved from zero.
rows.pass_line: All 37 unit tests pass; the clean copy passes and each of the 36 planted defects fails at least one test; base against branch with the flag absent has no differing value in 120 model steps and an equal final hash, with at least one liveness revival during the run; with the flag on, no value differs before the model step at which the path's output layer has first moved, and a later one does.
rows.pass_line_basis: These are identities, not thresholds. With the flag off the path's module is never imported or built, so no arithmetic can differ; with the output layer at zero the hook adds exactly 0 to the motor encoder's output. THE FIRST RUN (2:01 to 2:11 AM PDT Oct 3, 580.6 s; results kept in cpu_checks_first): 22 of 22 unit tests passed, 32 of 32 planted defects were caught, base against branch with the flag absent was equal at all 120 model steps with equal final hashes and three revived layers; the run failed on the flag-on comparison, which differed at model step 1 while the output layer was still zero. Cause: the liveness repair built the revived rows of the path's hidden layer in the random stream it shares with its pool paths, so a fresh build with the flag on gave the motor and touch pools' all-element paths other starting weights (a switch at a checkpoint loads those weights and was unaffected: the unit test of the switch passed). Repaired: the layer's rows are built in a random stream of their own (lem/model/liveness.py add_layer). THE SECOND RUN (2:27 to 2:40 AM PDT, 803 s; cpu_checks_second), with that repair and the path's weights detached on every imagined row: 36 of 36 tests, 35 of 35 planted defects, the lockstep equal with the flag absent, and with the flag on the first differing model step is 2, the model step before which the output layer first moved. Changed after the second run, so this run is the third: the path's output is added to the pooled vector in float32 instead of the run's bf16 (at the pooled vector's size a bf16 sum rounds away an output under 0.002 to 0.003 token units), with 1 test and 1 planted defect.

cost.where: beside production training, CPU only, one process at a time under the coordinator's limits of Oct 3 (1.5 GB of RAM each, no start with under 8 GB of commit room)
cost.basis: Measured in the second run (Oct 3, 2:27 to 2:40 AM PDT): 803 s for 36 tests, 35 planted defects and the lockstep; the largest process held 0.60 GB of RAM and committed 1.62 GB (importing torch alone commits 1.35 GB); 86 processes in all, never 2 above 200 MB at once. This run adds 1 planted defect and 1 test. Limit 3,600 s, 4.5 times the second run.

rows.title: Asked-change path: token read-out against the path's output size

A line may only be declared with the arithmetic that shows it reachable: this job measures which output size of the path the line needs, and the bound on the output's growth per update then gives the least number of updates.

No other weight, no world, no trainer.

The regression code of read-out 2 at commit a334a8f90, loaded with git show.

The read-out of the token without the path (the reading before the trial).

Output size: root mean square per number of the path's output in token units; 0 = the path adds nothing, 1 = as large as the pooled vector after standardising.
Token change: root mean square over the token's 192 numbers of (token with the path - token without); 0 = unchanged, 1.41 = as far as two unrelated tokens.
rows.pass_line: No pass line of its own: it is a measurement. It completes when the route check passes (largest difference at most 0.02 per number; the first two jobs read 0).
rows.pass_line_basis: The route check is the first job's (row motor_encoder_asked_change_stages_455800: the recomputed token equalled the recorded one on all 2,000 rows).

rows.title: Controllability's two gates on the same graded commands
rows.question: From production's first stats record on the restart candidate's code through model step 465,800: after how many graded commands does the gate in force stand open, after how many does the shadow gate stand open, and on how many graded commands are the two in different states?
rows.why: The operator's decision of Oct 3, 2026: read how often each gate opens on the same data before the gate is switched to the size-matched control, since the switch changes which goals the planner picks. The controllability wellness channel's weight in the goal ranking is 0 while the gate in force is shut. The gate in force compares the own command against another body's absolute command. That control has the swap test's defect: a body head whose output grows with the asked change forms a larger, worse expected change from a mismatched command, so the gate's difference grows with no use of the own command (docs/gain_of_function_v4/agents/swap_test_phases_2026-10-02.md, section 8 finding 1). The shadow gate is the same rule fed by the size-matched control: the other body's command taken as a change from the other body's own pose and applied to this body's pose. The decision that depends on this reading: what the gate switch's own row declares as its change to the goal ranking, at the first relaunch after the vestibular watch ends (model step 465,800).
inputs: Production's stats records (replay_training_stats.jsonl, block controllability) from the first record on the candidate's code through model step 465,800, across the run folders of the supervisor's parent chain.

A graded command = the 8 bodies' commands (each 26 body handles x 9 numbers) latched on one model step, graded together on the model step the next commands appear (every 5 model steps with --motor-hold 5: 20 per report window of 100 model steps).

Per graded command, from the efference record: per body, the body head's expected change over the hold from the own command, from another body's absolute command and from another body's size-matched command, and the achieved change (each 26 handles x 3 numbers; moves in cm, turns in degrees).

Per report window the trainer writes: gate_commands, gate_open_commands, shadow_gate_commands, shadow_gate_open_commands, gates_same_commands, gates_both_open_commands, gate_only_open_commands, shadow_gate_only_open_commands, gate_mean, gate_standard_error, gate_readings_held, shadow_gate_mean, shadow_gate_standard_error, shadow_gate_readings_held, difference_mean, size_matched_difference_mean.
steps: The trainer, at each graded command (ControllabilityTracker._grade): a body is measured when its expected change and its commanded effect are above the stillness floors. Agreement = direction cosine x smaller length / larger length between the expected and the achieved change of the 25 body handles (moves in cm / 1.80, turns in degrees / 11.0). The reading of the gate in force = mean over the measured bodies of (agreement with the own command's expected change - agreement with the absolute control's). The shadow gate's reading = the same with the size-matched control's expected change, on the same measured bodies.

Each gate keeps its last 32 readings. A gate is shut until 32 readings exist; a shut gate opens when their mean is above 3 of their standard errors; an open gate shuts when the mean is under 1 standard error.

The coordinator's script sums the per-window counts over every record of the period. Report windows at whose end shadow_gate_readings_held is under 32 are left out of the comparison and counted apart (after the first load on this code the shadow gate starts with no readings, so it cannot be open in its first 32).
It writes the four counts per 100 graded commands judged by both gates, the number of graded commands they rest on, and the two gates' means and standard errors at the last record, into this row.
measures: Of every 100 graded commands judged by both gates: both open, only the gate in force open, only the shadow gate open, both shut (the four sum to 100).

gate_mean and shadow_gate_mean: mean of the gate's last 32 readings, -2 to +2. 0 = the own command's expected change agreed with the achieved change no better than the control's; +2 = the own command's expected change exact and the control's the opposite change.
The number of graded commands the counts rest on (reachable: (465,800 - 457,800) / 5 = 1,600 when at least one body is above the stillness floors at each).
rows.pass_line: Declared Oct 3, 2026 3:00 AM PDT, before the first record on this code. No pass or fail line: the gate switch is the operator's decision of Oct 3 and this reading does not gate it. The reading is complete when the period's counts are summed and written here with the number of graded commands they rest on. Its use is fixed in advance: the gate switch's row quotes the four counts as the switch's change to the goal ranking (graded commands where only the gate in force stood open are those where the controllability weight goes from its set value to 0; graded commands where only the shadow gate stood open are those where it goes from 0 to its set value).
rows.pass_line_basis: The gates' own lines (open above 3 standard errors, shut under 1, over 32 readings) are the tracker's and are not changed by this reading. The counts are exact sums of the trainer's per-window counts, which the branch's tests check against a count kept by the test (the gate in force open after 9 of 40 graded commands, the shadow gate after 0) and against 6 planted defects, all caught (test_controllability_shadow_gate.py; swap_test_phases_2026-10-02.md section 11.2). Known limit: an open gate fed readings of exactly 0 can stay open (9 of 12 seeded trials), because the closing test mean < 1 standard error is false at 0 against 0; the script therefore also reports how many windows end with a gate open at a mean of exactly 0.

cost.where: a script reading production's stats files
cost.basis: Reads stats files only; nothing is loaded on the graphics card and no world is built.

result_source.file: Saved/mimo_bridge/experiments/<each run folder from the candidate's relaunch through model step 465,800>/replay_training_stats.jsonl

rows.on_pass: The four counts are written into the gate switch's row, which is declared before the first relaunch after model step 465,800. The switch carries the closing line's repair (shut when the mean is at or under 1 standard error).
rows.on_fail: No record carries the shadow gate's keys, or the shadow gate holds under 32 readings at model step 465,800 (no body above the stillness floors): this row records that, the reading runs for one more segment, and the operator is told before the gate switch.

values: Read Oct 3, 2026 12:08 PM PDT on production's records from model step 457,900 to 465,800 (runs H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41f_0322 and H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41f_0322_resume_20261003_044641): 80 report windows compared, 1 left out (the shadow gate held under 32 readings at its end). Both gates took a reading at 1,579 graded commands.

Of every 100 graded commands judged by both: both gates open 98.9, only the gate in force open 1.1, only the shadow gate open 0.0, both shut 0.0. The 17 graded commands with only the gate in force open all fall in the report ending at model step 458,000, the first after the shadow gate reached 32 readings.

At model step 465,800 the gate in force held a mean of 0.395 with a standard error of 0.019 over its 32 readings, and the shadow gate a mean of 0.411 with a standard error of 0.021 (scale -2 to +2; 0 = the own command's expected change agreed with the achieved change no better than the control's). The absolute control's mean agreement was 0.046 and the size-matched control's 0.018 (-1 to +1). No window ended with a gate open at a mean of exactly 0.

rows.decision: The gate switch would have changed the controllability weight on 1.1 of every 100 graded commands in this period (from its set value to 0), all of them in the shadow gate's first report. On H84 the controllability channel's payment does not come from the absolute control's defect: the size-matched control reads a larger difference. The switch to the size-matched control, with the closing line's repair (shut when the mean is at or under 1 standard error), is still to be built; it gets its own row and goes in at a relaunch that carries no other training change. Stated Oct 3, 2026 12:08 PM PDT.

The declared rule of the own-command read-outs selected a repair of the motor encoder or a direct command input; the measurement of Oct 3 found the asked change lost between each handle's input and its per-handle network output and the pooling reading one handle per head. This arm gives the encoder the asked change through a path with its own weights for every handle and lets production's lessons train it.
inputs: The control arm's finished record (out/arm_off.json): its checkpoint, command and seed.

The same command with --motor-asked-change on. The candidate worktree: production's tip at that time (with the swap test's size-matched reading and its hold-first block) merged with branch fix/motor_encoder_asked_change-2026-10-03; passed to the pause runner as --candidate.
steps: The driver (arm on) refuses without the control arm's finished record.

The load is the switch: the path's output layer is zero, and the trainer writes a motor_asked_change_switch record with the motor token's largest change on 64 probe rows in float32 and under the run's autocast.
3,000 training updates, a report every 100, one checkpoint at the end, under D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/motor_asked_change_trial/2026-10-03/runs/on.
Every 30 s the driver reads the arm's reports and judges the kill criterion; a stop writes snapshot_and_stop into the arm's folder.
It writes out/arm_on.json: the switch record, the kill reading, and per 1,000-update window each report's readings.
measures: The switch record: the motor token's largest change with the path against without it, 0.0 = the same number.

The path's own gauges per report: its output's root mean square in token units (0 = it adds nothing, 1 = as large as the pooled vector after standardising), how evenly the 26 handles share that output (1 = even, 0 = one handle), its hidden layer's live share (0 to 1).
The same readings as the control arm.
The kill reading: per other sense, ln(median on / median off) of its next-model-step error ratio over the newest up to 10 reports matched by step with the control.
rows.pass_line: No pass line of its own; lines S1, S2 and C are judged in row motor_asked_change_trial_verdict. It completes when the trainer exits 0 with its final checkpoint, exactly one switch record at the checkpoint's step, and no stop by the kill criterion. KILL CRITERION, declared before any run: a non-finite step; the path's hidden layer under 0.9 live share in 2 consecutive reports; or, from 5 reports after report 1 matched by step with the control, any other sense's ln(median on / median off) over the newest up to 10 of them above ln 1.716 = 0.540 (tactile, audio, proprioception) or ln 3.948 = 1.373 (vision).
rows.pass_line_basis: The stop multiples are the kill-line watcher's RISE x 1.2 (docs/gain_of_function_v4/vestibular_repair_watch.py LINES), which stopped 0 of 206 and 0 of 234 out-of-sample watches with nothing switched. Between three arms that ran production's configuration from one checkpoint on Oct 2 the largest ln(median / median) over 5 to 9 matched reports after report 1 was 0.179 for vision, 0.182 tactile, 0.353 audio and 0.326 proprioception, under both lines; over 2 to 4 reports audio reached 0.576, so the reading waits for 5 reports. The liveness line and count are the watcher's K4 (0.9 in 2 consecutive reports); the path's hidden layer starts fully live (64 of 64 units on the recorded rows at three seeds) and the liveness repair revives its units. Expected transient: the path's output starts at exactly 0 and can grow by at most 0.0027 token units per update (learning rate 3e-4 x a summed input size of 239 / 26, measured on the recorded rows), so the motor token the transformer reads changes slowly; the other senses' errors can rise while the transformer adapts, which the kill reading watches from update 600 on.

Need 37 GB: an 8-world trainer held 32.7 to 37.0 GB at six coordinated stops (persistent_memory_switch_trial.py). The path adds 23,408 weights and one small matrix product per call of the motor encoder.

rows.title: Asked-change trial: the token's read-out on both arms
rows.question: On each arm's final checkpoint: does the motor token carry the asked change, by read-out 2's rule (held-out R^2 of the asked position change or the asked turn above 0.04 and above its permuted control)?
rows.why: The read-out that selected this repair read 0.0043 for the asked position change on checkpoint 455,800. Line S2 of the verdict repeats it on both arms' final weights: on the on arm it says whether the path wrote the asked change into the token, on the off arm that production's encoder still does not.
inputs: Each arm's final checkpoint: only the motor encoder's tensors, the liveness repair's all-element path for the motor pool and, on the on arm, the asked-change path are read from it, one by one on the CPU.
The 2,000 recorded encoder inputs of checkpoint 455,800 (D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/own_command_readouts/2026-10-02/transitions.npz, read only). No world, no trainer, no other weight.
The regression code of read-out 2 at commit a334a8f90, loaded with git show.
steps: The driver (readout both) runs docs/gain_of_function_v4/motor_encoder_asked_change_measure.py --token-only for the off arm, then for the on arm.
Per arm: the recorded rows pass through the arm's motor encoder (and path); the token is computed on the bf16 grid, as the model consumes it, and in float32.
Ridge read-out of the 25 body handles' asked position change and asked turn from the token, one body held out in turn, bodies 0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7, with 20 row permutations as the control.
Write out/readout_off/stages.json, out/readout_on/stages.json and the two summaries.

The path's output size on the recorded rows in token units (0 = it adds nothing, 1 = as large as the pooled vector after standardising).
rows.pass_line: No pass line of its own: line S2 is judged in row motor_asked_change_trial_verdict. It completes when both read-outs are written.
rows.pass_line_basis: The rule is read-out 2's own (row own_command_readout_motor_token). Reach, measured on the recorded rows with the motor encoder of 455,800 and the path's output layer planted (row motor_encoder_asked_change_reach_455800, Oct 3): without the path the token reads 0.0043 and 0.0206; with the path writing only the asked change at an output of 0.01 token units it reads 0.81 to 0.82 (position) and 0.79 (turn), at 0.1 token units 0.97; with random weights on all the path's inputs 0.77 and 0.73 at 0.01 token units. The line is therefore reached at an output of 0.01 token units or less, which the output's growth bound of 0.0027 token units per update allows after 4 updates.

rows.title: Asked-change trial: the declared verdict
rows.question: With the asked-change path on for 3,000 updates from a production checkpoint, against production's behaviour from the same checkpoint: does the motor token carry the asked change (S2), does the main route's prediction of the body's next posture token use the body's own command on the size-matched swap (S1), and does every other sense stay inside the kill-line watcher's stop line (C)?
rows.why: The trial's judgement, declared before any run. A pass says the path repairs what the own-command read-outs found: a motor token without the asked change and a main route blind to the body's own command. It is the measurement a switch in production would rest on; the switch itself is the operator's and the deploy plan's.
inputs: out/arm_off.json and out/arm_on.json (the two arms' records).
out/readout_off/stages.json and out/readout_on/stages.json (the token's read-outs).
steps: The driver (verdict) reads the four files; no training, no model.
S2: read-out 2's rule on both arms' read-outs.

S1: proprioception at the hold's first model step over updates 2,001 to 3,000: each arm's size-matched own-command reading pooled over the window's reports and the 7 bodies without body 2, its standard error from 2,000 seeded resamplings of the (report, body) cells, and the difference on minus off.
C: per other sense, ln(median on / median off) of the next-model-step error ratio over the same reports matched by step.

Beside the lines, never judged: all three 1,000-update windows, every sense and both hold phases on the size-matched and the absolute swap, the path's output size per report, the hold loss's ratio, the contact gates, controllability's gate, the step rate.
Write out/verdict.json.
measures: Own-command reading on the size-matched swap: 0 = this body's command predicts no better than another body's of the same size, 1 = exact where the other is not. Goal ladder: the rung is the main route's prediction of the body's next posture token using the body's own command; the last lineage measured to depend on its command read 0.08 pooled (H71, absolute swap); on the size-matched swap the goal line is unmeasured, and the verdict says so and gives the reading as a share of 0.08.
Token read-out R^2: 0 = predicts nothing beyond the training mean, 1 = exact.
ln(median on / median off) per other sense: 0 = the same error ratio in both arms; the stop lines are ln 1.716 = 0.540 and ln 3.948 = 1.373.
rows.pass_line: PASS when all hold: S2 the on arm's token R^2 for the asked position change or the asked turn above 0.04 and above its permuted control's 97.5th percentile, and the off arm's not; S1 for proprioception at the hold's first model step over updates 2,001 to 3,000, the on arm's reading above 3.14 times its standard error and above the off arm's by more than 3.14 times the standard error of the difference; C no other sense's ln(median on / median off) above ln 1.716 (tactile, audio, proprioception) or ln 3.948 (vision); both arms finished with their final checkpoint, no non-finite step, the switch record exact, the on arm not stopped by its kill criterion. S2 met and S1 not: the token carries the asked change and the main route does not use it within 3,000 updates; the verdict names whether S1's reading rose from the second window to the third by more than its standard error. S2 not met: the path did not put the asked change into the token. NO VERDICT: a record, a window report or a read-out missing.
rows.pass_line_basis: S2 is read-out 2's rule, the rule that selected this repair. Its reach is measured (row motor_encoder_asked_change_reach_455800): an output of the path of 0.01 token units already gives a token R^2 of 0.77 to 0.82, and the output's growth bound of 0.0027 token units per update allows that after 4 updates. S2 therefore says that the path wrote the asked change into the token at all, not how strongly; gradient noise alone could meet it. The judgement of use is S1. S1's noise: on 350 transitions (7 bodies x 50 audited model steps of one hold phase in 1,000 updates) production's reading for proprioception at the hold's first model step was -0.000022 with a standard error of 0.000093, and between -0.000127 and 0.000129 with standard errors of 0.000096 to 0.000137 at the four later phases (D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/own_command_readouts/2026-10-02/decision.json, checkpoint 455,800). The difference of two arms then has a standard error near 0.00013, so the smallest rise the line can declare is 3.14 x 0.00013 = 0.0004 of the reading's 0-to-1 scale; 3.14 is the read-outs' own line. S1 is an admission line (not blind), not the goal: H71's 0.08 is 200 times it. Reachability in time: the path's output can grow by at most 0.0027 token units per update, so 0.1 token units need at least 37 updates and 1 token unit at least 365; a direct command input into the prediction heads (the body copy trial of Oct 1) brought proprioception's next-model-step error to 0.950 of the 'nothing changes' error over its updates 501 to 1,000 against 1.016 without it (planner_repair_2026-09-30.md section 11); the judged window starts after 2,000 updates, twice that. How fast the transformer comes to use the token's new content is not measured before this trial: a miss on S1 with S2 met is reported with its trend over the three windows, and a reading still rising calls for more updates on the on arm before another route is tried. C's lines and their false-stop measurement are in row motor_asked_change_trial_arm_on.

cost.where: training pause, last job of the file; safe to repeat
cost.basis: Pure arithmetic on JSON files of a few MB: 2 arms x 3 windows x 4 senses x 2 phases x 2 swaps readings, 2,000 seeded resamplings each over at most 70 cells.

rows.on_pass: The verdict and its readings go into this row and the record (docs/gain_of_function_v4/agents/motor_encoder_asked_change_2026-10-03.md, section 6). Switching the path on in production is then a decision for the operator under the deploy plan, with production's own kill lines; the arms' checkpoints are deleted (cleanup --confirm) only after the record holds the verdict.
rows.on_fail: S2 met and S1 not, the reading still rising: the on arm is resumed from its final checkpoint for more updates before any other route is tried. S2 met and S1 not, not rising: the token carries the asked change and the transformer does not use it; the next route named by the read-outs' rule is a loss on the main route that is lower when the own command's error is below the size-matched command's, with its margin set from this trial's measured reading and noise. S2 not met: the path's gauges say where it stopped (output size near 0: no lesson moved it). C not met or the arm stopped: the sense that rose and the path's output size at that point are read from the kept checkpoint.

diagram.operation: apply the declared lines S2, S1 and C to the two arms; no training, no model
diagram.measurement: own-command reading on the size-matched swap (0 to 1) and the token's held-out R^2
diagram.decision: PASS: switching the path on in production is the operator's decision; FAIL names the next route

rows.title: Swap test phases: CPU identity and unit checks
rows.question: With the swap test's second phase (the hold's first model step), its size-matched and shifted-own arms and the side heads' size-matched control added, does a small learner built from H84's learner flags train bit for bit as production's code does, and does each new reading compute what its definition says?
rows.why: The branch may go live at the next resume only if it changes no loss, gradient, weight, executed command or random stream; the new readings are used to judge command use only if their arithmetic and their phase selection are right.
inputs: Branch fix/swap_test_phases-2026-10-02 (working folder C:/Users/bhart/Documents/UEMA_wt/swap_phases/Source/Python) and production commit 06223f2df (lem, mimo_bridge and tokenizer extracted with git archive).

The fixture Source/Python/mimo_bridge/tests/swap_test_fixture.py: a learner built by train_mimo.build_learner from H84's learner flags (efference heads, contact head, liveness repair on, persistent memory, vestibular, normalized ranking, controllability, learning progress, causal chain, imagination, planner every 10 model steps) at width 32, 3 bodies, CPU.

Synthetic frames through the real frame packing and tokenizer: 26 handles that move a fifth of the way toward their commanded position each model step plus seeded noise, eyes that move six tenths of the way toward the gaze sent, seeded random skin contacts, vision patches, audio and vestibular readings. No MuJoCo world, no checkpoint.
steps: Lockstep (docs/gain_of_function_v4/swap_test_phases/lockstep_vs_production.py): the fixture runs 260 model steps in a child process under production's code, under the branch's code, and under the branch's code with the added readings off (prediction_audit.ADDED_READINGS = False), with the trainer's latch rule, in two launch settings: --motor-hold 5 with --intention-every 10 (H84's) and --motor-hold 3 with --intention-every 7.

Every model step each child records the loss and the gradient norm (exact float hex), hashes of the command (26 handles x 9 numbers) and the gaze sent, of the loss breakdown, of the wellness values and of the torch, numpy and noise random streams; every 10 model steps one hash over every parameter, buffer and Adam state tensor. The rows are compared model step by model step.

Unit tests (pytest, Source/Python/mimo_bridge/tests/test_swap_test_phases.py and the existing tests of the changed files): each reading's arithmetic, the phase selection against the trainer's latch rule under --motor-hold 5 and 3 and others, the size-matched command against contact_head.shuffled_order, the shifted-own noise against the measured per-column spread, the episode companion carrying the new state, and the same lockstep in-process with the readings on against off while the liveness repair revives units.

Planted defects, each in a copy of the source tree: the phase off by one model step, the absolute command in place of the size-matched one, the noise not added, the liveness watching left on for the added passes. The tests run on each copy.
measures: Per model step and launch setting: equal or not in every recorded field (counts of model steps that differ, 0 to 260).
Pass or fail of each unit test, and which tests fail on each planted defect.
rows.pass_line: Every model step equal in every recorded field and every state hash equal, in both launch settings, production against branch and branch with the added readings off against on; every unit test passes; each planted defect makes at least one test fail.
rows.pass_line_basis: Bit-for-bit identity is the condition for a measurement change that must not move training (the caused-change branch's world tests use the same condition, docs/gain_of_function_v4/agents/caused_change_consequence_2026-10-02.md). 260 model steps cover 13 audited model steps of each phase, the shifted-own arm's start after 200 model steps of command stream, and the liveness repair's revivals (its watching window is 800 rows, which the three prediction-head layers fill within this run).

rows.on_fail: No merge; the first differing model step and field, or the failing test, name the defect to repair.

rows.title: Controllability shadow gate: CPU unit and identity checks
rows.question: With a second, recorded-only evidence gate fed by the size-matched control added to the controllability tracker, does a small learner built from H84's learner flags still train bit for bit as production's code does, does the shadow gate compute what its definition says, and does the controllability weight in the goal ranking still read only the gate that was there before?
rows.why: The operator decided on Oct 3 that the restart segment runs this branch and that both gates are read on the same graded commands for one segment before the gate is switched to the size-matched control. That plan holds only if the shadow gate changes no loss, weight, executed command or random stream, if its readings and its open counts are computed as defined, and if a state saved by production's code loads on this code.
inputs: Branch fix/swap_test_phases-2026-10-02 with the shadow gate (working folder C:/Users/bhart/Documents/UEMA_wt/swap_phases/Source/Python) and production commit 1d76c144d, the production branch's newest commit at 1:04 AM PDT Oct 3 (lem, mimo_bridge and tokenizer extracted with git archive; no file under Source/Python differs between it and e022cae26, the newest commit when this row was written).

Hand-made graded commands for the tracker (lem/model/wellness_channels.py ControllabilityTracker): 2 bodies, 4 handles, a hold of 2 model steps; per body the achieved turn of one handle in degrees, the body head's expected turn, the expected turn formed from another body's absolute command and the expected turn formed from another body's size-matched command, so every agreement (direction cosine x smaller size / larger size) is a number known beforehand.

The fixture Source/Python/mimo_bridge/tests/swap_test_fixture.py: a learner built by train_mimo.build_learner from H84's learner flags (efference heads, contact head, liveness repair on, persistent memory, vestibular, normalized ranking, controllability, learning progress, causal chain, imagination, planner every 10 model steps) at width 32, 3 bodies, CPU, on synthetic frames through the real frame packing and tokenizer. No MuJoCo world, no checkpoint of H84.
steps: Unit tests (pytest, Source/Python/mimo_bridge/tests/test_controllability_shadow_gate.py). The shadow reading: per graded command, the mean over the measured bodies of (agreement with the body's own expectation - agreement with the size-matched expectation), checked against numbers computed by hand, beside the unchanged reading of the gate in force. Fed the same control as the gate in force over 150 graded commands that open, close and reopen it, the shadow gate's 32 readings and its open or shut state must equal the gate's after every command. The per-window counts of graded commands and of commands with each gate open, checked against a count kept by the test. The state's save and load: through a file, under the gate's own load rule (readings kept, the gate shut and judged again by the opening line), and from a state without the shadow gate's keys. The controllability weight (LemLite._rank_weights_now) and the ranking (wellness_channels.rank_values) under each of the 4 pairings of the two gates' states. A fixture run of 45 model steps with the shadow gate held open against one with it held shut: every model step's row, the state hash and the controllability weight of every planning event must be equal, and with the shadow gate's state joined to the gate in force (planted) the weights must differ. The stillness floors are 0 in these fixture runs: measured Oct 3 over 60 model steps of the fixture, the fresh body head's expected effect is 0.9 to 3.0 measured hold spreads per body, under the floor of 6.67 measured on H84's bodies, so with the floors as they stand no body is measured and neither gate takes a reading; at 0 both gates take a reading at each of the 11 graded commands.

Planted defects (docs/gain_of_function_v4/swap_test_phases/planted_defects.py), each one text substitution in a copy of the source tree, the tests run on each copy: the shadow gate fed the absolute control; the shadow gate's state joined to the answer of the gate in force; the ranking weight reading the shadow gate; the shadow gate's update writing the state of the gate in force; the open count of the gate in force not incremented; the open count of the shadow gate not incremented.

Lockstep (docs/gain_of_function_v4/swap_test_phases/lockstep_vs_production.py --production 1d76c144d): the fixture runs 260 model steps in a child process under production's code and under the branch's code, in three launch settings: --motor-hold 5 with --intention-every 10 (H84's); --motor-hold 3 with --intention-every 7; and H84's again with both stillness floors set to 0 in both codes, so that the gate in force takes a reading at every graded command under both codes and the shadow gate under the branch's. Every model step's loss and gradient norm (exact float hex) and hashes of the command, the gaze sent, the loss breakdown, the wellness values and the torch, numpy and noise random streams are compared, and every 10 model steps one hash over every parameter, buffer and Adam state tensor. In the third setting a further run of the branch plants the defect the shadow gate must not have (the shadow gate held open and its state joined to the answer of the gate in force); that run must differ from the branch.

Resume from a state saved by production's code (docs/gain_of_function_v4/swap_test_phases/resume_from_production_state.py --production 1d76c144d): under production's code the fixture runs 190 model steps and saves its checkpoint (weights, Adam state, runtime_state.pt with the wellness channels' state) and its learner continuation state (continuation_state.capture_learner). Production's code and the branch's code each load both in a new process and run 230 more model steps on the same synthetic bodies; the rows are compared model step by model step. On the branch's side the loaded tracker is read before the first model step: the readings of the gate in force equal the saved ones, the shadow gate holds no reading and is shut, and LemLite._command_spread is empty. Both stillness floors are 0 in all three processes, for the reason given in the first step, so the saved state carries the gate's readings.

The same resume from the state the restart candidate meets (added Oct 3, 1:45 AM PDT on the coordinator's note, before this step ran): a checkpoint written by production's code after --vestibular-encoder-repair rescale_restart switched, in a run with --agency-prior 0 and --contact-control-wellness 2. Production's code, the launch line as it stands, with the vestibular encoder's last layer multiplied by 2 to the power 15 before the first model step (a bias spread above the switch line of 1,000, as on H84), runs 60 model steps and saves. Production's code with the three flags loads that state (the load divides the layer by a power of two, restarts that encoder's Adam state and writes the switch into the receipt), runs 130 model steps and saves: a runtime state without the shadow gate's keys, a learner state without LemLite._command_spread, a receipt carrying the switch. Production's code and the branch's code, each with the three flags, load that second state and run 230 more model steps; the rows are compared model step by model step, and each side's receipt and vestibular encoder are read right after the load.

The stats record's size against the readers that take the newest record from the file's end (added Oct 3, 2:02 AM PDT, before this step ran at 2:03 AM). Measured on H84's last 59 records (4 run folders): 182,761 to 234,927 bytes each; the swap test's added readings add 33,344 bytes and the shadow gate's keys 2,871, which puts 7 of the 59 past the 256,000 bytes the Development page's reader took from the file's end and 3 past the 262,144 bytes of the phase reader. Both readers now grow their tail until a complete record is found. Unit tests (pytest, Source/Python/mimo_bridge/tests/test_stats_record_tail_readers.py, temporary files): records of 200,000, 256,500, 271,142 and 900,000 bytes are each found; a record still being written does not replace the last complete one; with each reader held to its first tail size (the planted defect) the 271,142-byte record is not found.
measures: Pass or fail of each unit test, and which tests fail on each planted defect.
Lockstep and resume: per model step and launch setting, equal or not in every recorded field (count of model steps that differ, 0 to 260 and 0 to 230) and equal or not for each state hash.
Resume: the count of readings each gate holds at the save and at the end of the run (0 to 32).

rows.question: With --motor-asked-change on in a relaunch of production that changes no other launch setting: does the switch leave the motor token unchanged on its probe rows, does no stop line cross from the switch through the first full report at or past 10,000 model steps after it, does the main route's prediction of proprioception at the hold's first model step come to depend on the body's own command (line S1), and does the motor token then carry the asked change (line S2)?
rows.why: The operator's open choice of Oct 3 between two ways to decide the asked-change path: the two-arm trial in a training pause (rows motor_asked_change_trial_gate to motor_asked_change_trial_verdict), and this way: the path switched on in production itself under stop lines and judged against production's own readings from before the switch, the way the operator chose for the vestibular repair (row vestibular_repair_restart_segment). A pass keeps the path on and names the next rung: the planner's candidates must then differ in predicted outcome (its chosen command tied with another candidate at 100 of 100 planning events in the reports of model steps 457,900 to 458,425). A stop reverts production to the checkpoint before the switch. S1 not met through 10,000 model steps with no stop: the token carries the asked change and the transformer does not use it, and a direct command input into the prediction heads is the next route (docs/gain_of_function_v4/agents/motor_encoder_asked_change_2026-10-03.md, section 3). What this way cannot show and the trial can: there is no control arm from the same checkpoint, so a change after the switch cannot be told from what production would have done anyway from that checkpoint; and a stop on the other senses or the step rate cannot be put down to the path when another launch setting changes at the same relaunch. SEQUENCE (coordinator, Oct 3 noon): the vestibular repair's watch ended at model step 465,800 with no stop, so the switch no longer waits for it; --self-percept-release on is switched on first, at the relaunch after the test window that opened at model step 470,425 (row self_percept_release_segment); this switch takes a later relaunch of its own, and controllability's gate switch, still to be built, another one (row controllability_two_gate_reading: both gates stood open on 98.9 of every 100 of 1,579 graded commands).
inputs: A production checkpoint with all eight worlds, written by a requested stop (snapshot_and_stop) under a supervisor pause, or by the stop of a scheduled test window, at least 20 full reports after the relaunch that switched --self-percept-release on (model step 470,625). Training was turned off at model step 472,275 on Oct 3, 2026 at 2:25 PM PDT on the operator's instruction, with 15 of those reports written; a resume's first record is partial, so the 20th is the report at model step 472,800 when the resumed run is not stopped before it. Test before the stop: docs/gain_of_function_v4/motor_asked_change_segment.py before --run <the supervisor's active run> returns exit code 0. The switch at the resume from checkpoint 472,275 itself is the other place for it, with its costs in the record's section 5.6; that choice waits on the coordinator.

Production's recorded command with one change: --motor-asked-change on. Code: branch restart/candidate-motor-2026-10-03 fast-forwarded into production (docs/gain_of_function_v4/restart_candidate/RESTART_CANDIDATE_MOTOR_2026-10-03.md, sections 3 and 9; CPU checks: row restart_candidate_motor_cpu_checks).

The up to 100 full stats reports (100 model steps each) before the switch, read through the parent chain of run folders: per report each sense's next-model-step error ratio, the model steps per second, and the hold-first swap test's per-body transitions and mean prediction errors for proprioception (block prediction_audit_hold_first, the own command and the size-matched command).

After the switch, per stats report: the motor_asked_change block (the path's output size, the size of its output layer's weights, how evenly the 26 handles share the output, its features' sizes, its hidden layer's live share on the commanded handles), liveness.layers, next_frame_norm.ratio, model_steps_per_s, nan_steps and prediction_audit_hold_first; and the one motor_asked_change_switch record.

The launch settings (args.json) of the switched run and of each run behind the up to 100 reports before the switch, each against the run it continues: the watch prints which settings each relaunch changed.

For line S2: a checkpoint written after the switch and the checkpoint the switch resumed (read only: the motor encoder's tensors, the liveness repair's all-element path for the motor pool and the asked-change path), the switched run's args.json, and the 2,000 recorded motor encoder inputs of checkpoint 455,800 (D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/own_command_readouts/2026-10-02/transitions.npz).
steps: Before the stop: C:/Users/bhart/Documents/UEMA_wt/candidate_motor/docs/gain_of_function_v4/motor_asked_change_segment.py before --run <the supervisor's active run> (run from the candidate's worktree: the tool is not in the production checkout before the fast-forward) prints every relaunch inside the 100 newest full reports that changed a launch setting and returns exit code 0 when none lies inside the newest 20; production's newest commit is merged into the candidate's branch after every commit production makes (git merge --ff-only refuses otherwise); when that merge changes a file under Source/Python the trial's gate, the lockstep and the resume tool run again on the merged code, and when it changes the hourly watcher's file, vestibular_repair_watch.py or a watch program, the watch program's test file and the test files that load the hourly watcher run again (the record's section 9).

With the supervisor paused and the trainer stopped by snapshot_and_stop, production is fast-forwarded to branch restart/candidate-motor-2026-10-03 and relaunched with docs/gain_of_function_v4/coordinator/relaunch_h84_seg41_2026-09-29.py --set motor-asked-change on and no other --set. The checkpoint the relaunch resumes is kept on C: with its episode companion until the watch has ended, since a revert resumes it: right after the relaunch its folder is named in the keep list of Saved/mimo_bridge/archive_keep.json (an entry with path, reason and added). Without that entry the checkpoint archiver moves it to D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_recordings/H84_checkpoint_archive once the supervisor's recorded command resumes a later checkpoint and 3 newer complete checkpoints exist, and the relaunch script, which reads <run>/checkpoints alone, refuses the revert or resumes an older checkpoint still in that folder.

At the load the trainer builds the path beside the motor encoder: per handle 10 numbers computed from the encoder's own input row (the asked position change in units of 12 cm, the asked turn in units of 20 degrees, strength, radius, two flags), a shared network 10 -> 64 -> 16, and an output layer 676 -> 192 that starts at zero. It computes the motor token on 64 probe rows with the path and without it in float32 and under the run's bf16 autocast, refuses the load when they differ, and writes one motor_asked_change_switch record into the stats stream. load_report.json names motor_asked_change as the one component that starts fresh.

From the next model step the path's output, multiplied by the standard deviation of the motor encoder's output over its 192 numbers and by 1/26, is added to that output before the registry's LayerNorm. The path's weights get gradients from the delayed next-model-step lesson, its re-study in replay and the hold loss; on every imagined row (the imagination chain, the planner's descent, the plan chain, the causal record) they are detached. A model step's planning event runs after that model step's optimizer update, so the planner's descent meets an output layer that has moved by one learning rate from the first model step on.

The hourly watcher's 5-minute check (docs/gain_of_function_v4/motor_asked_change_watch.py, loaded by docs/h84_launch_2026-09-18/hourly_watch.py) judges stop lines M1 to M6 on every record from the switch through the first full report at or past N + 10,000 model steps and writes snapshot_and_stop itself on a crossing. Its hourly sweep prints the stop lines' states, lines S1 and S2, the launch settings around the switch and the free readings.
The coordinator reads the first three full reports against the readings listed in the record's section 9.

After the first checkpoint written 100 model steps or more past the switch: the read-out job, beside training on the CPU (docs/gain_of_function_v4/motor_asked_change_segment.py readout --run <the switched run> --checkpoint <that checkpoint> --before <the checkpoint the switch resumed> --publish).

After the full report at model step N + 3,000 and again after the watch's end (N = the switch's model step): docs/gain_of_function_v4/motor_asked_change_segment.py verdict --run <the newest run>; its sentences are written into this row.
measures: The switch record: the largest absolute change of the motor token on 64 probe rows with the path against without it, in float32 and under autocast (0.0 = the same number), and the output layer's largest absolute weight (0.0 = zero).

The path's output (motor_asked_change.output_rms), in token units: the root mean square over the newest lesson rows of the 192 numbers the path adds. 0 = the path adds nothing, 1 = as large as the motor encoder's own standardised output. Beside it its growth line: 0.0027 token units x the optimizer updates since the switch (H84 makes 1.5 optimizer updates per model step: 1 from the live lessons and 1 every second model step from replay; 0.41 token units per report of 100 model steps).

The path's hidden layer's live share: the share of its 64 units whose input rose above -3 on the sampled rows; 0 = none, 1 = all. Two readings per report: the whole-model monitor's (every handle of every row the layer saw on the model steps the monitor samples, every 7th on H84) and the path's own (the commanded handles of at most 64 newest lesson rows); the line reads the lower one.

Each other sense's next-model-step error ratio (prediction error over the error of predicting no change: 0 = exact, 1 = no better than predicting no change), as a multiple of its level before the switch (the larger of its median over the 20 and over the up to 100 full reports before it).
Model steps per second: each 20-report window's median as a share of the window before it.

Line S1's reading: 1 - (summed prediction error of proprioception's next token with the body's own command) / (summed error with another body's command applied as a change from this body's pose), over the hold-first transitions of a window's full reports and the bodies without body 2. 0 = the own command predicts no better, 1 = exact where the other is not. Goal ladder: the last lineage measured to depend on its command read 0.08 (H71, on the absolute swap); on the size-matched swap the goal line is unmeasured.

Line S2's reading: the held-out R^2 of a ridge read-out of the asked position change and the asked turn from the motor token (0 = nothing beyond the training mean, 1 = exact), beside its permuted control's 97.5th percentile.

Free readings, never judged: the hold loss's ratio (1 = the command adds nothing to the pose prediction over the hold; the hinge's line is 0.96), the contact gates' open shares, both controllability gates' open counts on the same graded commands, the planner's tied share (1 = its chosen command tied with another candidate at every planning event), and which launch settings changed at the switch's relaunch and at each relaunch inside the 100 reports before it.
rows.pass_line: Declared Oct 3, 2026 4:44 AM PDT, before any switch. Redeclared Oct 3, 2026 1:58 PM PDT, again before any switch, after planted cases and a second, independent review: the hidden layer's reading and count (M3), the trainer's log as a second source of M2, a non-finite output (M6), vestibular's alert multiple, the watch's end, and which taken stops stand. STOP LINES, each writing snapshot_and_stop, judged on every record from the switch through the first full report at or past N + 10,000 model steps (N = the switch's model step): M1 the switch record as declared (it says exact; 0.0 and bit-identical tokens in float32 and, on the graphics card, under autocast; the output layer zero; 64 probe rows; this build's path version). M2 no non-finite update: no stats record whose nan_steps is above 0, and no line of the trainer's log that reports a skipped optimizer update, in any run from the switch on. M3 the path's hidden layer not under 0.9 live share in 2 full reports with a reading running, the reading being the lower of the whole-model monitor's and the path's own on the commanded handles. M4 no sense among vision, tactile, audio and proprioception above its median over the 20 reports before the switch x W1 (4.01, 2.09, 2.75, 2.17) in report 2 and in report 3; and in every window of 20 full reports from report 2, and in the 20 full reports that end the watch, no such sense's median above its level before the switch x 1.72 (tactile, audio, proprioception) or x 3.95 (vision); above x 1.43 and x 3.29 it is an alert, printed and recorded, never a stop; vestibular's ratio above 3.67 times its level is an alert only. M5 the median model steps per second of such a window not under 0.9 of the window before it (the first window: of the 20 reports before the switch) in two windows running. M6 the path's output a finite number and not above 0.0027 token units x the optimizer updates since the switch; at or above 1 token unit it is an alert, never a stop. PASS LINES: S1 over the full reports of model steps N + 2,001 to N + 3,000: the reading is above 3.14 times its standard error and exceeds the reference (the same reading over the up to 100 full reports before the switch above model step 457,825, the path absent) by more than 3.14 times the standard error of the difference; read again over N + 9,001 to N + 10,000. S2: on a checkpoint after the switch the token's held-out R^2 for the asked position change or the asked turn is above 0.04 and above its permuted control, and on the checkpoint before the switch it is not. PASS: no stop through the watch's end and S1 met in one of its two windows. S1 met in neither window, with no stop: the path stays on (a build without it refuses the checkpoint), the result reads 'the token carries the asked change and the main route does not use it within 10,000 model steps', and the next route gets its own row.
rows.pass_line_basis: FALSE STOPS, measured with the watch program's own judge at every switch position of the lineage's 1,198 full reports (model steps 344,600 to 470,500, read Oct 3, 2026 1:18 PM PDT; docs/gain_of_function_v4/restart_candidate/motor/false_stops_result.json on the candidate's branch) with nothing switched: 0 stops and 0 alerts in 409 positions since model step 415,200 (4 watches whose watched reports do not overlap, 3 that share no report before or after), reports written after the vestibular watch's multiples were drawn on Sep 26; 0 stops and 1 alert in 702 positions since 382,800; 5 stops (the step rate at 4 positions, the early line at 1) and 1 alert in 1,079 positions since Sep 23. So the vestibular watch's multiples are kept. The reports since model step 415,000 alone would give lower multiples (a largest rise of 1.20 for vision and 1.32 for the other three, against 3.29 and 1.43); drawn from them and judged on the positions before 415,000 they stop 31 of every 100 watches, so they are not used. BY RELAUNCH, since 415,200: positions with 1 to 9 full reports between the relaunch before them and themselves stop 0 of 147, with 10 to 19 0 of 122, with 20 or more 0 of 140; positions that a relaunch follows directly, as it does a real switch, stop 0 of 20, and their first window's step rate read 89 to 118 of every 100 parts of the 20 reports before, 1 of 20 under the line of 90 (one window under the line is not a stop). WHAT THE LINES STOP: audio at 3, 4 or 5 times its level from reports 2 to 62 stops within 2 windows at 409 of 409 positions, and from report 82, inside the 20 reports that end the watch, at 387, 408 and 409 of 409; all four senses creeping at the vestibular plan's third-review rates stop within 2 windows at 365 of 409 and at every position by window 3. WHAT PASSES: a rise under 1.72 times the level (3.95 for vision) stops nothing; vision at 3 times its level from report 22 stops at 0 of 409 positions and alerts within 2 windows at 37; the step rate halving once stops at 42 of 409. M2: 0 of the lineage's 4,439 stats records (full and partial, 129 run folders) hold a non-finite live loss, and 0 lines of its 104 trainer logs (48 MB) report a skipped optimizer update (the stats count non-finite live losses only; a non-finite gradient norm or replay loss skips the optimizer update and is written in the log alone). M3 and M6 have no record with nothing switched (the lineage's reports carry no path). M3 at the switch, measured on the 2,000 recorded rows of checkpoint 455,800 in 32 blocks of at most 64 rows for three seeds of the path's network: the path's own reading is 1.0 in every block, and the lowest of the 64 units' largest inputs is 0.74 against the line of -3; how the share moves under training is unmeasured before this segment. M6's line is the most one optimizer update can add on one row (learning rate 3e-4 x a summed input size of 239 / 26); on the same rows a path whose every weight has moved one learning rate per optimizer update in the direction that makes the output largest reads 59 to 62 of every 100 parts of the line and cannot read above 91 (growth_line_result.json), and on the small CPU learner the output read 3.3 of every 100 parts of the line after 230 model steps with the path on. VESTIBULAR, alert only: its token was dead until model step 455,800, so its record is the 145 full reports from 455,900 to 470,500; in them a 20-report median reached 3.06 times the level before it with nothing switched, and the alert sits at that rise x 1.2 = 3.67; 145 reports are at most 1 watch, so its false-alert chance is unmeasured and no stop line is put on it. S1: 3.14 is the trial's line (a one-sided chance of 0.00084 per window under a normal null, 2 windows). Its reference as a switch at the newest full report would hold it, read Oct 3, 2026 2:19 PM PDT: 0.000072 with a standard error of 0.000045 on 3,500 transitions in the 100 newest full reports (model steps 462,000 to 472,100); at the switch the watch program builds it from the up to 100 full reports before it. Over every full report above model step 457,825 (139 reports) the same reading is 0.000059 with a standard error of 0.000033. With nothing switched, 130 runs of 10 consecutive reports among all of them read -0.000341 to 0.000672, and 0 of them cleared 3.14 of its own standard errors, the line's first condition. Smallest rise the line can declare: 3.14 x sqrt(the reference's standard error^2 + the judged window's^2) = 0.00031 on the reports a switch now would hold (0.00027 with every such report in the reference, the number this row carried until Oct 3, 2026 2:22 PM PDT), against 0.0004 for the trial's two arms of 350 transitions each. Reachability in time: the path's output can grow by at most 0.0041 token units per model step (0.0027 per optimizer update x 1.5), so 0.1 token units need at least 25 model steps and 1 token unit at least 242; how fast the transformer comes to use the token's new content is unmeasured before this segment, so S1 is read again over N + 9,001 to N + 10,000 and every window of 1,000 model steps is printed. S2 is reachable by an output of 0.01 token units (row motor_encoder_asked_change_reach_455800), which the growth bound allows after 3 model steps: it says only that the path's output is not zero. WHAT THE LINES NEED FROM THE REPORTS BEFORE THE SWITCH when --self-percept-release was switched on earlier: the 20 full reports before the switch for the early line and the step rate's first window, and up to 100 for the level and for S1's reference, read through the parent chain whatever relaunch lies inside them. By the code that flag reaches none of the senses' ratios or S1's cells (the self-state module reads the tokens with no gradient back, its weights are a clipping group of their own, and with --self-state learn and --self-choice off no command, goal, wellness channel or main-route prediction reads its output); it can change the step rate, and a non-finite update in its group skips the whole optimizer update. With 1,000 model steps between the two relaunches 10 or 11 of the 20 reports predate the flag; with 2,000, none or 1 does (a relaunch off the hundreds leaves its first record partial); with 20 full reports after the relaunch none does, which is what this row asks for: the self-percept relaunch was at model step 470,625 (Oct 3, 2026 1:17 PM PDT, run H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41g_1317), its 20th full report would have been the one at model step 472,700. Training was turned off at model step 472,275 (Oct 3, 2026 2:25 PM PDT, the operator's instruction) with 15 full reports after that relaunch; a resume's first record is partial, so the 20th is the report at model step 472,800 when the resumed run is not stopped before it. For a switch at the resume from checkpoint 472,275 itself, 5 of the 20 reports before the switch predate the flag, and the step rate's first window is read against a median of 0.44 model steps per second over those 20 (reports written while CPU checks ran beside training; the 3 full reports before the stop of 12:11 PM PDT read 0.46 to 0.49). The path changes one input of the self-state module (the motor token) once its output layer has moved, so the self-percept row's own readings at 10,000 model steps are attributable to the release alone only when this switch comes after them.

rows.on_pass: The path stays on in production's command through every relaunch (a build without it refuses the checkpoint). The row is closed with S1's reading as a share of the goal reference 0.08, S2, and the free readings; the planner's tied share and the candidates' spread against the tie band are read next, since the planner's candidates can only differ once the predictions depend on the command.
rows.on_fail: A stop: the watcher has paused the supervisor and written snapshot_and_stop. The sweep's line on the launch settings says whether the switch's relaunch changed anything besides the flag; when it did and the stop is on the other senses or the step rate, the stop cannot be put down to the path alone. The self-percept release's own watch (docs/gain_of_function_v4/coordinator/self_percept_watch_loop.py) can stop the same run: its stop_reason.json names its own lines. Then the revert: resume the checkpoint the switch resumed (kept on C: by its entry in Saved/mimo_bridge/archive_keep.json), with --motor-asked-change off, reattach the supervisor and lift the pause (docs/gain_of_function_v4/coordinator/relaunch_h84_seg41_2026-09-29.py --parent <the run before the switch> --set motor-asked-change off; with --parent that script ends the hourly watcher of the folder --parent names and not the stopped run's, which is ended by hand first); the model steps trained since the switch are lost. S1 met in neither window with no stop: no revert; the result and the readings are written here and the operator is asked before the next route is built.
