rows.title: Self-percept release switched on in production
rows.question: With --self-percept-release on at a relaunch of production, are the bodies whose stored self-percepts sit at the limit released at the load, and does every live model step then stay under the limit of 8: fewer than 2 live model steps over it in any 1,000, and at most 25 perceive calls over it per 100 model steps?
rows.why: The self-state module keeps, per body, its last 128 self-percepts (each 128 numbers; size = the largest absolute value among them; healthy on H84 1.4 to 2.0; above 8 a percept is rescaled to size 8). From about 11:55 AM PDT Oct 3 the live percept passed the limit on 8, 26 and 42 of 100 live model steps in the reports ending at model steps 470,200, 470,300 and 470,400, after 0 in the run's 117 reports before. On Sep 25 the same state held through every resume, because the stored percepts are restored with the episode (docs/gain_of_function_v4/agents/self_percept_runaway_2026-09-26.md). Its cause, measured there: the module's recall returns a stored percept pointing the other way and 2 to 4.5 times larger; when one stored percept takes the whole attention, each new percept is that percept's mirror image and the limit holds the loop in place. The repair was built, reviewed and replayed on H84's stuck checkpoints on Sep 26 and merged with its switch off; that record names this deploy as its next executable test and leaves it to the coordinator. The decision that depends on this row: whether the switch stays on in production's command. What it cannot change: H84 runs --self-state learn and --self-choice off, so no command, goal, wellness channel or prediction of the main route reads the percept (lem_model.py reads it into the transformer only in mode perceive); the module's own lessons and gauges do.
inputs: Production's recorded command with one change: --self-percept-release on. No code change: production's tip already holds the switch (default off).
The newest complete checkpoint of the supervisor's active run at the stop, with all eight worlds and the episode companion that holds each body's 128 stored self-percepts and the saved step inputs.

Per report the trainer writes in the stats block self_state, counted over every model step since the report before: window_steps, window_live_over_limit, window_bounded_calls, window_releases, window_body_releases, window_restored_bodies, window_belief_size_max, window_attention_peak_max, window_attention_capped_steps, window_cleared_rehearsal_windows, window_cleared_events.
steps: Stop: the coordinator's hold in supervisor_control.json, snapshot_and_stop, then docs/gain_of_function_v4/coordinator/relaunch_h84_seg41_2026-09-29.py with --set self-percept-release on. The new run's args.json must read self_percept_release = on; the supervisor's later relaunches reuse that recorded command.

The cap: in every perceive call, a body whose largest attention weight over its stored percepts is above 0.05 has its softmax temperature raised until that weight is 0.05 (the ranking and the gradient are kept); with under 20 stored percepts the recall is the plain average.

The restore: before the first live perceive call after the load, a body with a stored percept at the limit has all 128 stored percepts set to zero, and its rows zeroed in the saved step inputs and in every rehearsal window that holds one at the limit.
The release: after any live call in which a body's size before the rescale is over 8, the same zeroing for that body.

The watch: docs/gain_of_function_v4/coordinator/self_percept_watch_loop.py runs mimo_bridge.tools.self_percept_watch on the supervisor's active run every 5 minutes and, on verdict stop, pauses the supervisor and writes stop_reason.json and snapshot_and_stop, once per run.
The coordinator reads the readings at 1,000 and at 10,000 model steps after the relaunch into this row.
measures: Live model steps over the limit of 8 within any 1,000 model steps since the relaunch (0 = never; with the switch off the run read 76 in its last 300).
Perceive calls over the limit per 100 model steps in a report (about 425 calls are made per 100 model steps: the live one, the recomputed ones and the rehearsal).
Bodies released before the first model step (0 to 8).

Recovery: the median over the last 10 reports of each report's largest live percept size (healthy top 2.0; 2.52 measured with the Sep 25 weights frozen; above 4.3 calls for attribution work; limit 8).
Cap use: the share of model steps on which the 5 in 100 cap spread a body's recall (0 = never needed).
rows.pass_line: Declared Oct 3, 2026 12:07 PM PDT, before the relaunch; the lines are the record's. STOP LINES, each writing snapshot_and_stop: (1) 2 or more live model steps over the limit within any 1,000 model steps since the relaunch; (2) more than 25 perceive calls over the limit in a report of 100 model steps. PASS: 1,000 model steps since the relaunch with neither line crossed (the tool's verdict pass). READINGS at 1,000 and 10,000 model steps, never a stop: the bodies released at the load; the recovery median; the cap's share of model steps. Also read in the first 3 full reports: no non-finite update, and model steps per second at least 0.9 of the mean over the 3 full reports before the stop.
rows.pass_line_basis: The record's replays with the switch on, 1,024 model steps from each of H84's four stuck checkpoints and the 415,075 weights on two other memories: 0 model steps over the limit, largest percept 2.1 to 5.7, no release after the restore. The line can fail: the review's planted body, stuck again every 144 model steps, gives 7 live model steps over the limit in 1,100 and crosses line 1 while the last model step of each of its reports stays under 8. One live model step over the limit is allowed for a single spike of the kind the lineage showed before Sep 25. Not covered by those replays: today's weights (470,000 against 415,075); the tool's own tests (mimo_bridge/tests/test_grounded_self_dynamics.py, 23 tests on Sep 26) cover the cap, the restore, the release and the planted body. The loop's glue was run once on the live run with the switch off and judging forced: verdict stop, 76 live model steps over the limit, nothing written.

cost.where: production training, from the relaunch on
cost.basis: One stop for the relaunch (a save, a load and the first report); the watch itself reads stats files only.

rows.on_pass: The switch stays on in production's command through every relaunch. The readings at 10,000 model steps are written here and the row is closed.
rows.on_fail: A stop line: the loop has paused the supervisor and written snapshot_and_stop. The coordinator resumes the stopped checkpoint with --self-percept-release off (the state before this row), reattaches the supervisor, and reads the per-step counts and the saved self history at the stop before any further attempt.

The trainer's log holds no self-percept warning.

rows.title: Caused change: reading on production's stats
rows.question: With production relaunched in measure mode (the flags' count still decides every goal), what does each sense's caused change read, how often do each sense's evidence gate and its null gate stand open, and what is the ranking floor of the caused-change consequence wellness channel?
rows.why: The channel may be switched to caused mode only after its floor constant is set by a commit that cites the floor file and each sense's null gate has passed its 5-in-100 line; the operator then chooses the channel's weight. Read from production's own stats, this needs no separate trainer and no stopped training of its own; the arm it replaces (rows caused_change_measure_arm and caused_change_measure_summary) needed 37 GB with production stopped, under a limit of 4,500 s.
inputs: Production's run folders under Saved/mimo_bridge/experiments, read only: the active run named by Saved/mimo_bridge/training_continuation.json and the runs before it, back through each folder's continuation_receipt.json (parent_run, checkpoint), for as long as a folder's args.json holds consequence_mode = measure.

From each 'mimo' stats record (one per 100 model steps) its caused_change block. Per sense (vision when rendered, tactile, audio, proprioception, vestibular): the scored body-model-steps, the mean own and swapped agreements and their difference (the advantage), the caused and changed shares, the habituation factor, the repeat line, the gate's readings and open share, the would-be pay. The same for the null block (two commands, neither the body's own). For the window: the spread of the value with every gate open (would_value_jitter) and the scoring's ms per model step.
For the step rate: model_steps_per_s and machine.model_ms of the same records and of the 20 full reports before the relaunch.
steps: The coordinator relaunches production on branch restart/candidate-b-2026-10-03 with --consequence-mode measure added to its command (record docs/gain_of_function_v4/restart_candidate/RESTART_CANDIDATE_B_2026-10-03.md on that branch, section 8). Every model step the learner then runs two more passes without gradient (another body's command of the same size, one and two bodies along, through the motor encoder, the transformer and the prediction heads) and scores each sense's predicted change against the change that happened. The flags' count still feeds the goal value and the ranking.

At any time, beside training: python docs/gain_of_function_v4/caused_change_measure_2026-10-02.py production. It reads the records; a report counts when its block scored all 100 model steps and its whole window lies after the first 300 model steps of its run (every load starts every gate shut and empty; 32 readings at one per 7 model steps are 224 model steps). It writes summary.json.

Per sense over the counted reports: the advantage, the own and swapped agreements, the caused and changed shares (each weighted by scored body-model-steps); the mean gate open share; the mean null gate open share; the mean repeat line and habituation factor.

The floor: the mean of would_value_jitter over the counted reports in which every scored sense's repeat line is set. It is taken, and floor.json written, at 30 or more such reports with a standard error (the standard deviation between reports over the square root of their count) of at most 5 in 100 of the mean.
The null line is judged at 200 counted reports; before that the shares are printed as interim.
The cost: the block's ms_per_step beside machine.model_ms, and model steps per second against the 20 full reports before the relaunch.
measures: Agreement: direction match x (smaller length / larger length). +1 = the predicted change is the change, 0 = unrelated or no change, -1 = the opposite change.
Advantage per sense: -2 to +2. 0 = the command made no difference; +1 = only the own command predicts the change.
Gate and null gate open shares: 0 to 1 of a report's model steps (0 = shut on every model step, 1 = open on every one).

Floor: the standard deviation of the value's successive changes over the square root of 2, in the channel's own units (the advantage summed over senses and averaged over 25 model steps), with its standard error.
Step rate: model steps per second as a share of the 20 full reports before the relaunch (1 = the same rate).
rows.pass_line: Per sense: the null gate open on at most 5 in 100 model steps, the mean over 200 counted reports. The floor carries no pass line: it is taken at 30 counted reports with every repeat line set and a standard error of at most 5 in 100 of its mean.
rows.pass_line_basis: The null line is the caused-change branch's (docs/gain_of_function_v4/agents/caused_change_consequence_2026-10-02.md, section 8). The count of 200 reports is arithmetic on the gate's own rule (docs/gain_of_function_v4/restart_candidate/candidate_b/null_gate_arithmetic.json on branch restart/candidate-b-2026-10-03, 1,500,000 readings): on independent readings of mean 0 the gate stands open on 1.1 of every 100 readings, in stretches of 22 readings (152 model steps) that begin once in 13,780 model steps. A sense whose null is as designed is read above 0.05 in 5.6 of 100 readings of 7 reports (the arm's 700 model steps), in 1.9 of 100 at 100 reports and in 0 of 525 at 200 reports. A gate whose successive readings each carry half of the one before (true open share 11.4 in 100) is read above 0.05 in 44 of 100 readings of 7 reports and in 99 of 100 at 200. The floor's 30 reports are two caregiver cycles (60 s present + 15 s absent = 1,500 model steps); one report holds 800 successive changes, whose standard deviation is known to 2.5 in 100 for Gaussian values and to 9.5 in 100 at a kurtosis of 30, so 30 reports reach 5 in 100 unless the kurtosis is above about 240.

cost.where: beside training
cost.basis: The reading parses stats lines only (no model, no graphics card). The measurement rides production training: per model step two more passes without gradient and the scoring, measured on the CPU learner of H84's widths at 8.2 in 100 of a model step (148 ms of H84's 1,806 ms model step, the mean over the 120 full reports of model steps 458,600 to 470,500; expected step rate 93.3 in 100 of the rate before), and 9,241 more bytes in each stats record (row restart_candidate_b_cpu_checks). The relaunch itself is one stop of production, and its changed launch flags start the ability scheduler's five triggered checks in a saved comparison window.

rows.on_pass: The floor constant CAUSED_CHANGE_FLOOR is set in lem/model/caused_change.py by a commit that cites floor.json; the operator chooses the weight and the launch with --consequence-mode caused. The two arm rows are closed as replaced.
rows.on_fail: A sense over the null line may not pay under caused mode until its gate is repaired (fewer, more widely spaced readings, or a stricter opening line). The floor is still taken.

diagram.input: production's run folders while their launch settings hold consequence_mode = measure
diagram.operation: read each stats record's caused-change block beside training; no model is loaded
diagram.measurement: per sense: the advantage (-2 to +2), gate and null gate open shares, and the channel's floor
diagram.decision: pass: the floor constant is set from floor.json; a sense over the null line may not pay

rows.title: Vestibular token: what each checkpoint since the switch saved, and the route check
rows.question: At each of the 14 checkpoints from 455,800 on: does the vestibular token recomputed on the CPU, from the saved encoder input and the checkpoint's own encoder weights, equal the token the trainer saved for the same model step? And what did each checkpoint save of the vestibular input, token, encoder weights and input normaliser?
rows.why: The trainer's probe reads no head tilt from the revived vestibular token (row vestibular_repair_restart_segment, reading A4). Finding where the tilt is lost needs recorded inputs passed through one encoder on the CPU. That is valid only when the CPU's encoder computes what the trainer's does: the route check decides it. The saved inputs, tokens, weights and statistics are the data the later read-outs use. The decision that depends on it: which repair of the vestibular encoder or of its lessons the coordinator chooses.
inputs: The 14 checkpoints 455,800 (saved before the switch divided the encoder's last layer), 457,191, 457,825, 458,425, 459,961, 461,631, 463,308, 464,986, 466,662, 468,335, 470,005, 470,525, 470,550 and 470,625 of the H84 lineage (D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_recordings/H84_checkpoint_archive and Saved/mimo_bridge/experiments, read only): model.safetensors (only the 14 tensors of encoder_registry.encoders.vestibular), runtime_state.pt (only vestibular_norm: the running mean and variance of the 28 input fields), episode_state.json (where the companion is and its sha256).

Each checkpoint's episode companion (a .pt.gz of 0.6 to 1.0 GB, read only): the learner's saved model step (the encoder's input, 8 bodies x 28 numbers, and the token the trainer computed from it, 8 x 192), the collapse watch's ring of tokens (200 samples x 8 bodies, every 5th model step), the 4 newest tokens of the imagination chain's history, and, where a world's record is under 64 MB, each world's newest raw vestibular vector (29 numbers: the frame of the next model step). For checkpoints 455,800, 459,961, 464,986 and 470,625 also the replay ring's stored vestibular and proprioception tokens (8 bodies x 6,000 model steps x 192, float16) and the stored pose of the head, the lower trunk and the chest (position / 200 cm, orientation as 4 numbers).
No world is built, no model beyond the vestibular encoder's seven layers, no trainer.
steps: Per checkpoint: decompress the companion into D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/vestibular_token2/companions in 4 MB pieces while hashing the compressed bytes; refuse it when the sha256 is not the receipt's.

Read the decompressed file memory-mapped with every world left as its byte record (a world is unpickled only when its record is under 64 MB, and then only to copy its newest raw vector, time and frame number).
Copy the saved input, token, rings and stored poses into snap_<step>.npz; copy the encoder's 14 tensors into enc_<step>.npz; copy the normaliser's mean and variance.

Route check (amended Oct 3, 2026 2:33 PM PDT after the first run, see the result): the trainer computes a model step's token before that model step's optimizer update, and the checkpoint saves the weights after it. So for every checkpoint after the switch the encoder's weights before the last update are rebuilt from the saved weights and the saved AdamW state of optimizer.pt (old = (new + step size x running mean gradient) / (1 - learning rate x weight decay), AdamW's own arithmetic inverted; the encoder's 14 Adam states are the ones whose update count is the checkpoint's step minus 455,800). The token is computed from the saved input with those weights, in float32 and on the bf16 grid (each Linear's input, weight, bias and output rounded to bf16, the LayerNorms in float32, as the card's autocast computes them), and compared with the saved token. The same comparison with the saved weights is kept beside it: it reads how far one optimizer update moves the token. At 455,800 (before the switch, where every update of this encoder rounded away) the saved weights are used.
Centre and scale each world's raw vector with the saved statistics: the input of the next model step.

Remove the decompressed file (459,961's is kept for the replay job) and write snapshots.json after every checkpoint. A second run with --reuse reads only the checkpoint's own files again and repeats the route check on the inputs and tokens the first run copied.
measures: Route check: the largest and the root-mean-square difference per token number between the recomputed and the saved token. 0 = the same computation; a token's 192 numbers have root mean square 1; the 8 bodies' tokens differ from each other by 0.26 to 0.31 per number in the stats records of the watch, so a wrongly rebuilt encoder reads tenths.
The last layer's bias spread (74,425 before the switch, 18.17 right after it) and the root mean square of its weight (0.0007 right after the switch): how far learning has moved the layer.
The count of worlds whose raw vector was read (8 = every world; 0 at the three checkpoints saved before the caregiver's bounded event list).
rows.pass_line: The route check passes at every checkpoint read: on the bf16 grid the largest difference between the recomputed and the saved token is at most 0.02 per number, the token recomputed with the weights before the last optimizer update (amended Oct 3, 2026 2:33 PM PDT: the first run compared with the saved weights and failed at 470,525 with 0.0233; see the result). The job also fails when a checkpoint cannot be read.
rows.pass_line_basis: The CPU repeats the trainer's computation with the same weights and the same input; what can differ is the card's own sequence of bf16 roundings. The last layer's output holds numbers up to about 55 (the divided constant), where one bf16 step is 0.25, and the output LayerNorm divides by the spread 18.17: a number that lands on the other side of one rounding boundary moves its token number by 0.25 / 18.17 = 0.014. The line 0.02 admits one such step and refuses a wrongly rebuilt encoder (tenths). The motor encoder's route check of Oct 3 used the same line and read at most 0.0015. Reachability of the amended check, measured on three checkpoints before the second run (a reading on the first run's saved inputs, no new data): with the weights before the last update the largest difference was 0.000000 at 459,961, 0.000125 at 470,525 and 0.000965 at 470,625, 87 to 100 of every 100 numbers equal within 1e-6; the rest is the float32 rounding of the rebuilt weights.

cost.where: the CPU, beside production training: one process under a hard limit of 2.9 GB of RAM and 4.5 GB committed, started only with 8 GB or more of commit room and ended when the room falls under 5 GB
cost.basis: Measured on checkpoint 470,625 before the row was written (a reading of file structure, no measurement): decompressing 594 MB took 6 s and gave 811 MB; reading it memory-mapped held 0.43 GB of RAM and 2.2 GB committed (1.35 GB of that is the torch library's own). The three checkpoints saved before the caregiver's bounded event list are 0.95 to 1.0 GB compressed. Disk: one decompressed companion at a time in the scratch folder, and under 0.2 GB of results.

rows.on_pass: The later jobs (the replay, the read-outs, the lesson pulls) use the CPU's encoder and these saved inputs; the readings go into this row and into the record docs/gain_of_function_v4/agents/vestibular_token_readouts_2026-10-03.md on branch fix/vestibular_token_readouts-2026-10-03.
rows.on_fail: A failed route check: the encoder was not rebuilt as the trainer's (or the saved input is not the input of the saved token); no read-out is taken from it, the rebuild is corrected and the job run again. An unreadable checkpoint is named in the row and left out of the later jobs.

values: First run, Oct 3, 2026 2:25 to 2:28 PM PDT (180.8 s; the process held at most 0.65 GB of RAM and 3.08 GB committed; commit room 26.1 GB at the start, 25.0 GB at its lowest): all 14 checkpoints were read, none refused.

Route check as first declared (the token recomputed with the SAVED weights against the saved token, bf16 grid): 455,800 read 6.0e-8 (the dead token, exact); the 13 checkpoints after the switch read a largest difference of 0.0138 to 0.0186 per number, except 470,525 at 0.0233, over the line of 0.02. Root mean square 0.0014 to 0.0073. So the first run FAILED by its declared line at one checkpoint.

Cause, measured right after the run on the first run's saved inputs: float32 and three different bf16 emulations all read the same differences, so the rounding was not the cause. The saved token was computed before the saved model step's optimizer update, and the saved weights are the weights after it. Undoing that one AdamW update from the checkpoint's own Adam state gives the weights that made the token. At 470,525 the last update moved single weights by up to 3.2 learning rates, at 470,625 by up to 1.1 and at 459,961 by up to 0.6: the larger update gave the larger difference.

Second run, Oct 3, 2026 2:33 to 2:34 PM PDT (36.1 s, 0.42 GB of RAM, 1.23 GB committed; it reused the inputs and tokens the first run copied and read each checkpoint's encoder, Adam state and normaliser again). Route check with the weights before the last optimizer update, bf16 grid: PASSED at 14 of 14 checkpoints. Largest difference per token number: 7.2e-7 or less at 9 checkpoints (every number equal within 1e-6), 7.8e-6 at 470,550, 0.000125 at 470,525, 0.00096 at 470,625, 0.0010 at 468,335 and 0.0034 at 466,662, against the line of 0.02 and the 0.30 to 0.43 by which the 8 bodies' tokens differ from each other. At those last three checkpoints 7 of the 8 bodies' tokens are equal within 1e-6 and one body's differs: the float32 rounding of the rebuilt weights puts single numbers on the other side of a bf16 rounding boundary.

What the comparison with the saved weights measured: one optimizer update moves the vestibular token by 0.0014 to 0.0073 per number (root mean square over the 8 bodies and 192 numbers) with the inputs unchanged.

Other readings: the last layer's bias spread fell from 18.146 (457,191) to 18.102 (470,625); the root mean square of the last layer's weight rose from 0.064 to 0.116 (0.0007 right after the switch). The raw vectors of all 8 worlds were read at the 11 checkpoints from 458,425 on; the three earlier ones hold worlds of 137 to 144 MB each and were not unpickled.
result.verdict: pass on the second run: the CPU's rebuilt encoder computes the trainer's token

rows.decision: The later jobs use the CPU's encoder (bf16 grid for tokens the model consumes, float32 for the stage read-outs) and the saved inputs, tokens, weights, Adam states and normaliser statistics of the 14 checkpoints. A token recomputed for a model step is computed with the weights before that model step's update. Written Oct 3, 2026 2:35 PM PDT.

rows.title: Vestibular inputs model step by model step: the saved worlds of 459,961 replayed on the CPU under the recorded commands
rows.question: What are the vestibular encoder's 29 raw input numbers at every model step for each of the 8 bodies over 1,670 consecutive model steps (459,961 to 461,631), when each saved world is restored on the CPU and handed the commands production handed it? How far does the replayed body stay from the lived one?
rows.why: The trainer saves the vestibular input of one model step per checkpoint and records none in between, while the trainer's probe judges how each body's token follows that body's own change of head tilt and trunk roll over 100 consecutive model steps. Reading the tilt out of the inputs, out of each encoder stage and out of planted tokens in that same form needs consecutive inputs. The observer's world recording holds every command and the joint positions of every model step, so the saved worlds can be replayed and compared with the lived ones. The decision that depends on it: the same as row vestibular_token_snapshots (which repair follows).
inputs: Checkpoint 459,961's episode companion (decompressed by the snapshots job, read only): the 8 saved worlds, each with its own settings and its full simulator state (4.7 MB a world at checkpoint 470,625, the one read before this row was written).

The observer's world recording of run H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41f_0322_resume_20261003_044641 (Saved/mimo_bridge/experiments/<run>/observer/world/b0 to b7, read only): per body and model step the command the world was handed (26 body handles x 9 numbers: target position xyz in cm, orientation as 4 numbers, radius, strength 0-1; the handle mask; the hand's 44 joint goals; the eye command's 2 angles), stored as float32, and the joint positions at the model step's last physics frame (146 numbers, exact to 1e-6), the frame number and the head accelerometer's size per physics frame.
The snapshots job's snap_461631.npz: the next checkpoint's saved raw vector per world (the end check).

The world's own code (mimo_bridge/env.py BridgeEnv, built with vision off: no picture is rendered and no graphics context is made) and the observer baseline's restore helpers (mimo_bridge/tools/observer/baseline.py). No model, no trainer, no learning.
steps: A first run: body 0 for 200 model steps into its own folder. It measures the world's build time, the stepping rate, the memory and the fidelity before the full run is started.

The full run, one body after another in one process: build the world from the saved settings with two changes (the scene files go to the scratch folder; the caregiver records nothing: its event tape is replaced by a counter) and vision off; restore the saved state; compare the restored state with the saved one exactly (time, frame, joint positions and velocities, MuJoCo's integration state, the edited model fields, the caregiver's phase) and stop the body when anything differs.
Check that the record of model step 459,961 ends 5 physics frames after the saved world's frame (the records continue the saved state).

For each model step s from 459,961 to 461,630: hand the world the recorded command of model step s for 5 physics frames of 10 ms; after the 5th frame keep the raw vestibular vector (29 numbers: the input of model step s + 1), the joint positions, the head's and the chest's orientation, and the accelerometer's size at each of the 5 frames.

Fidelity per model step: the replayed joint positions minus the recorded ones (root mean square and largest over the body's joints, the 4 eye joints apart); the replayed accelerometer size against the recorded one.
End check: the replayed raw vector of model step 461,631 minus the next checkpoint's saved world vector, per body.
Write replay_b<body>.npz per body and replay.json after every body.
measures: The raw vestibular vector per body and model step: 8 x 1,670 x 29 numbers in the fields' own units (head accelerometer in g, gyro / 2 rad/s, neck angles on each joint's range -1 to 1, neck speeds / 1.5 rad/s, neck efforts -1 to 1, the trunk's up direction, support shares 0 to 1, total support in body weights, effort in units of its measured 99th percentile, the share of joints at a limit, the lowest and the mean motor capacity 0 to 1, the validity flag).
Joint difference: replayed minus recorded, in radians (hinge joints) and metres (the root's position). 0 = the lived trajectory repeated; 1e-6 = the recording's own rounding; 0.017 rad = 1 degree.
Model steps until any body joint first differs by 1e-4 (0.006 degree): how long the replay repeats the lived trajectory.
End check: difference per field between the replayed and the saved vector at 461,631 (0 = equal).

Three things differ from the lived run and each can let the trajectories part: the lived eyes also followed a motion reflex that reads the rendered pictures (the replay has no pictures); the recorded commands are float32 where the trainer handed float64; each process draws its own skin sensor points (they feed touch, not the joints' motors). rows.title: Prediction heads, state today: what each head reads and outputs on three saved checkpoints
rows.question: On checkpoints 476,501 (the newest of the running segment), 474,875 (the one before the motor switch) and 455,800: what numbers does each of the five prediction heads receive from the transformer and the persistent memory, and what does it output, with the body's own command and with another body's size-matched command in the motor token?
rows.why: The tactile, vision and vestibular predictions do not depend on the command while proprioception's does since model step 474,875. Contact control and the consequence rebuild both need tactile predictions that depend on the command. The repair has to follow from the measured mechanism (operator rule of Sep 26: understand the mechanism before repairing), and these arrays are the input of every reading in the row prediction_heads_state_readings.
inputs: Checkpoint folders ckpt_step_476501 and ckpt_step_479350 (run H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41m_0402; 479,350 is the checkpoint the coordinator's stop wrote and the state production resumes), ckpt_step_474875 (run H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41h_0223, the one before the motor switch) and ckpt_step_455800 (run H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41s_1146_resume_20261001_213502, in the archive D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_recordings/H84_checkpoint_archive): model.safetensors and runtime_state.pt, read only.

Each checkpoint's episode companion on D: (the file its episode_state.json names): the replay ring, per body the newest 6,000 model steps of the 6 tokens (192 numbers each), the achieved pose (26 handles x 10 numbers), the executed command (26 handles x 9 numbers), which senses were real, and the persistent memory's state.
No world, no graphics card, no trainer.
steps: Load the companion, keep the replay ring. Build the model on the CPU with the trainer's own builder and load the checkpoint without its optimizer.

Choose the ages (model steps behind the ring's newest step) at which all 8 bodies have a window of 129 consecutive model steps in one episode whose step-from model steps all carry an executed command and production's replay action contract: 127 context steps, the current model step t, the target model step t+1. STATE CAPTURES (476,501, 474,875, 455,800): 80 ages, 11 model steps apart (11 shares no factor with the 5-model-step hold). BENCH CAPTURE (479,350): 700 ages, 8 model steps apart (8 shares no factor with 5), 5,600 windows.

Per age, one batch of 8 windows (one per body). Repeat the forward part of the trainer's replay lesson: context tokens plus modality embeddings, the motor token rebuilt from [achieved pose, executed command] at every step, the memory bias rebuilt from the stored memory state, the transformer, the five heads, the gaze copy into vision.

Do it twice per batch: with the executed command A_t at model step t, and with the previous body's A_t taken as a change from that body's pose and applied to this body's pose (the size-matched control of the stats block prediction_audit_hold_first).

State captures only, on the first 40 ages: both again with every matrix product's inputs and output rounded to bf16 (what the graphics card computes on); LayerNorm and softmax stay in fp32, as on the card.

Check on the first batch: the same windows through the trainer's own replay update, stopped after the heads; this script's heads input and predictions must equal the trainer's to 1e-4, else the job stops. Check a digest of every weight before and after.
Write one file per capture under D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/candidate_heads/captures/.
measures: Per window (up to 960 per checkpoint): the transformer's final LayerNorm output at the newest model step's 6 slots (6 x 192 numbers) for both commands; the memory bias added to it (6 x 192); the current and next tokens; the five predictions for both commands in fp32 and on the bf16 grid; vision's prediction after the gaze copy; body, age, whether the command changed into model step t (the hold's first model step).

Once per checkpoint: the memory's constant per slot (root mean square per number: 0 = no offset; the tokens themselves are about 5 per number), the running centres of the revived first-layer rows, the vision head's input scale.
The check's two differences (0 = this script computes exactly what the trainer computes).
rows.pass_line: The job passes when, for each of the three checkpoints, the check against the trainer's own replay forward reads at most 1e-4 for the predictions and at most 1e-4 of the largest input value for the heads' input, the weight digest is unchanged, and at least 400 windows were captured.
rows.pass_line_basis: This job produces inputs for the readings; its own line is that the arrays are the trainer's. 1e-4 is the line the Sep 26 capture met at 0 to 4.8e-7 with the same construction (prediction_heads_slot_lock_2026-09-26.md, section 1a). 400 windows: each ring holds 6,000 model steps per body, and 120 ages 11 apart need 1,449; a ring cut by an episode boundary or an unlabelled step gives fewer, and 400 windows (50 ages) still leave 350 windows in the seven-body pool, the count the Oct 2 read-out used per hold phase.

rows.title: Prediction heads, state today: attention, sizes, first layer, output, own-command reading, the offset hypothesis
rows.question: Per prediction head on checkpoints 476,501, 474,875 and 455,800: where does its attention put its weight and what sets that, how large is what its first layer reads and how much of it differs between model steps, does its output vary, how much of the real next-token change does it explain, does the output change when the command or one slot's token changes, and does subtracting the memory's offset or centring and normalising the head's input bring the command into the prediction without retraining?
rows.why: It states the defect as numbers and checks the Sep 26 review's hypothesis (the memory's offset on the heads' input) directly. The comparison of proprioception (uses the command since model step 474,875) with tactile (does not) names what the repair has to change; the design of the repair on branch restart/candidate-heads-2026-10-04 follows from these readings.
inputs: The three capture files of row prediction_heads_state_capture: per window the transformer's final LayerNorm output at the 6 slots for the own and the size-matched swapped command, the memory bias, current and next tokens, the model's five predictions (fp32 and bf16 grid), body, age, hold-first flag.
Each checkpoint's model.safetensors (the heads' weights and the revived first-layer rows) and the revived rows' running centres kept in the capture.
steps: Pool: bodies 0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 (body 2 left out by the operator's decision of Sep 25). A window counts for a sense when its current and next token are real readings and the step carries its executed command.
Recompute each head from its saved weights on the captured input; record the largest difference from the model's own prediction.

Attention, per attention head (4 per head): mean weight per slot, entropy share, median lead of the best slot over the second in logits, the softmax's gradient share; the lead the memory's constant alone gives, the lead the transformer output's shared part alone gives, and the standard deviation over windows of the scores' part that differs between windows.

Sizes: root mean square per number of the memory bias and of the transformer's output per slot; the attention output's size, its variation between windows inside a body, the bf16 rounding step at its size and the share of that variation left after rounding to bf16.

First layer: units revived by the liveness repair; share of units whose input rises above -3 on some window and share whose output range exceeds the liveness monitor's floor, with the revived rows, with every unit on its own old row, and with the head's products rounded to bf16; for revived rows the lag ratio (the shared offset of input minus running centre over what differs between windows) and the divisor their LayerNorm applies.
Output: the head's own output (prediction minus current token), its size per number, its variation between bodies and between model steps inside a body, beside the real change; fp32 and bf16.

Explained share: 1 - (summed prediction error) / (summed no-change error). Own-command reading: 1 - (summed error with the own command) / (summed error with the size-matched command), all windows and the hold's first model step; standard errors from 1,000 two-level bootstrap draws (bodies, then windows). Command move: root mean square of own minus swapped prediction over root mean square of the predicted change.

Slot swap: replace one slot's token by the previous body's at the same age (each of the 6 slots in turn, the motor slot among them) and read the output's change over its within-body variation and over the predicted change.

Variants without retraining, in fp32: the constant subtracted from the head's keys and values; each slot centred on its mean over the capture and divided by its root mean square; each also with the mean prediction shift against the unchanged head subtracted (one vector per sense, no target used).

Linear read-out: ridge regression, one body held out in turn, from the transformer's output at the 6 slots to the real change of the sense's token; held-out error over no-change error, and the own-command reading of that read-out when fed the swapped command's transformer output.
The next-model-step lesson's gradient (squared error, own command, fp32) per parameter group of the head and on the tokens it reads.
measures: Entropy share: 0 = all weight on one slot, 1 = even over the six slots. Lead in logits: a lead of m leaves the second slot exp(-m) of the best slot's weight. Gradient share: 0.83 = even, 0 = one slot.

Explained share: 0 = the prediction is no better than predicting no change, 1 = exact, below 0 = worse than no change. Own-command reading: 0 = the command makes no difference to the error, 1 = the own command leaves no error. Command move: 0 = swapping the command leaves the prediction where it was, 1 = it moves it as far as the whole predicted change.
Share of the attention output's between-step variation that survives bf16: 1 = all, 0 = none, below 0 = the rounding is larger than the variation.
Live share and varying share of the first layer: 0 to 1 of its 192 units. Lag ratio: 0 = the running centre sits on the windows' mean; 80 = the offset is 80 times what differs between windows.
rows.pass_line: Three rules, each judged per head on checkpoint 476,501 in the seven-body pool. THE HEAD IS CONSTANT: its output's variation between model steps inside a body is under 5 of 100 of the real change's same variation, on the bf16 grid. THE OFFSET HYPOTHESIS, WITHOUT RETRAINING: met for a head when a variant's own-command reading and its gain over the unchanged head's reading on the same windows are each above 3.14 standard errors (the Oct 2 read-out's line). THE LATENT CARRIES THE COMMAND'S EFFECT: met for a sense when the linear read-out's own-command reading is above 0.01 and its held-out error is under the no-change error.
rows.pass_line_basis: Declared before the readings ran. 5 of 100: a head that follows the real change at all must vary with it; the Sep 26 scale survey read the tactile head's between-body spread at 0 against 0.026 to 0.029 before model step 350,926. 3.14 standard errors is the one-sided normal line for 5 in 100 shared over 60 comparisons, the line of row own_command_readout_hold_phases, where no variant met it at 455,800 (before the motor switch, when the motor token carried no command). Reachability of the variant rule: proprioception's head reads 27 to 38 of 100 on the live size-matched reading since model step 474,875, so a head that reads the command through its input shows far above the line; a head trained with the constant present may not respond to a changed input without retraining, which is why the third rule reads the latent itself. 0.01 for the read-out: the bootstrap spread of a ridge read-out on about 560 windows is not known before the run; the value and the swapped read-out's error are recorded beside the verdict.

cost.where: CPU beside training: one process at a time, idle priority, at most 4 threads, hard RAM maximum 2.8 GB, started only with 8 GB or more of commit room; refused while the active run's two newest reports both read under 0.42 model steps per second, and ended when two reports written during the job both do
cost.basis: arithmetic on at most 960 windows x 6 x 192 numbers per checkpoint: five heads, 6 slot swaps and 2 variants each, a ridge with 7 held-out bodies on 1,152 features; no model build

rows.on_pass: The rules that are met name the mechanism: a constant head whose latent carries the command's effect is repaired at the head (the record's section on the repair); a variant that meets the offset rule without retraining would make centring alone the repair.
rows.on_fail: A head that is not constant, or a latent that does not carry the command's effect on a sense, moves the repair for that sense upstream of the head (the transformer or the sense's encoder); the record says so per sense.
rows.result: Checkpoint 479,350, 4,900 windows of 7 bodies (readings_479350.json; the same picture at 474,875 and 476,501). Every attention head of all five prediction heads puts a weight of 0.999998 to 1.0 on one slot. Tactile, vision and vestibular read slots whose persistent-memory constant is 107 to 268 per number: what their first layer reads is 1.6 to 14.6 million per number, of which 394 to 2,450 differs between model steps, under the bf16 rounding step of 7,609 to 79,701; all 192 first-layer units of each were revived and their running centre lags by 49 to 132 times the part that differs. Their output is one constant vector (error over no-change error: tactile 1.043, vestibular 1.001, vision's head alone 94.8; own-command reading 0.0000). Proprioception and audio read the vestibular slot (constant 6.4 per number): their first layer reads 0.57 per number with 0.32 to 0.35 that differs, no unit revived; error ratio 0.820 and 0.901, own-command reading 0.236 and 0.001. Vision with the gaze copy: error ratio 0.688, own-command reading 0.125. The lesson's gradient on the transformer's output per lesson row: tactile 3e-10, vestibular 6e-10, proprioception 4e-5. A ridge fit from the transformer's output reads an error ratio of 0.987 for tactile, 0.996 for vestibular, 0.729 for vision, 0.874 for audio, 0.913 for proprioception. The Sep 26 review's hypothesis applied without retraining (the constant subtracted from keys and values; each slot centred and divided by its size) leaves the three dead heads' readings where they are and lowers proprioception's own-command reading.
rows.decision: The mechanism is taken as measured: the pool on one slot, the constant's image under the bf16 step, the revived units' lagging centre. The repair therefore reads the slots with the constant subtracted and centred, beside the old head, and starts at zero (the record's section 5).

rows.title: Prediction heads over the lineage since model step 415,075, from saved weights alone
rows.question: Since model step 415,075 (where the Sep 26 record's timeline ends): how large is the memory's constant per slot at each archived checkpoint, how far ahead does it put each attention head's best slot, how large is its image in what each head's first layer reads, and what divisor do the revived first-layer rows' LayerNorms apply?
rows.why: It dates the defect: whether the heads' lock and the size of their first layers' input changed with the memory repair, the vestibular switch at 455,800 or the motor switch at 474,875, or stood unchanged through all of them. The Sep 26 record (prediction_heads_slot_lock_2026-09-26.md, section 1c) holds the same quantities from model step 3,764 to 415,075.
inputs: model.safetensors and runtime_state.pt of about 20 checkpoints from 415,075 to the newest, read only: from D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_recordings/H84_checkpoint_archive and from production's checkpoint folders (474,875 and the newest).

Per checkpoint: each head's query, key, value and output projections, its first layer and revived rows, the persistent memory's readout bias (6 x 192 numbers: the constant), the revived rows' running centres.
steps: Per head and attention head: score of each slot from the constant alone (score direction times the slot's constant), its lead in logits, the winning slot, the entropy share of the softmax of those scores.
The constant's image in the attention output under those weights; its root mean square per number and the bf16 rounding step at that size.

For heads with revived first-layer rows: the length of (constant's image minus running centre) with its mean over the 192 numbers removed, over sqrt(192): the divisor the rows' LayerNorm applies to what differs between model steps.
measures: Constant per slot, root mean square per number: the tokens themselves are about 5 per number.
Lead in logits: a lead of m leaves the second slot exp(-m) of the best slot's weight (10 logits: 5 in 100,000). Entropy share: 0 = one slot, 1 = even.
Image size per number and its bf16 step: a variation between model steps smaller than half the step is rounded away on the graphics card.
LayerNorm divisor: 1 = the rows read the input's variation at its own size; 10,000 = they read it and pass gradient back divided by 10,000.
rows.pass_line: A dating, with one rule: the lock predates the motor switch for a head when every one of its attention heads has a constant-only lead above 10 logits at every checkpoint read from 415,075 to 474,875.
rows.pass_line_basis: 10 logits is the Sep 26 record's lock line: above it the score directions moved 1.4e-7 per 1,000 model steps over the lineage against 0.03 below 2 logits. The rule can fail: the audio and proprioception heads read leads of 0.1 to 4.3 logits at 415,075 on real windows.

cost.where: CPU beside training: one process at a time, idle priority, at most 4 threads, hard RAM maximum 2.8 GB, started only with 8 GB or more of commit room; refused while the active run's two newest reports both read under 0.42 model steps per second, and ended when two reports written during the job both do
cost.basis: each checkpoint: two file reads (70 MB and 489 MB, the second from the USB disk D:) and matrix products on 192 x 192 weights; the Sep 26 lineage script of the same kind took about 2 s per checkpoint without the runtime file

rows.on_pass: The record dates the lock before the switches named and states which quantity each switch changed.
rows.on_fail: A head whose lead fell under 10 logits at some checkpoint is read on that checkpoint's own windows (a further capture, in a row of its own) before the record states when it locked.
rows.result: 15 checkpoints from model step 421,461 to 479,350, weights only (lineage_weights.json; checkpoint 415,075 cannot be read by this arithmetic, the memory was not yet repaired there). The persistent memory's constant keeps its size per slot throughout. The lead the constant alone gives the best slot: tactile 273 logits at 421,461 and 164 at 479,350; vestibular 66 to 574, then 39 to 338; vision 21 to 61, then 17 to 43. The size of the constant's image at vision's first layer grows from 103,000 to 14.5 million per number. Audio's and proprioception's leads grow from 0.1 to 5.4 logits at 421,461 to 8.8 to 11.7 at 479,350 (entropy share 0.35 to 0.39, then 0.0001 to 0.0008): their pools locked onto the vestibular slot during segment 41. The rule declared for dating (a lead above 10 logits at every checkpoint) is not met by these two heads.
rows.decision: The dead heads' lock predates this lineage window (the Sep 26 record dates it to model steps 350,926 to 386,750). Proprioception's and audio's pools are locked as well but read a slot whose constant is small, so their input still varies; the candidate leaves the old pools as they are.

rows.title: The all-slot path trained on frozen transformer outputs of checkpoints 476,501 (640 windows) and 479,350 (5,600 windows)
rows.question: With the transformer of checkpoint 476,501 frozen, how much of each sense's next-token change does an all-slot path beside the head learn to predict on bodies it did not train on, and does its prediction then depend on the command (own command against the size-matched swapped command)?
rows.why: It gives the reachability arithmetic for the production segment's pass lines before any run: what the path can read from the latent as it is today (a floor: in production the transformer also learns, and the tactile, vision and vestibular lessons then send it gradient, which today they do not). It also checks that the path as built (constant removed, running centre, LayerNorm, one weight block per slot) learns at all on H84's real numbers, and that it does not lower proprioception's reading.
inputs: D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/candidate_heads/captures/capture_476501.pt (640 windows, 80 per body) and capture_479350_big.pt (5,600 windows, 700 per body, of the checkpoint production resumes): per window the transformer's final LayerNorm output at the 6 slots (6 x 192 numbers) for the own and the size-matched swapped command, the memory bias and constant, current and next tokens, the old heads' predictions for both commands.
The branch's module lem/model/heads_all_slot_path.py at the model's width 192 (and 96 and 384 as the width's control, and with the running centre switched off as the centre's control).

Second round (written Oct 4, 2026 before it ran): capture_479350_big.pt only; vision's base prediction is the trainer's own composition, the old head's prediction with the gaze copy added (the capture's vision_copy_own and vision_copy_swap; the first round read vision's head without the gaze copy, which the trainer never does); the module as built, and two variants built in the bench alone: each slot's centred, LayerNormed row is first multiplied by one 192-to-32 (or 192-to-16) weight matrix the 6 slots share, so the first layer reads 6 x 32 (or 6 x 16) numbers; and the running centre switched off.
steps: Path input: final LayerNorm output plus (memory bias minus constant), as the trainer would hand it (the heads' input minus the constant).
Two folds: train on bodies 0, 1, 3, 4 and read on bodies 5, 6, 7; then train on 4, 5, 6, 7 and read on 0, 1, 3. Body 2 is in neither.

3,000 optimizer updates per fold: AdamW, learning rate 3e-4, betas 0.9 and 0.999, weight decay 0.01 on matrices, batches of 24 windows; loss = sum over the five senses of the mean squared error of (old head's prediction + path's output - next token) on the windows whose tokens are real, each divided by that sense's no-change error on the training windows; the running centre moves at every batch.

Every 250 updates, on the held-out bodies and per sense: error over no-change error, and the own-command reading 1 - (error with the own command's transformer output) / (error with the swapped command's), with the same reading on the hold's first model step alone.

Record per sense the lowest held-out error, the update it came at, the own-command reading there and the largest own-command reading; the path's own gauges at the end (output size, slot reach, live share, centre lag); and head_read at the end (how evenly the old head's prediction plus the path's output answers to the 6 slots).

Second round: the same two folds with three random seeds each (the path's starting weights and the batch draws differ by seed), 1,500 optimizer updates, read every 125 updates. The spread over the three seeds is the noise against which the as-built module and the variants are compared.

Second round, the lesson's gradient on the transformer's output through the trained path: on 512 held-out windows, per sense, the derivative of that sense's mean squared error with respect to the path's input x (6 slots x 192 numbers), as the root mean square per number per slot. The same derivative through the old head is in row prediction_heads_state_readings (tactile 1e-13 per number, proprioception 2e-8 per number at 479,350).
measures: Error over no-change error: 1 = no better than predicting that the token stays as it is, 0 = exact. The old heads at update 0: tactile 1.02, vestibular 1.00, vision's head alone about 103, proprioception 0.81, audio 0.94 (row prediction_heads_state_readings).

Own-command reading: 0 = the command makes no difference to the error, 1 = the own command leaves no error. The old heads: tactile 0.0000, vestibular 0.0000, vision's head alone 0.0000, proprioception 0.23, audio 0.005.
Slot reach spread of the path: 0 = its output answers to one slot, 1 = to all six evenly.
rows.pass_line: REACHABLE FOR A SENSE when, in both folds, the lowest held-out error is under the old head's error and the own-command reading at that update is above 0.01. NO HARM TO PROPRIOCEPTION when its lowest held-out error is at or under the old head's in both folds.
rows.pass_line_basis: Declared before the run. 0.01 is 1 of 100 of the reading's scale; proprioception's old head reads 0.23 on the same windows, and a linear read-out of the frozen latent reads 0.17 for proprioception, 0.006 for vision and 0.000 for tactile (row prediction_heads_state_readings), so on the frozen latent the rule is expected to be met for proprioception, to be open for vision and NOT to be met for tactile: the tactile lesson has sent the transformer a gradient of 5e-12 per number against proprioception's 2e-7, so the latent holds no tactile change yet. A tactile miss here is that finding stated as a number, and the segment's tactile line then rests on the transformer learning under the path's gradient, which this bench cannot show.

cost.where: CPU only, one process at a time, idle priority, at most 4 threads, hard RAM maximum 2.8 GB and 5 GB of commit per process. Training is stopped while these jobs run: the coordinator stopped the trainer at model step 479,350 on Oct 4, 2026, 6:56 AM PDT (supervisor control = pause) for this chain; this work starts no trainer and writes no control file
cost.basis: measured Oct 4 on 640 windows: 74 s for both folds at width 192 with 2 threads, 0.93 GB of commit; on 5,600 windows the reads every 250 updates are 9 times larger

rows.on_pass: The senses that meet the rule get their segment pass line from these readings (the record's section on the pass lines).
rows.on_fail: A sense that misses the rule on the frozen latent gets a pass line that reads the latent as well as the head (the command must move the prediction, and the error must fall below the no-change error), with its reachability stated as unmeasured before the segment.
rows.result: Checkpoint 479,350, 2,800 training windows of 4 bodies, read on 2,100 windows of the 3 other bodies, 2 folds, 3 seeds, vision's base with the gaze copy (bench2_rank32_s*.json, bench2_w192_s*.json, bench3_module_s0.json). Held-out, at optimizer update 250, the 32-number path, fold 0 and fold 1. Error over no-change error: tactile 0.997 and 0.995 (old head 1.042 and 1.043); vestibular 1.005 and 1.006 (1.001 and 1.001); proprioception 0.768 and 0.849 (0.800 and 0.864); vision 0.669 and 0.672 (0.698 and 0.692); audio 0.863 and 0.883 (0.897 and 0.917). Own-command reading with its standard error: tactile 0.002 and 0.003 (0.003), vestibular 0.004 and 0.003 (0.002 to 0.006), both 0 within noise; proprioception 0.274 and 0.273 (old head 0.233 and 0.250); vision 0.135 and 0.132; audio 0.001 and 0.001. On the training windows the same readings are tactile 0.008 and 0.007, vestibular 0.010 and 0.009, rising to 0.05 to 0.06 by update 1,500 while the held-out ones stay at noise. The swapped command moves the tactile and vestibular predictions by 0.47 to 0.81 of the predicted change. With every slot's 192 numbers read directly the held-out error rises from update 250 on (tactile 1.055 and 1.086 at update 1,000; with 32 numbers per slot 0.994 and 1.013). The lesson's gradient on the transformer's output through the trained path: tactile 3e-4 to 4e-4 per row, vestibular 6e-5 to 1e-4. head_read spread 0.87 to 1.0; every hidden unit live. By the row's rule: proprioception and vision are reachable and proprioception is not harmed; tactile, vestibular and audio miss the own-command part of the rule (under 0.01).
rows.decision: The path keeps 32 numbers per slot (lower held-out error over 3 seeds). The segment's lines are not declared from this bench alone: with the transformer held fixed the path makes tactile and vestibular predictions depend on the command without a held-out gain, so the coordinator asked for a probe that goes around the transformer (row prediction_heads_reachability_probe) and declared the lines from it.

rows.title: Heads candidate (restart/candidate-heads-2026-10-04): unit tests, planted defects, lockstep with production, resume from production's state
rows.question: Does the branch with --heads-all-slot-path absent train bit for bit as production's commit, does a state saved by production's code with production's flags load with the flag on with every prediction unchanged at the switch, do the path's tests pass, and does each test fail when the defect it guards against is planted?
rows.why: These are the identity checks the candidate must pass before production is fast-forwarded to it (the coordinator's instruction of Oct 4: the candidate deploys as soon as it is reviewed and its identity checks pass). A difference with the flag absent would change production's training by the merge alone; a prediction that moves at the switch would make the segment's first reports unreadable against the reports before it.
inputs: Branch restart/candidate-heads-2026-10-04 (worktree C:/Users/bhart/Documents/UEMA_wt/candidate_heads) and production's commit 8472d72fc, extracted by git archive into a scratch folder.

The small H84-shaped learner of mimo_bridge/tests/motor_asked_change_fixture.py: built by the trainer's own builder from H84's learner flags at width 32, 3 bodies, CPU, seeded synthetic frames (no world, no checkpoint of production).

Production's flags on that learner: --vestibular-encoder-repair rescale_restart --agency-prior 0 --contact-control-wellness 2 --motor-asked-change on (--self-percept-release on needs the self-state module, which needs body-function frames from a MuJoCo world: the fixture builds none, as in the motor candidate's checks).

Production's own checkpoint ckpt_step_479350 of run H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41m_0402 (the state production resumes), read only, with its optimizer state and the replay ring of its episode companion; the run's own args.json as the launch settings, on the CPU.
steps: Unit tests on the commit: mimo_bridge/tests/test_heads_all_slot_path.py (the path alone; the learner with the path switched on at a checkpoint trained without it; the stats block with the lesson's gradient reading), test_heads_all_slot_path_watch.py (the watch program's stop lines, early lines and late pass lines), and the test files of the code the branch touches: the asked-change path and its watch, the residual prediction, the gaze copy's heads, the liveness repair, the hourly watcher, the swap-test phases, the transition contract.
Planted defects: each defect is one text substitution on a copy of the source, followed by the tests named for it; the clean copy must pass and every planted copy must fail a test.

Lockstep: production's commit and the branch drive the fixture the same number of model steps with the flag absent (replay every second model step, liveness revivals planted so that a stray forward pass would move weights); every model step's loss, gradient norm, command, gaze, loss breakdown, wellness values, tokens, predictions and random streams, and every 10th model step a hash over every weight and Adam state, must be equal. Then the branch with the flag on: equal while every output layer is zero, different afterwards.

Resume from production's state on the fixture: production's code trains the fixture with production's flags and saves; production's code, the branch with the flag absent and the branch with --heads-all-slot-path on each load that save and train on. Flag absent: every model step equal to production's. Flag on: the load's switch check must read 0.0 on 64 probe rows, the first resumed model step's predictions, loss and tokens must equal production's, and with the output layers put back to zero after every optimizer update every model step must equal production's in every recorded value and in every hash over the shared weights.

Resume from production's checkpoint 479,350: production's code and the branch, each in a process of its own, build the learner on the CPU from the run's args.json, load the checkpoint with its optimizer state and attach the checkpoint's replay ring; each runs the same 12 replay updates (the trainer's own replay_update on the ring's windows, the random streams seeded alike). Compared: each update's loss (exact), the heads' predictions on one fixed batch of 8 ring windows before the first update (exact), and a hash over every weight and Adam state the builds share after the last update. Arms: production's code; the branch with the flag absent; the branch with the flag on and every output layer put back to zero after each update; the branch with the flag on left free. The flag-on load must write its switch record with 0.0 on 64 probe rows; the heads' predictions on 64 probe rows must also be bit-identical with and without the path under the CPU's bf16 autocast.
The first candidate's lockstep in production's three launch settings (docs/gain_of_function_v4/swap_test_phases/lockstep_vs_production.py), flag absent.
measures: Counts: tests passed of tests run; planted defects caught of planted; model steps equal of model steps compared; state hashes equal of hashes compared.
The switch check's largest absolute change of any prediction on the probe rows (0.0 = bit-identical predictions with and without the path).
The first model step at which the flag-on run differs from the flag-off run (it must not be before an output layer has moved).
rows.pass_line: Every unit test passes; every planted defect is caught; flag absent equals production at every model step and in every state hash, in the lockstep and in the resume; flag on reads 0.0 at the switch, equals production at the first resumed model step, equals it at every model step when the output layers are held at zero, and differs from it once they move.
rows.pass_line_basis: Identity is exact by construction when the flag is absent (the path is not built, PredictionHeads finds no path in its instance dict) and at the switch (every output layer is zero and the sum is formed after the head's own output), so any difference is a defect; the motor candidate's same checks read 120 of 120 and 230 of 230 model steps equal (RESTART_CANDIDATE_MOTOR_2026-10-03.md section 3). The check can fail: the planted defects include an output layer that does not start at zero, a path that moves its centre in a measurement pass and a path whose parameters are not appended last.
