rows.title: The heads watch's stop lines on the lineage's own record with nothing switched
rows.question: Taking every full report of the H84 lineage as if the all-slot paths had been switched on there, with nothing switched: how often would the watch program's stop lines on the senses' error ratios and on the step rate have stopped the run, how often would they have alerted, and do they stop the planted faults?
rows.why: A stop line that fires on the lineage's own variation stops production for nothing, and one that never fires protects nothing. The production segment's row cites these counts as its false-stop arithmetic; the operator's rule is that every declared line ships with the control that would catch it lying.
inputs: Every stats file of the lineage (Saved/mimo_bridge/experiments/H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg*/replay_training_stats.jsonl in the production checkout, read only): the full reports (records whose next-model-step window holds 100 model steps) from model step 344,600 to the newest, each with the five senses' error ratios, the step rate and the count of non-finite updates; and the trainer logs' lines about skipped optimizer updates.
The watch program docs/gain_of_function_v4/heads_all_slot_path_watch.py of the branch (its own judge and lines).
steps: Read every full report into the watch program's own compact form; where a relaunch ran model steps again, keep the record written last.

Take each full report as a switch position N: the reports up to it are the reports before the switch (the last 20 for the early line, up to 100 for the level), the reports after it through the first one at or past N + 10,000 are the watch. Run the watch program's judge with a switch record that is as declared.

Count, per stretch of positions (since model steps 344,600, 382,800, 415,200 and 455,900): positions, stops, alerts, per line, by the number of full reports since the last relaunch, and at positions a relaunch follows directly.

Planted faults (the vestibular plan's): a sense's ratio multiplied from a report on, the step rate halved or creeping, multiplied into the lineage's own reports at every position since 415,200 whose unplanted watch neither stops nor alerts; count the positions at which the stop comes within 2 windows.

Second round (written Oct 4, 2026 before it ran), for the two stop lines the coordinator declared on Oct 4: line M7 (proprioception's own-command reading over a window of 1,000 model steps at or under 3.14 times its standard error; judged only at positions whose 20 reports before already read above that floor) and line M8 (a head's audited error ratio above its value over the 20 reports before the switch by more than its spread in two windows of 1,000 model steps running) are judged at every position by the watch program's own judge and counted with the other lines. The audit section measures what the two lines are set from: per head the largest rise of one 10-report window's pooled error ratio over the 20 reports before it, at every position whose reports carry the hold-first audit (from model step 458,000); proprioception's own-command reading with its standard error in every separate window since model step 475,900; per head the standard error of one window's pooled error ratio.
measures: Stops and alerts with nothing switched, as counts of positions (0 = the lines never fire on the lineage's own variation).
Planted faults stopped, as counts of positions (all = the line catches the fault wherever it is planted).
The lines on a path's hidden layer and on the paths' output are silent here: the lineage's records carry no such block.
The audit section's largest rise per head, in units of the error ratio (0 = exact, 1 = no better than no change): the watch program's spread constants are these numbers.
rows.pass_line: Since model step 415,200: 0 stops with nothing switched; and proprioception at 2.5 times its level from report 42 stopped at every position.
rows.pass_line_basis: The asked-change watch's same lines read 0 stops and 0 alerts in 409 positions since 415,200 on the record as it stood on Oct 3 (RESTART_CANDIDATE_MOTOR_2026-10-03.md section 5.2); this run reads the record as it stands on Oct 4, which adds the reports since 470,500: the asked-change switch at 474,875, two relaunches and the scheduler's tests beside training. A stop found there would be a false stop of this watch at today's switch and is reported at once.

cost.where: CPU only, reading stats files; run under the coordinator's training hold of Oct 4, 2026 (it reads no file a trainer writes while it runs)
cost.basis: the asked-change watch's same tool ran 18 s on Oct 3 at 0.02 GB

rows.on_pass: The production segment's row cites the counts as its false-stop arithmetic.
rows.on_fail: A stop with nothing switched: the position and the line are named in the record, and the line's multiple or its window is changed before the segment (with the count run again), never after.
rows.result: 1,282 full reports from model step 344,600 to 479,300, 106 trainer logs with 0 lines about a skipped optimizer update. With nothing switched: 0 stops and 0 alerts in the 497 switch positions since model step 415,200 (5 watches whose reports after the switch do not overlap) and in the 114 since 455,900; 5 stops in 1,167 positions since 344,600 (4 on the step rate at 375,100 to 379,100 and 1 on the early line at 373,000, the vestibular plan's own counts). The audit: at the 94 positions whose 20 reports before carry the hold-first audit (460,000 to 469,300), the largest rise of any of the 10 windows over the 20 reports before is 0.1551 for vision, 0.0177 for tactile, 0.1553 for audio and 0.0121 for vestibular; proprioception's largest rise from one separate window to a later one since 475,500 is 0.0748 (3 windows). A planted rise of 1.5 spreads from the switch on stops at 94 of 94 positions for each of the five heads. Proprioception's own-command reading in the 3 separate windows since 475,900 is 0.324, 0.404 and 0.400 with standard errors of 0.027 to 0.029: 11.3, 15.2 and 13.6 standard errors. One window's standard error of the error ratio: tactile 0.0024, vestibular 0.0013, proprioception 0.0046, vision 0.027, audio 0.028 (medians of 20 windows). Of the 30 planted faults of the vestibular plan, 25 stop at every clean position; the 5 others are the inherited lines' known gaps (a tactile ratio 1.55 times its level from report 2 stops at 179 of 497 positions; vision 3 times its level from report 22 at none; the step rate halved from report 42 at 42).
rows.decision: The spreads of the audited-error stop line are set to these largest rises (vision 0.156, tactile 0.0178, audio 0.156, vestibular 0.0121, proprioception 0.075); their false-stop count of 0 is in-sample. The pass line is met: 0 stops since 415,200, and proprioception at 2.5 times its level from report 42 is stopped at every position.

rows.title: What the encoder tokens and the command hold about the next tactile and vestibular token, with no transformer (checkpoint 479,350's replay ring)
rows.question: Fitted straight from the 6 encoder tokens of the last 3 model steps and the command, with no transformer and no head: how far below the no-change error can the next token of each sense be predicted on bodies the fit did not see, 50 ms ahead and at the end of the 250 ms hold, and does that prediction's error depend on the command (own command against the size-matched swapped command)?
rows.why: The production segment of the all-slot paths declares a late pass line 'error below the no-change error' for tactile and vestibular. The bench on the transformer's output cannot say whether that line can be met, because the transformer was never trained on those two lessons (their gradient on its output reads 1e-13 per number). This probe goes around the transformer, so it gives the line that the model's own inputs allow. The coordinator's rule of Oct 4, 2026: if the probe also reads 1.0 at 50 ms, the 50 ms error line is not demandable and the late line is declared at the horizon where the probe shows something, or as a watched reading with its goal line unmeasured.
inputs: The episode companion of Saved/mimo_bridge/experiments/H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41m_0402/checkpoints/ckpt_step_479350 (read only): the trainer's replay ring, per body the newest 6,000 model steps; per model step the 6 encoder tokens of 192 numbers (vision, tactile, audio, proprioception, motor, vestibular), the achieved pose (26 body handles x 10 numbers), the executed command (26 body handles x 9 numbers), which senses were real, the episode number.
D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/candidate_heads/captures/capture_479350_big.pt for the sequence of the 6 slots, the eyes' handle index and the replay action contract only.
No model is built; no weight is read.
steps: Rows: one body at one model step t whose model steps t-2 to the target lie in one episode and carry an executed command under production's action contract. 50 ms rows: target = token(t+1) minus token(t). 250 ms rows: only model steps at which the held command changed and then stayed the same through t+4 (the hold is 5 model steps); target = token(t+5) minus token(t).

Features of a row (3,758 numbers): the 6 tokens of model steps t-2 and t-1, the 5 tokens of model step t without the motor token, the achieved pose at t (260 numbers), the command (234 numbers). The swapped arm replaces the command by the previous body's command at the same model step, taken as a change from that body's pose and applied to this body's pose (lem/model/contact_head.shuffled_order).

Two folds: fit on bodies 0, 1, 3, 4 and read on 5, 6, 7; then fit on 4, 5, 6, 7 and read on 0, 1, 3. Body 2 is in neither. Features centred and divided by their standard deviation on the training rows.
Fit 1, ridge regression: the penalty (one of 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 100 times the row count) chosen on the last training body, kept out of that fit; then fitted on all four training bodies.

Fit 2, one network 3,758 -> 512 -> GELU -> 192: AdamW, learning rate 1e-3, weight decay 0.01, batches of 256, at most 40 passes over three training bodies; the weights kept are those of the pass with the lowest error on the fourth.

Per sense (tactile, vestibular; proprioception, vision and audio as the fits' own control), horizon, fold and fit, on the training bodies and on the held-out bodies: the two readings below with a two-level bootstrap standard error (bodies, then rows).

Second run (written Oct 4, 2026 before it ran): every standardised feature is limited to between -6 and 6 training standard deviations. The first run read 7.0 for proprioception's ridge fit in the fold that reads bodies 0, 1, 3 and 0.64 in the other fold: a feature that hardly varies on the training bodies becomes hundreds of standard deviations on a held-out body and the linear map multiplies it. The first run's file is kept as probe_479350_run1.json.

Third run (written Oct 4, 2026 before it ran): every feature first has the body's own mean over that body's rows subtracted (inputs only; no target enters; the swapped arm is shifted by the same vector). The second run's limit of 6 standard deviations left proprioception's ridge fit at 4.2 in the fold that reads bodies 0, 1, 3: a body's tokens and pose carry a part that is the same at every model step of that body, and on a body the fit never saw that part enters the linear map as a constant offset of the predicted change. The second run's file is kept as probe_479350_run2.json.
measures: Error over no-change error: summed squared error / summed squared size of the token's change. 1 = no better than predicting that the token stays as it is, 0 = exact.

Own-command reading: 1 - error with the own command / error with the swapped command. 0 = the command makes no difference to the error, 1 = the own command leaves no error. The live trainer's reading of the same kind for proprioception since model step 475,000: 0.33.

The control of the fits: proprioception, whose head reads 0.82 and whose live own-command reading is 0.33. A probe that reads 1.0 and 0 for proprioception would be a probe that cannot find what is there.
rows.pass_line: DEMANDABLE for a sense at a horizon when, in both folds, the better fit's held-out error over no-change error is below 1.0 by more than 3 of its standard errors. COMMAND-DEPENDENT when, in both folds, that fit's held-out own-command reading is above 0 by more than 3 of its standard errors.
rows.pass_line_basis: Declared before the run. 3 standard errors: with 5 senses x 2 horizons x 2 folds = 20 readings, one false pass by chance at 3 standard errors has a probability of about 0.03. A sense that misses the line at 50 ms and meets it at 250 ms gets its late pass line at 250 ms; a sense that misses both gets a watched reading with its goal line written as unmeasured. Reachability of the probe itself: its control (proprioception) is expected to pass both rules, since the model's own head already reads 0.82 and 0.24 on these bodies.

cost.where: CPU only, one process, 8 threads, below-normal priority, under 5 GB of RAM and 9 GB committed (the hold limits). Training is stopped while it runs: the coordinator holds training at model step 479,350 since Oct 4, 2026, 6:56 AM PDT for this chain; this work starts no trainer and writes no control file
cost.basis: the capture of the same companion read its ring in 34 s at 1.95 GB committed; the fits are 20 ridge solutions of 3,758 unknowns and 20 networks of 2 million weights

rows.on_pass: The production segment's row declares the tactile and vestibular late error line at the horizon the probe passes, with the probe's held-out reading as its reachability.
rows.on_fail: The production segment's row declares the tactile and vestibular error as a watched reading with its goal line written as unmeasured, and the record states the probe's readings.
rows.result: Run 3 (per-body centring; runs 1 and 2 are kept as probe_479350_run1.json and _run2.json). 47,976 rows at 50 ms and 9,584 at the end of the 250 ms hold; the ridge fit is the better fit everywhere. Held-out, fold 0 and fold 1, error over no-change error with its standard error, then the own-command reading with its standard error. 50 ms: tactile 0.877 (0.005) and 0.902 (0.014), own 0.007 (0.003) and 0.003 (0.002); vestibular 0.963 (0.011) and 1.030 (0.068), own 0.052 (0.003) and 0.041 (0.015); proprioception 0.650 (0.006) and 0.966 (0.562), own 0.520 (0.104) and 0.575 (0.053); vision 0.610 and 0.674, own 0.077 and 0.066; audio 0.879 and 0.896, own 0.005 and 0.000. 250 ms: tactile 0.773 and 0.813, own 0.037 and 0.012; vestibular 0.849 and 1.060, own 0.142 and 0.087; proprioception 0.525 and 0.761, own 0.629 and 0.561; vision 0.832 and 0.835; audio 0.673 and 0.710. By the row's rule: tactile is DEMANDABLE at both horizons and not COMMAND-DEPENDENT; vestibular is not DEMANDABLE (one fold above 1.0) and its own-command reading clears 3 standard errors in one fold (20) and reads 2.7 in the other; the control (proprioception) is COMMAND-DEPENDENT in both folds and DEMANDABLE in one (the other fold's standard error is 0.56).

These readings are the goal references of row heads_all_slot_path_production_segment.

rows.title: Vestibular token: where head tilt is lost between the 29 raw inputs and the token, stage by stage
rows.question: On the replayed consecutive inputs of H84's 8 bodies: at which stage between the 29 raw vestibular numbers and the token does a held-out linear read-out of each body's change of head tilt within 100 model steps stop working, for the encoder as saved at checkpoints 461,631 and 479,350?
rows.why: The trainer's probe reads no head tilt from the vestibular token (row vestibular_repair_restart_segment, reading A4: -0.6 of 100 against a goal of 25), and at checkpoint 479,350 the transformer's output does not predict the next vestibular token. A repair has to act on the stage that loses the tilt: the input's scaling, a layer inside the encoder, the last layer, the card's bf16 rounding of the token, or what training does to the token between model steps. The decision that depends on it: which repair of the vestibular encoder is built and offered for a production segment.
inputs: The replay job's files (row vestibular_token_inputs_replay_459961, D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/vestibular_token2/replay_459961/replay_b0.npz to replay_b7.npz): per body 1,670 consecutive model steps of the 29 raw vestibular numbers in their own units (head accelerometer in g, gyro / 2 rad/s, neck angles -1 to 1 of each joint's range, neck speeds / 1.5 rad/s, neck efforts -1 to 1, the trunk's up direction, support shares 0 to 1, total support in body weights, effort, the share of joints at a limit, motor capacity 0 to 1, the validity flag), and the world's up direction written in the head accelerometer's frame at the same physics frame (a unit vector: where gravity alone pulls in the head).

The vestibular encoder's 14 tensors of checkpoints 461,631 and 479,350 (model.safetensors, read only) and each checkpoint's saved running mean and variance of the 28 input fields (runtime_state.pt, read only).
A freshly initialised encoder of the same shape (torch's default initialisation, seed 0): the control for what the shape alone passes.
No world, no model beyond the encoder's seven layers, no trainer, no learning.
steps: Form each row's encoder input: the 28 fields without the validity flag, clipped to +-4, minus the checkpoint's saved running mean, divided by its saved running spread, clipped to +-4.

Compute every stage of the encoder for every row in float32: the input (28 numbers), each Linear's output, each LayerNorm's output, each hidden layer's output after GELU (192 numbers each), the last layer's output, the token; and the token again on the bf16 grid the graphics card computes on (each Linear's input, weight, bias and output rounded to bf16).

Read-out, the trainer's own probe restated: group the rows into reports of 100 consecutive model steps; take a stage's numbers and a label's numbers as each body's change from its own mean over the report; fit a ridge regression (strength 1e-3 of the mean diagonal) on the even-numbered bodies and score it on the odd ones, and the other way round. Control: the same with every body's stage numbers paired with the previous body's label at the same model step.

Labels: head tilt as the trainer's probe defines it (the accelerometer's unit direction, 3 numbers); the trunk's roll (its sine and cosine); gravity in the head (the world's up direction in the head sensor's frame, 3 numbers); each of the 28 input fields in the encoder's units.

Feed the trainer's own probe class (mimo_bridge/vestibular_sense.BalanceProbe) the same tokens and raw vectors model step by model step and compare its reading with the restated read-out on the same last 10 reports.
Fit the token's 192 changes within a report on the 28 input changes by least squares: the share of the token's change a linear map of the input gives, and the part each group of input fields gives.

Per field: its saved running spread, its root-mean-square change within a report in units of that spread, the share of values either clip changed. For the token: its spread between the bodies, between a body's reports, within a report, and the float32 token minus the bf16-grid token.
Write stage_readouts.json after every encoder.

AMENDED Oct 4, 2026 8:21 AM PDT, before the second run, on the coordinator's review of the first run's result (the second hidden layer's output read -0.010 and a linear map of it, the third Linear, 0.33; a linear read-out cannot gain information through a linear layer, so the read-out with one ridge strength relative to the stage's mean diagonal reads a stage mostly through its largest numbers). Added: (a) the same read-out with every stage number divided by its root mean square over the fitted bodies' rows and the ridge strength chosen on the fitted bodies (each of them left out in turn; strengths 1e-8 to 10 per row); (b) for the stages from the second hidden layer on, the head-tilt read-out from the stage's first 1, 2, 4, ... 192 principal components, with the share of the stage's change those components hold; (c) the change per number within a report that a linear map of the 3 head-accelerometer inputs gives at the third hidden layer, the last layer and the token, beside the stage's whole change and the bf16 rounding's size. The second run writes D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/vestibular_token2/stage_readouts_v2/stage_readouts.json; the first run's file is kept.
measures: R squared of each read-out on the scored bodies: 1 = every scored change of the label within a report predicted exactly, 0 = no better than predicting no change, below 0 = worse. The trainer's acceptance line A4 for the token is 0.25. Beside each: the same for the body-shuffled control (0 expected, since the bodies move independently).
The size of what is read: the root-mean-square change of head tilt, of gravity in the head and of the trunk's roll within a report, in degrees.
Token sizes per number (a token's 192 numbers have root mean square 1): spread between the 8 bodies at one model step, within a report, and the difference the bf16 rounding makes.
The share of the token's change within a report that follows each group of input fields (0 = none of it, 1 = all of it).
rows.pass_line: A measurement with a declared reading rule, no pass or fail of the model. RULE 1 (the input): the 28 input numbers read head tilt at 0.5 or more with the control under 0.05; if not, the tilt is lost at the input (its scaling or clipping). RULE 2 (the stage): going from the input to the token, the stage where tilt is lost is the first stage whose head-tilt R squared is under 0.25 while the stage before it reads 0.25 or more; a float32 token at 0.25 or more with the bf16-grid token under 0.25 names the bf16 rounding. RULE 3 (nothing lost at fixed weights): if the bf16-grid token reads 0.25 or more, the encoder as saved carries tilt, and the trainer's reading near 0 comes from the lived stream (the weights change at every model step) or from the probe; the lived-token read-out (its own row) then decides. CHECK: the trainer's probe class and the restated read-out agree within 0.01 on the same 10 reports; if not, no reading of this job is used until the difference is explained. AMENDED Oct 4, 2026 8:21 AM PDT (second run): RULE 4, the two cases apart: with every number scaled to unit spread and the ridge chosen on the fitted bodies, a last layer or bf16-grid token that reads head tilt at 0.25 or more HOLDS the tilt at a size too small against its other change (the case of the lineage's other scale defects); one that still reads under 0.25 does not hold it in a form a linear reader finds at any scale the rounding leaves.
rows.pass_line_basis: Reachability of rule 1: the head-tilt label is the accelerometer's unit direction, which is fields 0 to 2 of the input divided by their length, so a linear read-out of the centred input reads it except for the changes of the length (the accelerometer's size reaches 2.4 g at the 99th percentile under babble against 1.0 g at rest: mimo_bridge/vestibular_adapter.py MEASUREMENT). 0.25 is the trainer's own acceptance line A4 for the token (docs/gain_of_function_v4/agents/vestibular_encoder_2026-09-25.md section 6). The replay parts from the lived trajectory after 8 model steps (first run of row vestibular_token_inputs_replay_459961: head direction within 0.4 degrees at the median and 3.1 degrees at most over 200 model steps), so by that row's pairing rule these rows are consecutive inputs of H84's own worlds under H84's own commands, and every stage here is computed from them by one fixed encoder; no lived token enters. The fresh encoder shows what a read-out of this kind gives when no lesson has shaped the layers.

cost.where: the CPU, with training held at checkpoint 479,350: one process, 4 threads, under a hard limit of 2.9 GB of RAM and 6 GB committed, no graphics card; ended when a trainer process starts
cost.basis: 13,360 rows through a 4-layer network of width 192 and 13 stages x 36 labels of 192 x 192 ridge solves: seconds each on 4 threads. Memory: 13,360 x 192 x 13 stages in float64 is 0.27 GB per encoder.

rows.on_pass: The stage named by the rules is reported to the coordinator at once and the repair is built for that stage; the readings go into this row and into docs/gain_of_function_v4/agents/vestibular_token_2026-10-04.md on branch fix/vestibular_token_readouts-2026-10-03.
rows.on_fail: The check between the trainer's probe class and the restated read-out fails: the read-out code is corrected and the job run again before any stage is named. Fewer than 6 replayed bodies: the job runs on the bodies there are and the row says so.

values: Ran Oct 4, 2026 8:16 AM PDT, 14 s, largest RAM 0.74 GB, on the 8 replayed bodies x 1,670 model steps (13,360 rows, 16 reports of 100 model steps). Within a report the bodies' head tilt changed by 18.9 degrees (root mean square), gravity in the head by 6.9 degrees, the trunk's roll by 4.4 degrees.

CHECK met: the trainer's own probe class and the restated read-out read the same on the same 10 reports (head tilt 0.0186 and 0.0186 on the token of the encoder of 461,631; -0.0378 and -0.0378 on that of 479,350).

RULE 1 met: the 28 input numbers read head tilt at 0.56 (control -0.008), gravity in the head at 0.66 and the trunk's roll at 0.99. The tilt is in the encoder's input in linear form; either clip changed 0.08 and 1.2 of every 100 values.

RULE 2, the encoder saved at 461,631 (5,831 updates after its revival): every stage from the first Linear to the third hidden layer's output reads head tilt at 0.40 to 0.64; the last layer's output reads -0.002 and the token 0.020 (float32) and 0.020 (bf16 grid). The tilt is lost at the last layer.

RULE 2, the encoder saved at 479,350: the first Linear to the second LayerNorm read 0.56 to 0.61; the second hidden layer's output reads -0.010, the third Linear 0.33, the third LayerNorm 0.35, the third hidden layer's output -0.013, the last layer's output -0.010, the token -0.024 (float32) and -0.014 (bf16 grid). By the rule the first stage under 0.25 is the second hidden layer's output; a linear map of it (the third Linear) reads 0.33 again, so there the tilt is still present at a size the read-out's ridge discounts, and it is gone at the last layer's output and the token.

A freshly initialised encoder of the same shape reads head tilt at 0.42 at its third hidden layer, 0.42 at its last layer and 0.41 at its token (control -0.05): the shape passes the tilt; training removed it.

Not the bf16 rounding: the float32 token and the bf16-grid token read the same within 0.01 at both checkpoints, and the rounding changes the token by 0.0017 per number within a report against a token change of 0.057 (479,350) and 0.164 (461,631).

The whole input is lost, not only the tilt: read back from the token (bf16 grid), 27 of the 28 input fields read under 0.25 with the encoder of 479,350 (the one above: a neck angle at 0.45; none of the others above 0.21), 26 of 28 with that of 461,631 (a neck angle at 0.39, one number of the trunk's up direction at 0.45); from the fresh encoder's token 24 of 28 read above 0.5 and 2 under 0.25.

What the trained token's change within a report follows (least squares on the input's change; 0.72 of the token's change is a linear map of it at 479,350): the neck angles 0.53, the motor capacity 0.09, the neck speeds 0.06, the trunk's up direction 0.03, the head accelerometer 0.004. At 461,631: neck angles 0.19, neck speeds 0.18, trunk up 0.09, head accelerometer 0.000.

The token's sizes per number, replayed rows: spread between the 8 bodies 0.37 (461,631) and 0.25 (479,350), a fresh encoder 0.68; change between two consecutive model steps 0.080, 0.020 and 0.58; change within a report 0.164, 0.057 and 0.65. The trained token changes 29 times less from one model step to the next than a fresh encoder's on the same inputs.

SECOND RUN (Oct 4, 2026 8:21 AM PDT, 54 s, 0.75 GB; the amended steps). Why the first run's second hidden layer read under a linear map of itself: the trained stages' change within a report sits in very few directions. Share of a stage's change held by its 2 largest principal components: the token 0.999 (encoder of 461,631) and 0.967 (479,350), a fresh encoder's token 0.20; the third hidden layer's output 0.98 and 0.93 against 0.21. The 8th component's variance over the first one's: 2e-7 and 2e-5 at the token against 0.3 for a fresh encoder. One ridge strength on such a stage reads only the 2 to 4 large directions.

RULE 4, the encoder of 461,631: the last layer and the float32 token HOLD the tilt at a size too small against their other change: with every number scaled to unit spread they read 0.30 and 0.28 (control 0.00), and from principal components 0.27 to 0.33 only once 64 or more components are read, components whose variance is 2e-11 or less of the first one's (0.000005 of its size). On the bf16 grid the graphics card computes on, the same token reads -0.01 scaled and 0.02 or less from any number of components: the rounding (0.0017 per number) is larger than the tilt's part, so the model never received it.

RULE 4, the encoder of 479,350: the last layer and the token do NOT hold the tilt at any size a read-out that has to carry over to other bodies finds: scaled to unit spread they read -0.92 and -1.80 (float32) and -0.02 (bf16 grid); from the first 1 to 8 principal components (all of the change) -0.05 to 0.00, and from more components -0.2 to -4.6 (a fit on four bodies' small directions does not carry over to the other four). Inside the encoder the last stage that reads it at both scalings is the second LayerNorm (0.59 plain, 0.57 scaled); the second hidden layer's output holds it in its 33rd to 64th components (0.39 from 64 components, each under 1e-3 of the first one's variance), the third LayerNorm reads 0.35 plain and 0.24 scaled, the third hidden layer's output reads it from no number of components.

The scaled read-out is not a safe single number on the trained stages: where a stage holds numbers that change in some bodies only, dividing by their small spread makes the fit carry over badly (readings of -0.3 to -4.6 above). The component read-out is the one used for the two cases. On the input, the first hidden layers and the fresh encoder the plain and the scaled read-outs agree within 0.03.

What the trained token's change is made of (479,350): 0.68 of the last layer's change within a report is a linear map of the input's change, of which the neck angles give 0.51, the motor capacity 0.08, the neck speeds 0.06; the head accelerometer 0.004.
result.verdict: the tilt is in the input (0.56) and is lost inside the encoder by training (a fresh encoder's token reads 0.41). At 461,631 the last layer still held it at 0.000005 of the size of the token's main change, under the card's rounding. At 479,350 the last layer and the token hold it at no size; the token's change within a report sits in 2 directions (0.97 of it) that follow the neck angles. Not a case for rescaling one layer: the content has to be put back at a set size and kept.

rows.decision: Reported to the coordinator (the stage, 8:19 AM PDT; the two cases apart after the coordinator's review, in the record). Next: the bench of the two lessons that reach the encoder directly, with the repair path (row vestibular_token_path_bench). Written Oct 4, 2026 8:23 AM PDT.

rows.title: Vestibular token: head tilt in the lived tokens and in the transformer's output at checkpoint 479,350
rows.question: On the model steps production lived before checkpoint 479,350: does a held-out linear read-out find each body's change of gravity in the head (head tilt without the head's own acceleration) and of the trunk's roll within 100 model steps in the vestibular token as the trainer computed it, in the other senses' tokens, and in the transformer's output?
rows.why: The stage read-outs (row vestibular_token_stage_readouts) compute every encoder stage from replayed inputs with one fixed set of weights. The model itself consumes the token as lived (computed by weights that change at every model step, on the graphics card's bf16 grid), and the prediction heads read the transformer's output. Whether tilt is absent there too, and whether the transformer's output holds it from another sense, decides where a repair has to put it. The decision that depends on it: the same as the stage read-outs' (which repair is built).

rows.title: Planner's four weaknesses: BEFORE reading at 479,350
rows.question: On checkpoint 479,350 (prediction heads not yet repaired): per sense, how much of the planner's goal distance differs between candidate commands in prediction and in the real outcome; how old and how far is the goal against what the body covers in one 250 ms hold; does predicted wellness rank candidate commands as their realised wellness ranks them; and does the planned command, whose strength the search cuts, end nearer its goal in the real world than the motor controller's own command?
rows.why: The operator's decision of Oct 4, 2026: wellness changes behaviour through the planner's search, with no network trained to raise wellness and no hand-coded goal. Four weaknesses of the search stay after the prediction-head repair. Three switches answer them: --goal-sense-weights own_command (new), --goal-locality on, --prospective-wellness add. This reading is the BEFORE of each, taken with one probe that is re-run unchanged on the first checkpoint trained with the head repair. Which switch goes into a production segment first, and each segment's pass and stop lines, are set from these numbers and their noise (docs/gain_of_function_v4/restart_candidate/RESTART_CANDIDATE_PLANNER_2026-10-04.md on branch restart/candidate-planner-2026-10-04).
inputs: Production checkpoint ckpt_step_479350 of run H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41m_0402 (read only) and its saved eight-world episode.
32 saved planning decisions: 8 bodies x 4, at least 20 model steps apart, each a planning event of the checkpoint's own behaviour (the planner-candidate probe's start rule).

Per decision the five candidate commands of the production causal chain (the planner's chosen command, hold, the motor controller's own command, two perturbations of the chosen command at the babble's size, seeded as production seeds them), each 26 body handles x 9 numbers.

Per decision four replanned commands from the decision's own captured state (context, pose, smoother state, random stream): weighted = the goal distance with each sense's part multiplied by its weight; local = the goal picked by goal locality's rule on the decision's goal ring; prospective = today's search plus 0.15 x (1 - the approximate evaluator's mean of tactile_comfort, capability and motor_state on the predicted next tokens); effort_off = today's search with the effort term's weight at 0 instead of 0.01 (no launch flag sets this: it measures what the effort term does to the real outcome).

The weights of the weighted arm: per sense, the lower bound (reading minus 2 standard errors, floored at 0) of the swap test's own-command reading on the hold's first model step, from the run's last 20 stats reports at or before 479,350 (block prediction_audit_hold_first, size-matched control); weight = 5 x lower bound / the sum of the five lower bounds.

The saved episode's replay ring (the newest 3,000 model steps of every body: each sense's raw token, 192 numbers) and the run's causal-chain record (every planning event's goal age and planned strength).
The probe script planner_weaknesses_v1 and the planner-candidate probe version 3 it imports; their SHA-256 digests are written into declaration.json.
steps: Build the checkpoint's model on the CPU with learning off (weights hashed before and after; a change stops the probe). Read the replay ring's token changes over 1, 5, 14, 50, 100 and 200 model steps, then drop the ring from memory.
Per body, restore its saved world and model state; run the model's own behaviour to the next planning event; save a snapshot.

Recompute the goal ranking on the decision's goal ring; it must give the ring index the decision recorded, else the probe stops. Apply goal locality's rule: distance of a ring model step = the mean over the active senses of the mean squared token difference to the present; radius = the ring's mean distance between model steps 14 apart; the pick is the largest ranked value within the radius.

Run the search again from the decision's captured state with nothing changed; its command must equal the chosen command exactly, else the probe stops. On this run read the gradient of the goal term and of the effort term (0.01 x sum of squared strength) at the starting command. Then run the four replanned arms.

Predict every command 1 model step ahead on the planner's route (each sense's token, the approximate evaluator's five terms). The five candidates' predicted wellness sums and goal distances must equal the production planning record's to 0.001, else the probe stops.

Execute each command from the identical restored snapshot for its 5-model-step hold, twice; the two physical traces must be bit-identical. After every model step read each sense's top-down-gated token, the five grounded wellness terms and the pose of the 26 handles.

Per decision compute: per sense the goal distance at the decision, predicted and real (after 1 model step and after the hold) for every command; the real token change over one hold; strength, handle displacement in cm and handle turn in degrees per command.
Summarise over the 32 decisions with a 95% interval from resampling whole bodies (5,000 draws) and the count of bodies on each side of zero. Write result.json.
measures: Share of the goal distance per sense (the five shares sum to 1).

Per sense, (largest - smallest goal distance among the five candidates) / the goal distance at the decision, in prediction and in the real outcome: 0 = every candidate command gives the same distance (a command of this size changes nothing), 1 = the candidates differ by the whole distance.

Goal age in model steps: 0 = the present model step, 199 = the oldest of the goal ring. Goal distance / the real token change over one hold: 1 = the goal is as far as the sense changes in one hold, 10 = ten times as far (squared token units).

Goal locality: today's goal's distance / the ring's 14-model-step radius (Sep 6 basis: 1.6 to 1.9); goals inside the radius out of 100; ranked value given up by the pick inside the radius, as a share of the ring's value range (0 = same goal, 1 = the whole range).
Wellness ranking: candidate pairs out of 100 that the predicted five-term sum ranks as the realised grounded sum ranks them (50 = chance, 80 to 90 = a ranking a search can use, 100 = every pair).

Strength of the planned command and of the motor controller's own command (0 = no force asked, 1 = full); real handle displacement over the hold in cm; length of the goal term's gradient on strength / the effort term's (0 = the effort term alone sets the strength, 1 = equally long).

Per arm and for production's planner: the summed goal distance after the hold under the planned command minus under the motor controller's own command from the same saved state (below 0 = the planned command ended nearer its goal), and 1 - planned / motor controller's (0 = no nearer, 1 = on the goal, below 0 = farther).

Per replanned arm against production's planner from the same saved state: goal distance after the hold, strength and handle displacement, arm minus planner (below 0 on the distance = the arm ended nearer today's goal).
Noise: the replays are bit-identical, so every difference between two commands from one saved state is caused by the commands; the interval of each reading is the spread between bodies.

Ranked sequence: the weighted goal distance first, goal locality second, predicted wellness in the search last; no change to the effort term's weight. Why not the prospective term: the predicted wellness ranks 56 of 100 command pairs as realised (chance 50) and the arm's realised wellness is not above production's planner's. What would show the ranking wrong: the AFTER reading (row planner_weaknesses_after_head_repair) or a segment's own pass reading with the weighted arm's interval reaching 0, or its gain staying in audio alone, a sense whose weight is 0. rows.title: Production segment with the all-slot paths switched on beside the five prediction heads (--heads-all-slot-path on), from checkpoint 479,350
rows.question: With an all-slot path switched on beside each of the five prediction heads at model step 479,350: do the tactile and vestibular lessons' gradients reach the transformer, does tactile's prediction error fall below the no-change error, does vestibular's error become lower with the body's own command than with the size-matched swapped command, and do proprioception, vision and audio keep the readings they have today?
rows.why: The tactile, vision and vestibular prediction heads output the same vector at every model step (rows prediction_heads_state_capture and prediction_heads_state_readings: each head's attention reads one slot, that slot holds the persistent memory's constant at 20,000 to 300,000 times the size of what changes between model steps, and the graphics card's 8-bit arithmetic rounds the changing part away), so the tactile and vestibular lessons have sent the transformer a gradient of 3e-10 and 6e-10 per number against proprioception's 4e-5. The operator's instruction of Oct 4, 2026: the heads come before training. The decision that depends on this segment: the paths stay in production's command (pass), or production returns to checkpoint 479,350 without the flag and the fallback is taken, the Sep 26 repair's third round that unlocks the old attention pools (stop or miss).
inputs: Checkpoint Saved/mimo_bridge/experiments/H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41m_0402/checkpoints/ckpt_step_479350 (production's state at the coordinator's hold of Oct 4, 2026, 6:56 AM PDT), resumed by docs/gain_of_function_v4/coordinator/relaunch_h84_seg41_2026-09-29.py with one launch setting changed: --heads-all-slot-path on. Every other setting is production's last run's (among them --vestibular-encoder-repair rescale_restart --agency-prior 0 --contact-control-wellness 2 --self-percept-release on --motor-asked-change on).
The code of branch restart/candidate-heads-2026-10-04, fast-forwarded into production's checkout (the commit is named in the record's section 9).
The 8 bodies' worlds and the graphics card, as production runs them.

The watch program docs/gain_of_function_v4/heads_all_slot_path_watch.py, called by the hourly watcher (docs/h84_launch_2026-09-18/hourly_watch.py) every 5 minutes for the stop lines and every hour for the printed lines.
steps: At the load, per head, a path is built: the tensor the heads are called with (6 slots x 192 numbers) minus the persistent memory's constant, minus a running centre, LayerNorm per slot, one 192-to-32 weight matrix shared by the 6 slots, then a 2-layer network (192 -> 192 -> 192) times 1/sqrt(192), whose last layer is zero. 403,200 new weights in all. The load's switch check computes every head's prediction on 64 probe rows with and without the paths, in float32 and under the graphics card's autocast, and the trainer writes one heads_all_slot_path_switch record into the stats stream.

From the first optimizer update on, each path's output is added to its head's prediction. The paths learn from the next-model-step lesson on lived model steps and in replay (the heads' optimizer settings: AdamW, learning rate 3e-4); imagined rows pass through with the paths' weights detached.

Every 100 model steps the trainer's full report carries the block heads_all_slot_path: per head the path's output size, its hidden layer's live share, how evenly the head's whole prediction answers to the 6 slots (head_read), and the lesson's gradient on the transformer's output (lesson_gradient).

rows.title: Planner candidate: unit tests, identity, planted defects
rows.question: Does the planner branch (restart/candidate-planner-2026-10-04) pass its unit tests; does it train bit for bit as production's code with --goal-sense-weights off, and with it on before its window holds 32 audited model steps; and is each of 16 planted defects caught?
rows.why: The branch adds a switch to the planner's goal distance, a stats reading beside intention.gap_closed_pct, a planner_switch record and a watch program. Before the coordinator can merge it, the switch must be shown to change nothing while off (the operator's rule: default off and bit-identical when off), and the tests must be shown able to fail. A pass makes the branch ready for the merge steps of its record; the production-segment rows name their own lines.
inputs: The branch's code at its tip (production's tips c30b86a0e, the heads candidate, and c59ecab7e are merged into it), and production's Source/Python at commit c59ecab7e (git archive into a temporary folder).
A width-32 learner built by the trainer's own builder from H84's learner flags, 3 bodies, on seeded synthetic frames (Source/Python/mimo_bridge/tests/swap_test_fixture.py): no world, no checkpoint.
16 planted defects, each one exact text replacement in a temporary copy of the branch's code (docs/gain_of_function_v4/planner_weaknesses/planted_defects.py lists them).
steps: Unit tests: pytest on the three new test files (the switch's arithmetic and wiring, the probe's arithmetic, the watch program and the planner_switch record) and on five existing test files of the code the branch edits (planning window, transition contract, effort term, swap-test phases, hourly watcher). An existing test that fails is run again on an export of production's commit: failing there too, it is listed as failing on production's code as well and does not count against the branch; passing there, it does.

Identity: in two launch settings (--motor-hold 5 with --intention-every 10; --motor-hold 3 with --intention-every 7), production's code and the branch's code each drive the same learner for 260 model steps in a child process. Every model step each records the loss and gradient norm (exact float hex), hashes of the command and gaze sent, of the loss breakdown, of the wellness values and of three random streams; every 10 model steps a hash over every parameter, buffer, Adam state tensor and goal-ring value. Compared: the branch with the flag absent; the branch with the flag on (13 audited model steps in 260, under the 32 the weights wait for); the branch with the flag on and its window filled before the first model step. On the first setting two more runs must complete all 260 model steps and differ from production: --goal-locality on, and --prospective-wellness add (the two older switches still run on today's code under H84's learner flags).
Planted defects: each defect is planted alone, its named tests are run on the copy and must fail; the clean copy must pass before the first and after the last.
Write cpu_checks_result.json with every count and the pass flag.
measures: Unit tests passed and failed (counts).
Identity: the first model step and value at which a branch run differs from production's, or none (none = equal at all 260 model steps and in the final state hash).
Planted defects caught, 0 to 16.
rows.pass_line: Every new unit test passes and no existing test fails on this branch only (a test that also fails on an export of production's commit is listed, not counted); flag absent and flag on with an unfilled window both equal production at every model step and in the final state hash, in both settings; flag on with a filled window differs from production in both settings; 16 of 16 planted defects are caught and the clean copy passes before and after.
rows.pass_line_basis: Bit identity is reachable: with the flag absent no state is built and the goal distance's original expression runs; with an unfilled window the weights function returns no weights and the same expression runs (unit test: 42 model steps equal). The filled window must differ because proprioception then takes the whole weight (unit test: the command differs from model step 20 on). The same fixture and comparison proved the swap test's added readings identical on Oct 2 (docs/gain_of_function_v4/swap_test_phases/lockstep_vs_production.py). Runs of this row: a first attempt was ended after its unit tests to add the re-run of failing existing tests on production's export; the run of 9:07 AM PDT passed on branch commit 89bd93d6b; the row is run again on the branch's final code, which adds the switch's sentence on the explainer page and merges production's c59ecab7e.

rows.title: Vestibular encoder under its two direct lessons on the replayed rows: today's encoder, a fresh one, and the linear input path
rows.question: On the replayed consecutive inputs of H84's 8 bodies, with the two lessons whose gradient reaches the vestibular encoder without passing the transformer (VICReg over the 8 bodies at one model step, and the next-model-step lesson's token-change term): (a) does more of today's training leave the token without head tilt; (b) do the same two lessons take head tilt out of a fresh encoder's token; (c) with the linear input path added (weight zero at the start), after how many updates does a held-out read-out of each body's change of head tilt from the token reach 0.25, and does it stay there?
rows.why: The stage read-outs name where the tilt is lost; the repair has to be shown to put it into the token under the lessons production runs, before a production segment is asked for. The bench also gives the reachability arithmetic for the segment's pass line: how many updates the path needs, which sets the window in which the trainer's own probe is judged. The decision that depends on it: whether --vestibular-input-path on is offered for a production segment, and with which pass line.
inputs: The replay job's rows (row vestibular_token_inputs_replay_459961): 8 bodies x 1,670 consecutive model steps of the 29 raw vestibular numbers and of gravity in the head (a unit vector from the simulator's own orientation matrix).

Checkpoint 479,350's vestibular encoder (14 tensors), its saved AdamW state for those tensors (optimizer.pt: running mean and running mean square of each weight's gradient, 23,550 updates) and the input normaliser's saved statistics, held fixed (all read only).

The path as production would build it: lem/model/vestibular_input_path.py on branch fix/vestibular_token_readouts-2026-10-03 (one Linear(28 -> 192) without bias, weight zero at the start, output x 1/sqrt(28), added to the encoder's last-layer output in units of that output's standard deviation over its 192 numbers).
No world, no transformer, no trainer; no lesson that reaches the encoder through the transformer.
steps: Form the encoder's input of every row (28 fields, clipped, centred and scaled with the checkpoint's statistics).

Per arm, 3,000 updates, one per model step of the first 1,100 model steps in the sequence they were lived (cycled), on the 8 bodies' rows: token of model step t with gradient; loss = VICReg(token) / 6 + mean squared (token of model step t - 1 encoded again with gradient, minus the token of model step t without gradient); AdamW with the checkpoint's learning rate, betas, eps and weight decay (the checkpoint's saved running averages of each weight's gradient where the arm starts from its encoder); float32.

Arms: as_is (today's encoder, both lessons); fresh (a freshly initialised encoder, both lessons); path (today's encoder with the path, both lessons reaching every weight); path_live_only (the same, the path's weight detached inside the token-change term's re-encoding: the production wiring); no_token_change (today's encoder, no path, VICReg only); fresh_path_live_only (a fresh encoder with the path wired as in production); path_no_token_change (today's encoder with the path, VICReg only: the token-change term cut for the encoder's own weights too).

At updates 0, 100, 200, 500, 1,000, 2,000 and 3,000: the token of every row on the bf16 grid (the encoder's Linears rounded as the graphics card rounds them, the path's sum and the LayerNorm in float32); the trainer's probe restated (reports of 100 model steps, each body's change from its report mean, even bodies fitted and odd scored and the other way round, body-shuffled control) for head tilt, gravity in the head and the trunk's roll, on all 16 whole reports and on the 5 reports after model step 1,100 of the rows (read by no update).
Write bench.json after every reading.

rows.title: Vestibular input path: its unit tests, its watch's tests and the tests of the files it touches
rows.question: Do the tests of the vestibular input path (the module's arithmetic, the learner-level contract on a small CPU learner with synthetic frames, the watch's stop and pass lines on hand-made records) pass, and do the existing tests of the files this work changed (the hourly watcher, the asked-change path and its watch, the vestibular repair's watch) still pass on the branch?

rows.question: Does the branch's code with --vestibular-input-path absent from the launch line train a small learner bit for bit as production's commit c59ecab7e (amended Oct 4, 2026 9:05 AM PDT: production's tip after the heads candidate, merged into the branch as 93e5d3b9a; before the merge the base was 7bafda80b, and no run was made on it) does over 120 model steps? With the flag on, is model step 0 equal to the run without it, and does the path's weight move before model step 1? And resumed from a checkpoint production's code saved: does the branch without the flag continue as production's code does over 40 model steps, and with the flag on at that load, does the load's check read the vestibular token unchanged and is the first resumed model step equal to production's?
rows.why: The switch has to be off by default and bit-identical when off: merging the branch must change nothing in production until the flag is set. And the switch must change no prediction at the model step it is switched on. The decision that depends on it: whether the branch can be merged with the flag off, and whether the switch's first model step can be trusted to be the unchanged model.
inputs: Production's commit c59ecab7e (its tip after the heads candidate) (git archive of Source/Python/lem, mimo_bridge and tokenizer into a temporary folder under D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/vestibular_token2/lockstep) and the branch's Source/Python.

The fixture Source/Python/mimo_bridge/tests/motor_asked_change_fixture.py, loaded by path under each code: a learner built by the trainer's own builder from H84's learner flags at width 32, 3 bodies, CPU, one thread, a 64-model-step replay ring, seeded synthetic frames, the trainer's latch rule, replay every second model step; every second unit of three prediction-head first layers planted dead so the liveness repair revives units during the run.
No MuJoCo world, no checkpoint of production, no trainer process (the learner's step function is called directly).
steps: Three child processes, one after another: production's code without the flag; the branch's code without the flag; the branch's code with --vestibular-input-path on. Each drives 120 model steps.

Per model step each records the loss and the gradient norm (exact float hex), hashes of the command and gaze sent, of the loss breakdown, of the wellness values, of the replay loss, of the live tokens and the predictions, and of the three random streams; every 10 model steps one hash over every parameter, buffer and Adam state (the path's own left out).
Compare production's rows with the branch's rows without the flag; compare the branch's rows without and with the flag.

Production's code drives 30 model steps and saves a checkpoint (the trainer's own save); the synthetic bodies' state and the held command are written beside it. measures: The first model step at which any recorded field differs (none = every row equal), and whether the final state hashes are equal.
With the flag on: the model step before which the path's largest absolute weight first reads above 0.
rows.pass_line: Production against the branch without the flag: no row differs in 120 model steps and the final states are equal, with the liveness repair having revived units in both (so the comparison would see a forward pass that joined a watching window). The branch without against with the flag: the row of model step 0 is equal, the path's weight has moved before model step 1, and a later row differs. RESUME (amended before the first run): production against the branch without the flag: no row differs in 40 model steps and the final states are equal, all three loads at model step 30. The branch with the flag on: the load's switch record says exact at model step 30 (the vestibular token with the path against without it on 64 probe rows bit-identical in float32, the weight's largest absolute value 0.0); its first resumed row equals production's; the weight has moved before the second resumed model step; a later row differs.
rows.pass_line_basis: With the flag absent the branch's added lines are a constructor argument that reads off, attribute look-ups that read None and one comparison in the step function that takes the unchanged line, so equality is what the code says; the lockstep is the measurement of it. With the flag on the weight is zero through model step 0 (token, predictions, loss and the other weights' update equal), and the live row's lessons (VICReg) give the weight a gradient at that model step, so it has moved before model step 1: the asked-change path's own lockstep passed in this form on Oct 3 (docs/gain_of_function_v4/restart_candidate/motor/gate_lockstep_result.json) with its first difference at model step 2.

rows.title: Planner's four weaknesses: AFTER reading, head repair
rows.question: On the first production checkpoint trained with the prediction-head repair for at least 5,000 model steps: the same four readings as the BEFORE row (planner_weaknesses_before_479350), and which of the three planner switches passes its gate?
rows.why: It is the gate of every planner segment: no switch goes into production on a number measured before the head repair. Each segment row names the gate lines this reading must meet for its switch. It also gives the after-repair reading of the four weaknesses (the BEFORE reading: docs/gain_of_function_v4/restart_candidate/RESTART_CANDIDATE_PLANNER_2026-10-04.md section 5).
inputs: The newest production checkpoint at least 5,000 model steps after the head repair's switch (--heads-all-slot-path on), read only, and its saved eight-world episode.

The same probe script, candidate commands, four replanned arms and 32 decisions (8 bodies x 4, at least 20 model steps apart) as the BEFORE row; --code names the Source/Python tree that builds the checkpoint's model.
The weighted arm's weights from the run's last 20 stats reports at or before the checkpoint (or from the checkpoint's own running window when it was trained with the switch on).
steps: Run docs/gain_of_function_v4/planner_weaknesses/probe_planner_weaknesses.py on the checkpoint exactly as the BEFORE row ran it; every route check must hold.
Write the summary's lines into this row; compare each reading with the BEFORE row's.
Judge each switch's gate lines (its segment row) and write which gates are met.
measures: The BEFORE row's measures, unchanged.
Per switch, gate met or not met, with the readings it was judged on.
rows.pass_line: No pass or fail line of its own: a measurement. A switch's gate is met when its arm's goal distance after the hold, minus the motor controller's own command's, has its 95% interval over bodies entirely below 0 with at least 7 of 8 bodies below 0, and the arm gains more on the motor controller's command than production's planner does (that difference's interval entirely below 0); the prospective term's gate is in its own row.
rows.pass_line_basis: The gates are the segment rows' own target readings, taken on the arm before any training runs with the switch (the style guide: no experiment launches on an unmeasured number). BEFORE reading on checkpoint 479350 for scale: production's planner minus the motor controller's command -0.0140 (-0.0847 to 0.0542; 4 of 8 bodies below 0). NOISE OF THE TARGET: between decisions, the planned command's goal distance minus the motor controller's has a standard deviation of 0.301 (measured on 32 decisions of checkpoint 479350; the motor controller's own distance is 0.939). Over 32 decisions the mean's standard error is 0.053, so the interval can lie below 0 only when the planned command ends nearer by about 0.11 or more, 11 of 100 parts of the motor controller's distance; a smaller true gain needs more decisions (64 give 0.038).

rows.title: Planner segment: goal distance weighted per sense
rows.question: With --goal-sense-weights own_command (PLANNER_SENSE_WEIGHTS), does the search's command end nearer its goal, in the senses the weights count, than the command of the same search without the weights, from the same saved planning decision and the same saved world state?
rows.why: What the switch changes: how many times each sense's command-dependent gradient is counted in the search (with the weights of checkpoint 479,350: proprioception's 3.87 times and vision's 1.13 times where the plain sum counts each once; tactile's, audio's and vestibular's 0 times), and the goal term's size beside the effort term. A part of the goal distance that no command changes has a gradient of 0 at any weight, so setting its weight to 0 changes nothing in the search; the first version of this row gave that as its reason (59 of 100 parts of the distance in weight-0 senses), and the review's finding M1 corrects it. The decision that depends on this row: whether PLANNER_SENSE_WEIGHTS leaves BUILT/OFF for a production segment. NOT EVIDENCE: the Oct 4 reading that met the first version of this row's gate (the weighted command's plain sum after the hold -0.107 against production's planner's, 7 of 8 bodies below 0). It sat in audio, a sense the weights give 0, on 4 of 31 decisions where a sound event falls inside the hold; on the two senses the weights act on it read -0.050 with a Student t interval of -0.162 to +0.062 (recomputed here from the probe's rows: -0.050, -0.162 to 0.062); it compared one search draw with one; and four arms were read against one gate (12 in 100 that one of four passes with no effect). Source: docs/gain_of_function_v4/agents/planner_weights_review_2026-10-04.md on branch review/planner-weights-2026-10-04, findings H1 and M5.
inputs: The newest qualified production checkpoint (model step N for the launch) and its saved eight-world episode, read only; it stays on disk as the revert point.
The repaired search, named to the gate tool with --override planner_search=<its setting>.

The senses' readings, standard errors and lower bounds: the checkpoint's own running window when it was trained with the switch on, else one pair per stats report of its run (the last 20 reports). On checkpoint 481,800 the last 20 stats reports give the weights vision 0.94, tactile 0.00, audio 0.00, proprioception 3.72, vestibular 0.34.
For the segment: production's launch command with one flag added, --goal-sense-weights own_command; the stats records of the 20 full reports before N and of every report after it.
steps: PRECONDITIONS, each checked before the gate is queued: PLANNER_SEARCH_REPAIR is merged and its own rows show its selected command repeatable (the gate tool writes no verdict for the adam search, whose selected command turns by 23.2 degrees per body handle under a token change of 0.00001: D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/planner_review/search_noise_479350/lines.txt); the goal-progress readings of this branch are in production's code and every one of the 20 full reports before N carries them (without that level the watch program judges no kill line and says so).

GATE, stage 1 and stage 2 (paired_gate.py --switch weights, in a training pause): per saved decision the search without the weights (arm A) and with them (arm B), each run 5 times (draw 0 on the captured tokens, 4 with Gaussian noise of standard deviation 0.00001 on the present tokens), each command executed from the same saved world state for its hold, every replay bit-identical. THE GATE IS SIZED IN TWO STAGES. Stage 1: 16 saved decisions (8 bodies x 2), 5 draws per arm, with the repaired search. It reads the standard deviation s between decisions of the primary reading and writes the count of decisions that shows the declared effect E in 80 of 100 runs with an interval of 2 standard errors: n = (2.84 x s / E)^2, rounded up, and at least 64 (8 per body, so that one decision is 1/8 of a body's mean; on Oct 4 one body's decision carried the reading). Stage 1 gives no verdict on the switch. The coordinator then decides whether the pause for stage 2 is spent: its cost, n x the measured seconds per decision, is written into this row before it runs. Stage 2: n decisions (stage 1's among them), the line below read once.
Gate not met, or stage 1 shows that the declared effect cannot be shown in a pause the coordinator will spend: no launch.
LAUNCH (the coordinator): supervisor pause, snapshot_and_stop, relaunch with the flag added. The trainer writes a planner_switch record at model step N.

TRANSIENT, declared: the window of pairs starts empty, so for the first 640 model steps (32 audited model steps) every decision runs on equal weights and the commands are today's; the weights then change until 100 pairs are held (N + 2,000). Window 1 (N to N + 2,000) is judged on P1, P2 and P3 only.

Every 5 minutes the hourly watcher judges the stop lines. PASS READING at the first checkpoint at or past N + 10,000: the paired gate again on that checkpoint, the same count of decisions and the same line.
measures: PRIMARY (gate and pass reading): the weighted distance after the 5-model-step hold (the decision's weights times each sense's mean squared difference between the fed token and the goal's token), arm B minus arm A, each the mean of 5 draws: below 0 = the search with the weights ended nearer its goal in the senses the weights count, 0 = no nearer.

CHECKS beside it (must not get worse): the plain sum after the hold and tactile's part after the hold, B minus A (above 0 = farther). Also written: the weighted distance after 1 model step (the model step the search predicts), the realised wellness over the hold, and between the draws of one decision the turn of the selected command in degrees per body handle.

LIVE (kill line P4): the realised closed share of planner-authored commands, 100 x (1 - plain goal distance at the commands' end / at their latch), from the stats block causal_chain.goal_progress.realised: 0 = the bodies ended as far from their goals as they began, 100 = on the goals, below 0 = farther.
Stop-line readings per window of 20 full reports: the commands' asked rotation in radians, the step rate in model steps per second, skipped optimizer updates (0 = none).
Alerts: the predicted plain gap of a window at or under 0 of 100 (the planned commands predicted no nearer the goal, in plain units, than the motor controller's commands).
rows.pass_line: GATE and PASS READING, the same line (the first on the checkpoint before the launch, the second on the segment's checkpoint at or past N + 10,000): over the n saved decisions of stage 2, each arm the mean of 5 draws, the weighted distance after the hold under the search with the weights minus under the search without them has its 95% Student t interval over the 8 body means entirely below 0; and neither the plain sum nor tactile's part after the hold has its interval entirely above 0. SEGMENT: no stop line reached between N and the pass reading.
rows.pass_line_basis: DECLARED EFFECT E = 0.00459 in the weighted distance: the search's own predicted gain (the Oct 4 probe's saved rows, D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/candidate_planner/before_479350 and before_479350_bodies_3_7, starts.jsonl). REACHABILITY with the spreads measured under the adam search: showing E in 80 of 100 runs needs (2.84 x 0.0631 / 0.00459)^2 = 1,525 decisions after 1 model step and (2.84 x 0.2213 / 0.00459)^2 = 18,749 after the hold (the review counts 820 and 10,091 for an interval of 2 standard errors alone and E = 0.0044). A gate of 64 decisions shows only an effect of 0.079 or more after the hold and 0.022 after 1 model step, 17 and 4.9 times E. So with the adam search's spread the predicted effect cannot be shown in a pause; whether it can with the repaired search is what stage 1 reads (5 draws averaged and a repeatable search both shrink the spread: the scatter between draws alone is 0.127 per draw). One decision of the 8 the review re-measured (body 3) showed a repeatable gain of 0.208 where the search predicted 0.028, so an effect larger than E on a part of the decisions is possible. THE REALISED READING ON CHECKPOINT 481,800 (file D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/planner_corrections/saved_decisions_481800/result.json; 32 planner-authored body commands; the model on the processor, one body at a time, learning off): the plain goal distance read 1.032 at the latch and changed by -0.0126 over the hold (standard deviation 0.202 between body commands; 17 of 32 ended nearer), a closed share of 1.2 of 100; the closed share of single body commands has a standard deviation of 22.8 of 100. The motor controller's next commands, to the same goals (32 body commands): 1.020 at their latch, a change of -0.0047, a closed share of 0.5 of 100 (the two authors start from different states, so this pair is no comparison of the planner with the motor controller). A stats report holds 80 planner-authored body commands; were they independent and equally weighted, one report's closed share would carry a standard error of 2.55 of 100 and the 20-report level 0.57. The watch program measures the real figure from the 20 full reports before the switch, with the correlation between neighbouring reports. NO LINE READS THE SEARCH'S OWN GAP. With the weights on the search reports its gap in weighted units: production's unchanged command read 12.42 of 100 there and 4.61 in the plain sum on the same 31 decisions (the review's section 4), so a line on that gap is crossed by the change of units. The predicted gap in plain units (stats block causal_chain.goal_progress.predicted.plain; it read 4.90 of 100 on the 40 decisions of checkpoint 481,800, where 0 = the planned command is predicted no nearer the goal than the motor controller's command and 100 = predicted on the goal) is an alert when a window reads 0 or less, never a pass line or a stop line. STOP LINES, each a snapshot_and_stop written by the hourly watcher (docs/gain_of_function_v4/planner_segment_watch.py version 2), in windows of 20 full reports after N: P1 an optimizer update skipped for a non-finite value; P2 the median asked rotation of the commands in a window under 0.6 of its level before the switch, two windows running (the held run's last 20 reports, model steps 479,900 to 481,800, read a median of 0.475 rad); P3 the median step rate of a window under 0.9 of its level before, two windows running (0.407 model steps per second now; the review's caution: before checkpoint 479,350 the level read 0.445 and the two newest reports 0.369 and 0.339, inside the run's own range, so the line stops only on two whole windows); P4, the kill line: over windows 2 and 3 (N + 2,000 to N + 6,000) the realised closed share of planner-authored commands under its level before the switch by more than 3 standard errors of the difference. The weighting leaves the goal's choice as it was, so that share is the same quantity before and after. Its false-stop chance with no change is 0.13 in 100 (one side of 3 standard errors); were body commands independent the difference's standard error would be 0.70 of 100, so a true fall of 2.10 of 100 would be caught in half the runs. REVERT (the coordinator): write the supervisor pause, snapshot_and_stop the segment's run, relaunch from the checkpoint the segment resumed (model step N, kept on disk for the whole segment) with the flag back at its value before. That run carries a planner_switch record that turns the setting off and is not judged by the watch program.
