rows.title: Planner segment: goal within the body's own reach
rows.question: With --goal-locality weighted (PLANNER_GOAL_LOCALITY), does the search's command toward the goal inside the radius gain more on the motor controller's command, toward its own goal, than the search's command toward the ranking's goal does, from the same saved decision and world state; and are goals reached in training?
rows.why: The goal is the highest-ranked state of the last 200 model steps: on checkpoint 479,350 a median 90.5 model steps old on the probe's 32 decisions and 98 in production's own record, and 2.88 times as far as the same tokens change in one hold (D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/candidate_planner/before_479350/resummary.json); the search looks 1 model step ahead. The switch takes the goal from the ring's model steps within the model's own 14-model-step radius and keeps it until it is reached, leaves the radius or was picked 200 model steps ago. Under 'on' (built Sep 6) the radius and every distance are a plain mean over every active sense, the motor token included; under 'weighted' (built Oct 5) they are the search's own goal distance (the sum over the real senses except motor, times the search's sense weights when those are on), so the goal is picked in the units the search then lowers. The gate's declared arm is 'weighted'; 'on' is read beside it without a verdict (two arms against one gate double the chance of a pass with no effect). The decision that depends on this row: whether PLANNER_GOAL_LOCALITY leaves BUILT/OFF for a production segment.
inputs: The newest qualified production checkpoint (model step N for the launch) and its saved eight-world episode, read only; it stays on disk as the revert point.
The repaired search, named to the gate tool with --override planner_search=<its setting>.

Per saved decision: the goal ring (200 model steps of every sense's fed token and its ranked value), the present tokens, and the rule's pick computed by the second implementation (goal_reference.py LocalityReference) with no earlier decision, so the radius is that decision's own distance to the ring model step 14 back.
For the segment: production's launch command with --goal-locality off changed to weighted; the stats records of the 20 full reports before N and of every report after it.
steps: PRECONDITIONS, each checked before the gate is queued: PLANNER_SEARCH_REPAIR is merged and its own rows show its selected command repeatable (the gate tool writes no verdict for the adam search, whose selected command turns by 23.2 degrees per body handle under a token change of 0.00001: D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/planner_review/search_noise_479350/lines.txt); the goal-progress readings of this branch are in production's code and every one of the 20 full reports before N carries them (without that level the watch program judges no kill line and says so).

GATE, stage 1 and stage 2 (paired_gate.py --switch locality_weighted,locality_on, in a training pause): per saved decision the search toward the ranking's goal (arm A) and toward the rule's pick (arm B), each run 5 times, each command and the motor controller's command executed from the same saved world state for the hold, every replay bit-identical. A decision at which the rule's pick is the ranking's pick has one goal for both arms and enters no reading (its count is written). THE GATE IS SIZED IN TWO STAGES. Stage 1: 16 saved decisions (8 bodies x 2), 5 draws per arm, with the repaired search. It reads the standard deviation s between decisions of the primary reading and writes the count of decisions that shows the declared effect E in 80 of 100 runs with an interval of 2 standard errors: n = (2.84 x s / E)^2, rounded up, and at least 64 (8 per body, so that one decision is 1/8 of a body's mean; on Oct 4 one body's decision carried the reading). Stage 1 gives no verdict on the switch. The coordinator then decides whether the pause for stage 2 is spent: its cost, n x the measured seconds per decision, is written into this row before it runs. Stage 2: n decisions (stage 1's among them), the line below read once.
Gate not met, or stage 1 shows that the declared effect cannot be shown in a pause the coordinator will spend: no launch.
LAUNCH (the coordinator): supervisor pause, snapshot_and_stop, relaunch with the flag at weighted. The trainer writes a planner_switch record at model step N.

TRANSIENT, declared: the ring is restored with the checkpoint, so the radius is this decision's own value at the first planning decision and every body takes a goal inside it at once; a kept goal is dropped when reached, when it leaves the radius or after 200 model steps, so every body has re-picked by N + 200. Goals that were far and highly ranked stop being picked; behaviour tied to them can fall in window 1 and is read per window, never as one blend (the error of the Sep 6 judgement). Window 1 is judged on P1, P2 and P3 only.

Every 5 minutes the hourly watcher judges the stop lines. PASS READING at the first checkpoint at or past N + 10,000: the paired gate again on that checkpoint, the same count of decisions and the same line.
measures: PRIMARY (gate and pass reading): the gain beyond the motor controller's command, (plain goal distance after the hold under the motor controller's command - under the arm's command), each arm to its OWN goal; arm B minus arm A, each the mean of 5 draws: above 0 = the command toward the goal inside the radius gains more on the motor controller's command, 0 = the same.

Beside it: the same gain as a share of the goal's distance at the decision; how many decisions had one goal for both arms; the rule's radius and arrival line; the turn of the selected command between draws.
LIVE (kill line P4): goals reached since the switch (the stats field intention.goal_locality.arrivals_total at the end of window 3 minus its value in the last report before N): 0 = none.
Per window, without a line: the radius, the arrival line, kept goals' age and the count of decisions with no ring model step inside the radius (fallbacks_total).
Stop-line readings per window of 20 full reports: the commands' asked rotation in radians, the step rate in model steps per second, skipped optimizer updates (0 = none).
Alerts: the predicted plain gap of a window at or under 0 of 100 (the planned commands predicted no nearer the goal, in plain units, than the motor controller's commands).
rows.pass_line: GATE and PASS READING, the same line, for the declared arm --goal-locality weighted: over the n saved decisions of stage 2 at which the two arms have different goals, each arm the mean of 5 draws, the gain beyond the motor controller's command toward the arm's own goal (plain goal distance after the hold) under the search toward the goal inside the radius minus under the search toward the ranking's goal has its 95% Student t interval over the 8 body means entirely above 0. SEGMENT: no stop line reached between N and the pass reading, and goals reached since the switch above 0.
rows.pass_line_basis: DECLARED EFFECT E = 0.0739 in plain goal-distance units (the mean of the Oct 4 local arm's reading on the decisions with another goal). REACHABILITY with the Oct 4 spread: showing E in 80 of 100 runs needs (2.84 x 0.5118 / 0.0739)^2 = 387 decisions with another goal (26 of 32 decisions had one on Oct 4). Stage 1 re-reads the spread with the repaired search. WHAT THE SEP 6 RUN MEASURED (run H67_gaze_world_r, its own stats and arguments: --goal-locality on, 247 reports, model steps 3,160,825 to 3,185,475, 3.02 hours, 8 bodies, a plan every 5 model steps with a hold of 5, so every latched command was the planner's): 47 goals reached where no earlier run had one (1.19 per 1,000 body decisions), 0 decisions without a ring model step inside the radius, a radius of 0.261 and an arrival line of 0.035 on average (mean squared token difference over every active sense), kept goals a mean 6.6 model steps old; a hand touched the mobile in 2.61, 1.24 and 2.24 of 100 body model steps in the run's three thirds (a fall in the middle third and a return in the last). It did not measure whether a planned command ended nearer its goal than the motor controller's command: no command was executed twice from one state. It was reverted the same night on the strike rate over the whole run; the project's rules later recorded that judgement as mistaken (a recovering dip read on a blended window). NO LINE READS THE SEARCH'S OWN GAP. With the weights on the search reports its gap in weighted units: production's unchanged command read 12.42 of 100 there and 4.61 in the plain sum on the same 31 decisions (the review's section 4), so a line on that gap is crossed by the change of units. The predicted gap in plain units (stats block causal_chain.goal_progress.predicted.plain; it read 4.90 of 100 on the 40 decisions of checkpoint 481,800, where 0 = the planned command is predicted no nearer the goal than the motor controller's command and 100 = predicted on the goal) is an alert when a window reads 0 or less, never a pass line or a stop line. STOP LINES, each a snapshot_and_stop written by the hourly watcher (docs/gain_of_function_v4/planner_segment_watch.py version 2), in windows of 20 full reports after N: P1 an optimizer update skipped for a non-finite value; P2 the median asked rotation of the commands in a window under 0.6 of its level before the switch, two windows running (the held run's last 20 reports, model steps 479,900 to 481,800, read a median of 0.475 rad); P3 the median step rate of a window under 0.9 of its level before, two windows running (0.407 model steps per second now; the review's caution: before checkpoint 479,350 the level read 0.445 and the two newest reports 0.369 and 0.339, inside the run's own range, so the line stops only on two whole windows); P4, the kill line: goals reached since the switch must be above 0 at the end of window 3 (N + 6,000). Reachability: at the Sep 6 rate, the 4,800 body decisions by N + 6,000 give 5.7 goals reached expected, and 0 would come up in 0.3 of 100 such segments. That rate was measured under 'on' on another model (a plan every 5 model steps, every command the planner's); under 'weighted' on H84 it is unmeasured in training. On the saved-decision job's replay of checkpoint 481,800 (production's own frames, the rule applied without its commands being executed) goals reached: 1 in 24 decisions under 'weighted', 0 in 24 under 'on'. A stop on this line sends the segment back to its checkpoint, and the row then records the radius and the arrival line per window. The realised closed share is not judged for this switch: it changes which goals are picked, and a goal inside the radius is nearer, so its distance changes by a larger share over one hold than a far goal's. REVERT (the coordinator): write the supervisor pause, snapshot_and_stop the segment's run, relaunch from the checkpoint the segment resumed (model step N, kept on disk for the whole segment) with the flag back at its value before. That run carries a planner_switch record that turns the setting off and is not judged by the watch program.

cost.where: the paired gate and the pass reading run on the processor in a training pause (one process, 8 threads, each process held to 5 GB of RAM and 9 GB committed); the segment itself is production training with one flag changed and no added process; the hourly watcher reads the stats file
cost.basis: the time limit is stage 1's (16 decisions); stage 2's limit is written into this row from stage 1's count before it runs. The segment itself is 10,000 model steps of production training.

rows.on_pass: Gate met: the coordinator launches the segment (one flag, weighted). Pass reading met with no stop line reached: the flag stays in production's command and PLANNER_GOAL_LOCALITY reads IN TRAINING; VERIFIED needs the planner-against-motor-controller physical test of the directive's section 3.C on a later checkpoint.
rows.on_fail: Stage 1 shows the effect cannot be shown in a pause the coordinator spends: the switch stays BUILT/OFF. Gate not met at stage 2: PLANNER_GOAL_LOCALITY (weighted) reads FAILED/SUPERSEDED with the reading; the three candidates recorded on Sep 6 (a re-pick when a ring model step outranks the kept goal by more than noise, a larger radius, locality only without a strongly ranked model step in the ring) are the next builds, each with its own row. A stop line reached or the pass reading not met during the segment: the revert, and the row records the per-window readings, never one blended number. Owner: the planner corrections builder (branch planner/corrections-2026-10-05) for the gate tool; the coordinator for the launch and the revert.
rows.decision: Rewritten Oct 5, 2026 after the independent review (the first version's gate compared one search draw with one and read its search gap in the search's own units). Not run and not queued: the gate needs the repaired search.

rows.target_metric: The gain beyond the motor controller's command toward the arm's own goal, in plain goal-distance units after the hold, the search toward the goal inside the radius minus the search toward the ranking's goal: above 0 = goal locality buys real progress toward the goal; 0 = none.
rows.baseline: 0. The Oct 4 probe's local arm (the rule of 'on' without its keeping history, single draws of the adam search, 32 decisions of checkpoint 479,350; the Oct 4 probe's saved rows, D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/candidate_planner/before_479350 and before_479350_bodies_3_7, starts.jsonl) read 0.060 with a Student t interval over the 8 body means of -0.056 to 0.176, which reaches 0; on the 26 decisions where the rule picked another goal than the ranking it read 0.074.

Noise: on Oct 4 the same reading had a standard deviation of 0.5118 between the 26 decisions with another goal (single draws; single decisions read from -1.09 to 1.24, the size of sound and contact events inside one hold); stage 1 re-measures the spread with the repaired search and 5 draws.
rows.material_gof_line: not yet defined: no measurement links a given gain in goal distance to an ability. The gate is sized to show a gain of 0.0739, the size the Oct 4 reading had (not evidence by itself: one draw per arm, several arms against one gate).

rows.title: Planner segment: predicted wellness in the search
rows.question: With --prospective-wellness add (PLANNER_PROSPECTIVE_TERM, weight 0.15), does the search's command give more realised bodily wellness over its hold than the command of the same search without the term, from the same saved decision and world state, without ending farther from its goal?
rows.why: The search gives predicted wellness weight 0: wellness only picks which remembered state is the goal. The switch (built Sep 9, unchanged by this work) adds 0.15 x (1 - the wellness predictor's mean of tactile_comfort, capability and motor_state on the predicted next tokens) to the search's objective; the motor token is detached from that term. It can change a command only as far as those outputs differ between candidate commands, and it helps only when they differ the way the realised values differ. Two things stand before any gate: the predictor's ranking of one decision's commands (row planner_prospective_gate_reading_481800), and the predictor's middle layer wellness.approximate.net.2, which received a gradient of exactly 0 in the audit of Oct 4 (row autocast_cache_gradient_audit_479350): a layer that is not trained cannot learn to rank. Repairing the predictor is not this work's. The decision that depends on this row: whether PLANNER_PROSPECTIVE_TERM leaves BUILT/OFF.
inputs: The newest qualified production checkpoint (model step N for the launch) and its saved eight-world episode, read only; it stays on disk as the revert point.
The repaired search, named to the gate tool with --override planner_search=<its setting>.
The wellness predictor (5 outputs, each 0 to 1, trained to copy the grounded wellness terms from the present tokens) and the forward model's predicted next tokens for each searched command.
For the segment: production's launch command with --prospective-wellness off changed to add (weight 0.15); the stats records of the 20 full reports before N and of every report after it.
steps: PRECONDITIONS, each checked before the gate is queued: PLANNER_SEARCH_REPAIR is merged and its own rows show its selected command repeatable (the gate tool writes no verdict for the adam search, whose selected command turns by 23.2 degrees per body handle under a token change of 0.00001: D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/planner_review/search_noise_479350/lines.txt); the goal-progress readings of this branch are in production's code and every one of the 20 full reports before N carries them (without that level the watch program judges no kill line and says so).

GATE READINGS BEFORE THE PAIRED GATE, both on the checkpoint to be resumed: G1 the predictor ranks one decision's candidate commands better than chance (prospective_gate_reading.py: the lower end of the 95% interval above 50 of 100 pairs, the bodily three over the hold); G2 every tensor that computes the wellness predictor's output (its own layers, and the liveness repair's rows where they compute a layer's units) receives a gradient above 0 from the wellness lesson in a live model step (restated Oct 5, 2026: the liveness repair computes all 128 units of wellness.approximate.net.2, whose own weights are read by nothing and so always get 0; row investigate_wellness_predictor_gradient_481800, docs/gain_of_function_v4/coordinator/INVESTIGATION_WELLNESS_GRADIENT_MOTOR_POOL_2026-10-05.md on branch investigate/wellness-gradient-motor-pool-2026-10-05) (the gradient audit's own tool; last measured exactly 0 on the middle layer). Either not met: no paired gate, no launch.

PAIRED GATE, stage 1 and stage 2 (paired_gate.py --switch prospective, in a training pause): per saved decision the search without the term (arm A) and with it (arm B), each run 5 times, each command executed from the same saved world state for its hold, every replay bit-identical. THE GATE IS SIZED IN TWO STAGES. Stage 1: 16 saved decisions (8 bodies x 2), 5 draws per arm, with the repaired search. It reads the standard deviation s between decisions of the primary reading and writes the count of decisions that shows the declared effect E in 80 of 100 runs with an interval of 2 standard errors: n = (2.84 x s / E)^2, rounded up, and at least 64 (8 per body, so that one decision is 1/8 of a body's mean; on Oct 4 one body's decision carried the reading). Stage 1 gives no verdict on the switch. The coordinator then decides whether the pause for stage 2 is spent: its cost, n x the measured seconds per decision, is written into this row before it runs. Stage 2: n decisions (stage 1's among them), the line below read once.
LAUNCH (the coordinator): supervisor pause, snapshot_and_stop, relaunch with the flag at add. The trainer writes a planner_switch record at model step N.
TRANSIENT, declared: the term acts from the first planning decision and holds no state; no weight is trained by it. Window 1 (N to N + 2,000) is judged on P1, P2 and P3 only.

Every 5 minutes the hourly watcher judges the stop lines. PASS READING at the first checkpoint at or past N + 10,000: the paired gate again on that checkpoint, the same count of decisions and the same line.
measures: PRIMARY (gate and pass reading): the grounded mean of tactile_comfort, capability and motor_state (each 0 to 1) averaged over the 5-model-step hold, arm B minus arm A, each the mean of 5 draws: above 0 = the term's command gave more of the wellness it is made of, 0 = the same.
CHECK beside it (must not get worse): the plain goal distance after the hold, B minus A (above 0 = farther from the goal). Also written: the five-term sum over the hold.
LIVE (kill line P5): the report mean of the grounded five-term wellness sum (0 to 5) over windows 2 and 3 against its level before the switch.
Stop-line readings per window of 20 full reports: the commands' asked rotation in radians, the step rate in model steps per second, skipped optimizer updates (0 = none).
Alerts: the predicted plain gap of a window at or under 0 of 100 (the planned commands predicted no nearer the goal, in plain units, than the motor controller's commands).
rows.pass_line: GATE READINGS G1 and G2 met on the checkpoint to be resumed. PAIRED GATE and PASS READING, the same line: over the n saved decisions of stage 2, each arm the mean of 5 draws, the grounded mean of tactile_comfort, capability and motor_state over the hold under the search with the term minus under the search without it has its 95% Student t interval over the 8 body means entirely above 0; and the plain goal distance after the hold does not have its interval entirely above 0. SEGMENT: no stop line reached between N and the pass reading.
rows.pass_line_basis: DECLARED EFFECT E = 0.00135 in the bodily mean: the rise the search itself predicted for the term's command on Oct 4 (the term fell by 0.000202 on 0.0613 over 32 searches; divided by the weight 0.15). REACHABILITY with the Oct 4 spread (single draws of the adam search): showing E in 80 of 100 runs needs (2.84 x 0.00476 / 0.00135)^2 = 101 decisions. Stage 1 re-reads the spread and the predicted rise with the repaired search. While G1 reads chance the gate cannot be met for the term's reason (a term made of a predictor that ranks commands at chance changes the command without raising wellness), which is why G1 and G2 stand before it. STOP LINES, each a snapshot_and_stop written by the hourly watcher (docs/gain_of_function_v4/planner_segment_watch.py version 2), in windows of 20 full reports after N: P1 an optimizer update skipped for a non-finite value; P2 the median asked rotation of the commands in a window under 0.6 of its level before the switch, two windows running (the held run's last 20 reports, model steps 479,900 to 481,800, read a median of 0.475 rad); P3 the median step rate of a window under 0.9 of its level before, two windows running (0.407 model steps per second now; the review's caution: before checkpoint 479,350 the level read 0.445 and the two newest reports 0.369 and 0.339, inside the run's own range, so the line stops only on two whole windows); P5, the kill line: the grounded five-term wellness sum over windows 2 and 3 under its level before the switch by more than 3 standard errors of the difference (false-stop chance with no change 0.13 in 100, one side of 3 standard errors; the level's spread between reports is read by the watch program from the 20 full reports before N). NO LINE READS THE SEARCH'S OWN GAP. With the weights on the search reports its gap in weighted units: production's unchanged command read 12.42 of 100 there and 4.61 in the plain sum on the same 31 decisions (the review's section 4), so a line on that gap is crossed by the change of units. The predicted gap in plain units (stats block causal_chain.goal_progress.predicted.plain; it read 4.90 of 100 on the 40 decisions of checkpoint 481,800, where 0 = the planned command is predicted no nearer the goal than the motor controller's command and 100 = predicted on the goal) is an alert when a window reads 0 or less, never a pass line or a stop line. REVERT (the coordinator): write the supervisor pause, snapshot_and_stop the segment's run, relaunch from the checkpoint the segment resumed (model step N, kept on disk for the whole segment) with the flag back at its value before. That run carries a planner_switch record that turns the setting off and is not judged by the watch program.

rows.title: Vestibular input path on in production (--vestibular-input-path on, or on_delayed_encoder_only), with its watch and standing lines
rows.question: With the vestibular input path switched on from the resumed checkpoint (model step N) in the wiring without the exception (the flag value on: the delayed lesson trains neither the encoder's own layers nor the path), does the trainer's own probe read each body's change of head tilt from the vestibular token at 0.25 or more in every window of 1,000 model steps from N + 2,001 on, with no stop line crossed through 10,000 model steps after the switch and no standing alert for as long as the flag is on?
rows.why: The vestibular token carries almost none of its 28 inputs' change over time: the trainer's probe reads head tilt at -0.6 of 100, the encoder's stages show the tilt lost inside the encoder by training (row vestibular_token_stage_readouts), and no other sense's token and no slot of the transformer's output carries it (row vestibular_token_lived_readouts). The path puts a linear map of the encoder's own input into the token, zero at the switch, its weight held so that no row's output passes 0.3 token units. THE INDEPENDENT REVIEW of Oct 4, 2026 (vestibular_input_path_review_2026-10-04.md) said: do not deploy as first declared; deploy with its named changes. They are in this row: both wirings selectable by the flag's value; T1 as a standing line; the change slope and the weight size on standing lines; M6 stated as what it is; the weight's growth under the cap stopped; the checkpoint before the switch kept until T1 has held past the bench's horizon. THE WIRING IS DECIDED (the coordinator, Oct 4, after the reviewer's long bench, row vestibular_input_path_review_long_bench; path version 1, 240,000 updates, 16 reports read by no update): under the exception the encoder's part cancels 70 to 83 of 100 parts of the path's change, where it levels, with the read-out at 0.46, while the path's weight (6.5) and fixed vector (0.15) keep growing; the wiring without the exception reads 0.43 to 0.56 with no opposition. So the flag value `on` is the wiring without the exception, and the exception stays selectable as `on_delayed_encoder_only`. The decision that depends on this row: the path stays on in production's command, or the run is reverted to the checkpoint before the switch.
inputs: The checkpoint the relaunch resumes (model step N), with all eight worlds. Training is held at checkpoint 481,800 as this row is written. THE CHECKPOINT BEFORE THE SWITCH IS KEPT (named in Saved/mimo_bridge/archive_keep.json right after the relaunch) UNTIL THE STANDING LINE T1 HAS HELD IN EVERY WINDOW PAST THE HORIZON TO WHICH THE OPPOSITION WAS MEASURED; the watch's own end at N + 10,000 is before it. Under `on`: through N + 60,000 model steps (this branch's bench of version 2 read no opposition in this wiring through 60,000 updates, and the read-out at 0.43 to 0.54). Under `on_delayed_encoder_only`, should it ever be selected: through N + 240,000 (the reviewer's long bench read its cancelling still rising at 60,000 updates and levelling at 70 to 83 of 100 by 240,000). Cost: disk for one checkpoint with its 8 worlds for that long.

Production's recorded command with ONE change, the flag at one of its two on values (the relaunch script's --set vestibular-input-path <value>; no other --set). `on_delayed_encoder_only`: the delayed lesson's re-encoding of the previous row trains the encoder's own layers and not the path. `on`: it trains neither (the previous row's vestibular token enters the delayed lesson without gradient). The same path, the same tokens at the switch; the wiring may be changed at a later relaunch (the load logs and stamps the change). WHICH VALUE: `on` (the coordinator's decision, in this row's why). --vestibular-encoder-repair rescale_restart stays in the command: the stats block vestibular.repair.balance_probe, which T1 reads, is written only with it on.

If another switch's watch is open at the relaunch (the prediction heads' all-slot path), a stop on the other senses or on the step rate cannot be put down to one of the two switches; the package asks for this switch at a relaunch outside such a watch, or the coordinator states the overlap in the relaunch's reason.

Code: production's code with the repair merged off by default at 1bd91c3b1 (Oct 8, 2026, 2:52 AM PDT) through branch merge/head-tilt-repair-2026-10-07 at 865ece161, which also holds the text corrections b30453b31: lem/model/vestibular_input_path.py path version 2 (the same blob 41fb31c91 at fe276c7de, 865ece161, 1bd91c3b1 and f0dd472a3), its wiring in mimo_bridge/lem_model.py and train_mimo.py, docs/gain_of_function_v4/vestibular_input_path_watch.py and the hook in docs/h84_launch_2026-09-18/hourly_watch.py. With the flag absent the merged code trains bit for bit as production's (rows vestibular_input_path_lockstep and head_tilt_repair_merge_lockstep_85d616e9e). Since 865ece161, eight definitions naming the path changed by lines that compute nothing of the path, its hold, its cap, its switch or which lessons train it (D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/head_tilt_reconciliation_20261013/RECONCILIATION.md, section 4). The switching run's exact code is the pin of the bounded activation package D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/head_tilt_activation_494025 (PACKAGE.md), whose trainer code equals ca77bb8d0's and 641c931a6's by a zero-line diff; its processor test is row head_tilt_repair_module_tests_f0dd472a3.
The 100 full reports before the switch, read through the parent chain of run folders (the other senses' level before the switch).
steps: The merge is done (1bd91c3b1, Oct 8, 2026). Under proxy decision proxy-head-tilt-route-20261013 (Saved/gof_coordination/mailbox/proxy-head-tilt-route-20261013/message.json, sha256 f30297e2...; author: the overseer) the switch is made by ONE bounded run of the activation package D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/head_tilt_activation_494025, from the adoption run's verified complete endpoint (expected model step 494,025): its launcher starts the trainer with the adopted command and --vestibular-input-path on as the only new behaviour setting (the wiring without the exception; the exception would be on_delayed_encoder_only), ends at the first full report at or after N + 10,000, and leaves nothing to continue automatically; the launch itself is the decision from the endpoint's evidence.

At the load the build adds one Linear(28 -> 192) without bias beside the vestibular encoder, its weight zero; the load's check computes the vestibular token on 64 probe rows with the path and without it, in float32 and under the run's autocast, and refuses the load unless both are bit-identical; the trainer writes one vestibular_input_path_switch record into the stats stream. Every Adam state of the other weights is carried by name; the path's one weight starts with a fresh Adam state. Both flag values pass the same check.

From the first model step on: on the live row of every training model step, when the largest of the 8 rows' plain outputs weight x input x 1/sqrt(28) has a root mean square over its 192 numbers above 0.3, the whole weight is multiplied by 0.3 / that size (the hold: the weight cannot grow past what the cap lets through). Then u = weight x the encoder's own input row x 1/sqrt(28); a row of any other call whose u is above 0.3 is multiplied by 0.3 / its size (the per-row cap); u is added to the encoder's last-layer output in units of that output's standard deviation over its 192 numbers (18.09 at 479,350), in float32, before the registry's LayerNorm.

WHICH LESSONS TRAIN WHICH PART (the token is made of the sum of the encoder's part and the path's part; measured on a run with every lesson live, tests/test_vestibular_input_path.py). Both parts, in both wirings: vicreg and recon_dec (the live row's lessons). Every lesson that reads the delayed row's re-encoding (next_frame.vestibular and the other senses' next_frame terms, contact_head, efference_gaze, efference_body, latent_reg): under `on_delayed_encoder_only` the encoder's part and not the path's; under `on` neither part. Neither part, in both wirings: the imagination chain and the planner's rows (they hold the prediction head's output; no vestibular row is encoded there), the hold-end lessons, replay, the motor, wellness, persistent-memory and synergy terms. No lesson trains the path alone.

The hourly watcher's 5-minute check judges stop lines M1, M2, M4, M5 and M6 on every record from the switch through the first full report at or past N + 10,000 and writes snapshot_and_stop itself on a crossing. On every check, past the watch's end too and for as long as the run's flag is on, it judges the three standing lines on every complete window of 1,000 model steps from N + 2,001 on, and prints and records an alert when two windows running are across one of them.

At N + 3,000 read T1 and write it into this row; at N + 10,000 the stop lines close; the standing lines go on; at N + 60,000 with no standing alert the checkpoint before the switch may be released and the row closed.
measures: T1, the target: vestibular.repair.balance_probe.r2.head_tilt, the trainer's own probe: a ridge regression from each body's token change to that body's change of head tilt within a report of 100 model steps, fitted on the even-numbered bodies and scored on the odd ones and the other way round, over the last 10 reports. 0 = no better than predicting no change, 1 = every scored change predicted; today -0.01; the 28 input numbers themselves read 0.56. Beside it r2_shuffled.head_tilt, the same with every body's token paired with another body's tilt (0 expected). WHAT THIS READING CANNOT SHOW (the review, section 4): it reads a direction as long as that direction is larger than a thousandth part of the token's main change, so it stays level while head tilt's part of the token shrinks and falls late; the change slope is read beside it for that reason.

The change slope (vestibular_input_path.change_slope, per report): over each body's change from its own mean over the report's live rows, the summed product of the encoder's part's change and the path's change over the path's summed squared change. -1 = the encoder's part takes the path's change out of the sum, 0 = unrelated. Encoder bench of version 2 (path_bench_hold/bench.json): `on` -0.015 to +0.198 at every reading from 2,000 updates on; `on_delayed_encoder_only` 0.01 at 4,000 updates, -0.20 at 10,000, -0.34 at 40,000, -0.46 at 60,000. CORRECTED Oct 5, 2026 12:55 PM PDT on the independent review's finding of that day: the range first read `on_delayed_encoder_only`, and 'throughout' held only for the readings from 2,000 updates on (under `on` the readings at 100 to 1,000 updates are +12.8 to +1.86, while the path's change is small).

The path's weight size (vestibular_input_path.output_weight_rms, the root mean square of its 5,376 weights) and the share of model steps at which the hold scaled it back (weight_held_share). Encoder bench of version 2: 0.07 to 0.105 from 4,000 through 60,000 updates in both wirings, scaled back at 1 in 100 of the updates or fewer; without the hold 3.39 at 60,000.
The path's output per number (vestibular_input_path.output_rms, token units: 0 = the path adds nothing, 0.3 = every row at the cap) and the share of rows the per-row cap scaled down (capped_share).
T2: vestibular.improvement_over_persistence = 1 - prediction error / the error of predicting no change. 0 = no better than no change, 1 = exact, below 0 = worse; today -0.001 to -0.006.

Each other sense's next-model-step error ratio (0 = exact, 1 = no better than predicting no change) as a multiple of its level over the up to 100 full reports before the switch; model steps per second per 20-report window against the window before.
The switch record: exact, the token's largest change with the path against without it (0.0 = the same number), the weight's largest absolute value (0.0).

NOT READ IN PRODUCTION: the path's fixed vector, the path's mean output over all rows (what it adds to every row alike), root mean square over its 192 numbers, in token units (0 = the path adds nothing that every row shares; the cap on any row's path output is 0.3). The independent review of Oct 4 asked for a standing line on it. The stats block vestibular_input_path holds no key for it and the watch has no line on it; the builder's record named that change as done, and was corrected on Oct 5, 2026 (commit b30453b31 on branch fix/head_tilt_text-2026-10-05). It is left out of production's stats (the coordinator's choice, Oct 5, 2026); no stats field is added. Encoder bench of version 2 (path_bench_hold/bench.json, arm path_none_cap03, key two_parts.fixed_path): `on` 0.0020 to 0.0061 token units at every reading from 2,000 updates on. With the whole model under `on` (row head_tilt_repair_whole_model_check_481800, readings.fixed_vector): 0.0052 to 0.0102 token units at the readings from update 2,000 to 6,000, still not read in production.
rows.pass_line: STOP LINES, each writing snapshot_and_stop, judged through N + 10,000 (docs/gain_of_function_v4/vestibular_input_path_watch.py): M1 the switch record as declared (exact; bit-identical tokens in float32 and under the run's autocast; the weight 0.0; 64 probe rows; path version 2); M2 no non-finite update; M4 no other sense above its median over the 20 reports before the switch x W1 in report 2 and in report 3 (W1: vision 4.01, tactile 2.09, audio 2.75, proprioception 2.17), and no other sense's 20-report median above its level before the switch x 1.72 (tactile, audio, proprioception) or x 3.95 (vision); above x 1.43 and x 3.29 an alert, never a stop; vestibular's own ratio an alert only; M5 model steps per second not under 0.9 of the window before in two windows running. M6, STATED AS WHAT IT IS: the path's output not above 0.0013 token units x the model steps since the switch; this line can be crossed in the first 232 model steps only (from there on it is above the cap of 0.3), after which it stops a run only on an output that is not a finite number; it is no bound on the path and the encoder's part together. STANDING LINES, each an ALERT to the coordinator, printed once and recorded, never a stop, judged on every window of 1,000 model steps from N + 2,001 on for as long as the flag is on: T1 standing: the window's median head-tilt reading of the trainer's probe at least 0.25 and at least 0.25 above its control's median; S1: the window's median change slope at or above -0.10; W1: the window's median weight size at or under 0.2. Two windows running across a line raise the alert, which names the windows and the three readings. PASS LINE at the watch's end, never a stop: T2 over the 20 full reports ending at N + 10,000 the 5th percentile of 2,000 bootstrap medians of vestibular.improvement_over_persistence, drawn in blocks of 5 consecutive reports, above 0.
rows.pass_line_basis: T1'S REACHABILITY. Encoder bench of version 2 (row vestibular_token_path_bench; 60,000 updates, 5 reports read by no update): the read-out on unread rows reads 0.33 (on) and 0.44 (on_delayed_encoder_only) at 1,000 updates, 0.42 and 0.51 at 2,000, and 0.43 to 0.54 and 0.46 to 0.53 from 4,000 through 60,000, against the line 0.25. The trainer's probe at a report reads the 1,000 model steps before it, so the first standing window (N + 2,001 to N + 3,000) covers updates 1,000 to 3,000. With the whole model (checkpoint 481,800; 6,000 card updates per arm; head tilt read on the 500 model steps no update read, line 0.25): path version 2 under `on` has three whole-model runs, reading 0.44 to 0.50 (row head_tilt_repair_whole_model_check_481800, Oct 5, 2026), 0.455 to 0.496 (seed 1, row head_tilt_repair_on_seed1_diagnosis_481800, Oct 5) and 0.431 to 0.484 (seed 0 rerun, row head_tilt_repair_on_seed0_rerun_481800, Oct 8, PASS) from update 2,000 on, against 0.012 in the control arm; under `on_delayed_encoder_only` two runs (row head_tilt_repair_delayed_encoder_only_check_481800, 0.45 to 0.49, and the seed-1 row's second arm). Vision's cost under `on`: the first run read a median 1.107 times the control arm's error ratio on the read set against the seed-to-seed line 1.035 (FAIL); the seed-1 run (median ln ratio -0.0084 against 0.034) and the seed-0 rerun with the first run's replay draws (0.0089 against 0.0342) did not repeat it. Path version 1 under on_delayed_encoder_only read 0.29 at 100 updates, 0.53 at 2,500 and 0.46 at 6,000 (row vestibular_token_path_live_bench). Every whole-model reading is on 481,800; the state to be switched (the adoption's endpoint) has none with the path, where the trainer's probe reads head tilt at -0.0181 at 489,350 (control -0.0414); the production segment's T1 is the first reading of that state. M4's vision stop admits a rise of vision's error ratio up to 3.95 times its level before the switch, where the bench's line was 1.035 times the control arm: the first run's largest reading, 1.28 times, would cross neither M4 nor its alert (3.29 times), so a run that reads no stop has not shown that vision's prediction is unchanged. S1'S LINE: -0.10 is under every reading of `on` on the bench (-0.02 at the lowest) and is passed by `on_delayed_encoder_only` near 10,000 updates; so under `on`, the wiring offered, an S1 alert is outside what any bench read; under `on_delayed_encoder_only` it is EXPECTED between N + 10,000 and N + 20,000 (the exception's measured cost arriving). W1'S LINE: 0.2 is 1.9 times the bench's largest weight size with the hold (0.105) and the size at which, without the hold, rows first reached the cap. THE EXPECTED TRANSIENT: none of the other senses' lines dips at the switch (the path's output is exactly 0 at the load; in the whole-model bench it grew at 4 to 10 in 100 of the growth line). T2'S REACHABILITY: NOT SHOWN BY A BENCH; with the whole model vestibular's error stayed at its no-change error with the path and without it, and on the encoder bench what a linear reader of the token's own two last values gives of its next change reads 0.147 at 2,000 updates and 0.039 at 60,000 under `on`, and 0.142 and 0.008 under `on_delayed_encoder_only` (0 = no better than predicting no change, 1 = exact; path_bench_hold/bench.json, key next_model_step_from_own_history.improvement, arms path_none_cap03 and path_live_only_cap03; CORRECTED Oct 5, 2026 12:55 PM PDT on the independent review's finding of that day: the two readings first both named `on_delayed_encoder_only`, as 0.13 to 0.03 and 0.17 to 0.008). T2's miss says the transformer does not yet predict the token, not that the path failed. Stop lines M4 and M5 are the vestibular repair watch's multiples, measured on the lineage with nothing switched (out of sample the stop fired in 0 of 206 and 0 of 234 watches). M6's constant: learning rate 3e-4 x the measured summed input size 22.8 x the gain 1/sqrt(28).

cost.where: production training, one segment; the path adds 5,376 weights (28 x 192) and one matrix product of 8 x 28 per encoder call
cost.basis: No stop of its own: it is the production run. The watch covers 10,000 model steps after the switch. The relaunch itself stops training for as long as a relaunch does (the motor path's relaunch of Oct 4 is the reference).

result_source.file: the switched run's replay_training_stats.jsonl and those of its continuations (Saved/mimo_bridge/experiments/<run>)

rows.on_pass: No stop through N + 10,000 and no standing alert through N + 60,000: the path stays on in production's command through every relaunch (a checkpoint saved with the path is refused by a build without it), the checkpoint before the switch is released, and the row is closed. T2 missed with T1 held: the path stays, and T2 is read again after the prediction heads' repair.
rows.on_fail: A stop: the watcher has paused the supervisor and written snapshot_and_stop. Revert: resume the checkpoint the switch resumed with the flag off: relaunch_h84_seg41_2026-09-29.py --tag <letter> --reason "<why>" --parent <the run before the switch> --set vestibular-input-path off; reattach the supervisor and lift the pause. Every checkpoint written after the switch is refused by a build without the path, so the model steps since the switch are lost at a revert; that is why the checkpoint before the switch is kept through N + 60,000. A STANDING ALERT ON T1: the target is missed while the path is on; the alert carries the change slope and the weight size; the coordinator decides between the revert and going on (the other wiring is the exception, which the reviewer's bench read at the same read-out with the opposition added). A standing alert on S1 with T1 held: under `on` it is outside what any bench read (the encoder's part working against the path's without the delayed lesson's help) and is reported to the operator with the readings; under `on_delayed_encoder_only` it is the expected opposition. A standing alert on W1: the hold is not doing what it was benched to do; reported with the weight's size per report.
rows.decision: Not switched on (coordinator, Oct 4, 2026). The builder's branch fix/vestibular_token_readouts-2026-10-03 at fe276c7de holds the independent review's named changes (review/vestibular-input-path-2026-10-04, commit 238d29462): flag value on = the wiring in which the delayed lesson trains neither the encoder nor the path (the coordinator's decision on the review's long bench); on_delayed_encoder_only = the first wiring; the weight held at the cap; standing alerts on the head-tilt read-out, the change slope and the weight size; the checkpoint before the switch kept through N + 60,000. Since then (corrected Oct 13, 2026 from D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/head_tilt_reconciliation_20261013/RECONCILIATION.md): path version 2 under `on` ran three times with the whole model on the graphics card (Oct 5 and Oct 8; the first failed on vision, the seed-1 and seed-0 runs did not repeat the rise, and the seed-0 rerun's PASS selected `on` for the restart under the operator's rule of Oct 7); the merge 1bd91c3b1 carries the code off by default; the operator's decision of Oct 8 stopped automatic deployment, and the flag reads off in every H84 run folder since (seg41j_1526, seg41u_1718, seg41r_1539, B1LO, B1C, B1E). Oct 13, 2026: proxy decision proxy-head-tilt-route-20261013 (Saved/gof_coordination/mailbox/proxy-head-tilt-route-20261013/message.json, sha256 f30297e2...; author: the overseer) approved the processor test (row head_tilt_repair_module_tests_f0dd472a3) and the preparation of one bounded full-training activation after the adoption endpoint; the launch is the decision from that endpoint's evidence. Not switched on.

rows.title: Vestibular inputs model step by model step up to the held checkpoint: the saved worlds of 478,029 replayed on the CPU to 479,350
rows.question: What are the vestibular encoder's 29 raw input numbers at every model step for each of the 8 bodies over the 1,321 model steps from checkpoint 478,029 to checkpoint 479,350, when each saved world is restored on the CPU and handed the commands production handed it, and how far does the replayed body stay from the lived one?
rows.why: The repair path beside the vestibular encoder has to be benched with the transformer and the lessons live on checkpoint 479,350 (the coordinator's instruction of Oct 4, after the heads' paths ran away in production within 250 model steps although their bench on fixed windows had passed). That bench needs the vestibular encoder's inputs of the same model steps whose other senses' tokens checkpoint 479,350's replay ring holds (model steps 473,350 to 479,350). No file holds them (row vestibular_token_snapshots); the replay of 459,961 gave inputs of another stretch. The decision that depends on it: whether the path is offered as deployable.
inputs: Checkpoint 478,029's episode companion of run H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41m_0402 (read only; decompressed into D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/vestibular_token2/companions with its sha256 checked against the checkpoint's receipt): the 8 saved worlds, each with its own settings and its full simulator state.

The observer's world recording of that run (Saved/mimo_bridge/experiments/<run>/observer/world/b0 to b7, read only): per body and model step the command the world was handed (26 body handles x 9 numbers: target position xyz in cm, orientation as 4 numbers, radius, strength 0-1; the handle mask; the hand's 44 joint goals; the eye command's 2 angles) and the joint positions at the model step's last physics frame.

The world's own code (mimo_bridge/env.py BridgeEnv, built with vision off: no picture is rendered and no graphics context is made) and the observer baseline's restore helpers. No model, no trainer, no learning.
steps: One body after another in one process: build the world from its saved settings (scene files into the scratch folder, the caregiver's event tape replaced by a counter, vision off); restore the saved state; compare the restored state with the saved one exactly and stop the body when anything differs.

For each model step s from 478,029 to 479,349: hand the world the recorded command of model step s for 5 physics frames of 10 ms; after the 5th frame keep the raw vestibular vector (29 numbers: the input of model step s + 1), the joint positions, gravity in the head from the simulator's own orientation matrix, and the same direction for the lived body by forward kinematics of the recorded joint positions.
Fidelity per model step: the replayed joint positions minus the recorded ones; the angle between the replayed and the lived direction of gravity in the head.
Write replay_b<body>.npz per body and replay.json after every body.
measures: The raw vestibular vector per body and model step: 8 x 1,321 x 29 numbers in the fields' own units.
Joint difference, replayed minus recorded, in radians and metres (0 = the lived trajectory repeated); model steps until any body joint first differs by 1e-4.
The angle between the replayed and the lived direction of gravity in the head, degrees (0 = the same head orientation).
rows.pass_line: No pass line on the fidelity: it is measured and reported. The job completes when every world restores to its saved state under the exact comparison, every model step's frame number equals the recorded one, and all 8 bodies reach 479,350. PAIRING RULE, declared before the run: the replayed vestibular inputs are paired with the ring's lived tokens of the other senses at the same model step as APPROXIMATE lived inputs; the bench that uses them states the median and the largest angle between the replayed and the lived head direction, and its read-outs take their labels from the replayed rows themselves.
rows.pass_line_basis: Measured on the replay of 459,961 (row vestibular_token_inputs_replay_459961, Oct 4): the replay equals the lived trajectory for 2 to 10 model steps and then stays near it, gravity in the head within 0.6 to 1.5 degrees of the lived direction at the median for seven bodies and 3.6 degrees for the body lying face down (largest 4.9 to 13.0), against 6.9 degrees of the bodies' own change of that direction within a report. So the replayed vestibular input of a model step is the lived one to about a seventh of what the read-out reads.

cost.where: the CPU, with training held (the heads segment stopped at 479,600; supervisor control = pause, no trainer): one process, 4 threads, under a hard limit of 2.9 GB of RAM and 6 GB committed, no graphics card; a job that builds MuJoCo worlds, so it starts only with 45 GB or more of commit room and no lockstep or trainer process running, and its process tree is ended when a trainer process starts
cost.basis: Measured on the replay of 459,961: 194 to 309 s a body for 1,670 model steps (1,900 s for 8 bodies), largest RAM of the process 0.79 GB, most committed 4.27 GB. This one has 1,321 model steps a body.

rows.on_pass: The bench with the transformer and the lessons live (its own row) reads these rows as the vestibular inputs of model steps 478,030 to 479,350.
rows.on_fail: A world that does not restore exactly, or a frame number that does not match: that body is left out and named; with fewer than 8 bodies the bench cannot form the 8-body rows VICReg's term needs, and falls back on the rows of the replay of 459,961 paired with ring windows of other model steps (stated in its row).

values: Ran Oct 4, 2026 10:45:10 AM to 11:09:40 AM PDT with training held (one process, 4 threads, the graphics card hidden): 8 of 8 worlds restored to their saved state under the exact comparison and reached model step 479,350 (1,321 model steps each, 147 to 316 s a body).

FIDELITY: the first model step at which any body joint differs from the recorded position by 1e-4 is model step 6, 11, 8, 11, 5, 5, 3, 5 after the start, per body. The joint difference (root mean square over the body's joints) has a median of 0.019 to 0.070 rad or m over the 1,321 model steps, per body.

The direction of gravity in the head differs from the lived one (forward kinematics of the recorded joint positions) by 0.5 to 1.5 degrees at the median for seven bodies and by 1.9 degrees for body 5; the largest angle per body is 3.0 to 12.1 degrees. For scale: the bodies' own change of that direction within a report of 100 model steps was 6.9 degrees on the replay of 459,961.

PAIRING RULE as declared: the rows are paired with checkpoint 479,350's ring at the same model step as approximate lived inputs (replay model step s = the ring's entry 479,349 - s model steps before its newest); the bench that uses them (row vestibular_token_path_live_bench) checks that pairing on the first model step against the ring's stored token and takes its read-out labels from the replayed rows.
result.verdict: completed: 8 of 8 bodies restored exactly and replayed to 479,350; gravity in the head within 1.9 degrees of the lived direction at the median for the worst body

rows.decision: The live bench reads these rows as the vestibular inputs of model steps 478,030 to 479,349. Written Oct 4, 2026 11:09 AM PDT.

rows.title: The runaway of the tactile all-slot path: checkpoint 479,700 read against checkpoint 479,350
rows.question: In the checkpoint the stopped run saved (model step 479,700), which part of the tactile path carries its output of 2.7 token units: the output layer's weights, the layers before it, the offset between the running centre and the rows the path reads, or the transformer's output having moved since the switch?
rows.why: The repair of the runaway must follow from its mechanism (the coordinator's task of Oct 4, 10:40 AM PDT; training is off until the repaired candidate is delivered). The four reports of the stopped run give sizes only; this reading separates the candidate causes on the saved weights before any reproduction is run, and it names what the reproduction must switch off to confirm each one.
inputs: Checkpoint ckpt_step_479350 of run H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41m_0402 (the state at the switch; built with the flag on, so its paths are the fresh ones the run started from).

Checkpoint ckpt_step_479700 of run H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41n_0856 (saved by the stopped run: the paths as trained, their running centre, their Adam state) and its episode companion: per body the newest 6,000 model steps of tokens (6 senses x 192 numbers), achieved poses, executed commands and memory states.
400 windows of 129 model steps (50 ring ages 7 model steps apart x 8 bodies) inside the 350 model steps the stopped run lived, and the 8 newest ages (64 rows).

Checkpoint ckpt_step_478029 of run H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41m_0402 (1,321 model steps before the switch, trained without the paths): the baseline for how far the transformer's output moves without them.
steps: Both models run the trainer's replay forward on the same windows without gradient: x = the transformer's output at the 6 slots plus the memory bias minus the memory's constant (6 x 192 numbers per row), once from the 479,350 transformer and once from the 479,700 transformer.

Per slot: root mean square per number of (rows' mean of x at 479,700 minus rows' mean of x at 479,350), of the per-row difference, and of what differs between rows; the length of (rows' mean minus the saved running centre) over the mean length of a row's own departure from the rows' mean.

Per head: the path's output and its hidden layer's input as root mean square per number, split into the part every row shares (the mean over rows) and the part that differs between rows; the share of hidden units whose input is under -3 on every row.

The same output recomputed four ways: with the centre put on the rows' own mean; with the 479,350 transformer's x; with the layers before the output layer put back to their fresh weights; with the output layer's bias alone.

Per weight tensor of each path: root mean square of its change from the fresh value, the mean absolute change over (learning rate 3e-4 x 525 optimizer updates), and Adam's mean |running average of the gradient| / sqrt(running average of the squared gradient).
Per head: summed squared error of (old head + path) and of the old head alone over the no-change error on the valid rows.

The old heads alone (no path, no gaze copy): each checkpoint's heads on each checkpoint's transformer output for the same windows; the output as root mean square per number, split into the part every row shares and the part that differs between rows. And how far the transformer's output moved between checkpoints 478,029 and 479,350 on the same windows.
measures: Sizes in token units, root mean square per number (a token's own size is 1 per number; the real change of a tactile token between model steps is about 0.16 per number).
Centre offset as a ratio: 0 = the centre sits on the rows' mean, 1 = the offset is as long as a row's own departure from that mean.
Mean absolute weight change over (learning rate x updates): 0 = no weight moved, 1 = every weight moved the same way at every update.
Adam's sign ratio: 0 = the gradient changed sign from update to update, 1 = it kept one sign.
Error over no-change error: 1 = no better than predicting that the token stays as it is, 0 = exact.
rows.pass_line: No pass or fail: a reading. It is complete when the JSON holds the four recomputed outputs for the tactile path and the per-slot movement of the transformer's output.
rows.pass_line_basis: The reading feeds the reproduction's arms; its own cross-check is the report of model step 479,700: on the newest 8 ages the centre offset read here must agree with the report's centre_lag (0.63 to 2.41 per slot) and the tactile path's output with the report's 2.69, within the difference between replayed rows and lived rows.

cost.where: CPU with training held (supervisor control = pause, no trainer): the hold limits of heads_registry.py, 8 threads, under 5 GB of RAM and 9 GB committed; ended when a trainer process starts
cost.basis: two builds of the H84 learner on the CPU and 2 x 464 windows through the trainer's replay forward; the capture of 4,900 windows of Oct 4 ran inside the same limits

rows.on_pass: The reproduction (row heads_all_slot_path_runaway_reproduction) runs the arms this reading names.
rows.on_fail: If the reading does not agree with the report of model step 479,700 on the newest ages, the tool is corrected before the reproduction is designed on it.

values: 400 windows of the 350 model steps the stopped run lived (50 ring ages x 8 bodies) through both checkpoints' models on the CPU; the tool was run 3 times (the old heads' cross-evaluation, the baseline checkpoint 478,029 and the two fixed vectors' directions were added in the second and third run).

THE OLD TACTILE HEAD outputs one fixed vector on every row, whichever checkpoint's transformer output it is given. Its size, root mean square per number: 0.0261 at checkpoint 478,029, 0.0301 at 479,350, 2.7785 at 479,700 (the part that differs between rows: 0.0001). Alone it now reads 252.9 times the no-change error.

THE TACTILE PATH at 479,700 outputs 2.68 token units per number, of which 2.68 is one fixed vector (the mean over the rows) and 0.10 differs between rows. The cosine between the old head's fixed vector and the path's is -0.99978; their sum's fixed part is 0.114. Old head + path read 1.68 times the no-change error.

The same pair in the other heads at 479,700 (old head's fixed vector / path's fixed vector / cosine): vision with the gaze copy 0.066 / 0.065 / -0.985; audio 0.083 / 0.064 / -0.924; proprioception 0.011 / 0.006 / -0.763; vestibular 0.0046 / 0.0087 / -0.401.

WHICH WEIGHTS MOVED IN THE OLD TACTILE HEAD (root mean square before -> change; mean absolute change over learning rate x 525 updates, where 1 = every number moved one way at every update): the revived first-layer units' LayerNorm gain 0.0015 -> 0.046 (0.27), its bias 0.006 -> 0.062 (0.38), their weights 0.041 -> 0.044 (0.24), their bias 0.223 -> 0.038 (0.21), the second layer's weights 0.0075 -> 0.0193 (0.10). No tensor of the old head moved faster than Adam's step allows: the fixed vector grew through the product of layers that each moved one way.

THE TACTILE PATH'S LAYERS (the same ratio): LayerNorm gain 0.47, slot matrix 0.24, hidden weights 0.17, hidden bias 0.72, output weights 0.17, output bias 0.29; the other four paths read 0.03 to 0.26. With the layers before the output layer put back to their fresh weights the tactile path's output is 0.032, so the size is in those layers, not in the output layer alone (the growth line assumed the output layer alone). 65 of 100 hidden units have a mean input beyond 3 in size; 6 units were revived.

THE RUNNING CENTRE lags the rows' mean by 0.63 to 2.51 row departures per slot (the report of model step 479,700 read 0.63 to 2.41 on the newest 64 rows; this reading on the newest 8 ages: 0.63 to 2.42). With the centre put on the rows' own mean the tactile path's output is 1.13; with the 479,350 transformer's output in place of the 479,700 one it is 0.35.

THE TRANSFORMER'S OUTPUT MEAN moved between 479,350 and 479,700, root mean square per number per slot: vision 0.95, tactile 1.63, audio 1.64, proprioception 1.70, motor 1.80, vestibular 0.65 (what differs between rows is 0.61 to 1.21). Between 478,029 and 479,350 (1,321 model steps without the paths) it moved 0.50 to 1.02.
result.verdict: reading complete: the size sits in two fixed vectors, the old tactile head's and the tactile path's, pointing against each other; their sum is what the lesson grades

rows.decision: The reproduction (row heads_all_slot_path_runaway_reproduction) tests which lesson drives the two vectors apart: arms without the imagination chain, with the paths' gradient into the transformer cut, and with the path trained by the chain as the old head is (row heads_all_slot_path_repair_bounded). Row heads_all_slot_path_lesson_forces measures each lesson's request on the fixed vector directly.

rows.title: The runaway of the tactile all-slot path reproduced on the CPU from checkpoint 479,350, with one cause switched off per arm
rows.question: Does the tactile path's output grow on the CPU as it grew in the stopped run (0.0097, 0.081, 0.52 and 2.69 token units at model steps 479,400, 479,500, 479,600 and 479,700) when the run's own lesson sequence is repeated from checkpoint 479,350, and which single change stops the growth: no gradient from the paths into the transformer, no imagination chain, no replay updates, no revival of the paths' hidden units, a running centre that starts on the rows' mean, a smaller tactile lesson weight, a smaller learning rate for the paths, or the old heads held fixed?
rows.why: The reading of checkpoint 479,700 (row heads_all_slot_path_runaway_read) shows two parts that each output one fixed vector growing against each other: the old tactile head's output went from 0.030 to 2.78 token units per number and the tactile path's output from 0 to 2.68, and their sum is what the lesson grades. The repair must remove the term that drives them apart, so each candidate cause is switched off alone and the growth read again. Training stays off until the repaired candidate is delivered.
inputs: Checkpoint ckpt_step_479350 of run H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41m_0402 with its optimizer state, built with --heads-all-slot-path on (fresh paths, as the stopped run built them).

The episode companion of ckpt_step_479700 of run H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41n_0856: the replay ring, per body the newest 6,000 model steps of the 6 senses' tokens (192 numbers each), achieved poses, executed commands, memory states and validity; its newest 350 model steps are the ones the stopped run lived after the switch.
Per arm one setting of the tool's switches (the arm's name states it); every arm sees the same rows in the same sequence (one random stream for the replay draws, seed 1234).
steps: Per emulated model step s = 1 to 350: the lived lesson on the 8 bodies' rows of model step 479,350 + s (context of 127 stored model steps, current motor token rebuilt from pose and executed command, memory bias rebuilt from the stored state; loss = sum over the senses of the persistence normaliser's weight x mean squared error of old head + path against the stored next token).

In arms with the imagination chain: from the row of 3 model steps earlier, 3 predictions in a row through lem.model.predictive_state.transition (each passes the encoders' output LayerNorm and is fed back in; the paths' weights are detached, the row keeps its gradient), loss 0.5 x the summed mean squared errors, added to the lived lesson's loss.

One optimizer update on that sum: backward, the trainer's gradient clipping, AdamW with the checkpoint's Adam state. The paths' running centre takes the lived rows a second time (production's two learning calls per model step).
Every second model step one replay update (LemLite.replay_update, 24 windows drawn from the ring's model steps before the emulated one).
The liveness repair's step end after every model step (a full watching window of 800 rows revives hidden units whose input stayed under -3).

Every model step: per head the old head's output and the path's output on the lived rows, each as the root mean square per number of its mean over the rows, the same for their sum, and the cosine between the two mean vectors; per slot the centre offset. Every 50 model steps on 64 fixed rows of model steps before the switch: error over no-change error with and without the path, the path's output size, how far the transformer's output mean moved since the start.
measures: The tactile path's output in token units, root mean square per number (0 = the switch; the stopped run read 0.0097, 0.081, 0.52, 2.69 at 50, 150, 250, 350 model steps; a tactile token changes by about 0.17 per number between model steps).
The old tactile head's output, the same unit (0.030 at the switch; 2.78 in checkpoint 479,700).

Error over no-change error on the fixed rows: 1 = no better than predicting that the token stays as it is, 0 = exact; the tactile head read 1.04 at the switch and 1.85 in the stopped run's last report.

Transformer movement: the length of the change of the rows' mean output per slot over the mean length of a row's own departure from that mean (0 = unmoved, 1 = moved as far as rows differ from each other).
rows.pass_line: REPRODUCED when the base arm's tactile path output at 350 model steps is above 0.29 token units (the stopped run's growth line at 375 updates) with the old tactile head's output above 0.3. A CAUSE IS CONFIRMED for an arm whose single change keeps both under 0.1 through 350 model steps while the base arm reproduces. If no arm without the worlds reproduces, the row's result says so and names what the emulation leaves out.
rows.pass_line_basis: 0.29 is the line that stopped the production run (0.00078 token units x 375 optimizer updates). The stopped run's own readings are 0.52 at 250 model steps and 2.69 at 350, so an arm that reproduces the mechanism passes the line with room; 0.1 is under the 0.52 by a factor of 5 and above the bench's largest reading (0.068 after 1,500 updates with the transformer held fixed), so an arm under 0.1 at 350 model steps behaves as the bench did. The emulation can miss the mechanism: it runs no world, no planner, no encoder learning and float32 in place of the graphics card's 16-bit arithmetic; the base arm is the control for that.

cost.where: CPU with training held (supervisor control = pause, no trainer): the hold limits of heads_registry.py, up to 3 arms side by side, 8 threads each, under 5 GB of RAM and 9 GB committed per process; ended when a trainer process starts
cost.basis: one replay update of 24 windows took 5.3 s on 8 threads (the resume check of Oct 4); an emulated model step is one update on 8 rows, 3 chain passes on 8 rows and half a replay update

rows.on_pass: The confirmed cause is removed in the design (lem/model/heads_all_slot_path.py and its hooks); the repaired design runs the same sequence for 4 x the stopped run's updates (row heads_all_slot_path_repair_bounded) before the identity chain.
rows.on_fail: If the base arm does not reproduce, the difference between the emulation and the live model step is narrowed arm by arm (the chain, the replay share, the centre's two calls); if it cannot be reproduced without the worlds, the repair is derived from checkpoint 479,700's reading and its bound is shown on the sequence that can be run.

values: BASE ARM (the first design with the chain), stopped by hand after 201 of 350 model steps (301 optimizer updates) with both fixed vectors past the line. The old tactile head's fixed vector / the tactile path's fixed vector on the lived rows, token units per number, and the cosine between the two: 0.037 / 0.002, -0.97 at 25 model steps; 0.038 / 0.010, -0.96 at 50; 0.045 / 0.022, -0.98 at 75; 0.054 / 0.046, -1.00 at 100; 0.123 / 0.098, -0.99 at 125; 0.122 / 0.108, -1.00 at 150; 0.261 / 0.267, -1.00 at 175; 0.409 / 0.523, -1.00 at 200. The stopped production run read a path output of 0.0097 at 50 model steps, 0.081 at 150 and 0.52 at 250. On the 64 fixed rows the tactile error with the path / old head alone read 1.026 / 1.047, 1.006 / 1.086, 1.034 / 1.512 and 1.252 / 6.670 at 50, 100, 150 and 200. No hidden unit of any path was revived.

ARM WITHOUT THE CHAIN'S LOSS (first design's rule), 350 model steps, 525 updates: the old tactile head's fixed vector fell from 0.030 to 0.005 within 60 model steps and stayed between 0.004 and 0.008; the tactile path's output on the fixed rows 0.004 to 0.047; tactile error with the path / old head alone 0.999 / 1.001 at 50, 0.989 / 0.998 at 100, 0.982 / 1.000 at 150, 0.956 / 0.999 at 200, 0.965 / 0.999 at 250, 0.976 / 1.001 at 300, 0.962 / 0.997 at 350.

ARM WITH THE PATHS' GRADIENT INTO THE TRANSFORMER CUT (first design, 150 model steps on the base arm's rows): the pair grew faster: 0.039 / 0.018 at 50 model steps, 0.088 / 0.082 at 100, 0.327 / 0.301 at 150, cosine -0.97 to -1.00; tactile error with the path / old head alone 1.019 / 1.050, 1.031 / 1.239, 1.169 / 4.502. The transformer's output mean moved 0.39 to 0.56 per number on the tactile, audio, proprioception and motor slots by 150 against 0.78 to 0.86 in arm base.

ARM WITH THE RUNNING CENTRE STARTED ON THE ROWS' MEAN AND FILLED (first design, 75 model steps on the base arm's rows; old tactile head's fixed vector / tactile path's fixed vector): at 25 model steps 0.037 / 0.006, cosine -0.96 (arm base 0.037 / 0.002, cosine -0.97); at 50 model steps 0.042 / 0.021, cosine -0.94 (arm base 0.038 / 0.010, cosine -0.96); at 75 model steps 0.065 / 0.037, cosine -0.99 (arm base 0.045 / 0.022, cosine -0.98). The pair grows with a filled centre too: a warming centre is not needed for the growth.
ARM WITH THE CHAIN TRAINING THE PATHS (the repair): row heads_all_slot_path_repair_bounded holds it: no growth of the pair.

rows.title: Vestibular input path benched with the transformer and the lessons live: 3,000 updates of checkpoint 479,350's whole model on the graphics card, with the path and without it
rows.question: When checkpoint 479,350's whole model (encoders, transformer, prediction heads, reconstruction decoders, its optimizer state) is updated 3,000 times on its own replay ring's last 1,320 model steps with the vestibular inputs of those model steps, does the vestibular input path (a) stay under the growth line the production watch will hold it to, (b) put head tilt into the vestibular token on model steps no update read, and (c) leave the other senses' prediction errors where the same updates without the path leave them?
rows.why: The prediction heads' all-slot paths passed a bench on fixed transformer outputs and then ran away in production: the tactile path's output read 0.52 token units 250 model steps after its switch against a growth line of 0.29, and the run was stopped at model step 479,600 (Oct 4, 9:10 AM PDT). The vestibular input path's first bench (row vestibular_token_path_bench) trained the encoder alone. The coordinator's instruction of Oct 4, 10:40 AM: bench it with the transformer and the lesson live and bound or test its growth before it is offered as deployable. The decision that depends on it: whether the production segment's row (vestibular_input_path_production_segment) is offered to the coordinator, and with which growth line and cap.
inputs: Checkpoint 479,350 of run H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41m_0402 (read only): model.safetensors, optimizer.pt, runtime_state.pt, args.json. The model is built by the trainer's own builder (mimo_bridge.tools.causal_test._build_model, which calls train_mimo.build_learner on the run's saved arguments) and loaded with LemLite.load_checkpoint and its optimizer state. Arm `path`: the run's arguments plus --vestibular-input-path on (the load is then the switch, and its check record is kept). Arm `control`: the run's arguments as they are.

The checkpoint's episode companion (read only, decompressed copy in the scratch folder): the replay ring, per body the newest 6,000 model steps: the 6 senses' tokens (6 x 192 numbers per model step, as the trainer stored them), the stored pose (26 body handles x 10 numbers), the executed command (26 body handles x 9 numbers), which senses were real, and the persistent memory's state (the numbers its readout turns into a bias on the transformer's input).

The rows of the replay job (row vestibular_token_inputs_replay_478029; D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/vestibular_token2/replay_478029): per body and model step from 478,030 to 479,349 the 29 raw vestibular numbers and gravity in the head (3 numbers, from the simulator's orientation matrix). They are the lived inputs to within the replay's measured distance from the lived body (stated in that row's result). The 28 encoder fields are clipped and scaled with checkpoint 479,350's saved input statistics, held fixed.
The branch's code at the commit named in the result (lem/model/vestibular_input_path.py with its output cap of 1.0 token units; docs/gain_of_function_v4/vestibular_token/vt_live_bench.py).
steps: ROUTE CHECK, before anything else: the vestibular token of model step 478,030 is computed on the CPU from the replayed input with checkpoint 478,029's saved encoder and input statistics and compared with the ring's stored vestibular tokens of model steps 478,028 to 478,032. Line: the stored token of 478,030 is the nearest of the five and within 0.02 token units (root mean square per number; the token's change between two model steps is 0.020 on this checkpoint). A miss stops the job: the replayed inputs and the ring would not belong to the same model steps.
CODE CHECK PASS: both arms for 100 updates into a folder of their own, to find a fault of the bench's code before the long pass; its readings are kept and stated.

MAIN PASS, one arm after the other, each in its own process on the graphics card under the model's own bf16 autocast, 3,000 updates. One update reads one model step t of the span's read part (478,158 to 478,849: every model step of the span whose 127 context model steps have replayed inputs, without the span's last 500), all 8 bodies in one batch, in the sequence they were lived, cycled.

Per update, the LIVE ROW (model step t): the 5 other senses' tokens from the ring (no gradient); the vestibular token encoded from the replayed input with gradient, the path open; the context is the 127 model steps before t with their vestibular tokens encoded by the weights as they are now and their motor tokens rebuilt from the stored pose and executed command, plus the transformer's sense embedding; transformer forward with the memory's bias of t. Its loss terms: VICReg on the real senses' tokens (LossManager.compute_vicreg) and the reconstruction decoders' term at the trainer's scheduled weight (0.02 to 0.3, half the mean next-model-step error).

Per update, the DELAYED LESSON (t - 1 to t): the row of t - 1 with its vestibular token encoded again with gradient through the encoder and the path's weight held out of the gradient (as LemLite.step does), its motor token rebuilt with the executed command; transformer forward with the memory's bias of t - 1; prediction heads with the gaze copy; per sense the mean squared error against the token of t (for vestibular: the live token of t, no gradient), each weighted by the persistence normalisation's own weight with the revival ceiling, the residual input's share kept at weight 1 (next_frame_norm.weighted_term), as LemLite.step weighs them; the running no-change errors take the reading as in the trainer.

Per update: loss.backward(), LemLite._clip_training_gradients() (the path is its own clipping group), the model's own AdamW step. After every 2nd update one LemLite.replay_update(batch 24), the trainer's own replay update on windows drawn from the whole ring. Every 100 updates the ring's vestibular tokens of the span are written again from the weights as they are.

READINGS at updates 0, 100, 200, 300, 500 and every 500 after: the path's output (root mean square per number over the span's 10,560 rows, and the largest row), its weight's size, the share of rows at the cap; the trainer's probe restated in numpy (each body's change from its own mean over a report of 100 model steps; ridge of 1e-3 of the mean diagonal; fitted on the even bodies and scored on the odd ones and the other way round; the body-shuffled control) for head tilt, gravity in the head and the trunk's roll, on all 13 reports and on the 5 reports of the unread 500 model steps alone; the token's spread between bodies and its change between two model steps; without gradient, on every 10th model step of the read part (70) and of the unread part (50), per sense the delayed lesson's error over the error of predicting no change; the loss's parts, the largest gradient norm and the count of non-finite losses since the reading before.

NOT IN THE BENCH, stated so the result is not read as more than it is: the top-down gate's blend; wellness, the planner and the motor controller's live terms; the efference, contact and self-state lessons; the imagination chain; the liveness repair's revivals (every pass runs outside its watching windows); new experience (the same 692 model steps are cycled 4.3 times); the running update of the input statistics.
