rows.title: What the lived lesson, the replay lesson and the imagination chain each ask of the fixed part of every head's prediction at checkpoint 479,350
rows.question: At the switch state, does the imagination chain's loss move a vector added to every row's tactile prediction in the direction opposite to the one the lived lesson moves it, and does the chain keep moving the old head's fixed vector further out once that vector is cancelled on every row (which is what a path trained by the lived lesson alone does to it)?
rows.why: The runaway's mechanism as read from checkpoint 479,700 is two lessons asking different fixed vectors of one sum while only one of them can train the path. This reading measures the two requests directly, per sense, before any training: the sign and size of each lesson's derivative along the old head's fixed vector. It is the control for the mechanism: if the chain and the lived lesson ask the same fixed vector, the mechanism is wrong and the repair that follows from it is not justified. It also states why the tactile sense ran first: the chain's request against the lived lesson's, per sense.
inputs: Checkpoint ckpt_step_479350 of run H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41m_0402, built with --heads-all-slot-path on (the paths' output layers are zero: every prediction is production's), and its own episode companion (the replay ring).
40 batches of the 8 bodies' rows at ring ages 3, 10, 17, ... (320 rows; each with the row of 3 model steps earlier for the chain), and 20 draws of 24 random windows for the replay lesson.

A second run on checkpoint ckpt_step_479700 of run H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41n_0856 (the paths as the stopped run trained them, loaded for reading under their saved version name) with its own episode companion: the same derivatives with both fixed vectors in place, and the path's fixed vector on the chain's rows against the lived rows.
steps: A vector of 192 numbers per sense is added to every prediction the heads make for that sense: in the lived lesson's call, in each of the chain's 3 calls (before the encoders' output LayerNorm), in the replay lesson's call.
Per batch: the derivative of the lived lesson's loss, of 0.5 x the chain's loss and of the replay lesson's loss with respect to that vector; averaged over the batches.
Taken twice: with the vector at zero (the old head's fixed vector in place) and with the vector at minus the old head's fixed vector (the fixed vector cancelled on every row, lived and imagined).
Per sense: each derivative's component along the old head's fixed vector, its size, and the cosines between the lessons' derivatives.

On checkpoint 479,700: every call of the paths is kept by where it came from (the lived lesson's call; the chain's calls at depth 1, 2 and 3); per head the path's fixed vector at each, and its share of the lived rows' fixed vector: (fixed vector at that depth . fixed vector on lived rows) / (fixed vector on lived rows . itself).
measures: Component of a lesson's derivative along the old head's fixed vector (loss units per token unit): positive = gradient descent on that lesson moves the fixed vector toward zero; negative = it moves it further out; 0 = the lesson asks nothing along it.
Cosine between the lived lesson's and the chain's derivatives: 1 = they ask the same change, -1 = opposite changes.

Share of the lived rows' fixed vector on the chain's rows: 1 = the path adds the same fixed vector where the chain grades as where the lived lesson trained it; above 1 = it adds more there, so each cancellation the lived lesson makes is larger in the chain's eyes and the chain's answer overshoots (a loop whose gain is that share); under 1 = less.
rows.pass_line: THE MECHANISM HOLDS FOR TACTILE when, with the fixed vector in place, the lived lesson's component is positive and the chain's is negative, and, with the fixed vector cancelled, the chain's component is still negative while the lived lesson's is under one tenth of its own value with the vector in place.
rows.pass_line_basis: Before the switch the old tactile head's fixed vector sat at 0.030 token units per number for more than 1,300 model steps (checkpoints 478,029 and 479,350 read 0.026 and 0.030) while costing the lived lesson 4.3 of 100 of its error: something other than the lived lesson held it there, and the reproduction's arm without the chain read it falling to 0.005 within 60 model steps. If that something is the chain, its derivative along the vector is negative and of the lived lesson's size. The reading can fail: a chain derivative that is positive or near zero along the vector would say the chain is not what holds it.

cost.where: CPU with training held (supervisor control = pause, no trainer): the hold limits of heads_registry.py, 8 threads, under 5 GB of RAM and 9 GB committed; ended when a trainer process starts
cost.basis: 80 lived batches, 80 chain passes and 40 replay batches without any optimizer update

rows.on_pass: The mechanism stands as measured; the repair gives the path the chain's gradient (the record's section 13).
rows.on_fail: The mechanism is read again from the reproduction's arms before any repair is kept.

values: Both runs ended with exit code 0: 40 batches of the 8 bodies' rows (320 rows) each for the lived lesson and the chain, 20 draws of 24 windows for the replay lesson, on checkpoint 479,350 and on checkpoint 479,700. A derivative's component along the old head's fixed vector is given in loss units per token unit: positive = gradient descent on that lesson moves the fixed vector toward zero, negative = further out.

CHECKPOINT 479,350, TACTILE, the old head's fixed vector (0.030 token units per number) in place: the lived lesson +0.00336, the replay lesson +0.00309, the chain -0.00430. One model step (lived + chain + half a replay update): +0.00061, a fifth of the lived lesson's own value: the fixed vector sat where the chain's request and the lived lesson's balance.

CHECKPOINT 479,350, TACTILE, the fixed vector cancelled on every row, lived and imagined (what a path trained by the lived lesson alone does to it): the lived lesson +0.00029 (0.087 of its value with the vector in place), the replay lesson +0.00007, the chain -0.00767. One model step: -0.00735. With the vector cancelled the lived lesson asks next to nothing and the chain moves the old head's fixed vector further out with 1.8 times the force it had before.

THE OTHER SENSES at 479,350 with the fixed vector cancelled, the chain's component along the old head's fixed vector: audio -0.00746, vestibular -0.00192, proprioception -0.00044 (vision's old head alone carries a fixed vector of 0.92 that the gaze copy cancels, so cancelling it by hand leaves the gaze copy's part and the reading is not comparable). The chain's loss carries no per-sense normalisation: the two senses whose tokens change most (the persistence normaliser's running mean squared change: audio 0.043, tactile 0.024, vision 0.008, proprioception 0.006, vestibular 0.004) receive the largest request.

CHECKPOINT 479,700 (both fixed vectors grown: old tactile head 2.78, tactile path 2.69 on these rows, cosine -0.9998): the chain's component along the old head's fixed vector is still negative, -0.00523; the lived lesson's is +0.00844.

THE PATH'S FIXED VECTOR ON THE CHAIN'S ROWS AGAINST THE LIVED ROWS at 479,700 (share of the lived rows' fixed vector present at chain depth 1, 2, 3): tactile 1.001, 0.997, 0.992; vision 1.003, 1.005, 1.007; audio 1.000, 1.028, 1.037; proprioception 1.004, 1.005, 1.014; vestibular 1.026, 1.030, 1.018. The path adds the same fixed vector where the chain grades as where the lived lesson trained it: each cancellation the lived lesson makes is present in full in the chain's predictions.
result.verdict: the mechanism holds for tactile: with the fixed vector in place the lived lesson's component is positive and the chain's negative; with it cancelled the chain's is still negative (-0.00767) while the lived lesson's is 0.087 of its own value with the vector in place (the line: under one tenth)

rows.decision: The repair gives the paths the chain's gradient (version heads_all_slot_path_v2), so that the two requests meet on the sum of old head and path as they met on the old head alone before the switch. The loop of the first design is: old head's fixed vector moves out (chain) -> path cancels it (lived lesson) -> the cancellation is present in full on the chain's rows (share 0.99 to 1.00) -> the chain's request is unmet by the same amount again. Its gain is 1: nothing damps it, and its speed is the speed at which Adam can move the two parts, which rises as the layers before their output layers grow one way. Why tactile first: its chain request is the largest together with audio's, and its old head is a pure fixed-vector generator (three layers of revived units that all read one fixed input); audio's pair is the second largest in checkpoint 479,700 (0.083 and 0.064).

rows.title: Which of production's weights lose their gradient to autocast's weight cache: one live model step and one replay update of the trainer's own code on the graphics card from checkpoint 479,350, cache on against cache off
rows.question: In one LemLite.step and one LemLite.replay_update run on the graphics card from checkpoint 479,350's saved state, which optimised parameter tensors get no gradient, or a different gradient, because PyTorch's autocast kept a bf16 copy of the weight that was first made under torch.no_grad() inside the same autocast block, and at which file and line is that first use?
rows.why: Measured Oct 4, 2026 on checkpoint 479,350's vestibular encoder (torch 2.6.0, the card; D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/vestibular_token2/logs/live_bench_debug3.log): after a no_grad call first inside one autocast block every Linear weight and bias of the encoder had gradient None; with the gradient call first, with a block of its own, or with cache_enabled=False the first Linear's gradient was 0.0196. LemLite.step is one autocast block from lem_model.py line 2617 with no_grad calls inside it, and no CPU test can show the loss (the CPU path has no autocast). The decision that depends on it (the coordinator's instruction of Oct 4, 2026, on that finding): whether a repair of production's code is needed, for which modules, and whether parts found untrained in this lineage were untrained for this reason. The repair is a separate decision; this test changes no production file.
inputs: Checkpoint 479,350 of run H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41m_0402 (read only): model.safetensors, optimizer.pt, runtime_state.pt, the run's args.json.

Its episode companion (read only; the decompressed copy D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/vestibular_token2/companions/ckpt_step_479350.pt, its sha256 checked against the checkpoint's receipt when it was made): the learner's continuation state (the context of 127 model steps, the delayed lesson's stored row, the short histories, the replay ring of 6,000 model steps per body, the random number generators' states), the trainer's state (the executed command of the model step before: 26 body handles x 9 numbers, its gaze command, its id, the babble bout's state, each frame's meta), and per body the saved payload (the tokenizer's frame bytes with the picture, the tactile rows, the 29 vestibular numbers) that the trainer's own resume turns into its first frame.

The branch's code (production's tip c59ecab7e merged; no file of production changed by this test): mimo_bridge/train_mimo.py (parse_args, build_learner, bind_schedule_to_config, switch_stored_eye_rows, planner_calf_geometry), mimo_bridge/lem_model.py (LemLite.step, LemLite.replay_update), mimo_bridge/continuation_state.py (restore_learner), mimo_bridge/datasource._payload_to_frame; the measuring script docs/gain_of_function_v4/vestibular_token/autocast_cache_audit.py.
steps: Six runs, one process each, one after the other on the graphics card: a_on, a_on2, a_off (one live model step), b_on, b_on2, b_off (one replay update). No MuJoCo world is built: the trainer's resume builds its first frame from the saved payload and collects no new one, and this test does the same.

Per run: the trainer's own construction and resume in main()'s sequence: parse_args defaults overwritten by the run's args.json (8 bodies, the card, bf16 autocast); build_learner; load_checkpoint with the optimizer state; the seeds folded with the model step count; the curriculum manager; reset_context; enable_replay; the 8 frames from the payloads with their saved meta; restore_learner (context, histories, ring, and torch's, CUDA's, numpy's and Python's generator states); switch_stored_eye_rows; the hand geometry the companion holds; the calf projection; the dev limits with the run's babble settings.

Part a: one LemLite.step(frames, dev, train=True, step_index=479350, executed_action=..., executed_ctrl_gaze=..., executed_order_id=...) as train_mimo calls it. Part b: torch's generator seeded with 20261004, then one LemLite.replay_update(batch=24).

Cache on: nothing is changed. Cache off: in that process torch's autocast class is entered with cache_enabled=False at every block (its __init__ is wrapped in memory), so every use casts the weight anew with its gradient. on2 repeats on from the same state and seed.

Read when LemLite._clip_training_gradients is called (after loss.backward(), before the clip): every optimised parameter tensor's gradient, saved whole. Read by a forward pre-hook on every module that owns parameters: per outermost autocast block, whether the module's first call inside it ran under no_grad, the file:line of that call (innermost project frames), whether its parameter had requires_grad then, and the file:line of its first later call with gradient.

Comparison per part and parameter tensor: lost = None or all zero with the cache on and not so with it off; changed = the root of the summed squared difference between the two gradients is more than 0.001 of the cache-off gradient's size and more than 10 times the on-against-on2 difference; none_both = None in both (no lesson of this call reaches it); same = the rest. A parameter used through torch.nn.functional with its weight passed by hand has no module call to hook: its first use is then read from the code and named in the result.
measures: Per part: the count of optimised parameter tensors and of their numbers that are lost and that are changed, of 621 tensors and 17.5 million numbers (0 = the cache takes no gradient in this call).

Per affected top-level module (encoder, transformer, prediction heads, motor controller, wellness, and the others the learner holds): its lost and changed tensors and numbers, and the file:line of the no_grad call that uses it first in the block and of the later call with gradient.

The run-to-run difference of the same call with the cache on (the root of the summed squared difference over the gradient's size; 0 = identical): the rounding level the changed line is judged against.
rows.pass_line: No pass line on the count: it is measured and reported. The job completes when all six runs end with exit code 0, each with exactly one call of LemLite._clip_training_gradients and a finite loss, and the comparison is written for both parts. Lines of the classification, declared before the run: lost and changed as in the steps (0.001 of the gradient's size, and 10 times the run-to-run difference).
rows.pass_line_basis: The cast copies hold the same numbers with the cache on and off (the same rounding of the same weights), so a parameter the cache does not touch has the same gradient in both up to the card's run-to-run rounding, which the on2 run measures; 0.001 sits above bf16's own relative step (0.004 per number averages down over a tensor's numbers) only when the run-to-run difference is small, which is why the second condition (10 times the measured run-to-run difference) is asked as well. A lost gradient is exact: None or all zero against not so.

RUN TO RUN: the on-again run equals the on run bit for bit in both parts (largest difference 0.0), so every difference above is the cache's.

In the replay update's block (entered at lem_model.py:4642) the same two embedding tables at lem_model.py:4657, with the same outcome. No other module's first call in either block runs under no_grad: the encoders' first call is the live encode with gradient (lem_model.py:2621 to 2627), the transformer's the delayed lesson's forward with gradient (2711), and the replay update encodes the stepped-from motor row with gradient before its no_grad context rebuild. NOT THE CACHE, READ FROM THE SAME TABLE (cache on = cache off): in this one model step 71 tensors got gradient None: wellness.grounded (prediction_error, tactile_comfort, capability, coherence, motor_state: 20 tensors), gaze_head 11, voice_head 11, tenure_heads (pose, order_proj) 8 with their 4 liveness rows, self_state 13, the liveness rows of motor_asked_change.net.0 4. 27 tensors got an all-zero gradient: the weight and bias of the first Linear (mlp.0) of prediction_heads.heads.vision, .tactile and .vestibular, of the first Linear of recon_decoders.vision, .tactile, .audio and .proprioception, of persistent_memory.outcome.0 and of wellness.approximate.net.2 (each of these layers is one the liveness repair holds rows for, and those rows do get gradient), motor_controller.confidence_head's two Linears with the 4 tensors of its liveness rows, and synergy.S3.bias. Production's step and replay update hold no such sequence today. rows.title: A fixed vector per head on imagined rows only: does the lived tactile prediction then fall below the no-change error while the paths stay bounded? (a measurement of a design that is not in the candidate)
rows.question: With the repaired rule (the chain trains the paths as it trains the old heads) plus one vector of 192 numbers per head that is added to the heads' prediction on imagined rows only and trained by the chain only, does the old tactile head's fixed vector fall from 0.030 token units toward the lived lesson's own best value, does the tactile error with the path on the fixed rows fall below the no-change error, and do the two fixed vectors stay bounded?
rows.why: The reproduction's arms read: without the imagination chain the tactile error with the path fell to 0.956 of the no-change error by 200 model steps and the old head's fixed vector to 0.005; with the chain training both parts (the repaired rule) the fixed vector stays near 0.036 and the error near 1.04 at 50 model steps: the chain's request for a fixed vector costs the lived tactile prediction about 4 of 100 of its error, as before the switch. The tactile late pass line of the production segment needs the error below 1.0. This arm measures whether giving the chain a fixed vector of its own removes that cost. The coordinator decides from the reading whether the design enters a candidate; it is not in this one.
inputs: Checkpoint ckpt_step_479350 of run H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41m_0402 with its optimizer state, built with --heads-all-slot-path on from the repaired module.
The episode companion of ckpt_step_479700 of run H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41n_0856 (the replay ring); the same 350 model steps in the same sequence as the reproduction's base arm.

The tool's switch imagined_offset=1: per head a vector of 192 numbers, zero at the start, added by a forward hook on the prediction heads while the call is inside lem.model.predictive_state.transition (before the encoders' output LayerNorm); AdamW at the run's learning rate 3e-4, no weight decay, the trainer's clip value.
steps: The reproduction tool's emulated model step, 350 of them: lived lesson, imagination chain (weight 0.5), one optimizer update, the running centre's second call, a replay update every second model step, the liveness repair's step end.
Every model step: per head the old head's fixed output, the path's, their sum and cosine, and the size of the imagined-row vector.
Every 50 model steps on the 64 fixed rows: error over no-change error with the path and with the old head alone.
measures: Error over no-change error on the fixed rows: 1 = no better than predicting that the token stays as it is, 0 = exact. The same rows read 1.04 with the repaired rule at 50 model steps and 0.956 without the chain at 200.
The old tactile head's fixed output, token units per number: 0.030 at the switch.
The imagined-row vector's size, token units per number: 0 at the start.
rows.pass_line: THE DESIGN REMOVES THE CHAIN'S COST when, at 350 model steps, the tactile error with the path on the fixed rows is under 1.0 and under the repaired rule's reading at the same model step by more than 0.0178 (stop line M8's tactile spread), with the tactile path's output under 0.17 and no non-finite update. Otherwise it does not, and the reading says what it does instead.
rows.pass_line_basis: Reachable: the arm without the chain read 0.982 at 150 and 0.956 at 200 model steps on these rows, so a prediction under 1.0 exists for this transformer and these lessons when the chain asks nothing of the lived prediction's fixed part. It can miss: the chain may ask more than a fixed vector of the prediction (a part that depends on the row), which this vector cannot take over. 0.0178 is the largest rise of the tactile head's audited error over one window in the lineage's record with nothing switched.

rows.title: Planner weights review: the search's command under a 0.00001 change of its input tokens (checkpoint 479,350)
rows.question: From one saved planning decision of checkpoint 479,350: when each of the five real senses' present tokens (192 numbers each) handed to the planner's Adam search is changed by Gaussian noise of standard deviation 0.00001 per number, how far does the selected command change, how far does the real goal distance after the 5-model-step hold change, and does the command selected under --goal-sense-weights own_command's weights still end nearer the goal than the command selected under equal weights once 5 searches of each kind are averaged?
rows.why: The independent review of the planner candidate (branch restart/candidate-planner-2026-10-04) has to state whether the candidate's measured gain (its weighted command ended 0.107 nearer the goal than production's planner's command, 0.074 of it in audio, a sense with weight 0) is produced by the weights. Two findings from the candidate's saved rows make this measurement necessary. First, 4 of 31 decisions carry 81 of 100 parts of the audio gain, and in three of them the audio token changes by 0.22 to 0.56 between two consecutive model steps of the hold (the median change between consecutive model steps is 0.004). Second, body 0's fourth decision was measured in two processes from present tokens equal to 0.000005: the planner's selected command differed between the two by up to 146 degrees on one handle's asked orientation, and the weighted command's distance minus the planner's read -0.267 in one process and +0.030 in the other. If a token change of that size re-draws the selected command, the difference between two commands on one decision is one draw, and the candidate's gate was judged on draws. The coordinator's decision to deploy the switch, deploy it with changes, or not deploy it rests on this.
inputs: Production checkpoint ckpt_step_479350 of run H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41m_0402 (read only) and its saved eight-world episode.

Per body its FIRST saved planning decision (model step 479,350): the only decision two processes reach with the same numbers (checked on the candidate's rows for bodies 0, 1 and 3). From it: the present tokens of vision, tactile, audio, proprioception and vestibular (192 numbers each, the top-down-gated tokens the search starts from), the goal's tokens, the motor controller's command (26 body handles x 9 numbers: target position, orientation as 4 numbers, radius, strength 0 to 1), and the decision's captured context, pose, smoother state and random stream.

The weights of the weighted kind: the candidate's own (per sense the lower bound of the swap test's own-command reading on the hold's first model step over the run's last 20 stats reports at or before 479,350; weight = 5 x lower bound / the sum of the five lower bounds; at this checkpoint proprioception 3.87, vision 1.13, tactile, audio and vestibular 0).

The noise: per draw and per sense 192 Gaussian numbers of standard deviation 0.00001 from a generator seeded by 241004, the body and the draw. Basis of the size: the vision token differs by up to 0.00001 between two drawings of one scene on this machine's graphics driver (Source/Python/mimo_bridge/tools/gof_probe_harness.py, ONE PICTURE PER SCENE), and by 0.000004 to 0.00004 between the two processes of the candidate's rows.
The script search_noise_probe.py of this review (version planner_search_noise_v1) and the two probes it imports; their SHA-256 digests are written into declaration.json.
steps: Build the checkpoint's model on the CPU with learning off (weights hashed before and after; a change stops the job). Drop the replay ring from memory.
Per body, restore its saved world and model state, run to its first planning event, save a snapshot.

Run the search (Adam, step size 0.1, 20 updates, started from the motor controller's command) 10 times from the decision's captured state: 2 kinds (equal weights = today's plain sum over the five senses; weighted = each sense's part times its weight) x 5 draws (draw 0 = the present tokens as they are; draws 1 to 4 = the five senses' present tokens plus the noise, the same noise for both kinds of one draw). The snapshot is restored before every search. Only the tokens handed to the search change; the world, the context, the goal, the pose and the random stream are the decision's.

Route checks that stop the job: the equal-weights search of draw 0 must equal the recorded chosen command exactly; one more unchanged search after the 10 must equal it again; the weighted kind must run on measured weights.

Execute each of the 10 selected commands and the motor controller's own command from the identical restored snapshot for the 5-model-step hold. The three commands of draw 0 are executed twice and the two physical traces must be bit-identical.
After the first and the fifth model step read each sense's top-down-gated token; goal distance per sense = the mean over the token's 192 numbers of (token - the goal's token) squared.

Summarise: (a) per kind, the selected command of each noise draw against draw 0: per handle the angle between the two asked orientations and the distance between the two asked positions; (b) per decision and kind, the standard deviation over the 5 draws of the goal distance after the hold; (c) per decision, the mean over the 5 weighted draws minus the mean over the 5 equal-weights draws, per sense and summed, then over the 8 bodies with a Student t 95% interval and the exact sign-flip share. Write result.json.
A first run of this row on body 1 alone with 1 noise draw checks the route and the cost before the 8-body run.

ADDED STEP (written Oct 4, 2026 before it runs): on bodies 0 and 1, the same 10 searches again with the search's own per-update record kept (the objective = goal distance + effort term at the starting command and after each of the 20 Adam updates, and the update whose command the search selects: the lowest objective of the 21 evaluated commands). No command is executed in the world. Script search_trace_probe.py.

SECOND ADDED STEP (written Oct 4, 2026 before it runs): on the bodies where the 8-body run's audio part differs most between the two kinds, the same 10 searches and 11 executions again, and at the last world step of each of the hold's 5 model steps the world's sound mixer is read (the list the two ears' spectrum is summed from): how many body-contact thumps are sounding and their summed ear gain (a thump starts when a new contact's impulse is above 0.15 N s and decays over 120 ms), the mobile's chime, the kick panel's squeak, the bee's and the dragonfly's continuous sound, and the root mean square of the caregiver's speech samples; beside it the audio token's distance to the goal's and the head's displacement in cm. Script audio_source_probe.py.
measures: Command change: degrees between the asked orientations of one handle in two selected commands (0 = the same orientation, 180 = opposite; two unrelated orientations average 126), and the count of the 26 handles above 10 degrees. Beside it the same between the weighted and the equal-weights command of draw 0, which is what the weights change plus what a re-draw changes.

Outcome spread between draws: the standard deviation, over the 5 draws of one decision and one kind, of the summed goal distance after the hold, of audio's part and of the weighted senses' part (0 = every draw's command ends at the same distance; the candidate's BEFORE reading has a standard deviation of 0.24 between decisions on the weighted command's distance minus the planner's).

Weighted minus equal weights, goal distance after the hold and after 1 model step, per sense and summed: below 0 = the weighted kind's commands end nearer the goal. Read twice: from draw 0 alone (the candidate's reading of these 8 decisions) and from the mean of the 5 draws.
Audio's part on body 1 and body 4, where the candidate's rows read -0.341 and -0.512 on this same decision: whether the mean of the 5 draws keeps that size.

Per noise draw, the first Adam update at which its objective differs from draw 0's by more than 0.0001 and by more than 0.001 (the objective at the starting command is 0.13 to 1.5), and whether the two searches select the same update: this reads where two searches from token states 0.00001 apart part ways.

Per executed command and model step of the hold: which sound sources are sounding (count and summed ear gain per kind; 0 = that source is silent) beside the audio token's distance to the goal's audio token. This reads which physical sound makes one command end near the goal in audio and another far.
rows.pass_line: No pass or fail line: a measurement. It is complete when all 8 decisions are measured with every route check held and the weights unchanged.
rows.pass_line_basis: The route checks are the candidate's probe's own (an unchanged search equals the chosen command exactly; bit-identical replays) plus one added here (the unchanged search again after the draws). The reading is interpreted against these stated lines, each computed from the candidate's saved rows before this job runs: a command change above 10 degrees on most handles from a 0.00001 token change means the selected command is one draw of the search and not a function of the decision; an audio difference on bodies 1 and 4 that falls from -0.341 and -0.512 at draw 0 to inside 2 of its own standard errors of 0 in the mean of the draws means the candidate's audio gain on those decisions came from which command the search selected and not from the weights.

cost.where: CPU only, one process, below-normal priority, 4 threads, hard RAM maximum 2.8 GB and 9 GB of commit (review_registry.py, the candidate's runner with this review's names). It runs only while training is held and is ended when a trainer process appears; this review starts no trainer and writes no control file
cost.basis: the candidate's probe measured on this checkpoint: 2,828 s for 20 decisions with 5 searches and 18 executions each (141 s per decision), 2.73 GB of RAM and 5.48 GB of commit at the largest; this job runs 11 searches and 14 executions per decision on 8 decisions

rows.on_pass: The readings are written into this row and into the review document docs/gain_of_function_v4/agents/planner_weights_review_2026-10-04.md (branch review/planner-weights-2026-10-04); the review's verdict on the candidate's gate is stated from them.
rows.on_fail: A stopped route check is written into this row with its numbers and the review states its verdict from the candidate's saved rows alone. A job ended because a trainer process appeared is not run again by this review; the row records how many decisions were measured.

values: COMPLETE: 8 decisions, one per body, model step 479,350; 5 searches of each of the 2 kinds per decision (D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/planner_review/search_noise_479350, lines.txt). Every route check held on every decision; weights unchanged; 2,497 s, 2.80 GB of RAM and 5.42 GB of commit at the largest. Ran Oct 4, 2026 12:24 PM to 1:06 PM PDT with training held.

(a) Token noise of standard deviation 0.00001 (largest change 0.00004) changed the selected command's asked orientation by 23.2 degrees on the average handle under equal weights (15.0 of 26 handles above 10 degrees; 20 of 32 pairs with more than 13 of 26 handles above 10 degrees) and by 38.8 degrees under the weights (18.2 of 26; 24 of 32 pairs). For scale: the weighted command differs from the equal-weights command by 66.9 degrees on the average handle at draw 0.

(b) Between the 5 draws of one decision and one kind, the summed goal distance after the hold has a standard deviation of 0.127 (both kinds); audio's part 0.128 (equal weights) and 0.111 (weighted). Two searches of one kind on one decision differ by more than 0.2 in audio on 6 of 32 pairs (equal weights) and 3 of 32 (weighted).

(c) Weighted minus equal weights, summed goal distance after the hold, 8 bodies: draw 0 alone -0.091 (t interval -0.260 to 0.079); the mean of the 5 draws -0.035 (-0.118 to 0.049; below 0 on 3 of 8 bodies). Audio's part: -0.112 at draw 0, -0.053 in the mean of the draws (-0.124 to 0.019). Without audio: +0.018 (-0.046 to 0.081). The weighted senses' distance (3.87 x proprioception + 1.13 x vision): -0.088 (-0.368 to 0.193; below 0 on 3 of 8 bodies); body 3 alone reads -0.904 and the other 7 bodies +0.029.

Body 4, whose draw 0 read -0.512 in audio (the candidate's second largest audio decision): mean of the draws +0.001 (standard error 0.176); its audio distance after the hold reads 0.560 0.060 0.145 0.089 0.663 on the 5 equal-weights draws and 0.048 0.662 0.509 0.232 0.073 on the 5 weighted draws. Body 1 (draw 0 -0.341): mean of the draws -0.251 (standard error 0.090); audio ended under 0.1 on 5 of 5 weighted draws and on 2 of 5 equal-weights draws.

Body 3: proprioception's distance after the hold reads 0.106 to 0.141 on the 5 weighted draws and 0.298 to 0.349 on the 5 equal-weights draws (the motor controller's command 0.238; the distance at the decision 0.123).

ADDED STEP (the search's per-update record, bodies 0 and 1): stopped at 1:12 PM PDT on a defect of its own script (a noise draw's search returned no per-update record), exit code 1, no reading. The script is repaired and has not run since: it restores a MuJoCo world and training runs again since 2:31 PM PDT. SECOND ADDED STEP (sound sources): not run, for the same reason. Both wait for a training pause; neither changes the readings above.

rows.decision: Oct 4, 2026: used by the review docs/gain_of_function_v4/agents/planner_weights_review_2026-10-04.md (branch review/planner-weights-2026-10-04). Reading: on these 8 decisions the candidate's audio gain is mostly which command the search selected (body 4 falls from -0.512 to +0.001 once 5 searches are averaged) with one decision where it repeats (body 1); the gain on the senses the weights act on sits in one body (3). The review's verdict on the switch: do not deploy as declared. What would show this reading wrong: a paired reading of weighted against equal weights with the draws averaged, on 32 or more decisions, whose interval lies below 0 on the weighted senses.

rows.title: Production segment 2 with the all-slot paths (path version 2: every lesson that trains a head trains the path beside it), from checkpoint 479,350
rows.question: With the repaired all-slot paths switched on beside the five prediction heads at model step 479,350: do the paths stay bounded (no path's output above its sense's real change, no pair of opposite fixed vectors growing), do the tactile and vestibular lessons' gradients reach the transformer, does vestibular's error become lower with the body's own command than with the size-matched swapped command, where does tactile's error settle against the no-change error, and do proprioception, vision and audio keep the readings they have today?
rows.why: The first segment (row heads_all_slot_path_production_segment) was stopped 250 model steps after its switch: the old tactile head's fixed vector and the tactile path's grew against each other, because the imagination chain trained the old head and not the path while the path's output was added to the chain's predictions (the record's section 13; rows heads_all_slot_path_runaway_read, heads_all_slot_path_lesson_forces, heads_all_slot_path_runaway_reproduction). The repair gives both parts the same lessons (row heads_all_slot_path_repair_bounded). The dead tactile, vision and vestibular heads are still production's state at checkpoint 479,350, and the operator's instruction of Oct 4 stands: the heads come before training. The decision that depends on this segment: the paths stay in production's command, or production returns to checkpoint 479,350 without the flag.
inputs: Checkpoint Saved/mimo_bridge/experiments/H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41m_0402/checkpoints/ckpt_step_479350, resumed by docs/gain_of_function_v4/coordinator/relaunch_h84_seg41_2026-09-29.py with --parent naming that run's folder and --set heads-all-slot-path on (the stopped run's checkpoint 479,700 holds version 1 paths and is refused by this build). Every other setting is the stopped run's.
The code of branch restart/candidate-heads2-2026-10-04 (the commit is named in the record's section 15).
The 8 bodies' worlds and the graphics card, as production runs them.

The watch program docs/gain_of_function_v4/heads_all_slot_path_watch.py with the re-derived stop line M6, called by the hourly watcher every 5 minutes for the stop lines and every hour for the printed lines.
steps: At the load, per head, a path is built: the tensor the heads are called with (6 slots x 192 numbers) minus the persistent memory's constant, minus a running centre, LayerNorm per slot, one 192-to-32 weight matrix shared by the 6 slots, then a 2-layer network (192 -> 192 -> 192) times 1/sqrt(192), whose last layer is zero. 403,200 new weights in all. The load's switch check computes every head's prediction on 64 probe rows with and without the paths, in float32 and under the graphics card's autocast, and the trainer writes one heads_all_slot_path_switch record into the stats stream.

From the first optimizer update on, each path's output is added to its head's prediction. The paths learn from every lesson that trains the head they sit beside: the next-model-step lesson on lived model steps, its re-study in replay, and the imagination chain's rows (path version 2; in the first segment the chain did not train them). The planner's descent trains nothing. The paths' running centre moves on lived rows only.

Every 100 model steps the trainer's full report carries the block heads_all_slot_path: per head the path's output size and its fixed part, its hidden layer's live share, how evenly the head's whole prediction answers to the 6 slots (head_read), the lesson's gradient on the transformer's output (lesson_gradient), and the two fixed vectors (fixed: the old head's, the path's, their sum, the cosine between them).

The watch program judges the stop lines from the switch at model step N = 479,350 through the first full report at or past model step 489,350; the early lines over model steps 481,351 to 482,350; tactile's late line over model steps 488,351 to 489,350; vestibular's late line pooled over model steps 481,351 to 489,350.

After the watch: rows prediction_heads_state_capture and prediction_heads_state_readings are run again on the newest checkpoint for each head's readings on 4,900 saved windows (attention, first layer, own-command reading).
measures: The switch record: the largest change of any head's prediction on the 64 probe rows, with the paths against without them. 0.0 = every prediction is the number it was (the declared value); anything else = the switch changed a prediction.

A path's output as a share of its sense's real change per number between two model steps (heads_all_slot_path.heads.<head>.output_rms over sqrt(next_frame_norm.persistence_ema)): 0 = the path adds nothing, 1 = it adds as much as the whole change it predicts. The first segment's tactile path read 0.06, 0.52, 3.3 and 17 at its four reports; the bench (transformer held fixed, to 1,500 updates) at most 0.50; the repaired design's CPU run at most 0.37 through emulated model step 541.

The two fixed vectors per head (heads_all_slot_path.fixed): root mean square per number of the old head's output and of the path's output averaged over the lesson rows, and the cosine between them (-1 = exactly opposite). Before the switch the old heads read: tactile 0.030, audio 0.03, proprioception 0.01, vestibular 0.002 (vision's old head alone 0.92, held by the gaze copy). In the first segment's checkpoint 479,700 the tactile pair read 2.78 and 2.68 with cosine -0.9998.

The lesson's gradient on the transformer's output, per head: per lesson row, the derivative of that row's mean squared error with respect to each of the 6 x 192 numbers the heads read, as a root mean square. 0 = the lesson sends the transformer nothing through this head. Through the old heads at checkpoint 479,350: tactile 3e-10, vestibular 6e-10, proprioception 4e-5; through a path trained on the bench: tactile 3e-4, vestibular 6e-5 to 1e-4.
head_read spread per head: 0 = the head's whole prediction answers to one slot, 1 = to all six slots evenly. The old attention pools read 0.0; on the bench the head with its path reads 0.87 to 1.0.

Audited error ratio per head at the hold's first model step, bodies without body 2: summed prediction error / summed no-change error; 1 = no better than predicting that the token stays as it is, 0 = exact. In the windows of 1,000 model steps since 475,500: tactile 1.02 to 1.04, vestibular 1.00, vision 0.68 to 0.82, audio 0.88 to 0.90, proprioception 0.68 to 0.79. Goal references (row prediction_heads_reachability_probe: a ridge fit from the encoder tokens of 3 model steps and the command, no transformer, the two folds of bodies it did not see), 50 ms: tactile 0.88 and 0.90, vestibular 0.96 and 1.03, proprioception 0.65 and 0.97, vision 0.61 and 0.67, audio 0.88 and 0.90; at the end of the 250 ms hold: tactile 0.77 and 0.81, vestibular 0.85 and 1.06, proprioception 0.53 and 0.76, vision 0.83 and 0.84, audio 0.67 and 0.71.

Own-command reading per head at the hold's first model step: 1 - (summed error with the body's own command) / (summed error with the size-matched swapped command); 0 = the command makes no difference to the error, 1 = the own command leaves no error. Since model step 475,900: tactile 0, vestibular 0, proprioception 0.32 to 0.40, vision 0.12 to 0.17, audio 0.000 to 0.014. Goal references from the same probe, 50 ms: tactile 0.003 and 0.007, vestibular 0.041 and 0.052, proprioception 0.52 and 0.58, vision 0.066 and 0.077, audio 0.000 and 0.005; at 250 ms: tactile 0.012 and 0.037, vestibular 0.087 and 0.142, proprioception 0.56 and 0.63, vision 0.010 and 0.011, audio 0.005 and 0.018.
rows.pass_line: STOP LINES (the watch program writes snapshot_and_stop): the switch record not as declared (exact, 0.0 in float32 and under autocast, every output layer zero, 64 probe rows, version heads_all_slot_path_v2); a non-finite or skipped optimizer update; a path's hidden layer under 0.9 live share in 2 full reports running; a sense's lesson error ratio past the vestibular plan's multiples (in reports 2 and 3, or a 20-report window's median past its level times 1.72, for vision 3.95); the step rate under 0.9 of the window before in two 20-report windows running; M6, RE-DERIVED: any path's output above 1.0 times its sense's real change per number (the real change taken as at least half its value at the last full report before the switch), or not a finite number; M9, NEW: a path's fixed vector at or above 0.5 of the sense's real change with cosine at or under -0.9 against the old head's fixed vector; proprioception's own-command reading over a window of 1,000 model steps at or under 3.14 times its standard error; any head's audited error ratio above its value over the 20 reports before the switch by more than its spread (vision 0.156, tactile 0.0178, audio 0.156, proprioception 0.075, vestibular 0.0121) in two windows of 1,000 model steps running. ALERT, never a stop: the tactile or vestibular lesson's gradient under 1e-6 past model step 480,350. EARLY LINES, over model steps 481,351 to 482,350: the switch record exact; the tactile and the vestibular lesson's gradient on the transformer's output at or above 1e-6; every head's head_read spread at or above 0.25. LATE LINES as the coordinator declared them for the first segment: tactile's audited error ratio over model steps 488,351 to 489,350 below 1.0 by more than 3.14 times its standard error; vestibular's own-command reading pooled over model steps 481,351 to 489,350 above 3.14 times its standard error. WATCHED, no line: tactile's own-command reading, vestibular's error ratio, audio, vision and proprioception against their values before the switch.
rows.pass_line_basis: Declared before the run. STOP LINE M6 (re-derived; row heads_all_slot_path_m6_line): both parts of the graded sum, old head and path, are trained by every lesson, so the sum is a prediction of the token's change, and a path's output above the whole change is what the old head must take away again. 0 of 480 bench readings and 0 of the repaired design's CPU readings are over the line (largest shares 0.50 and 0.37); the first segment crossed it at the report of 479,600. rows.title: The asked-change path beside the motor encoder: do the lived lesson and the imagination chain ask opposite things of its output?
rows.question: The asked-change path (live in production since model step 474,875) has the rule that made the heads' first design run away: the imagination chain does not train it, yet its output is added to the motor token on imagined rows. Do the lived lesson and the chain pull the path's fixed output in opposite directions at checkpoint 479,350, and did the encoder's fixed part and the path's fixed part grow against each other between checkpoints 478,029 and 479,350?
rows.why: If they do, the motor token has the same loop as the old tactile head and its path had (the record's section 13.4), running slowly in production now, and the path gets the same repair behind its flag (the chain trains it too). If they do not, the rule stays and the reading says so with its numbers. The coordinator asked for this reading on Oct 4 at 2:40 PM PDT.
inputs: Checkpoint ckpt_step_479350 of run H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41m_0402 (production's state at that model step, built with the run's own flags: the asked-change path on, no all-slot paths) and its episode companion: the replay ring, per body the newest 6,000 model steps of tokens, achieved poses (26 handles x 10 numbers), executed commands (26 handles x 9 numbers), memory states.
Checkpoint ckpt_step_478029 of the same run, for the second reading.

20 batches of 4 bodies' rows at ring ages 3, 10, 17, ... (each with the row of 3 model steps earlier for the chain), and the current rows of all 8 bodies at those ages (160 rows) for the second reading.
steps: READING 1. A vector of 192 numbers is added to the path's output on every row that holds a command (the lived lesson's current row, each of the chain's 3 imagined rows), in the output's units (one unit = one standard deviation of the encoder's pooled vector). Per batch: the derivative of the next-model-step lesson's loss and of 0.5 x the chain's loss with respect to that vector; averaged over the batches.
Taken twice: with the vector at zero (the path's fixed output in place) and at minus the path's fixed output (its mean over the lived rows), which cancels it on every row.
Per lesson: its PULL along the path's fixed output = minus the derivative's component along it.

READING 2. On the same 160 rows, both checkpoints, without gradient: the encoder's pooled vector with the path bypassed, standardised per row, and the path's output. Per checkpoint the two fixed vectors (means over the rows); between the checkpoints the change of each, the cosine of the two changes, and the change of their sum.
measures: Pull along the path's fixed output (loss units per unit of the output): positive = gradient descent on that lesson adds more of the fixed output, negative = it takes it away, 0 = the lesson asks nothing along it. The heads' first design read -0.0034 (lived) against +0.0043 (chain) along the old tactile head's fixed vector.

Cosine of the two fixed parts' changes between the checkpoints: -1 = the encoder's fixed part and the path's moved exactly against each other (the heads' pair read -0.9998), 0 = unrelated, 1 = together.
Sizes as root mean square per number, in units of the pooled vector's standard deviation (the stats block's output_rms read 0.46 to 0.92 over the reports since model step 475,800).
rows.pass_line: OPPOSITION when, at either value of the added vector, the two lessons' pulls have opposite signs and the smaller is at least a quarter of the larger; or when the two fixed parts' changes read a cosine at or under -0.9 with each change at least twice the change of their sum. NO OPPOSITION MEASURED otherwise.
rows.pass_line_basis: The quarter: in the heads' first design the two pulls read 0.0034 and 0.0043 (a ratio of 0.8) with the fixed vector in place; a chain pull under a quarter of the lived lesson's cannot hold the encoder's fixed part against the lived lesson. The cosine and the factor 2: the heads' pair read -0.9998 with each part 24 times their sum. Reachable either way: the readings exist for any state of the path. What it leaves out: the lived lessons other than the next-model-step lesson (the efference and contact heads' lessons, the hold loss), so a pull that only those lessons give is not seen.

The watch program judges the stop lines from the switch at model step N through the first full report at or past N + 10,000; the early line over model steps N + 1,001 to N + 2,000; the late pass line over model steps N + 9,001 to N + 10,000.
measures: Tactile's audited error ratio at the hold's first model step, bodies without body 2: summed prediction error / summed no-change error; 1 = no better than predicting that the token stays as it is, 0 = exact. Before the paths: 1.02 to 1.04. Goal reference 0.88 (row prediction_heads_reachability_probe: what the model's own inputs allow with no transformer).

A vector's size as a share of its sense's real change per number between two model steps (heads_all_slot_path.heads.<head>.imagined_offset_rms over sqrt(next_frame_norm.persistence_ema)): 0 = the switch, 1 = as large as the whole change the head predicts. The chain's request for tactile measured at checkpoint 479,350 is 0.44 of that change.

The old tactile head's fixed vector (heads_all_slot_path.fixed.tactile.old_rms), token units per number: 0.030 at checkpoint 479,350; without the chain's loss it fell to 0.005 on the CPU. With the vectors it is expected to fall as the tactile vector grows.

The two fixed vectors per head (heads_all_slot_path.fixed): root mean square per number of the old head's output and of the path's output averaged over the lesson rows, and the cosine between them (-1 = exactly opposite). Before the switch the old heads read: tactile 0.030, audio 0.03, proprioception 0.01, vestibular 0.002 (vision's old head alone 0.92, held by the gaze copy). In the first segment's checkpoint 479,700 the tactile pair read 2.78 and 2.68 with cosine -0.9998.
rows.pass_line: PASS LINE (the target): over model steps N + 9,001 to N + 10,000, tactile's audited error ratio below 1.0 by more than 3.14 times its standard error (goal 0.88). EARLY LINE: over model steps N + 1,001 to N + 2,000, tactile's audited error ratio lower than over the 20 full reports before the switch by more than 3.14 times the two readings' joint standard error. STOP LINES (the watch program writes snapshot_and_stop): M1, the vectors' switch record not as declared (exact, the imagined probe rows' output unchanged, every vector zero, 64 rows, version heads_imagined_offset_v1); a non-finite or skipped optimizer update; a path's hidden layer under 0.9 live share in 2 full reports running; a sense's lesson error ratio past the vestibular plan's multiples; the step rate under 0.9 of the window before in two 20-report windows running; M6, a path's output above its sense's real change; M7, proprioception's own-command reading at or under 3.14 times its standard error over a window of 1,000 model steps; M8, any head's audited error ratio above its value over the 20 reports before the switch by more than its spread (vision 0.156, tactile 0.0178, audio 0.156, proprioception 0.075, vestibular 0.0121) in two windows of 1,000 model steps running; M9, a path's fixed vector at or above 0.5 of the sense's real change with cosine at or under -0.9 against the old head's; M10, NEW: a vector's size above 1.0 times its sense's real change per number (the real change taken as at least half its value before the switch), or not a finite number.
rows.pass_line_basis: The two lines on tactile are the coordinator's decision of Oct 4, 2:40 PM PDT. REACHABILITY. Pass line: one window's standard error of tactile's ratio is 0.0024 (median of 20 windows; largest 0.0036), so the line sits at about 0.99. On the CPU the lived lesson with the path and without the chain's request read 0.96 at 200 to 350 emulated model steps on a fixed set of 64 rows (arm nochain), and 0.995 to 1.08 with the request on the lived prediction (arm repaired_1400); so a reading under 0.99 is reachable once the vectors hold the request, and the goal 0.88 needs the transformer to learn the tactile lesson, which no measurement before the run shows. Early line: the joint noise of two readings is about 3.14 x 0.0034 = 0.011; the cost the vectors remove is 0.03 to 0.07; a vector moves by at most 0.0003 per optimizer update, and at the pace the CPU read (0.0035 token units in 56 model steps) the tactile vector reaches the old head's 0.03 after about 500 model steps, which is why the window starts at N + 1,001. Shape: nothing changes at the switch (the vectors are zero), the old tactile head's fixed vector falls as the tactile vector grows, and no dip is expected before the fall. M10: the vector stands for the difference between the fixed vectors the two lessons ask of a prediction of the token's change, each at most as large as that change; the chain's request for tactile reads 0.068 token units, 0.44 of the real change (row heads_all_slot_path_lesson_forces); the lineage's records carry no vectors, so no false stop can be counted on them. M6, M9 and M8 as in row heads_all_slot_path_production_segment_2, with the 20 reports before this switch as M8's reference. What would show the design wrong: the old tactile head's fixed vector not falling while the tactile vector grows, or the early line missed with the vectors grown.

rows.title: Vestibular input path review: the long encoder bench
rows.question: On the encoder bench, with the vestibular input path wired as the package wires it and its output capped at 0.3 token units: past 60,000 updates, does the encoder's own part go on taking the path's change out of their sum until none is left (change slope -1), and does the head-tilt read-out from the token then stay at 0.25 or more on rows no update read? And which of the two lessons that reach the vestibular encoder directly takes head tilt out of a fresh encoder's token?
rows.why: The package's own bench ended at 60,000 updates with the change slope at -0.74 and lower at every later reading (file D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/vestibular_token2/path_bench_parts2/bench.json). No stop line of the production watch reads the slope, and pass line T1 is read for the last time 10,000 model steps after the switch. The decision that depends on it: the reviewer's verdict on the package (deploy as declared, deploy with named changes, or do not deploy), written in docs/gain_of_function_v4/agents/vestibular_input_path_review_2026-10-04.md on branch review/vestibular-input-path-2026-10-04.
inputs: The replay job's rows of model steps 478,030 to 479,350 (row vestibular_token_inputs_replay_478029, folder D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/vestibular_token2/replay_478029): 8 bodies x 1,321 consecutive model steps of the 29 raw vestibular numbers and of gravity in the head. The updates read the first 1,100 model steps.

A second set of rows that no update reads (row vestibular_token_inputs_replay_459961, folder D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/vestibular_token2/replay_459961): 8 bodies x 1,670 consecutive model steps lived 18,000 model steps earlier, 16 reports of 100 model steps.

Checkpoint 479,350's vestibular encoder (14 tensors), its saved AdamW state for those tensors and the input normaliser's saved statistics, held fixed (all read only, from production's run folder H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41m_0402).

The path as the package builds it: lem/model/vestibular_input_path.py at commit 48f11f612 (one Linear(28 -> 192) without bias, weight zero at the start, output x 1/sqrt(28), capped at 0.3 token units per row, added to the encoder's last-layer output in units of that output's standard deviation over its 192 numbers).
No world, no transformer, no trainer, no graphics card.
steps: Form the encoder's input of every row of both sets (28 fields, clipped, centred and scaled with the checkpoint's statistics).

Per arm, one update per model step of the first 1,100 model steps in the sequence they were lived (cycled), on the 8 bodies' rows, with the package's own bench code unchanged (docs/gain_of_function_v4/vestibular_token/vt_bench.py run_arm): token of model step t with gradient; loss = VICReg(token) / 6 + mean squared (token of model step t - 1 encoded again with gradient, minus the token of model step t without gradient); AdamW with the checkpoint's learning rate 3e-4, betas, eps and weight decay; float32.

Arms, in this sequence: fresh (a freshly initialised encoder, both lessons, 20,000 updates); fresh_vicreg_only (the same encoder, VICReg alone, 20,000); fresh_token_change_only (the same encoder, the token-change term alone, 20,000); path_live_only_cap03 (today's encoder with the path, the path's weight detached inside the token-change term's re-encoding: the package's wiring, 240,000 updates); path_none_cap03 (today's encoder with the path, the token-change term's gradient cut for the encoder's weights and for the path's: 60,000 updates).

At updates 0, 100, 200, 500, 1,000 and every 2,000 after: the package's own readings (the head-tilt read-out on all reports and on the 2 reports no update read, the change slope of the two parts, each part's change, the path's output and weight size), and three added readings: the same read-out on the 16 reports of the second set; per label the size of the label-following part of the path's change, of the encoder's part's change and of their sum's (least-squares fit of the label's change, root mean square per number), with the change slope on that part alone; and the change slope per group of input fields.
Write bench.json after every reading.
measures: Change slope: over each body's change from its own mean within a report of 100 model steps, the summed product of the encoder's part's change and the path's change over the path's summed squared change. 0 = the two are unrelated, -1 = the encoder's part takes all of the path's change out of the sum. The package's run read -0.74 at 60,000 updates.

Head-tilt read-out, R squared on bodies the fit did not read: 0 = no better than predicting no change, 1 = every scored change predicted exactly; the trainer's line is 0.25; the 28 input numbers themselves read 0.56. Read on the 2 reports after the rows the updates read and on the 16 reports of the second set, each beside its body-shuffled control (0 expected).

Head tilt's part of the sum's change, token units per number: 0 = the sum of the two parts does not follow head tilt at all; the graphics card's bf16 rounding of the encoder's output is 0.014 token units.
The path's weight size (root mean square of its 5,376 weights; 0 at the switch) and its fixed vector (its mean output over all rows, token units; 0 = it adds the same to no row).
rows.pass_line: This run has no pass line for production; it settles the reviewer's fourth question. The package's long-run claim HOLDS on this bench when arm path_live_only_cap03 reads head tilt at 0.25 or more, with its control under 0.05, on the 2 unread reports AND on the 16 reports of the second set at every reading from 60,000 to 240,000 updates. It FAILS when either read-out is under 0.25 at two readings running. Beside it, as readings: whether the change slope stops before -1; which fresh arm loses head tilt (the cause); whether arm path_none_cap03 reads 0.25 or more on the 16 reports of the second set.
rows.pass_line_basis: 0.25 is the trainer's line for its probe and the package's pass line T1. Reachable at the start of the extension: the package's run read 0.44 to 0.50 on the 2 unread reports from 4,000 through 60,000 updates (path_bench_parts2/bench.json). The time constant: the slope fell from -0.58 at 40,000 updates to -0.74 at 60,000, 0.08 per 10,000 updates, so a straight continuation reaches -1 near 90,000 updates; 240,000 updates cover 2.7 times that. The read-out on the second set has no earlier reading with the capped path: unmeasured before this run. Noise of the read-out: the package's unread reading moved by 0.03 between neighbouring readings from 20,000 to 60,000 updates (0.469 to 0.500), so one reading under the line is not judged, two running are.

cost.where: beside training: the CPU, one process, 2 threads, idle priority, under the shared lock D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/cpu_beside_training.lock, hard limits of 2.9 GB of RAM and 6 GB committed, the graphics card hidden, no world; ended by the runner when two trainer reports after its start both read under 0.42 model steps per second
cost.basis: The package's run of this bench made 60,000 updates of one arm in 399 s beside training and held 0.76 GB of RAM at its peak, 1.17 GB committed (path_bench_parts2/bench.json). This run makes 360,000 updates in five arms.

rows.on_pass: The review's fourth answer says the read-out held through 240,000 bench updates and names the size at which the slope stopped; the verdict still names the production lines that would read a later fall.
rows.on_fail: The review's fourth answer says at which update the read-out fell under 0.25 and that the package's wiring undoes its own repair on this bench; the verdict names the changes the package needs before a production segment.

values: The job ran Oct 4, 2026 from 4:23 PM to 5:01 PM PDT (2,273 s, 2 threads, idle priority, 0.88 GB of RAM at its peak), after 1,560 s of waiting for the shared lock and 681 s for a trainer report at or above 0.42 model steps per second. The trainer was not running in that span: the coordinator's hold stopped it at model step 481,800 with its checkpoint saved at 4:23 PM PDT.

Arm path_live_only_cap03 (the package's wiring), 240,000 updates. The head-tilt read-out (0 = no better than predicting no change, 1 = exact, line 0.25) read 0.455 to 0.490 on the 16 reports of the second set at all 91 readings from 60,000 to 240,000 updates (0.457 at 240,000; its control -0.009 to -0.018), and 0.311 to 0.487 on the 2 unread reports (0.479 at 60,000, 0.329 at 240,000; its control -0.10 to -0.22). Under 0.25 at 0 of 91 readings on either set.

The change slope (0 = the two parts' changes are unrelated, -1 = the encoder's part takes all of the path's change out of the sum) stopped falling: -0.70 to -0.83 at every reading from 60,000 to 240,000 updates on the rows the updates read (-0.77 at 240,000), and -0.31 to -0.51 from 40,000 updates on over the 16 reports no update read.

Three readings did not level by 240,000 updates. The path's fixed vector (0 = it adds the same vector to no row; the cap is 0.3 token units) rose from 0.057 at 60,000 updates to 0.149 at 240,000, by 0.005 per 10,000 updates. The path's weight size rose from 3.39 to 6.54 (0.20 where rows first reach the cap). Head tilt's part of the token's change on the rows the updates read fell from 0.041 token units at 18,000 updates to 0.017 at 240,000 (0 = the token does not follow head tilt; the bf16 rounding of the encoder's output is 0.014 token units).

Fresh encoder, 20,000 updates, head tilt on the 16 reports of the second set (0.41 before any update): both lessons 0.27, VICReg alone 0.36, the token-change term alone 0.08. Head tilt's part of the token's change (0.107 token units before any update): 0.022, 0.055 and 0.0001. The token-change term takes out more; under VICReg alone the read-out falls too.

Arm path_none_cap03 (the delayed lesson's gradient cut for the encoder's weights and for the path's), 60,000 updates. Head tilt on the 16 reports of the second set read 0.43 to 0.56 at all 28 readings from 6,000 updates on (0.54 at 60,000; its control -0.007 to -0.055), against 0.44 to 0.49 for the package's wiring over the same updates. Its change slope on those reports read +0.01 to +0.06 and the path's weight size 0.12 to 0.22. On the 2 unread reports the same arm reads -0.35 with its control at -5.94 at 60,000 updates: that set of 2 reports cannot judge this arm.

rows.title: PLANNER_SEARCH: where a 0.00001 change of the search's input is amplified (checkpoints 481,800 and 479,350, graphics card)
rows.question: On saved planning decisions of checkpoints 481,800 and 479,350: when the five real senses' present tokens handed to the search are changed by Gaussian noise of standard deviation 0.00001 per number, at which update of the 20 Adam updates do two searches part, in which group of searched numbers (position, orientation, radius, strength, hand joints), and which computation turns a difference of 0.00001 into a different command: Adam's update rule, the command's transform, or the predictor's response to the command (the motor encoder's attention over the 26 body handles)?
rows.why: PLANNER_SEARCH is FOUND unstable (review of Oct 4: a 0.00001 token change turns the selected command by 23.2 degrees on the average body handle) and its command goes to the body on half of all latched commands. The repair PLANNER_SEARCH_REPAIR (--planner-search trust_v1) must act at the place where the difference is amplified. Two readings are possible and they lead to different repairs. If Adam's sign-normalised update on numbers whose gradient is at numerical-noise level is the place, a search whose updates are proportional to the gradient removes the defect at any step size. If the predictor's response to the command changes abruptly where a pooling head of the motor encoder changes the body handle it reads, then the defect returns with any search that evaluates commands across such changes, and the repair's trust region has to be sized by where the predictor's response stays one function. The coordinator's design decision for the repair rests on which of the two this row reads.
rows.gof_link: The planner is the route by which wellness changes behaviour; a selected command that is not a repeatable function of the state and the goal cannot move the body toward a goal, so no planned command can beat the motor controller's command until the search is stable.
inputs: Production checkpoints ckpt_step_481800 (run H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41o_1431) and ckpt_step_479350 (run H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41m_0402), read only.

Decision files written by row planner_search_mechanism_arms: 32 decisions of 481,800 (8 bodies x 4) and 16 of 479,350 (8 bodies x 2). Each holds the present tokens of vision, tactile, audio, proprioception and vestibular (192 numbers each, the top-down-gated tokens the search starts from), the goal's tokens, the motor controller's command (26 body handles x 9 numbers: target position in units of 200 cm, orientation as 4 numbers, radius, strength 0 to 1) and the decision's captured context, pose, memory bias, smoother state and hand state.

The noise: per row and sense 192 Gaussian numbers of standard deviation 0.00001 from a generator seeded by 241005, the body, the decision and the row (docs/gain_of_function_v4/planner_recovery/search_lib.py token_noise). Basis of the size: the vision token differs by up to 0.00001 between two drawings of one scene on this machine's graphics driver, the size the review of Oct 4 used.

The script docs/gain_of_function_v4/planner_recovery/mechanism_offline.py (version planner_search_mechanism_offline_v2) and search_lib.py on branch planner/search-2026-10-05; their SHA-256 digests are written into declaration.json.
steps: Build each checkpoint's model on the graphics card through the trainer's own builder, learning off (weights hashed before and after). Configure the hand geometry from the decision files. Stop when the model's parameters and buffers differ from the digest the decision files carry.
Per decision, run LemLite._plan_chain once as production runs it (one body, hand stage included): this device's own selected command.

Per decision, form one batch of 5 rows: row 0 the present tokens as they are, rows 1 to 4 with the noise. Search the batch once per variant, the hand stage left out so that the search's own output is compared: production's Adam (learning rate 0.1, 20 updates) on every group; Adam on one group at a time (position, orientation, radius, strength, hand joints); Adam at learning rates 0.01 and 0.001; updates proportional to the gradient with one scale for all groups (the largest number moves 0.1 at the first update) and with one scale per group. Only the object torch.optim.Adam returns inside IntentionGenerator.generate_action is replaced; every other line that runs is production's. The gradients and the searched numbers are recorded at every update.

(a) At the first update of production's Adam, per group: the gradient's length, the length of row j's gradient minus row 0's, the count of numbers with opposite gradient signs in the two rows, and the count whose difference is at least as large as the gradient itself.
(b) Per update of production's Adam: the largest difference between row j's and row 0's searched numbers and the count of numbers updated in opposite directions, per group.

(c) Per variant: row j's selected command against row 0's, per group in physical units (degrees between asked orientations, cm between asked positions, strength, radians of hand joints), raw and as the body receives it (LemLite.planned_execution), beside the step the search took from the motor controller's command.

(d) From row 0 of production's Adam: the selected command with one group put back to the motor controller's values, and the motor controller's command with one group taken from the selected command; each is predicted again on the planner's route and its goal distance per sense and effort term are read.

Switch readings: production's Adam, Adam at 0.01 and 0.001 and the proportional updates are searched once more with the motor encoder's attention weights read at every evaluated command (2 attention layers among the 26 body handles, then 4 pooling heads that each form a weighted sum over the 26 handles): per evaluation, the handle each pooling head puts its largest weight on, the largest difference of any attention weight between row j and row 0, the largest difference of the executed command between the rows, and the count of searched numbers whose gradient differs between the rows by more than 10 of 100 parts.

Causal control: production's Adam once more with the motor encoder's attention weights held at the values they have at the starting command (each attention module's output computed as its output projection of the held weights times its value projection; this arithmetic is first compared with the module's own output and must agree to 0.0001 of the output's largest number).
Batch layout check: row 0's input searched alone as one body, against row 0 of the batch.

A development run on one decision (body 0, first decision of 481,800) was made while the script was written, before the pass line below was written; it is part of the 32 decisions and its readings are named in the pass line's basis.
measures: Command change between two searches whose inputs differ by 0.00001: degrees between the asked orientations of one body handle (0 = the same orientation, 180 = opposite; two unrelated orientations average 126), mean over the 15 body handles that are not fingers; cm between asked positions on the rows whose position the decoder solves for; strength (0 to 1); radians of the 44 hand joints.
First update at which the gradients of two rows differ by more than 10 of 100 parts on at least 1 in 20 searched numbers (1 = at the search's start, 20 = at its last update, none = never).

At that update: the largest difference of a motor encoder attention weight between the two rows (0 = the same handles are read with the same weights, 1 = a head reads one handle in one row and another handle in the other) and the largest difference of the executed command's numbers between the rows.
Heads reading another handle after the first update (0 to 4) and evaluations of the 20 at which a pooling head changed the handle it reads.

Predicted goal distance (sum over the five senses of the mean squared difference between the predicted next token and the goal's token) and effort term of each mixed command minus the motor controller's command's: below 0 = predicted nearer the goal.
rows.target_metric: The selected command's change, in degrees on the average body handle, when the present tokens change by 0.00001: 0 = the search is a repeatable function of its input; 23.2 = the review's reading of production's search on 479,350.
rows.baseline: Production's Adam on the same decisions and noise (the variant named adam).
rows.statistical_line: Each reading is a mean over 4 noise rows x the decisions (128 pairs on 481,800, 64 on 479,350); the two checkpoints are read apart and must agree in which line holds. The review's reading had per-body means from 1.9 to 40.3 degrees over 4 pairs each, so a mean over 128 pairs has a standard error of about 1 degree.
rows.pass_line: The mechanism is established (PLANNER_SEARCH: CAUSE KNOWN at the motor encoder's attention) when all three hold on the 32 decisions of 481,800 and again on the 16 of 479,350: (1) production's Adam changes the selected command by more than 5 degrees on the average body handle between row j and row 0; (2) in at least 80 of 100 pairs whose gradients come to differ, at the first update where they differ a motor encoder attention weight differs by more than 0.01 between the rows while the executed commands differ by under 0.001; (3) with the motor encoder's attention weights held, the same Adam's change of the selected command is under one hundredth of (1)'s.
rows.pass_line_basis: (1) reproduces the defect on the checkpoint training is held at: the review read 23.2 degrees on 479,350, the smallest body's mean was 1.9, and 5 is a fifth of the mean. (2) 80 of 100: with the amplification elsewhere the attention weights of two rows whose commands are 0.001 apart agree to the fourth decimal (the development decision read differences of 0.00001 to 0.0001 at the updates before the gradients differed and 0.14 to 0.27 at the update where they did); 0.01 is 100 times the former. (3) one hundredth: the coordinator's expectation for a repaired search is a change smaller by powers of ten; the development decision read 0.022 degrees against 32.6. Reachability: the three readings are properties of saved decisions under frozen weights; no transient and no training is involved. Noise: the smallest per-body mean of the review (1.9 degrees) is above 5 x one hundredth.

cost.where: this machine, graphics card under D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/gpu.lock, 1 job of the planner search agent's 2

rows.on_pass: PLANNER_SEARCH is written as CAUSE KNOWN in the record docs/gain_of_function_v4/planner_recovery/PLANNER_SEARCH_REPAIR_2026-10-05.md with the mechanism's input, operation and output; the coordinator is sent the finding once (it differs from the reading the work started from: the first update's gradient signs agree between the rows); the repair's trust region is then sized by a measurement of how far from the motor controller's command the pooling heads keep reading the same handles, and the two designs are compared inside that size.
rows.on_fail: The line that failed is named in the record with the per-group and per-update readings; the coordinator is sent the readings; no search design is built until the place of amplification is read by a further localisation written as its own row (the executed command's transform and the forward model's own attention are the two remaining sites).
rows.decision: Line 1 met on both checkpoints; lines 2 and 3 not met on either. What the readings show: the two searches' first updates agree (0.00 to 0.05 of 100 signs opposite), they part at update 5.5 and 7 (medians), at that update a motor encoder attention weight differs by more than 0.01 in 57 of 64 and 109 of 128 pairs, and holding those weights leaves 1/30 and 1/15 of the change; so the motor encoder's attention carries most of the amplification and not all of it, and in most pairs the commands are already more than 0.001 apart when the attention parts. PLANNER_SEARCH stays FOUND with the cause localised to the motor encoder's attention for the part the control removes; CAUSE KNOWN waits on row planner_search_mechanism_controls (the forward model's and every attention module held), which runs next on the graphics card. The record names both unmet lines with these readings and the coordinator is sent them. Owner: the planner search agent. The design reading of the repair (row planner_search_design_arms_481800_v2) was started before this result; the repair's stability is carried by its own evidence row (planner_search_evidence_offline_481800), whatever part of the amplification the controls leave unlocalised.

diagram.input: Saved planning decisions of checkpoints 481,800 and 479,350; present tokens with 0.00001 noise on 4 rows
diagram.operation: Production's Adam (rate 0.1, 20 updates) on each row; gradients, attention weights and commands read per update
