rows.title: HEAD_TILT_REPAIR whole-model check on checkpoint 481,800
rows.question: With checkpoint 481,800's whole model updated 6,000 times on the graphics card by the bench's model step (the live row's lessons, the delayed lesson through the transformer and the prediction heads, the trainer's gradient clipping, AdamW and replay update) and --vestibular-input-path on (path version 2, the wiring in which the delayed lesson trains neither the encoder's own layers nor the path), does the vestibular token carry head tilt on 500 model steps no update read, at 0.25 or more and 0.25 or more above its control from update 2,000 to the end, while every other sense's prediction error stays within the spread of two runs without the switch, and does the branch's code with the switch absent compute what production's code computes?
rows.why: HEAD_TILT_REPAIR is BUILT/OFF and its present code (fe276c7de) has no whole-model reading beyond a 200-update script check: path version 2 and the wiring on never ran with the transformer's lessons for longer. Under on, the vestibular encoder's own layers lose every delayed-row lesson's gradient at the switch (next_frame.vestibular, the other senses' next_frame terms, contact_head, efference_gaze, efference_body, latent_reg), and on the encoder bench the token's change between model steps rose from 0.053 token units before the first update to 0.14 to 0.22 from 4,000 to 60,000 updates; through the persistence normalisation and the shared gradient clip that can change the other senses' lessons. The directive (section 3A): run the owed whole-model graphics-card check; if it passes, switch the repair on. The decision that depends on it: HEAD_TILT_REPAIR goes to QUALIFIED/OFF for the wiring on and the production segment (row vestibular_input_path_production_segment) may be switched on at a relaunch, or it is not switched on and the cause is read from this check's readings. Of the training preflight's gates (directive section 19) it gives evidence for 1 (information flow: head tilt reaches the token), 2 (gradient flow: the path's weight learns under autocast, the hold included), 3 (scale: the path's output under its cap, the weight's size, the gradient norm before the clip) and 6 (its lines are on the purpose); it gives none for 4, 5 and 7 (no command is changed in it).
rows.gof_link: Sensing for gain of function: the directive's success list asks that head-tilt information be present and usable, and the vestibular token reads head tilt at -0.062 to 0.005 today (production's probe, model steps 479,600 to 481,800), so neither the predictor nor the planner can use the head's orientation; this check measures its presence with the whole model's lessons live.
rows.target_metric: Head tilt read from the vestibular token on held-out data: the trainer's probe (each body's change of the head accelerometer's unit direction within a report of 100 model steps; a ridge read-out from the token's change fitted on the even-numbered bodies and scored on the odd ones and the other way round) on the 5 reports of the 500 model steps no update encodes with gradient; R squared, 0 = no better than predicting no change, 1 = every scored change predicted; the 28 input numbers themselves read 0.56.
rows.baseline: No improvement reads as a run without the switch does: the same updates without the path read head tilt at 0.005 to 0.021 on checkpoint 479,350 (row vestibular_token_path_live_bench, its control arm); production's own probe read -0.062 to 0.005 over the 23 reports of model steps 479,600 to 481,800 (run H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41o_1431, vestibular.repair.balance_probe.r2.head_tilt).
rows.statistical_line: Head tilt: the read-out at least 0.25 above its body-shuffled control (every body's token paired with another body's head tilt; 0 expected) at every reading from update 2,000 on whose control is within 0.10 of zero, with at least 8 of every 10 such readings judged. Other senses: per sense and evaluation set, the median over the readings from update 1,000 on of ln(path arm's error ratio / control arm's) at or under the largest |ln(second control arm's / control arm's)| over the same readings (two runs without the switch that differ only in the replay update's random draws). Identity: per-update loss and gradient norm equal as exact hex over 200 updates, and the parameters' SHA-256 equal at updates 0, 100 and 200.
rows.material_gof_line: Presence: 0.25, the trainer's line for this read-out (the vestibular repair watch's A4, which production's standing line T1 uses). Other senses: no reading of the path arm above the control arm's error ratio x the production watch's alert multiple (1.43; vision 3.29), the level at which production's watch alerts. Usable (the transformer's output carrying head tilt; vestibular's prediction error under the no-change error): not yet defined.

steps: Training held and the card free: the runner (docs/gain_of_function_v4/head_tilt_review/ht_registry.py card) takes D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/gpu.lock exclusively with this branch's name inside, waits for it in one loop, and ends the job's process tree if a trainer process starts.

ROUTE CHECK in every leg before anything else: the vestibular token of model step 478,030 computed on the processor from the replayed input with checkpoint 478,029's saved encoder and statistics, against the ring's stored vestibular tokens of model steps 478,028 to 478,032; the stored token of 478,030 must be the nearest of the five and within 0.02 token units (root mean square per number); a miss stops the leg.

IDENTITY LEGS, 200 updates each, the switch absent, seed 0, deterministic kernels asked for (CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8, torch.use_deterministic_algorithms with warnings, PYTHONHASHSEED=0): production's code, then the branch's code. Per update the loss and the gradient norm before the clip as exact hex, and the replay update's loss; a SHA-256 over every parameter and buffer at updates 0, 100 and 200. Only when the two legs differ: production's code once more, to tell the card's own run-to-run difference from a difference of the code.

LONG ARMS, one after another, each in its own process, 6,000 updates: path (--vestibular-input-path on), control (the run's flags), control_seed1 (the run's flags; the torch and numpy streams seeded with 1 in place of 0 right before the first update, so the replay update draws other windows). One update reads one model step t of the span's read part (478,158 to 478,849) for all 8 bodies, cycled in the sequence lived. The live row: the 5 other senses' tokens from the ring; the vestibular token encoded from the replayed input with gradient, the path open; the context of the 127 model steps before t (vestibular tokens encoded again without gradient in an autocast block of their own, motor tokens rebuilt from the stored pose and executed command); VICReg and the reconstruction decoders' term. The delayed lesson t - 1 to t: the previous row's vestibular token encoded inside the path's frozen() and, under on, detached; the motor token rebuilt with the executed command; transformer forward; prediction heads with the gaze copy; per sense the squared error weighted by the persistence normalisation with the revival ceiling. Then loss.backward(), LemLite._clip_training_gradients(), AdamW; after every 2nd update LemLite.replay_update(batch 24); every 100 updates the ring's vestibular tokens of the span written again from the weights as they are.

READINGS at updates 0, 100, 200, 300, 500, then every 500: the trainer's probe restated for head tilt, gravity in the head and the trunk's roll with its body-shuffled control, on all 13 reports and on the 5 reports of the unread 500 model steps; head tilt's part of the token's change (token units); the path's output, largest row, share of rows at the cap, fixed vector and weight size; without gradient, on every 10th model step of the read part (70) and of the unread part (50), per sense the delayed lesson's error over the error of predicting no change; head tilt read from the transformer's output at the vestibular slot on the unread set (5 reports of 10 rows); the token's change between model steps; the loss's parts, the median and largest gradient norm before the clip, and the count of non-finite losses since the reading before. Per 100 updates the path's stats block (the change slope of the two parts, the weight's size, the share of updates at which the hold scaled it back).

NOT IN THE CHECK, so the result is not read as more than it is: the top-down gate's blend, wellness, the planner and the motor controller's live terms, the efference, contact and self-state lessons, the imagination chain, the liveness repair's revivals, new experience (692 model steps cycled 8.7 times per arm), the running input statistics. Those are read by the production segment's watch after a switch.

THE JUDGE (ht_whole_model_check.judge) writes check.json with P1 to P4; the runner writes the row's status and last run; the result and the decision are then written into this row and into the review's record.
measures: P1, the purpose: head tilt read from the vestibular token on the 500 unread model steps, path arm (R squared; 0 = no better than predicting no change, 1 = exact; the inputs read 0.56), and its body-shuffled control (0 expected).

P2, the other senses: per sense (vision, tactile, audio, proprioception) and per evaluation set (read: 70 model steps; unread: 50; 8 bodies each), the delayed lesson's error over the error of predicting no change (1 = no better than predicting no change, 0 = exact), in the three long arms at the same update.

P3, identity with the switch absent: the first update at which the branch's per-update loss or gradient norm differs from production's (none = every update equal), and the parameter hashes at updates 0, 100 and 200.

P4, the bound: the largest row of the path's output (token units; the cap is 0.3), the path's weight size (root mean square of its 5,376 weights; production's standing line W1 is 0.2), non-finite losses (0 = none), the switch record (exact = the token with the path equals the token without it bit for bit at the load).

Readings beside them, no line: the change slope of the two parts (-1 = the encoder's part takes the path's change out of the sum, 0 = unrelated), head tilt's part of the token (token units; 0 = the token's change does not follow head tilt), the path's fixed vector (token units), head tilt from the transformer's output at the vestibular slot, vestibular's own error ratio, the token's change between model steps, the gradient norm before the clip (median and largest per window) in the path arm against the control arms.
rows.pass_line: All four. P1: on the path arm, at every reading from update 2,000 on whose control is within 0.10 of zero, head tilt read on the unread 500 model steps at or above 0.25 and at least 0.25 above its control; at least 8 of every 10 readings from update 2,000 on judged; the last reading at or above 0.25. P2: for each of vision, tactile, audio and proprioception on both evaluation sets, over the readings from update 1,000 on, the median of ln(path arm / control arm) at or under the largest |ln(control_seed1 / control)|, and no reading of the path arm above the control arm x the production watch's alert multiple (1.43; vision 3.29). P3: the branch's code with the switch absent equal to production's at every one of 200 updates (loss and gradient norm as exact hex) and in the parameter hashes at 0, 100 and 200; when production's code differs from its own repeat at or before the first difference, P3 rests on the processor lockstep alone and the result says so. P4: the switch exact and the route check met; no row of the path's output above 0.3 x 1.01 (the bf16 rounding of a scaled row); the path's weight size at or under 0.2 at every 100 updates; 0 non-finite losses; the arm finished.
rows.pass_line_basis: REACHABILITY OF P1. Encoder bench of path version 2 under on (row vestibular_token_path_bench; D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/vestibular_token2/path_bench_hold/bench.json, arm path_none_cap03, 5 unread reports): 0.33 at 1,000 updates, 0.42 at 2,000, 0.47 at 4,000 and 0.43 to 0.54 at every reading through 60,000, its control -0.01 to -0.12. With the whole model, version 2 under on (the 200-update script check, D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/vestibular_token2/live_bench_v2_check): 0.22 at 100 updates and 0.265 at 200 on the unread model steps; version 1 under the exception read 0.26 and 0.34 at those updates, 0.44 at 1,000, 0.50 at 2,000 and 0.44 at 6,000 (row vestibular_token_path_live_bench). So the expected reading at update 2,000 is 0.42 (encoder bench, on) to 0.50 (whole model, version 1), 0.17 to 0.25 above the line, against 0.01 to 0.05 between neighbouring readings. The control limit of 0.10: inside 6,000 updates the unread control read -0.011 to -0.031 on the encoder bench and -0.014 to -0.029 on the whole model (version 1); it went past -0.10 only from 52,000 encoder-bench updates on. FROM UPDATE 2,000: production's standing line T1 is judged from N + 2,001, a window whose probe covers updates 1,000 to 3,000. P2: two runs without the switch differ only in the replay update's draws, so their spread is this bench's run-to-run noise on the same model steps; on version 1 the path arm's worst readings of the other senses were 1.002 to 1.09 x the control arm's in the first pass (3,000 updates) and one vision reading at 1.53 x in the second (update 2,500), while the control arm's own proprioception moved between 0.86 and 1.12 over its readings on the read set, so a cost cannot be told from that movement without the second control. The alert multiples are production's watch's, measured on the lineage with nothing switched (0 false stops in 206 and in 234 watches). P3: with the switch absent the branch adds a constructor branch that reads off and attribute look-ups that read None, so equality is what the code says; the processor lockstep measured it on a learner of width 32; the card legs measure it on the real model at its real size. P4: the hold keeps the largest live row at the cap (encoder bench of version 2: weight size 0.07 to 0.105 through 60,000 updates, scaled back at 1 in 100 updates or fewer; W1 is 0.2). LENGTH: 6,000 updates is the length the builder declared for this pass and 2.4 x the update at which the read-out had its highest value on the whole model (2,500, version 1); the switch's own standing lines then read production.

rows.title: HEAD_TILT_REPAIR whole-model check under on_delayed_encoder_only
rows.question: With checkpoint 481,800's whole model updated 6,000 times on the graphics card by the same bench as row head_tilt_repair_whole_model_check_481800 and --vestibular-input-path on_delayed_encoder_only (the delayed lesson trains the vestibular encoder's own layers and not the path), does the vestibular token carry head tilt on the 500 unread model steps at 0.25 or more and 0.25 or more above its control from update 2,000 on, and does vision's prediction error stay within the spread of the first check's two runs without the switch, where under the wiring on it read a median 10.7 of 100 parts above the control arm on the read set (6.1 on the unread set) against a seed-to-seed line of 3.5 (2.0)?
rows.why: The first check failed its line P2 for vision only under the wiring on (row head_tilt_repair_whole_model_check_481800, Oct 5, 2026 1:45 PM PDT), so HEAD_TILT_REPAIR is not switched on as it is, and that row's on_fail names this bench under on_delayed_encoder_only as the comparison. The two wirings build the same path with the same gradient (the live row's VICReg and reconstruction terms; the path frozen inside the delayed lesson in both) and differ in one thing: under on_delayed_encoder_only the delayed lesson still trains the vestibular encoder's own layers, the lesson whose residual term holds the token's change between model steps down (encoder bench: 0.08 to 0.13 token units against 0.14 to 0.22 under on). So vision's error under this wiring at the same readings says whether the cost comes with on's removal of the delayed lesson from the encoder (the token's larger change between model steps) or with the path in either wiring. The decisions that depend on it: the coordinator's wiring decision for HEAD_TILT_REPAIR, and what the builder is asked for (on_pass and on_fail).
rows.gof_link: Sensing and prediction for gain of function: head tilt has to reach the vestibular token without the other senses' predictions paying for it; this names which wiring of HEAD_TILT_REPAIR, if either, does both with the whole model's lessons live.
rows.target_metric: Two quantities at the first check's readings. rows.title: Where the handles' predicted directions merge
rows.question: On checkpoint 481,800, at the 16 states, 26 handles and 3 axes of row investigate_motor_handle_reach_481800, at which stage of the predictor's route do the changes that different body handles' commands make come to lie along one direction: the motor token; in each of the transformer's blocks the cross-modal attention (across the 6 senses' tokens of one model step), the causal-temporal attention (across 128 model steps of one sense), the cross-modal bridge (across the whole sequence) and the feed-forward layer; the heads' input; the proprioception head's attention, hidden layer and output; the all-slot path; the prediction? And is that stage an attention whose weights switch (which module, how saturated, how much of its change comes from the change of its weights) or a feed-forward or head layer?
rows.why: Register entry PREDICTION_HANDLE_DIRECTION_LOST (GOF-BLOCKER; the operator's ruling of Oct 5: fixed in a controlled training run): for 19 of 26 handles the predicted next proprioception does not point at the handle's own real consequence; different handles' changes are told apart in the motor token (mean absolute cosine 0.23) and merged in the prediction (0.86; 0.42 with both side paths off). The stage where they merge decides which components the repair run changes and what its gates 4, 5 and 7 measure again, and whether TRANSFORMER_BLOCK0_ATTENTION_SATURATED (CURRENT EFFECT UNKNOWN) damages this path.
rows.gof_link: Action causality: the planner can steer a handle only through predictions that say which handle's command does what; this locates where that information is lost on the way from the motor token to the prediction.
inputs: Checkpoint 481,800 of run seg41o_1431 built on the processor by the probe harness (mimo_bridge/tools/gof_probe_harness.py load_frozen, without the optimizer) and its episode companion: per body the saved world, context, memory and histories

The procedure of row investigate_motor_handle_reach_481800 (handle_reach.py): per body the same collect_starts (2 states, 15 model steps apart) from the checkpoint's saved episode, the same seeded axes drawn in the same sequence, the same turns, every command in its executed form. The development passes of 2:24 to 2:35 PM PDT showed that the states' base commands are not reproduced from one process to the next (three passes at 8/8, 8/4 and 4/4 environment/torch threads differed from each other by 14 to 61 of 100 parts of the executed command changes and from that row's saved changes), so this job measures its own real changes

Every command also run for 1 model step from the restored state in the saved world (handle_reach.py's real arms, Session.run_arm): the raw proprioception token of the new frame minus the base command's; the base command run twice (the physical floor)
Checkpoint 481,800's model.safetensors, read for handle_merge_heads.py: block 0's cross-modal attention and the proprioception head's attention (their value and output projections)
steps: Run docs/gain_of_function_v4/coordinator/investigate_1005/handle_merge_location.py --real --analyse through investigate_registry.py run: the processor only (the card hidden), 8 threads, 6 GB of RAM and 9 GB committed. Before it, development passes of the same script on 2 states (--bodies 1 --starts-per-body 2; folders handle_merge_481800_dev, _dev4, _dev44 under D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/investigate_1005, through investigate_registry.py capped under the same limits; not used as results) showed that the code runs, that its checks hold, and that the states are not reproduced across processes

Per body: a Session from the saved episode and 2 states (Session.collect_starts, 15 model steps apart); per state the base command and the 78 turned commands (26 handles x 3 axes; the eyes: 10 degrees in 3 directions)

Per state and condition (deployed; asked change off; all-element path off; both off: handle_reach.py Conditions): lem.model.predictive_state.transition in batches of 40 rows whose row 0 is the base command; forward hooks (none returns a value) read each stage's vector: the motor token; per block the stream after the cross-modal attention, after the temporal attention, after the bridge and after the feed-forward layer, at all 6 slots of the newest model step; the final LayerNorm; the heads' input (plus the memory's bias); the proprioception head's attention output, hidden layer and output; the all-slot path's per-slot projection, hidden layer and output; the heads' sum; the predicted token

Deployed and both off: every attention module's weights recomputed in float64 from its own input and projection weights; at the base command the largest weight, entropy share and key read most per head; per turned command the module's change at each of the 6 queries split into a value part, a weight part and their product's part; the feed-forward hidden layers; the change of the head's and the path's output when only one slot of the heads' input carries the command's change; for block 0's cross-modal attention also each head's own value part at each query and the singular values of each head's value-to-output map

Per state, after the predictions: every command run for 1 model step from the restored state in the saved world (Session.run_arm, learning off) and the raw proprioception token of the new frame read; the base command run before and after the arms (the physical floor)

handle_merge_analysis.py on the saved vectors: per stage M, the first direction's share, the size, the float32 floor, the own-minus-swapped score against this run's real change (directly where the stage is in proprioception-token coordinates; through a linear read-out fitted on 7 bodies and scored on the 8th for every stage, with a shuffled-handle control); the attention parts; the slot parts; the declared merge rule

handle_merge_heads.py on the saved vectors and the checkpoint's weights (no model runs; added at 2:46 PM PDT, after the development pass of 2:40 PM showed that block 0's cross-modal attention carries the motor slot's change into another slot through one head each): every head's value-to-output map applied to the change of the slot it would read, alone and all heads summed (the reading if the attention spread over the keys)

handle_merge_switching.py on the saved vectors (no model runs; added at 3:35 PM PDT after the analysis showed parts that cancel at block 1's cross-modal attention): per attention module and query, the turns in which a head reads another key (total variation above 0.5) and the quiet turns (below 0.01), with the parts and M over the quiet turns
measures: M per stage: mean absolute cosine between two body handles' changes at the same state and axis (1 = every handle's change along one line; 0 = all at right angles); 300 pairs x 48 state-axis cells; with a 95% interval from resampling the 8 bodies
first_share per stage: the share of the 25 body handles' summed squared change on their first principal direction (median over cells; 1/25 = none shared, 1 = one direction)

own-minus-swapped per stage: the cosine of a handle's change with its own real proprioception change minus its mean cosine with the 25 other handles' real changes at the same state and axis (0 = no more toward its own consequence than toward others'; about 0.96 for the real change itself); direct where the stage is in proprioception-token coordinates, and through a linear read-out (ridge regression on unit-length changes, fitted on 7 bodies, scored on the 8th) at every stage; 95% intervals from resampling the 8 bodies

Attention, per module and query: the shares of the change's summed square carried by the value part, the weight part and their product (each 0 to 1 when they do not cancel); the weights' total variation per head (0 = the same weights, 1 = disjoint); at the base command each head's largest weight and entropy share (1 = even over the keys, 0 = one key)
Slot parts: the share of the head's and the path's output change carried by each of the 6 slots of the heads' input when it alone carries the command's change
Floors: per stage the float32 floor (the base command's vector in the second batch minus the first) and the median ratio of the changes to it

Block 0's cross-modal attention head by head: the share of each query's change carried by each head, M of each head's part, and the share of each head's value-to-output map's summed squared singular values on its largest one (1 = the map sends every input along one direction)
rows.target_metric: M per stage along the route, from the motor token (0.23 on Oct 5) to the predicted proprioception (0.86); the real proprioception's own M (0.45) is what a prediction that follows the body would show. The stage whose rise carries the merge is the target of the repair run.

No stage between the token and the prediction has been read.

rows.pass_line: The declared rule, written before the run: along the route's sequence of stages (the token; per block after the cross-modal attention, after the temporal attention, after the bridge, after the feed-forward layer; the final LayerNorm; the heads' input; then the branch, the proprioception head or the all-slot path, whose output change is the larger part of their sum; their sum; the prediction), each transformer stage read at the slot of the newest model step that carries the largest share of the prediction's change (from the slot parts), the merge stage is the stage whose M rises the most over the stage before it. PASS (LOCATED): that rise is at least half of the whole rise from the token to the prediction. FAIL (DISTRIBUTED): it is not; every stage with a rise of at least 0.10 is named. The mechanism is named from the same run: at an attention stage, weight switching when the weight part carries more than half of the summed squared change, otherwise the values; otherwise the feed-forward or head layer named. A reading counts only when its checks hold: the physical floor 0 (the base command run twice in the restored world gives the same proprioception token), the prediction with every hook inactive equal to the prediction with the hooks, the three attention parts summing to the module's change within 1e-6 and the recomputed attention output equal to the module's within 1e-4 (both relative).
rows.pass_line_basis: Half of the whole rise: a majority rule (one stage carries more of the merging than all others together), nothing tuned. 0.10 is a tenth of M's scale. The physical floor and the hookless prediction are equalities within one process (row investigate_motor_handle_reach_481800 read the physical floor 0 at all 16 of its states). The parts are exact algebra in float64 (value + weight + product = the change); 1e-4 is float32's rounding of a softmax output with room (the development passes read 5.4e-7 to 6.4e-7). The 10-times floor rule is row investigate_motor_handle_reach_481800's L2 line.

rows.title: HEAD_TILT_REPAIR diagnosis of on's vision cost, seed 1
rows.question: With checkpoint 481,800's whole model updated 6,000 times per arm on the graphics card by the first check's bench, under --vestibular-input-path on with the replay update's draws from seed 1 and under on_delayed_encoder_only with the same seed: does vision's rise under on recur against the seed-to-seed line, which module of the clip's shared group holds on's largest gradient norms, and does the vestibular token for the same input drift under on and not under on_delayed_encoder_only, at a size that costs vision's prediction?
rows.why: The first check failed its line P2 for vision under on (row head_tilt_repair_whole_model_check_481800); the same bench under on_delayed_encoder_only showed no vision cost (row head_tilt_repair_delayed_encoder_only_check_481800). One run per wiring cannot tell a one-time event of the first run (its largest gradient norm, 137,052 in updates 500 to 999, the window before vision's rise) from the wiring, and that run holds no gradient reading per module and no reading of the token's drift. The coordinator decided on Oct 5, 2026 to run this diagnosis; the first check's P2 failure stands as recorded and this run does not requalify the repair. The decisions that depend on it: what the builder is asked to repair in the wiring on, and the coordinator's wiring decision (on_pass).
rows.gof_link: Prediction for gain of function: head tilt in the vestibular token helps only if the other senses' predictions keep their accuracy; this names the mechanism by which the wiring on costs vision's prediction, so that a repair acts on it.
rows.target_metric: Three readings. (1) Vision's delayed-lesson error over its no-change error, the on arm over the control arm with the same seed (control_seed1), median over the readings from update 1,000 on (1.0 = no cost; the first on arm read 1.107 over its own-seed control). (2) Per window of updates, the module holding the largest gradient norm of the clip's shared group, and each module's median norm (the clip is at 1.0). (3) The vestibular token's drift since update 0: the root mean square per number of the same rows' token change, token units (0 = unchanged); and the swap: vision's error with today's weights and today's vestibular tokens over its error with the update-0 vestibular tokens of the same rows (1.0 = the same, above 1 = today's tokens cost vision's prediction).
rows.baseline: No rise: vision's ratio over its same-seed control within the first check's seed-to-seed line (ln ratio 0.034 on the read set, 0.019 on the unread set). No module specific to on: every window's largest norm in the other senses' encoders, as in all 15 windows of the on_delayed_encoder_only arm of seed 0 (36 to 9,028). No drift specific to on: the two wirings' drift within one model step's change of the token at update 0 (0.077 token units), and vision's swap ratio under on within 1.035 times the other wiring's.
rows.statistical_line: (1) The judge's P2 line for vision with control_seed1 as the primary control: the median over the readings from update 1,000 on of ln(on arm / control_seed1) against the largest |ln(control / control_seed1)| over the same readings (0.034 read, 0.019 unread; the same number either way round); the ratio over the seed-0 control is read beside it. (2) A module's median norm in a window under on against the larger of the two on_delayed_encoder_only runs' medians in the same window (seed 0 from the comparison, seed 1 from this job). (3) At the reading of on's largest vision excess from update 1,000 on (update 1,500 when vision's rise does not recur): on's drift minus the other wiring's (seed 1) against 0.077 token units, the token's change between model steps at update 0 (the size of change the transformer's input has from one model step to the next); and vision's swap ratio under on over the same under the other wiring against 1.035, the first check's seed-to-seed line for vision on the read set.
rows.material_gof_line: Vision's rise matters for gain of function at the production watch's alert multiple, 3.29 times the control (the first on arm reached 1.28 times, 39 of 100 of that line). For the mechanism readings: not yet defined.

NOT IN THE CHECK, as in the first check: the top-down gate's blend, wellness, the planner and the motor controller's live terms, the efference, contact and self-state lessons, the imagination chain, the liveness repair's revivals, new experience (692 model steps cycled 8.7 times per arm), the running input statistics.
measures: Vision's error over its no-change error (0 = exact, 1 = no better than predicting no change), each arm over control_seed1 and over control at the same update, on the read set (70 model steps) and the unread set (50), 8 bodies; the other senses the same way.

Per window of updates: the gradient norm of the clip's shared group before the clip per module (the vestibular encoder's own layers, the other senses' encoders, the transformer, the prediction heads, the rest) as median and largest, the module holding the window's largest, the count of updates above the clip of 1.0, and the path's own group.

The drift since update 0, token units (root mean square per number; 0 = unchanged): the token on all span rows, the read rows and the unread rows; the encoder's own part the same way; the anchor, the rows' spread at update 0.
The swap ratio per sense: today's evaluation error over the error with the update-0 vestibular tokens (1.0 = the same; above 1 = today's tokens cost that sense).

Beside them: P1 to P4 of each arm (head tilt from the token on the 500 unread model steps; the other senses; identity from the first check's legs; the bound), the change slope, the token's change between model steps.
rows.pass_line: The measurement is complete: the tests pass; the code check's reading at update 100 holds the drift, the swap and the gradient readings; both arms finish 6,000 updates with the route check met and 0 non-finite losses; both judge files and the outcomes file are written. The three outcomes are then read as the statistical_line declares; none of them qualifies or disqualifies the repair (a diagnosis, not a requalification).
rows.pass_line_basis: THE SEED: seed 1 gives the replay update the draws of control_seed1, so each new arm is divided by the control arm that shares its draws, and the seed-to-seed line (the two first-check controls) is the same number either way round. THE DRIFT'S LINE: 0.077 token units is the vestibular token's change between neighbouring model steps at update 0 (first check, every arm's reading at update 0: 0.0768), the size of change the transformer's input has from one model step to the next; a drift gap above it is a shift of the same rows larger than one model step's change. THE SWAP'S LINE: 1.035 is the first check's largest seed-to-seed ratio for vision on the read set, the bench's run-to-run spread on that quantity. THE MODULE LINE: two on_delayed_encoder_only runs (seed 0, seed 1) bracket that wiring's medians; on's median above both is outside what the other wiring shows on the same windows. REACHABILITY: the first on arm's vision excess was 1.284 at update 1,500 and its median 1.107 against the line's 1.035; under on_delayed_encoder_only the token's change between model steps reached 1.21 to 1.91 times the control's with no vision cost, so a drift reading of the token's size alone may not separate the wirings, and the swap reads whether today's tokens cost vision. WHAT WOULD SHOW AN OUTCOME WRONG: a second seed-1 run of either wiring (not run here) moving the reading by more than the gap it decides.

cost.basis: Measured on this bench at this model size on this card today: the comparison arm ran 6,000 updates with its readings in 2,123 s (largest RAM 2.28 GB, graphics memory 1,595 MiB, 5.87 GB committed); the first check's path arm in 1,264 s. This job runs two such arms, a code check of 100 updates and the tests; the swap adds one evaluation pass per reading. The limit of 9,000 s is 2.1 x two arms at today's measured 2,123 s.

rows.on_pass: Each outcome decides as declared here before the run. (1) VISION'S RISE RECURS (the P2 line for vision missed on either set against control_seed1): the cost belongs to the wiring on; HEAD_TILT_REPAIR is not switched on under on, and the builder is asked for a repair of on's mechanism as (2) and (3) name it. DOES NOT RECUR (met on both sets): the first run's cost is not shown to belong to on; the first check's failure stands, and whether on gets a requalification run (a new row) is the coordinator's decision. (2) A MODULE OTHER THAN THE OTHER SENSES' ENCODERS holds on's largest norm in any window, or its median lies above both on_delayed_encoder_only runs' in the window of vision's largest excess: that module is named to the builder as the route of on's cost. THE OTHER SENSES' ENCODERS hold every window's largest in both wirings: the norm spikes are the bench's motor-encoder property, not on's; they go to MOTOR_ENCODER_REPAIR's question (the coordinator's) and leave on's mechanism. (3) ON'S DRIFT exceeds the other wiring's by more than 0.077 token units AND vision's swap ratio under on is above the other wiring's by more than 1.035 times, both at the reading of vision's largest excess: the drift of the vestibular token for the same input is the mechanism named to the builder. Either not: the drift is not shown to be the mechanism; the remaining candidate is the module that (2) names, or none, and the record names the reading still missing. Nothing is switched on by this row.
rows.on_fail: The measurement is incomplete (a test fails, the code check misses a reading, or an arm does not finish): no outcome is read; the failing step is named with its log lines, the script is corrected, and the job runs again under this row with its status and last run written again; nothing else changes.

rows.title: ATTENTION_CAP's bound, measured on checkpoint 481,800 before any training: per bound, the jumps of the capped attention weights under one-handle command turns, the planner search's change under a token change of 1 in 100,000, and what the cap costs each sense's prediction
rows.owner: the attention cap builder (branch repair/attention-cap-2026-10-05)
rows.question: Which bound B does the repair run train ATTENTION_CAP with? With the bound set on the 7 covered attention modules of checkpoint 481,800 (the transformer's cross-modal attention in its 4 blocks, the motor encoder's 2 attention layers and its pool) and no training, for each B of 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 4 and 5 against the same model without the cap: in how many of the 1,200 one-handle command turns of row investigate_handle_merge_location_481800 does some head of a covered module still move its weights by more than half, how far does production's planner search move its selected command under a token change of 1 in 100,000, and what does the cap cost each sense's prediction before training?
rows.why: The operator's decision of Oct 5, 2026 (received by 4:47 PM PDT): build the attention cap now as the repair run's repair, off by default, and do not launch the repair run until the fresh relaunch-code review passes. (0) Release: the largest weight one key can take among the 6 keys of a cross-modal query at the bound, 1 / (1 + 5 exp(-2B)), is at most 99 in 100; of the bounds read this admits B = 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5 and 3 (5,964, 8,007, 9,161, 9,674 and 9,878 in 10,000) and not 4 or 5 (9,983 and 9,998 in 10,000), by arithmetic, before any reading. (1) Admissible: clause (0) holds and J(B) is at most J(off) / 10 (0 when J(off) is 0). (2) Among the admissible bounds, those with P(B) at most P(off) / 10 are preferred, and B is the largest preferred bound; with no preferred bound, B is the admissible bound with the smallest P(B) (a tie goes to the larger bound). (3) With no admissible bound the rule answers none and the row fails. Release, cost and merge are read and reported for each bound; beyond clause (0) they do not enter the choice. AMENDED Oct 5, 2026 at 5:35 PM PDT: clause (0) was added after the development pass of 5:26 to 5:31 PM PDT (1 body, 2 decisions; plumbing only, not a result; times from the runner's development-run log), in which every bound met (1) and (2), so the rule as first declared picked B = 5. rows.pass_line_basis: THE RELEASE LINE IS A SAFETY CONSTRAINT ON THE BOUND, NEVER EVIDENCE THAT THE REPAIR WORKS (the operator's ruling of Oct 5, 2026 (received after 6:22 PM PDT)): clause (0) keeps the bound where no head can hold its whole weight on one slot and its softmax still passes gradient to the scores; it says nothing about whether the repair works. The same holds for J: the attention readings of this row chose the bound among the bounds read before any training, and they are not evidence of the repair's success. The repair's success is judged only on outcomes, by the four qualification rows on the repair run's last checkpoint, which read the ruling's five requirements (the predictions under tiny command changes, the command-specific prediction, the handles' consequences, the planner search's stability and its real goal progress). PURPOSE: the operator's requirements 1 (tiny command changes no longer cause attention or routing jumps) and 4 (planner search stable) are what the cap is for, so the choice rests on J and P; clause (0) keeps the cap's own mechanism (no head held on one key, gradient to the scores). RELEASE, CLAUSE (0): the planner record counts a motor encoder pool head whose largest weight is above 99 in 100 as held on one handle (98 of 100 heads on 479,350; PLANNER_SEARCH_REPAIR_2026-10-05.md section 1.2); at 99 in 100 a head keeps at least 1 in 100 of its weight on the other slots and its softmax passes at least 243 in 10,000 of a lesson's gradient to its scores at that weighting (attention_cap.least_gradient_share; 0 at a weight of 1.000; 639 in 10,000 at B = 2.5, 33 at B = 4, 5 at B = 5). The bench of the Sep 26 prediction heads branch (bound times cosine over the same 6 slots, with training; commit 8275546ab) held every attention head at leads of at most 2.6 logits at bound 2.5, let vision's lead reach 5.1 at bound 5 and re-locked at 10 (lead 11.6). A TENTH: holding the motor encoder's 3 attention modules left 68 in 1,000 of the planner search's change on 481,800 (1.26 of 18.4 degrees) and holding them with the transformer's 12 left 12 in 100,000 (row planner_search_mechanism_controls); the cap covers 7 of those 15 modules and makes their weights smooth functions of the command instead of holding them, so a tenth is a share one hold of the covered modules met, and the closing line of PREDICTOR_ATTENTION_SWITCHING (a hundredth, with the attention live) is judged on the trained checkpoint (row attention_cap_qual_planner_stability). P is a preference with a fallback, not a gate. THE LARGEST BOUND: at a larger bound each head's weights come nearer a hard choice of the key whose cosine with the query is largest, so the cap changes today's routing least where today's highest dot product and highest cosine fall on the same key; the cost readings show how far that holds. The cost before training is what the repair run must recover and is judged on its last checkpoint by the qualification rows, since no reading relates a cost before training to the trained readings. REACHABILITY OF (1): the total variation between two softmax weightings is at most tanh(d / 2), d the largest change of a score, so a head's weights can move by more than half only when some score changes by more than ln 3 = 1.099, that is, when a query-key cosine (range -1 to 1) changes by more than 1.099 / B: 110, 73, 55, 44 and 37 hundredths at B = 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5 and 3. Without the cap a score has no such bound (the saturated heads lead by tens of logits), and 27 and 30 of 1,200 turns switch at two cross-modal queries. Whether a 20-degree turn of one handle's command changes a cosine that much is what this row reads; the rule answers none when no bound is admissible.

rows.pass_line_basis: THE LINE (the operator's ruling of Oct 5, 2026 (received after 6:22 PM PDT), line (e)): real goal progress that beats the current search beyond scatter, on paired same-state trials (each decision's searched command and the motor controller's command executed from the same saved state), with the difference's 95% interval above 0. THE TRIAL'S SIZE AND WHAT IT CAN SHOW: L and R each give 8 bodies (the eight worlds of their episodes); their states come from their own behaviour, so the two gains are compared as independent means of 8 body clusters. From the two existing readings of production's search against the motor controller's command on 481,800 (rows planner_search_design_arms_481800_v6 and _v7, 64 decisions each, raw tokens; goal_progress_reading.py's arithmetic, smallest_gain.py's estimates): the spread of g inside a body is 122.0 and 154.9 in 1,000 of P's unit and between bodies 36.8 and 0 in 1,000. With 32 decisions per body the difference of two checkpoints' gains has a standard error of 21.3 in 1,000 (the first reading's spreads) or 13.7 in 1,000 (the second's), so the smallest difference this trial shows in 80 of 100 runs is 64.3 or 41.3 in 1,000 of P's unit, 10 to 17 in 100 of the motor controller's own distance (with 8 decisions per body 85.5 and 82.5; with 64, 60.1 and 29.2; with any number, 55.5 and 0). The planner gate's paired trial against Adam shows 35 in 1,000 at the least, with 16 body clusters and any number of decisions per body at the spreads of the form s4 (PLANNER_SEARCH_REPAIR_2026-10-05.md section 2.3): this trial compares two checkpoints of 8 bodies each, so its reach is larger. 32 decisions per body is the largest held-out size the planner search work declared; 64 would lower the reach to 60.1 or 29.2 at twice the decisions. RUN-TO-RUN SCATTER: the two existing readings of the same checkpoint differ by 12.2 in 1,000 (interval -34.3 to +62.2 in 1,000; the plumbing check of goal_progress_reading.py, Oct 5, 2026); the interval must clear such differences. A smaller gain than the reach reads as not shown, and the record says so; the trial can be enlarged only with more body clusters (more held-out checkpoints), a decision for the coordinator and the operator.

rows.title: ATTENTION_CAP qualification's design under the NOT SHOWN rule: requirement 2's and 3's no-change scatter at the qualification's spacing, and the size requirement 1's per-sense interval needs
rows.owner: the attention cap builder (branch repair/attention-cap-2026-10-05)
rows.question: (1) Between two 2,000-step windows of the uncapped lineage spaced as the qualification spaces them (R the window ending at a record, L the last 2,000 model steps of a run of 2,500, 2,700 or 3,000 model steps after it), how far does each requirement-2 line's statistic scatter, what margin does that give, and how often does each line read PASS, NOT SHOWN and FAIL with no loss and with named losses? (2) Between uncapped checkpoints 479,350 and 481,800 (2,450 model steps apart), read by the qualification's procedure, how far do requirement 3's statistics and requirement 1's jump shares differ? (3) At how many states per checkpoint does a 10-fold cut of every sense's jumps read PASS in all five senses in 800 of 1,000 runs under requirement 1's per-sense interval?
rows.why: The cap reviewer's partial check of the fixes of 10:55 PM PDT (branch review/attention-cap-2026-10-05, commit 5b3e291d1, record section 7, evidence fix_check/), relayed by the coordinator: requirement 2's margins came from R's two adjacent halves, while windows spaced as the qualification spaces them spread 1.8 to 9.5 times wider (18 of 80 uncapped pairs failed, 225 in 1,000, not the stated 52); requirement 1's share line meets chance at R's small jump counts (a 20-fold cut passed all five senses in 453 of 1,000 simulated runs); requirement 3's margins were not checked against the spacing. And the operator's ruling of Oct 5, 2026 (received between 11:06 and 11:19 PM PDT), item 5: "A result indistinguishable from scatter is NOT SHOWN, not PASS."
rows.gof_link: A qualification line must separate a cap that keeps or improves the outcome from one that does not; a line narrower than the scatter between uncapped windows fails a working cap, a wider one passes a loss.
inputs: PART 1: the full stats records of the lineage that ends at 481,800 from 455,900 on (seg41e, seg41f and its two resumes, seg41g, seg41h, seg41m, seg41o; seg41n, a side branch, left out), read only; qual_swap_reading.py's pooled and ratios; qual_margins.json for R's levels at 481,800. A swap line is read only on the window pairs that hold its command dependence (both windows' body-mean improvement at least half of R's at 481,800): proprioception's hold_first dependence begins after the motor_asked_change switch of 474,875 and vestibular's after the heads_all_slot_path switch of 479,350; a line with fewer than 10 such pairs is named unmeasured at the spacing and keeps the halves of R's own window.

PART 2: checkpoints 481,800 and 479,350 (2,450 model steps before; built with seg41m's flags, without --heads-all-slot-path, which seg41o switched on), each with its episode companion, read only; qual_measurement.py's read_checkpoint and readings (16 states, 8 bodies x 2, one arm, no cap), the processor, 8 threads, one process. Checkpoint 480,829 (the same flags, 971 model steps before) is left out: its world ran 50 commands in 494 s against 53 s at 479,350 (the diagnosis passes of 12:06 and 12:16 AM PDT, Oct 6), so its 16 states would hold the processor for hours.
PART 3: row attention_cap_reachability_481800's per-body jump counts and judged cells of 481,800 (no cap) and part 2's, for the dispersion and the simulation.
steps: Run docs/gain_of_function_v4/attention_cap/qual_design.py --out D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/attention_cap/qual_design through production's test runner (test_runner run attention_cap_qual_design_481800 --threads 8), the processor only.

Part 1 per spacing (2,500, 2,700, 3,000 model steps) and line; part 2 the two checkpoints one after another; part 3 the dispersion and 2,000 simulated runs per sense, cut and state count; result.json, part1.json, part2.json.
measures: Part 1, per spacing and line: the statistic's drift, spread and root mean square over the window pairs; the margin (z x the root mean square, z for 50 joint false FAILs in 1,000); PASS, NOT SHOWN and FAIL per 1,000 simulated runs with no loss, a complete and a half loss (swap lines) or rises of 50 and 100 in 1,000 (error ratios); the same verdicts counted on the uncapped pairs.

Part 2, the pair 479,350 against 481,800: the pooled own-minus-swapped score's and M at the prediction's per-body differences (mean, spread, t interval), the count difference with its body interval, each sense's jump counts and the share ratio's interval and verdict.

Part 3: the dispersion; per state count and cut, the runs of 1,000 in which all five senses read PASS; the smallest state count at which a 10-fold cut does so in 800 of 1,000; seconds per state measured.
rows.target_metric: The margins and the verdict rates of requirements 2 and 3 at the qualification's spacing, and requirement 1's state count for a 10-fold cut to read PASS in 800 of 1,000 runs.
rows.baseline: The margins of 10:55 PM PDT (R's adjacent halves) and the reviewer's spacing reading (18 of 80 uncapped pairs failed, 225 in 1,000); requirement 1's share line (a 10-fold cut passing all five senses in 47 of 1,000 runs, the reviewer's simulation).
rows.statistical_line: Part 1: the window pairs overlap, so their count is not a count of independent runs; the simulated rates use the measured spread. Part 2: one pair per spacing (8 bodies, t with 7 degrees of freedom). Part 3: 2,000 simulated runs per case. A reading row.
rows.pass_line: PASS when part 1 reads at least 20 window pairs at each spacing, part 2 reads the two checkpoints' 16 states, and part 3's simulation runs. The readings decide no qualification line: the margins, the verdict rules and the sizes are written into the qualification rows from them, with notes.
rows.pass_line_basis: A reading row: the cap reviewer's partial check of the fixes of 10:55 PM PDT (branch review/attention-cap-2026-10-05, commit 5b3e291d1, record section 7, evidence fix_check/), relayed by the coordinator (items 1, 2 and 4) and the operator's ruling of Oct 5, 2026 (received between 11:06 and 11:19 PM PDT) (items 3 and 5). THE VERDICT RULE simulated is the coordinator's: for a claim of no loss, PASS when the interval excludes a loss as large as the margin, FAIL when it lies entirely beyond it, else NOT SHOWN; for requirement 1, PASS when the interval of the share ratio lies below 1, FAIL when above, else NOT SHOWN. THE SPACING: the qualification compares R's window (the 2,000 model steps ending at 481,800) with L's (the repair run's last 2,000), so the no-change scatter is read between windows that far apart in uncapped training. Requirement 3's spacing: no clean uncapped pair 2,500 model steps apart exists; 479,350 is 2,450 apart but before seg41o's --heads-all-slot-path switch, so its difference holds that switch's effect as well as 2,450 model steps of training; 480,829 (971 apart, the same flags) is left out for its world's speed. ACTIVE PAIRS: a swap line whose command dependence did not yet exist in a window (its improvement about 0 at every body, as proprioception's hold_first before 474,875 and vestibular's before 479,350) would read a scatter of 0 there; such pairs are left out of that line.

rows.title: ATTENTION_CAP learning signal: on checkpoint 481,800 with the cap at 3 set in place, do the 7 covered attention modules' parameters receive a usable gradient from the training's next-model-step lesson?
rows.owner: the attention cap builder (branch repair/attention-cap-2026-10-05)
rows.question: With the cap at 3 set in place on checkpoint 481,800, does each of the 7 covered modules (the transformer's cross-modal attention in blocks 0 to 3, the motor encoder's 2 attention layers and its pool) receive a gradient from the training's next-model-step lesson on its query and key in-projection (the parameters that reach the loss only through the softmax), at a size AdamW can use, and does every covered head's softmax pass gradient? Against the same modules without the cap.
rows.why: Under the operator's answers to the preflight questions (received between 1:38 AM PDT, the coordinator's reply before them, and 1:48 AM PDT, the clock after, Oct 6, 2026): "confirm that the learning signal needed to train the capped components exists and that the outcome measurements remain valid. If either is missing, that blocks this experiment." The cap was built because a softmax holding one key passes no gradient to its scores (block 0's heads at a weight of 1,000 in 1,000); the repair run (the cap arm against a matched control arm from 481,800, the operator's answers) can only train the covered modules if their parameters get gradient under the cap.
rows.gof_link: A repair run whose capped modules receive no usable gradient cannot show whether a trained cap improves command-specific prediction and stability; it would spend the run and the control arm on the untrained cap's effect only.
inputs: Checkpoint 481,800 of run H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41o_1431 (model.safetensors and its optimizer state), built on the processor by the trainer's own builder (causal_test._build_model) and load_checkpoint with the optimizer; its replay ring from the checkpoint's companion, decompressed by the whole-model bench into D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/head_tilt_review/companions/ckpt_step_481800.pt (read only), loaded by the bench's loader (vestibular_token_readouts_common.py at 03ce34b08, exported with git archive).

The lesson: the trainer's own LemLite.replay_update (mimo_bridge/lem_model.py) on 24 windows per draw, 24 draws, each draw with the cap at 3 and without it on the same windows (the torch and numpy streams seeded with 20261006 + the draw before each).
steps: Run docs/gain_of_function_v4/attention_cap/learning_signal.py --out D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/attention_cap/learning_signal --draws 24 --batch 24 --threads 8 through production's test runner (test_runner run attention_cap_learning_signal_481800 --threads 8 --device cpu), behind the memory guard.

The job replaces the optimizer's step by nothing (no parameter moves), wraps the learner's gradient clip to read every covered parameter's gradient before the clip, and puts a forward pre-hook on each covered module that recomputes its softmax weights from the call's inputs with the module's own scores (attention_cap.head_scores); per draw it runs replay_update with the cap at 3 set on the 7 covered modules and again without it, then writes result.json.
measures: Per covered module and arm (cap, off): the gradient's length on the query and key in-projection rows and biases, on the value rows, on the output projection (median and range over the draws); the query and key rows' root mean square per number (median, smallest); the draws with a non-zero query and key gradient.

Per covered head and arm: over every query row of every call, 1 - the sum over the keys of the squared weights (the trace of the softmax's Jacobian; 0 = one key holds all the weight and no gradient reaches the scores): the share of rows at least 1 in 1,000, the smallest and the median.

Per covered module and arm, a reading: AdamW's step as a share of a full step (the learning rate) at optimizer steps 1, 100, 1,000 and 4,500 of the repair run (3,000 model steps x 1.5 optimizer steps) and its mean over them, from the median squared gradient per number and the checkpoint's own running average of the squared gradient (AdamW's exp_avg_sq) (m from 0, v from the checkpoint's; the module's betas and epsilon).
rows.target_metric: Per covered module with the cap: the query and key gradient's root mean square per number against the optimizer's epsilon (in every draw), and the share of query rows at which every head passes gradient (1 - sum of squared weights at least 1 in 1,000).
rows.baseline: The same modules without the cap on the same windows (481,800 as it trains today: block 0's cross-modal heads at a weight of 1,000 in 1,000 on one key, the motor encoder's pool at 99,999 in 100,000 on one handle, the preflight record c007d2bb5af08224's gate 3).
rows.statistical_line: Existence in every draw (24 draws of 24 windows) for the line; medians and ranges over the draws for the readings. A reading row: no interval decides.
rows.pass_line: PASS when, for every one of the 7 covered modules with the cap at 3 set in place: (1) the root mean square per number of its query and key in-projection rows' gradient is at least the optimizer's own epsilon in every draw (where AdamW's running average of the squared gradient has adapted to it, a gradient of that size gets half a step), and (2) at every query row read, every head passes gradient: 1 - the sum of its squared weights at least 1 in 1,000. FAIL when either does not hold for some module: the learning signal is missing there, which blocks the experiment. INVALID when a draw gave no windows or fewer than 24 draws finished. Beside, deciding nothing: the same readings without the cap, the capped over the uncapped gradient length per module, and AdamW's movement with and without the cap.
rows.pass_line_basis: Written under the operator's answers to the preflight questions (received between 1:38 AM PDT, the coordinator's reply before them, and 1:48 AM PDT, the clock after, Oct 6, 2026) (item 3 of the coordinator's message relaying them). THE LESSON: replay_update is the training's next-model-step lesson as the trainer runs it after every 2nd model step; it rebuilds the motor token of the stepped-from model step through the motor encoder with gradient (its docstring: all 16 of the motor encoder's parameter tensors take gradient) and passes through the transformer's 4 blocks, so it reaches all 7 covered modules; the live step's other lessons (VICReg, efference, contact, the imagination chain) are not read. (1) THE SIZE: AdamW divides each number's step by sqrt(v) + eps; once v has adapted to a gradient of root mean square g, a number with g = eps gets half a step, so a gradient under the epsilon is a signal AdamW cannot use. (2) THE PASSAGE: the derivative of a softmax's weights with respect to its scores is diag(w) - w w^T, whose trace is 1 - sum of w^2; at 0 no lesson moves the scores (the defect the cap was built for). The bound guarantees at least 243 in 10,000 among 6 keys and 1,132 in 10,000 among 26 (attention_cap.least_gradient_share), so (2) checks that the cap is in force at every call of the lesson. ADAMW'S MOVEMENT is a reading, not a line: the checkpoint's running averages of the squared gradient were accumulated without the cap, so a capped gradient much smaller than the uncapped one gets steps smaller than the learning rate until v decays (b2 = 0.999: about 1,000 optimizer steps per factor e of v); the reading states how much of the run's 4,500 optimizer steps that costs.

rows.title: Reaching goal tokens against the ranked wellness value
rows.question: On 64 saved planning decisions of checkpoint 481,800 (8 bodies x 8, the model's own behaviour), when an executed candidate command ends nearer the goal tokens after the 5-model-step hold, does the ranked value of the goal ring (the value whose highest entry is the goal) and each of its 14 channels move toward the goal entry's stored values, and by how much against the scatter of the same value among candidates that made no goal progress?
rows.why: The goal ring ranks the last 200 model steps by 13 weighted wellness channels, and the planner search then minimises the distance from the predicted next senses to the winning entry's tokens. Reaching the tokens serves the objective only if it brings back what made the entry win. The answer decides whether a repair on the planner's input (PLANNER_PROSPECTIVE_TERM) can raise wellness through goal attainment, or whether candidates must be scored on the selecting quantities themselves (the operator's priority of Oct 6, 2026: which wellness quantities select goals, which are predicted, and whether successful goal attainment improves them).
rows.gof_link: Wellness changes behaviour only through the goal the ring selects; a goal whose tokens can be reached without regaining the selecting value gives the planner search no wellness gain to find.
inputs: Checkpoint D:/UEMA_Research/Saved/mimo_bridge/experiments/H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41o_1431/checkpoints/ckpt_step_481800 (read only), built on the processor by the probe harness (load_frozen: the trainer's builder on the run's args.json, loaded without the optimizer), and its episode companion: per body the saved world, context, memory, goal ring and wellness channel state.

Per body 8 planning decisions of the model's own behaviour, at least 20 model steps apart, the first at the companion's own model step 481,800, each with the planner's recorded inputs and its planning record.

Per decision 11 candidate commands in their executed form (the decision's execution transform, smoother and hand path): the five of production's planning record (the planner's command, hold, the motor controller's command, two babble-sized perturbations of the planner's command) and 6 babble-sized perturbations of the motor controller's command (5 cm per axis, a rotation of 0.5 rad per axis, strength plus |N(0, 0.05)|), seeded per decision.
The decision's goal ring (200 stored channel vectors), its normaliser (running centre and scale per channel), the floors and the weights in force (lem/model/wellness_channels.py).
steps: Run attainment_probe.py through test_runner run: the processor only (the card hidden), as two worker processes of 4 threads (bodies 0 to 3 and 4 to 7) that the job's own process starts at once; the job's process then merges their rows sorted by body, checks that both measured the same weights, and computes the readings.
Per body: a probe session from the saved episode; live on under the model's own behaviour to each planning decision; snapshot the world and the model state.

At the decision: rank the goal ring again with the decision's normaliser and weights (wellness_channels.rank_values); its best entry must be the planning record's goal (ring index equal, ranked value within 0.001); keep each channel's weighted normalised contribution u_c = w_c (s_c - centre_c) / max(scale_c, floor_c) of the goal entry and of the decision step (s_c the stored value: the channel minus the body's 10-model-step running average).

One transition per candidate on the planner's route: the wellness predictor's 5 outputs on the predicted senses with the candidate's own predicted motor token, with the decision's present motor token, and on the present senses with the candidate's motor token; its sums and goal distances must reproduce the planning record within 0.001. The gradients on the executed command of 0.15 x (1 - mean of outputs 1, 2, 4) in both motor-token forms and of the goal distance, at the motor controller's and the planner's command, inside the liveness repair's unwatched block.

Execute each candidate for the hold's 5 model steps from the identical restored snapshot (the motor controller's and the planner's commands twice, their physical traces required bit-identical); after each model step read the top-down-gated and raw tokens, the goal distance, the stored channel vector the goal ring keeps for that model step and its contributions under the decision's normaliser, the raw channel vector, the grounded wellness terms and the wellness predictor's outputs on the actual raw tokens.
Readings over the decisions, 95% intervals from resampling the 8 bodies (5,000 draws); write result.json with its verdict.
measures: f per candidate: 1 - (goal distance after the hold) / (goal distance at the decision); goal distance = the sum over the goal's real senses of the mean over 192 numbers of (top-down-gated token - goal token)^2, the planner's own definition; 0 = no nearer, 1 = the goal tokens reached, below 0 = farther.
G per decision: the goal entry's ranked value minus the decision step's (ranked value V = the sum over channels of u_c), in the ranking's own units.

Reproduction slope of the ranked value: within each decision over its 11 candidates, x = (f - mean f) x G and y = (V after the hold - V at the decision) - its mean; the slope through 0 of y on x pooled over decisions. 1 = ending a share f of the way to the goal tokens brings back the share f of the goal's lead; 0 = goal progress leaves the ranked value where it was; below 0 = it lowers it.

The same slope per channel (x = (f - mean f) x the channel's part of G); the slope of each grounded wellness term, of the bodily mean (tactile_comfort, capability, motor_state) and of the five-term sum on f (their change per full goal progress); the same reproduction slope on the raw channel values for goal entries stored on the probe's own timeline.
Share of G per channel: the channel's part of G summed over decisions over the sum of G (which channels the goal won by).

The scatter without goal progress: the standard deviation of y among candidates whose f is at or below 0; and per decision the change of V of the candidate with the most goal progress minus that of the candidate with the least, beside its value if the goal's lead came back in proportion.
rows.target_metric: The reproduction slope of the ranked value: 0 = reaching the goal tokens does not bring back the goal's ranked value, 1 = it brings it back in proportion to the goal progress.
rows.baseline: No reading of the ranked value against goal progress exists. Records already written (existing_records.json on branch investigate/wellness-goal-attainment-2026-10-06): in the paired same-state trials of 481,800 the five-term grounded sum averaged over the hold rose with goal progress by 0.0003 to 0.0149 per full progress (0 to 5 scale) with its interval above 0 in 3 of 5 sets, and on 480,829 and 479,350 the interval contained 0; in the causal-chain record of model steps 479,350 to 481,790 the channels the wellness predictor has no output for carried 51 of 100 parts of the goal's lead over the runner-up.
rows.statistical_line: The 95% interval of the reproduction slope from resampling whole bodies (8 bodies, 5,000 draws); a reading whose interval contains 0 reads NOT SHOWN.
rows.material_gof_line: not yet defined: a slope above 0 shows that goal attainment raises the selecting value; the share of the goal's lead that makes goal attainment a wellness gain worth the planner's search is not defined.
rows.pass_line: PASS: the reproduction slope's 95% interval lies entirely above 0 (goal progress raises the ranked value that selected the goal). FAIL: the interval contains 0 (reading NOT SHOWN) or lies below 0 (reading OPPOSITE). INVALID: fewer than 48 decisions or 6 bodies, a route check off by more than 0.001 (the ranked goal, the channel values at the decision, the predicted wellness and goal distances against the planning record), or a physical replay that differs.
rows.pass_line_basis: 0 is the slope of goal progress that leaves the ranked value unchanged; the line asks for a measurable rise, not a size. REACHABILITY: in the paired same-state rows of 481,800 the within-decision standard deviation of f is 0.095 to 0.142 (median per set; existing_records.json); the goal entry's ranked value in the causal-chain record is 4.85 at the median over 1,960 goal choices and the ring's centre is 0 by construction, so a slope of 1 gives x a within-decision spread of about 0.1 x 4.85 = 0.49. With 64 x 10 within-decision degrees of freedom the slope's standard error is the scatter of y over (0.49 x 25); a scatter up to 3 times 0.49 gives 0.12, and a doubling of it by the 8 body clusters keeps a slope of 1 at least 3 standard errors above 0. The scatter itself is unmeasured before this job (it is one of its readings).

rows.title: Prospective term with the present motor token
rows.question: On the saved planning decisions of row investigate_wellness_goal_attainment_481800 (checkpoint 481,800), does the wellness predictor's bodily mean (the mean of its outputs tactile_comfort, capability and motor_state) on the predicted next senses rank the candidate commands of one decision as their realised bodily wellness over the hold ranks them when it reads the decision's present motor token (command numbers 0, the input form of its lesson), against today's input (the candidate's own predicted motor token); how much of the difference between candidates comes from the motor token in each form, and how strong is the pull of PLANNER_PROSPECTIVE_TERM on the search beside the goal distance's in each form?
rows.why: The named comparison of PLANNER_PROSPECTIVE_READS_CANDIDATE_MOTOR_TOKEN (its next action since Oct 6, 2026): the minimal repair hands the term the decision's present motor token. Line G1 decides whether that input gives the term a ranking better than chance, and the pull decides whether the term at weight 0.15 could change the search's command at all. No production switch is built before PLANNER_SEARCH_REPAIR reaches VERIFIED (the operator's rule of Oct 5, 2026).
rows.gof_link: Prospective wellness can raise realised wellness only if the term's values rank commands as their real outcomes rank them and its gradient is large enough to change the search's command.
inputs: Row investigate_wellness_goal_attainment_481800's rows file D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/wellness_attain_runs/goal_attainment_481800/rows.jsonl: per decision and candidate the wellness predictor's 5 outputs on the predicted senses with the candidate's motor token, with the present motor token, and on the present senses with the candidate's motor token; the grounded wellness terms after each of the 5 hold steps; the predictor's outputs on the actual raw tokens of each hold step; the predicted goal distance; the gradients of the term in both forms and of the goal distance at the motor controller's and the planner's command.
mimo_bridge/tools/command_ranking.py ranking: pairs in 100 ranked as reality ranks them, with a 95% interval from resampling whole bodies.
steps: Run g1_comparison.py on that rows file through test_runner run: the processor only, arithmetic on saved values, nothing built or executed.

Per decision and candidate: the bodily mean predicted in each form, the realised bodily mean averaged over the hold (and after 1 model step), the five-term sums, and the predictor's bodily mean on the actual raw tokens of the hold as a reference.
G1 per form on the five candidates of production's planning record (G1's own definition) and on all 11 candidates; the paired difference present minus today on the same bootstrap draws.

The motor token's share of the difference between candidates per decision, the shift a command-holding motor token causes on the present senses, the within-decision spread of 0.15 x the bodily mean per form beside the predicted goal distance's spread, and the pull ratios and cosines at the motor controller's and the planner's command.
measures: G1 per form: of all pairs of one decision's candidates, how many in 100 the predicted bodily mean ranks as the realised bodily mean over the hold ranks them (a pair whose realised values differ by no more than 1 in 100 of that decision's spread is left out): 50 = chance, 80 to 90 = a ranking a search can use, 100 = every pair.
Present minus today: pairs in 100 ranked right with the present motor token minus with the candidate's, on the same judged pairs.
Reference: the same count for the predictor's bodily mean on the actual raw tokens of the hold (the predictor on the true outcomes in its lesson's input form).

Motor share: per decision var(present senses with the candidate's motor token) / (that + var(predicted senses with the present motor token)) over the candidates: 0 = candidates differ only through their predicted senses, 1 = only through their motor token.
Spread: within one decision the standard deviation of 0.15 x the bodily mean over the candidates, per form, over the predicted goal distance's (0 = the term gives every candidate the same value).
Pull: the length of the term's gradient on the executed command over the goal distance's (0 = the term gives the search no direction), per form, with the cosine between the two gradients.
rows.target_metric: G1 with the decision's present motor token: pairs in 100 of one decision's five candidates (production's record) that the bodily mean on the predicted senses ranks as the realised bodily mean over the hold ranks them; 50 = chance, 100 = every pair.
rows.baseline: On checkpoint 479,350 (Oct 4, 32 decisions) the predictor's five-term sum in today's input form ranked 56.0 of 100 pairs over the hold (interval 50.8 to 62.1). On 481,800 the motor token carried 70 of 100 parts of the bodily mean's difference between candidates and the term's pull was 0.0028 of the goal distance's (medians, row investigate_wellness_predictor_candidates_481800). G1 was never read on 481,800 (row planner_prospective_gate_reading_481800 was stopped before a result).
rows.statistical_line: The 95% interval from resampling whole bodies (8 bodies, 5,000 draws); the line is its lower end above 50.
rows.material_gof_line: 80 to 90 of 100 pairs: the ranking a search can use (mimo_bridge/tools/command_ranking.py RULES). The gate line (lower end above 50) only excludes chance.
rows.pass_line: PASS: G1 with the present motor token, on the five candidates of production's planning record, has the lower end of its 95% interval above 50 of 100. FAIL: it does not. INVALID: fewer than 48 decisions or 6 bodies in the rows read. Today's form, the paired difference, the reference, the motor share and the pull are read and reported whatever the verdict.
rows.pass_line_basis: G1 is the first gate line of PLANNER_PROSPECTIVE_TERM (row planner_prospective_gate_reading_481800): a term whose values rank commands at chance cannot raise wellness. Reachability: 64 decisions x 10 pairs is twice the pairs of the Oct 4 reading on 479,350, whose interval was 11.3 of 100 wide with 32 decisions, so a true ranking of 56 of 100 or better can meet the line and one at 50 cannot.

rows.title: PLANNER_SEARCH_REPAIR with --planner-judged executed_hold on checkpoint 481,800: is the stable search's command, judged by its predicted consequence after the 5-model-step hold as the body executes it, stable under a 0.00001 token change, and does it end nearer the goal after the hold than today's planner's command from the same saved states?
rows.owner: the planner builder (branch planner/hold-interval-2026-10-06)
rows.question: On 64 saved planning decisions of checkpoint 481,800 (8 bodies x 8; the development checkpoint only), every arm's command executed from the identical restored world state for the 5-model-step hold: (S) is the outcome spread Q of --planner-search trust_v2 with --planner-judged executed_hold (hold_s4) under Gaussian noise of 0.00001 per number on the present tokens within the operator's line 0.0039; (G) is the real goal distance in proprioception plus vision after the hold of hold_s4's command lower than that of today's planner's command executed as production executes it (chosen_live), with the 95% interval over bodies below 0?
rows.why: The operator's priority of Oct 6, 2026: 'Do not assume a passing cap completes planner repair. Use the existing planner work to address the prediction-versus-hold interval and the unscored final hand command. The prediction being judged must correspond to the command actually executed.' Today's objective reads the predicted senses one model step (50 ms) after the command while the body holds it for 5 (250 ms); the hand stage replaces the finger rows after the search, unscored; the eyes are sent the motor controller's command after the first model step of the hold (the evidence packet of Oct 6, section 4). The run's own causal chain record after model step 480,829 reads, for the planner's commands, a hold-end prediction of vision at 133 in 100 of the error of predicting no change. PLANNER_SEARCH_REPAIR's gate (the operator's joint verdict: stable AND nearer the goal than today's search beyond scatter) needs a stable form whose real gain over today's search can be shown; this row reads, on the development checkpoint and before any held-out checkpoint is spent, whether judging the command actually executed gives that.
rows.gof_link: The planner extends what the body can do only if the command it selects, as the body executes it, ends nearer the goal than the command it would otherwise send; this row reads that for the judged quantity of the command actually executed.
inputs: Checkpoint 481,800 of run H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41o_1431 (Saved/mimo_bridge/experiments/H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41o_1431/checkpoints/ckpt_step_481800), its args.json and its episode companion (the 8 saved worlds), read only.
