Branch planner/hold-interval-2026-10-06 at the commit the runner records: production's code with --planner-search (trust_v1, trust_v2 = the form s4 frozen at 6f845e5e1 of branch planner/search-2026-10-05) and --planner-judged (next_step, executed_hold), both off in the session's own planner.

Arms at every decision: reflex (the motor controller's command); start_hand (it, then the hand stage); chosen (today's planner: Adam, learning rate 0.1, 20 updates, on the next_step objective, then the hand stage; the session's own decision) executed with the eyes held at its eye command; chosen_live (the same command executed with the eyes as production sends them: the plan's eye command on the first model step, the motor controller's on each later one); s4 and s4@1 (trust_v2 on the next_step objective); hold_s4 and hold_s4@1 (trust_v2 with executed_hold). On each body's first 2 decisions (16 decisions) also: adam@1 (today's search after token noise draw 1, for today's Q), hold_adam and hold_adam@1 (Adam with executed_hold: the switch alone with today's search). @1 = Gaussian noise of 0.00001 per number on the five senses' present tokens, seeded by body, decision and draw.
steps: Run docs/gain_of_function_v4/planner_recovery/hold_jobs.py arms hold_arms_481800 --groups 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 --threads 8 (one worker of hold_arms_probe.py, bodies 0 to 7 one after another, 8 decisions per body 10 model steps apart; one worker because the smoke run's worker peaked at 4.2 GiB of RAM and the contract holds a job without the coordinator's word under 6 GB) through production's test runner (test_runner run planner_hold_arms_481800) on the branch's commit, processor only; no file under Saved/ is written (the probe harness's scene folder is redirected into the job's own folder).

Per body: the saved world and model state restored, run under the model's own behaviour to its next planning decision (probe_planner_candidates.next_decision), snapshot; on the body's first 2 decisions production's search re-run with no noise must reproduce the session's own selected command exactly.

Per arm: its search from the decision's captured state (search_lib.replan, the arm's --planner-search and --planner-judged set for that call only); the command's executed form (probe_planner_candidates.executed_candidate: the decision's execution transform, smoother and the arm's own raw hand joint goal); the prediction of that executed form held for 1 and for 5 model steps from the decision's state; then execution from the identical restored snapshot for the 5-model-step hold (chosen_live with the live eyes, every other arm with the eyes held at its own eye command, as executed_hold sends them); reflex, chosen and chosen_live run twice and their physical traces must be bit-identical.

Route checks, each refusing the decision above 0.001: chosen's and reflex's depth-1 goal distance against the planning record; every search arm's own recorded goal distance of its selected candidate against the probe's prediction of the composite that search judged: for executed_hold arms the composite sent, after 5 model steps (the command judged is the command executed); for next_step arms the hand stage's input, captured during the search, after 1 model step (today's planner judges a composite the hand stage then changes). Beside them, the hand stage's unscored change of each next_step search's predicted goal distance (composite sent minus composite judged) is recorded, not judged. Learned weights hashed before and after: a change refuses the job. measures: P: the real goal distance in proprioception plus vision after the hold on raw encoder tokens: per sense the mean over the token's 192 numbers of (real raw token - goal token)^2, summed over the two senses (0 = the senses are the goal's; the motor controller's command reads about 0.40 on this checkpoint).

Q per form: sqrt(mean over decisions of (P(form) - P(form@1))^2 / 2), for hold_s4 and s4 over the 64 decisions, and for hold_adam and today's search (chosen against adam@1) over the 16 decisions that read them.

Per pair of arms: the per-decision difference of P, its mean over the 8 body means and the 95% interval from resampling bodies; the same for the plain sum of the five senses, for P averaged over the 5 model steps of the hold, and per sense; the smallest gain the reading's own spreads show in 80 of 100 runs.

Per arm and sense: the prediction's error against the real raw token after 1 and after 5 model steps, beside the error of predicting no change (100 x sum of the first / sum of the second; 100 = no better than no change).

How far the eyes sent under chosen_live were from the plan's eye command on the later model steps of the hold (degrees); the command's difference from the motor controller's in cm and degrees; handle displacement and turn over the hold.

The hand stage's unscored change (today's mismatch 2): for today's search and every next_step search, the predicted goal distance of the composite sent minus that of the composite the search judged, after 1 and after 5 model steps (0 = the hand stage changed nothing the prediction reads).
rows.target_metric: P(hold_s4) - P(chosen_live): the real goal distance in proprioception plus vision after the hold of the executed_hold command minus that of today's planner's command as production executes it; below 0 = nearer the goal, 0 = no nearer. Beside it Q(hold_s4) against the line 0.0039.
rows.baseline: Today's planner's command executed as production executes it (chosen_live) from the same saved state. rows.title: PLANNER_SEARCH_REPAIR's --planner-judged executed_hold inside the model's own step on checkpoint 481,800: is the command the latch sends the composite the search judged, and is the plan's eye command held over the hold?
rows.owner: the planner builder (branch planner/hold-interval-2026-10-06)
rows.question: With --planner-judged executed_hold and --planner-search trust_v2 set on checkpoint 481,800's own model, at 16 planning decisions (8 bodies x 2) made inside LemLite.step with the hand stage and the causal chain's planning record, the trainer's latch rule run by the probe harness: does the command the latch sends equal the composite the search judged (every number of every body handle's row except the eyes', within 0.001), does every decision carry its judged record with the composite's goal distance predicted again alone within 0.001 of the search's own value, and is the eye command sent on each of the 4 later model steps of the hold the plan's own?
rows.why: The operator's priority of Oct 6, 2026: 'The prediction being judged must correspond to the command actually executed.' The unit tests run the switch on small stand-in models and the arms reading re-runs searches from saved decisions; the contract (docs/gain_of_function_v4/planner_recovery/CONTRACT_2026-10-05.md section 9, question 2) asks which test ran the whole loop the change lives in: a planning decision inside the model's own step, with the hand stage and the decision record, on which device, for how many decisions.
rows.gof_link: A planner's choice extends what the body can do only if the command the body receives is the one the choice was made on; this row reads that inside the loop the trainer runs.
inputs: Checkpoint 481,800 of run H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41o_1431 and its episode companion (the 8 saved worlds), read only; 480,829 and 479,350 are not read.

Branch planner/hold-interval-2026-10-06 at the commit the runner records; the session's model gets --planner-judged executed_hold and --planner-search trust_v2 (the form s4) after planner_hold.refusal finds the run's settings ones the switch is written for.
steps: Run docs/gain_of_function_v4/planner_recovery/hold_whole_loop.py --checkpoint <481,800> --out D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/planner_hold_runs/whole_loop_481800.json --threads 4 through production's test runner (test_runner run planner_hold_whole_loop_481800) on the branch's commit, processor only; no file under Saved/ is written.

Per body: the probe harness's session (the trainer's latch rule; the eyes sent the model's gaze output every model step) runs the model's own behaviour to its next planning decision (probe_planner_candidates.next_decision); the planning record, last_intention and the plan's eye command are read; the latch is run (Session.policy_act), then 4 model steps of the hold and the next latch (Session.policy_step x 5), each the model's own step.
Two decisions per body; learned weights hashed before and after (a change refuses the job).
measures: sent_vs_judged: the largest absolute difference over every body handle except the eyes and every number of its row between the command the latch sent (cm) and the composite the search judged (the planning record's exec_form, cm); 0 = the same command.
The judged record: present or not; |judged_minus_recorded| (the composite predicted again alone against the search's own goal distance); the goal distance after each model step of the hold.

The eye command sent on each of the 4 later model steps of the hold minus the plan's eye command, degrees (0 = held); the one sent at the next latch; the world's eye command over each burst after its saccades and gaze reflex minus the plan's, degrees.

rows.title: ATTENTION_CAP live learning signal: every lesson of one trainer model step on the 7 covered attention modules of checkpoint 481,800 with the cap at 3 set in place, and the movement the run's AdamW steps would give the motor encoder's 3 modules against the cross-modal attention's
rows.owner: the attention cap builder (branch repair/attention-cap-2026-10-05)
rows.question: With the cap at 3 set in place on checkpoint 481,800, how large is the gradient every lesson of one trainer model step (the live step's lessons and the replay lesson) gives the query and key in-projection of each covered attention module, and how far would the run's 4,500 AdamW steps, from the checkpoint's own optimizer state, move the motor encoder's 3 attention modules against the cross-modal attention's 4? With and without the cap.
rows.why: Under the cap's final check (branch review/attention-cap-final-2026-10-06, commit ad725c544, its record's section 8, finding F4): the learning-signal row (attention_cap_learning_signal_481800) read the replay lesson alone, which would move the motor encoder's 3 attention modules 9, 16 and 23 in 1,000 of full AdamW steps over the run, because the square root of their saved running average of the squared gradient is 163 to 406 times that lesson's gradient; the lesson that built that average was not read. The operator's condition (the answers received between 1:38 AM PDT (the coordinator's reply before them) and 1:48 AM PDT (the clock after), Oct 6, 2026): "confirm that the learning signal needed to train the capped components exists ... If either is missing, that blocks this experiment."
rows.gof_link: The motor encoder's attention is where holding 3 modules removed 14 of 15 parts of the search's change on 481,800; if the cap arm's training cannot move those modules, the experiment reads the untrained cap's effect there, not a trained one.
inputs: Checkpoint 481,800 of run H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41o_1431, built by the probe harness (gof_probe_harness.load_frozen, the trainer's builder from the run's args.json, the processor) and its optimizer state loaded from the checkpoint; its episode companion (the 8 bodies' saved worlds, model state and replay ring), read only.
The live step: per body a harness session of the saved episode with the camera off (no graphics card): vision's own lessons are absent from the live step and present in the replay lesson.
The replay lesson: LemLite.replay_update on the companion's ring, 8 draws of 24 windows.
steps: Run docs/gain_of_function_v4/attention_cap/live_signal.py --out D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/attention_cap/live_signal --bodies 8 --replay-draws 8 --threads 8 through production's test runner (test_runner run attention_cap_live_signal_481800 --threads 8 --device cpu), behind the memory guard.

The job replaces the optimizer's step by nothing, records every term each step adds to its loss with its graph (LemLite.lesson_probe, LossManager.term_probe) and reads each term's and the whole loss's gradient on the covered modules' query and key rows; each body's live step runs twice from one snapshot of the world and the model's execution state (the cap at 3 set in place; without it); the replay draws run with and without the cap on the same windows; at every update it reads the total length before the clip of the parameters the trainer clips together (LemLite._clip_training_gradients wrapped on its class, the job's own length checked against the trainer's); then the movement and result.json (version 2 of live_signal.py).
measures: Per covered module and arm (cap, off): the live batch gradient's length (the mean over the 8 bodies of their signed whole-loss gradients), each body's length (median), each term's length (median over the bodies), the replay gradient's root mean square length over the draws.

Per covered module and arm: AdamW's movement of the query and key rows over the run's 4,500 optimizer steps (3,000 live, 1,500 replay, in the sequence the trainer runs them) from the checkpoint's own exp_avg_sq, from the gradients as the trainer clips them (the live batch's gradient multiplied by min(1, 1.0 / (L + 1e-6)), L the clipped group's length before the clip of the mean over the 8 bodies of their whole gradients; each replay draw's by the same factor of its own length), as a share of full steps (|m| / (sqrt(v) + eps), its median over the numbers, averaged over the steps), with its value at steps 1, 100, 1,000 and 4,500 and the live and replay gradients' size against sqrt(v) at the switch; an upper bound (the gradient's sign taken as the same at every step). Beside: the same movement without the clip (the first reading's).

The clip's lengths: each body's and the batch's before the clip for the live step, each draw's for the replay lesson, the factors applied, and production's own (avg_grad_norm of the run's last 12 training records up to model step 481,800, each a mean over its window of model steps), beside.
rows.target_metric: Per motor encoder attention module with the cap, the run's AdamW movement as a share of full steps (0 = no movement, 1,000 in 1,000 = a full step at every optimizer step).
rows.baseline: The same modules without the cap on the same states and windows; the cross-modal attention's movement under the cap; the replay lesson alone (row attention_cap_learning_signal_481800): the motor encoder's 3 modules 9, 16 and 23 in 1,000, the cross-modal attention 847 to 1,111.
rows.statistical_line: The live gradient from 8 bodies' one step each and the replay gradient from 8 draws; the line reads an upper bound of the movement, so a reading under it is under it for any gradient signs. A reading row with one deciding line.
rows.pass_line: PASS when, with the cap at 3 set in place, each of the motor encoder's 3 attention modules (its 2 attention layers and its pool) moves over the run at least 500 in 1,000 of full AdamW steps (half a step on average) by the upper bound, from the gradients as the trainer clips them; FAIL when one moves less: the learning signal for that module is missing from the run, which blocks the experiment unless the operator names it an exception. INVALID: fewer than 8 bodies stepped, a replay draw without windows, a parameter changed by the optimizer state's load, or a clipped group's length read by the job differing from the trainer's own by more than 1 in 10,000 of it. Beside, deciding nothing: the cross-modal attention's movement, each module's movement without the cap, every term's gradient per module, the live and the replay parts, the movement without the clip.
rows.pass_line_basis: Written under the cap's final check (branch review/attention-cap-final-2026-10-06, commit ad725c544, its record's section 8, finding F4), before any reading. HALF A STEP: the learning-signal row called a gradient usable when AdamW, its running average adapted to the gradient, gives it at least half a step; the saved running averages of the motor encoder's attention do not adapt within the run (0.999 to the power 4,500 is 11 in 1,000 of itself), so the line reads the movement from the checkpoint's own state over the run's own steps. THE LIVE STEP: the trainer's own LemLite.step on the saved episode's states, one body at a time as the proprioception token measurement's live grade does, its lessons' mean over the 8 bodies standing for the trainer's batch of 8; VICReg in a one-body step is the temporal form, not the batch's. THE BOUND: m from 0 and a constant gradient size with one sign at every step: no sign change can make a module move more. THE CLIP (version 2, written before its re-run): the first reading (3:59 to 4:25 AM PDT, Oct 6) took every gradient before the trainer's clip. The trainer multiplies each update's gradient by min(1, 1.0 / (L + 1e-6)), L the total length of the parameters it clips together (LemLite._clip_training_gradients in lem_model.py; grad_clip 1.0 in lem/config/defaults.py), before AdamW sees it; that reading's live steps had L of 6.4 to 24.3 per body, and production's training records up to 481,800 an average L of 94 to 529, so its movement lay above what the run would give. With one factor for every update the clip can only lower the movement (|m| / sqrt(v) grows with the gradient's size while v starts from the saved state); the live and the replay factors differ, so the re-run reads the movement itself.

rows.decision: The learning signal of the motor encoder's attention is not usable in the run by the row's line (FAIL, version 2 run 5:07 AM to 5:34 AM PDT, the trainer's clip applied): with the cap at 3 set in place on 481,800, the trainer's live step (every lesson, the 8 bodies one at a time, the camera off) and its replay lesson (8 draws), each update's gradient clipped as the trainer clips it, would move the motor encoder's layer 0, layer 1 and pool over the run's 4,500 AdamW steps 11, 19 and 104 in 1,000 of full steps (an upper bound; the line 500), against 17, 10 and 0.4 without the cap; the cross-modal attention 819 to 1,019 (597 to 870 without). The clip: the live batch's total length before it 7.2 with the cap (factor 138 in 1,000) and 6.6 without, the replay draws' 2.40 to 4.06; the job's length equal to the trainer's at every update (0 mismatches). The first reading (3:59 to 4:25 AM PDT), taken before the clip, read 70, 122 and 493 for the motor modules and 1,048 to 1,073 for the cross-modal attention. The lessons giving the motor modules the most gradient: tenure, VICReg (in a one-body step its temporal form), efference_gaze, imagination. By the operator's condition this blocks the experiment for those modules unless the operator names an exception. Beside: production's own live model steps averaged a length before the clip of 85 to 710 in its last 12 training records up to 481,800, against this probe's 7.2 with the camera off; the camera's lessons, absent here, are part of production's length, and their gradient on these modules is unmeasured. Record ATTENTION_CAP_2026-10-05.md, section 6.6. OPERATOR EXCEPTION (the operator's decisions received between 6:35 AM PDT (the coordinator's status before them) and 6:47 AM PDT (the clock after), Oct 6, 2026, binding): "Exception for the small attention updates, for this bounded experiment only. Preserve optimizer state. Do not claim the experiment proves those modules can relearn their mappings. Missing learning paths needed elsewhere in the experiment, or invalid outcome measurements, still block it." THE FAILURE IT COVERS: this row's FAIL for the motor encoder's 3 attention modules (layer 0, layer 1, pool): 11, 19 and 104 in 1,000 of full AdamW steps over the run with the cap and the trainer's clip, an upper bound (one gradient sign at every step), the camera's lessons absent from the live step (their gradient on these modules unmeasured). THE LINE OF 500 HAD NO FUNCTIONAL EVIDENCE: it was written as half a full AdamW step on average, the size the learning-signal row calls usable; no measurement related a module's movement over the run to a change in its mapping or to any outcome line. WHAT THE EXPERIMENT THEN TESTS: a cap that stays mostly fixed in the motor encoder (its 3 attention modules moving at most 104 in 1,000 of full steps by the bound) while the downstream layers train: the cross-modal attention moves 819 to 1,019 in 1,000 by the same bound with the cap; the other trained parameters are trained as in production, their movement not read by this row. The optimizer state is preserved: every arm resumes the checkpoint's own AdamW state, no reset. NOT CLAIMED: that the motor encoder's attention modules can relearn their mappings under the cap. STILL BLOCKING: a learning path the experiment needs elsewhere found missing, or an outcome measurement found invalid.

rows.title: Bodily wellness differences in the wellness predictor's input tokens
rows.question: On the 64 saved decisions of row investigate_wellness_goal_attainment_481800 (checkpoint 481,800), do the raw tokens of vision, tactile, audio and proprioception at the hold's last model step (4 of the 5 tokens the wellness predictor reads) carry the differences in realised bodily wellness (the mean of the grounded terms tactile_comfort, capability and motor_state at that model step) between the 11 candidate commands of one decision, so that a linear readout trained on the other 7 bodies ranks them better than chance?
rows.why: Row investigate_prospective_present_motor_g1_481800 measured the wellness predictor ranking one decision's candidates at chance even on the actual outcome tokens (50.0 of 100 pairs, interval 44.2 to 55.9). The repair the record WELLNESS_GOAL_ATTAINMENT_2026-10-06.md names (grading the predictor on the change of the bodily terms) can work only if its input tokens carry those differences (training preflight gate 1, information flow). If they do not, the repair must act on the predictor's input, and a changed lesson would train against differences its input does not hold. The measurement needs no training and no model, only the saved tokens (the style guide: measure before you demand).
rows.gof_link: A prospective wellness term can raise realised wellness only if its input carries the differences between commands that it has to rank.
inputs: Row investigate_wellness_goal_attainment_481800's rows file D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/wellness_attain_runs/goal_attainment_481800/rows.jsonl: per decision and candidate the grounded terms tactile_comfort, capability and motor_state at the hold's last model step, and the wellness predictor's 5 outputs on the actual raw tokens of that model step with the live motor token.

Its token files D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/wellness_attain_runs/goal_attainment_481800/worker_0 and worker_1/tokens_<body>_<k>.npz: per candidate the raw tokens (encoder outputs before the top-down gate) of vision, tactile, audio, proprioception and vestibular at the hold's last model step, 192 numbers each. The motor token of that model step was not saved, so the readout reads 4 of the predictor's 5 tokens.
mimo_bridge/tools/command_ranking.py ranking: pairs in 100 ranked as reality ranks them, with a 95% interval from resampling whole bodies.
steps: Run token_information.py on those files through test_runner run: the processor only, one process, arithmetic on saved values; no model is built or loaded, nothing is executed.

Per decision: the 768 token numbers (vision, tactile, audio, proprioception) and the realised bodily mean of its 11 candidates, each minus its mean over the 11 (what is left is the difference between one state's commands).

Readout: ridge regression without intercept on the centred items, each token number divided by its standard deviation over the training items, penalty LAMBDA x (number of training items) with LAMBDA one of 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 100 and 1000, picked by the smallest squared error when each training body in turn is left out; trained on 7 bodies and applied to the 8th, each body held out once.
Pairs in 100 of the held-out readouts against the realised values (command_ranking.ranking with its tie rule) and the held-out R2.

Control: the same pipeline 100 times with the realised values shuffled among each decision's candidates (seed 20261006): its mean, its 95th percentile, and the share of its body intervals that exclude 50.

Reference: the wellness predictor's own bodily mean on the same raw tokens with the live motor token, against the same values. Additional readings: the readout for each bodily term alone, with vestibular added, the tactile token alone for tactile_comfort and the proprioception token alone for motor_state.
measures: Readout: of all pairs of one decision's candidates, how many in 100 the held-out readout ranks as the realised bodily mean ranks them (a pair whose realised values differ by no more than 1 in 100 of that decision's spread is left out): 50 = chance (the tokens carry none of the differences a linear readout finds), 100 = every pair.
Held-out R2: 1 - (squared error of the held-out readouts) / (squared size of the centred realised values): 0 = none of the differences, 1 = all of them, below 0 = worse than predicting no difference.
Control: the same count with the link between tokens and outcomes removed by shuffling; its mean must lie near 50 and its 95th percentile is the permutation line.
Reference: the same count for the wellness predictor itself on the same tokens.
rows.target_metric: Pairs in 100 of one decision's 11 candidates that the ridge readout of the four raw tokens, trained on the other 7 bodies, ranks as the realised bodily mean at the hold's last model step ranks them; 50 = chance, 100 = every pair.
rows.baseline: The wellness predictor itself on the actual raw tokens of the hold ranks 50.0 of 100 pairs of the five production candidates (interval 44.2 to 55.9) and 51.3 of all 11 (47.3 to 55.1), averaged over the hold (row investigate_prospective_present_motor_g1_481800). No readout of the tokens has been measured.
rows.statistical_line: Both: (a) the 95% interval from resampling whole bodies (8 bodies, 5,000 draws) has its lower end above 50; (b) the readout lies above the 95th percentile of its 100 shuffled controls (a permutation test at 5 in 100). Condition (b) is there because the body interval alone is too narrow on these data: with goal progress shuffled 200 times in the attainment row's readings, 10.5 to 18.5 in 100 body intervals excluded 0 against 5 for a correct interval (analysis_extra.json, shuffle_calibration); on 20 synthetic sets of this shape with no relation, the body interval's lower end lay above 50 in 3 and both conditions held in 2 (token_information.py --selftest, development run of Oct 6, 2026).
rows.material_gof_line: 80 to 90 of 100 pairs is a ranking a search can use (mimo_bridge/tools/command_ranking.py RULES); that line belongs to the trained predictor (line 1 of the repair, G1). Here any reading above chance shows the differences are present in the input for a lesson to use.
rows.pass_line: PASS: the readout's pairs in 100 (four tokens, bodily mean) has the lower end of its 95% body interval above 50 and lies above the 95th percentile of its 100 shuffled controls. FAIL: either condition is not met. INVALID: fewer than 48 decisions or 6 bodies, or the shuffled controls' mean outside 45 to 55. The reference, the held-out R2, the per-term and per-token readings and the controls' interval share are reported whatever the verdict.
rows.pass_line_basis: 50 is what a readout of tokens that carry none of the differences scores; the shuffled controls measure the pipeline's own spread around 50 on these data. Reachability: about 3,500 judged pairs (64 decisions x 55); on synthetic data of this shape the shuffled controls' 95th percentile lay between 52.4 and 53.7, and a target linear in 40 of the features plus noise of equal size read 64.4 (62.3 to 66.9), so a readout that ranks 55 of 100 pairs or better can meet the line and one at 50 cannot.

cost.where: the processor only, one process; arithmetic on the saved rows and token files of the attainment row. Time limit: the self-test's 21 synthetic sets of the same shape, each with its 100 shuffled controls, ran from 5:33 to 5:46 AM PDT in one development run (its development-run log and selftest.json); this job runs one such set plus 6 further readouts

rows.on_pass: The four tokens carry the bodily differences between one state's commands while the predictor ranks the same tokens at chance: the failing part is the predictor's mapping, and the repair the record names (grading the predictor on the change of the bodily terms, behind a new switch value with today's lesson the default) keeps this reading as its information-flow evidence (preflight gate 1). Not built before PLANNER_SEARCH_REPAIR reaches VERIFIED.
rows.on_fail: The four tokens do not carry the differences in a form a linear readout trained across bodies ranks above chance: a lesson change on these inputs is not supported as the smallest repair. The record names the input side from the per-term and per-token readings (which term's differences are missing; whether the tactile token or the proprioception token alone carries its term) and states that the motor token, not saved, is untested. No production switch. Owner: this investigation (branch investigate/wellness-goal-attainment-2026-10-06).

rows.title: ATTENTION_CAP experiment, the focused verdict: does the cap improve stability while preserving useful prediction? SUPPORTED, NOT SUPPORTED or NOT SHOWN, with the unresolved items listed
rows.owner: the attention cap builder until the repair run; then the coordinator
rows.question: From the four qualification rows' results on L, C1 and C2 (each line on L against C1, the same line on C2 against C1, and the attribution), does the cap improve stability (requirement 4's lines (1a) and (1b)) while preserving useful prediction (requirement 2's 11 no-loss lines and requirement 3's 2), and which safety questions stay unresolved?
rows.why: Under the operator's decisions received between 6:35 AM PDT (the coordinator's status before them) and 6:47 AM PDT (the clock after), Oct 6, 2026 (binding): the experiment answers "does the cap improve stability while preserving useful prediction"; it is not full qualification, planner qualification or gain of function. "'No loss detected' and 'loss ruled out' are different. Unresolved safety evidence must remain explicit"; inconclusive regression checks do not authorize deployment; the cap "should not be presented as the established repair for the missing handle-to-consequence mapping". The verdict is computed from the rows' result files by experiment_verdict.py, never typed by hand.
rows.gof_link: A planned command whose physical outcome stays put under rounding-sized input changes (requirement 4) is what the cap is tested for; predictions that still depend on the specific command (requirements 2 and 3) are what the planner steers by. Gain of function itself is not read here.
inputs: The four qualification rows' result files in D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/attention_cap/qual/: result_planner.json (row attention_cap_qual_planner_stability), result_swap.json (row attention_cap_qual_command_specific), result_handle_direction.json and result_switching.json (rows attention_cap_qual_handle_direction and attention_cap_qual_switching), each holding its lines on L against C1, the same lines on C2 against C1 and the attribution; read only.
steps: Run docs/gain_of_function_v4/attention_cap/experiment_verdict.py --out D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/attention_cap/qual/result_experiment.json through production's test runner (test_runner run attention_cap_experiment_verdict) after the four rows have run; arithmetic on the result files, nothing is run.
The job applies the rule of this row's pass_line to the deciding lines' words and writes the verdict, the lines that make it, the unresolved items and the readings beside.
measures: Per deciding line: its word on L against C1, the same line's word on C2 against C1, and whether it is attributable to the cap (the two differ; for line (1a): neither control reads L's word).

The verdict word, the lines that make it NOT SUPPORTED, the unresolved items, the invalid readings, and beside: requirement 1's and requirement 5's words and requirement 3's improvement lines with their attribution.

The preservation part's own word (PASS, NOT SHOWN or FAIL on n of the 13 no-loss lines; "not read (the verdict is INVALID)" beside an INVALID verdict with no preservation line read), the no-loss lines reading PASS listed apart, the arms each result file names and their model step, and each arm's heaviest-body share for line (1a), beside.
rows.target_metric: The focused verdict: SUPPORTED, NOT SUPPORTED or NOT SHOWN (INVALID when a deciding reading is missing or invalid), with the unresolved items listed.
rows.baseline: No arm of its own: the rows' lines compare L with C1, and C2 against C1 is the repeatability check (two control runs, not a measure of the variation across training runs).
rows.statistical_line: No new statistic: each deciding line's word comes from its row's interval and margin; the attribution compares two words; the rule's rates follow from the rows' stated rates (bounds only, the lines not being independent).
rows.pass_line: THE RULE (the operator's decisions received between 6:35 AM PDT (the coordinator's status before them) and 6:47 AM PDT (the clock after), Oct 6, 2026). DECIDING LINES: stability, requirement 4's (1a) (Q on L against the operator's outcome line of 39 in 10,000 of P's unit) and (1b) (L against C1); useful prediction preserved, requirement 2's 11 no-loss lines and requirement 3's two (the count and the pooled own-minus-swapped score), each on L against C1. INVALID: a result file absent or unreadable or a plumbing pass, a deciding row's measurement invalid, a deciding line or its C2 reading missing, None or INVALID ((1a) on L, on C1 and on C2; (1b) and C2 against C1; each of the 13 no-loss lines on L against C1 and C2 against C1, requirement 2's 11 named from qual_margins.json), the result files naming different arms, or an arm at another model step than 484,675 (the cap decisions check (branch review/attention-cap-decisions-2026-10-06, commit 792985287, record CAP_DECISIONS_CHECK_2026-10-06.md, read entire) and the coordinator's decisions relayed after it, findings F1 and F3). NOT SUPPORTED: (1a) reads FAIL; or (1b) reads FAIL and C2 against C1 does not read FAIL on (1b); or a no-loss line reads FAIL and C2 against C1 does not read FAIL on it (a loss attributable to the cap). SUPPORTED: (1a) and (1b) read PASS, C2 against C1 reads NOT SHOWN on (1b) (neither PASS nor FAIL: the coordinator's decision after the check's F4; a C2-against-C1 PASS or FAIL on (1b) makes the verdict NOT SHOWN, listed as unresolved), and no no-loss line reads FAIL attributable to the cap. Its statement on prediction is "no attributable loss detected; loss not ruled out on the lines listed", with the preservation part's own word beside it (NOT SHOWN on n of 13 lines, PASS on 13 of 13, or FAIL on n of 13). NOT SHOWN: every other case. UNRESOLVED, listed with every verdict: each no-loss line reading NOT SHOWN (no loss detected, loss not ruled out); each no-loss line whose FAIL C2 against C1 repeats; (1a) where C2 reads L's word (not attributable); (1a) or (1b) NOT SHOWN; the controls disagreeing (C2 against C1 PASS or FAIL on (1b), FAIL on a no-loss line); each beside reading that is INVALID (requirement 1, requirement 5, requirement 3's improvement lines); (1a) reading PASS on L: "(1a) PASS bounds only decisions like those read; rarer jumps are not bounded", with the number of decisions (1a) read on L (the re-check of Oct 6, 2026, commit 9fdcaa776, item 4, and the coordinator's decision after it); and the standing items (finding F6): the operator's exception (the motor encoder's 3 attention modules move 11, 19 and 104 in 1,000 of full AdamW steps over the run by an upper bound, row attention_cap_live_signal_481800; the experiment tests a mostly fixed cap there while the downstream layers train, and does not show those modules can relearn their mappings), full qualification, planner qualification and gain of function not read, and two control runs not establishing the variation across training runs. The no-loss lines that read PASS are listed apart (preservation_pass), not among the unresolved items (finding F9). Beside an INVALID verdict with no preservation line read, the preservation part's word reads "not read (the verdict is INVALID)", never "PASS on 0 of 0 lines" (the re-check of Oct 6, 2026, commit 9fdcaa776, its LATER item). Line (1a) is read on these 8 worlds; worlds outside them are not sampled (a standing item). DEPLOYMENT: no verdict of this row authorizes it; SUPPORTED answers the focused question only, and with an unresolved item the safety question stays open. BESIDE, deciding nothing: requirement 1's prediction jumps, requirement 5's goal progress (planner qualification), requirement 3's improvement lines (the cap is not presented as the repair for the handle-to-consequence mapping). The registry records SUPPORTED as pass, NOT SUPPORTED as fail, and NOT SHOWN and INVALID as invalid with the word beside, so neither can be read as PASS.
rows.pass_line_basis: Written under the operator's decisions received between 6:35 AM PDT (the coordinator's status before them) and 6:47 AM PDT (the clock after), Oct 6, 2026, before any qualification reading. RATES, from the rows' stated rates (no new simulation; the lines are not independent, so only bounds are stated): SUPPORTED needs (1b) to read PASS, which it does in 10 or 22 of 1,000 runs with no difference (both arms as 481,800 without the cap, or both as with the cap set in place) and in 509 of 1,000 for a difference as large as the cap's untrained start (q_rates.py, row attention_cap_qual_planner_stability); so a false SUPPORTED is at most 22 in 1,000, and SUPPORTED reads in at most 509 of 1,000 runs if the cap keeps that start's gain. (1a) on 481,800 with the cap set in place: Q 10 in 10,000 of P's unit (interval 3 to 14) against 39 (row attention_cap_reachability_481800). With no change requirement 2 reads NOT SHOWN in about 999 of 1,000 runs and requirement 3's row in 935 of 1,000 (q3_rates.py), so at the present sizes a verdict almost always lists no-loss lines as unresolved: no loss detected, loss not ruled out. An attributable loss: with no change some requirement 2 line reads FAIL in 0.7 of 1,000 runs, requirement 3's lines in 0 of 1,000; a complete loss of R's size-matched improvement reads FAIL on a part (a) line of requirement 2 in 77 to 1,000 of 1,000 runs (by line), a rise of 100 in 1,000 in a part (b) error ratio in 2 to 1,000 (by sense), and every score lost reads FAIL on requirement 3's pooled line in 22.5 (R's level, 41 in 1,000, lies inside its margin of 43). THE ARMS: two control runs give one run-to-run difference, not the variation across training runs; the 256 decisions or 48 states of one checkpoint are not independent training replications. INTERVAL CHECK (the coordinator's instruction after the wellness investigation, commit 4fa5bbd04: intervals from resampling 8 bodies excluded the null in 10.5 to 18.5 of 100 there): every deciding line's simulated false-pass rate at the rows' own sizes is under 50 in 1,000 after one replacement: (1a)'s t interval read PASS at the line in 351.3 and 97.0 of 1,000 under the two measured shapes of body means and was replaced by the multiplier 8 (41.3 and 6.8); (1b) 10 or 22 with no difference; requirement 2's lines 19.25 to 27.25 at their named losses; requirement 3's pooled line 27.8 and count line 7.5 at their margins (interval_rates.py, q_rates.py, q3_rates.py). So a false SUPPORTED is at most 22 in 1,000 (bounded by (1b)'s), and a false NOT SUPPORTED through a no-loss line needs a FAIL with no change (some requirement 2 line 2.4 in 1,000, requirement 3's pooled line 0.4, its count line 0) that C2 against C1 does not repeat. AMENDED after the cap decisions check (branch review/attention-cap-decisions-2026-10-06, commit 792985287, record CAP_DECISIONS_CHECK_2026-10-06.md, read entire) and the coordinator's decisions relayed after it. steps: Run through test_runner run with resource class BESIDE_TRAINING on the processor, behind commit_guard --need-gb 3: the script docs/gain_of_function_v4/coordinator/eight_body_passes_2026-10-06/signflip_reread.py reads the inputs above; it loads no model and steps no world.
Per pass, form the per-body paired difference d_b of the quantity the deciding line used (the same arms, senses, horizon and pooling inside a body as the original script).

Route check: recompute the recorded mean and interval from these values with the original script's draws and generator seed; a difference beyond the recorded decimals marks that pass INVALID and ends its reading.

With n bodies, the measured mean m of the n values d_b; for each of the 2^n patterns s of +1 and -1 the mean of s_b x d_b; the count of patterns whose mean lies at least as far from 0 as m (absolute values; ties within 1e-12 counted). For the no-regression claim the values are d_b minus the line and the count is one-sided: the claim is that the change stays under the line, so the count is of the patterns whose mean lies at or under the measured one.
Beside it, deciding nothing: over the 2^n sign-flipped sets, how many the original interval excludes 0 for (its false-pass rate at this size).
Write D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/eight_body_passes/result.json: per pass n, the d_b values, m, the count, 2^n, the line, the route check, the verdict word and the beside reading.
measures: Per pass, the count of sign patterns, of 2^n, whose mean lies at least as far from 0 as the measured one: 2 = the strongest evidence the test can give (the measured pattern and its mirror image), 2^n = none.
The line floor(0.05 x 2^n): 12 of 256 for 8 bodies; with 5 or fewer bodies the smallest count, 2 of 2^n, lies above 5 in 100.
The measured mean in the deciding line's own units, with the two ends the list states for each pass.
The original interval's exclusion count over the sign-flipped sets (0 to 2^n).
rows.pass_line: Per pass a word: CONFIRMED when n is 6 or more, the per-body values are saved, the route check holds, the list does not read either assumption (independent bodies; per-body differences symmetric about 0 with no effect) as failing or doubtful, and the count is at most floor(0.05 x 2^n); NOT CONFIRMED under the same conditions with the count above that line; NOT TESTABLE when n is 5 or fewer, the values are not saved, or the list reads an assumption as failing or doubtful (the eye prediction's comparison with a fixed floor, entry 2.5), its count still written; INVALID when the route check fails. The row reads PASS when every listed pass has one of these words, whatever the words are; it decides no deployment by itself.
rows.pass_line_basis: The reviewer document's definition ("12 of 256 is the 5-in-100 line") and the condition already declared and used in row planner_hold_arms_481800's decision. The test enumerates every pattern, so with independent bodies and per-body differences symmetric about 0 under no effect its false-pass rate is at most floor(0.05 x 2^n) in 2^n. Reachability: with 8 bodies all on one side the count is 2 of 256, under the line of 12; with 4 bodies the smallest count is 2 of 16, 12.5 in 100, so the HAND_STAGE passes (4 held-out bodies) read NOT TESTABLE before any value is read, and a test of them needs at least 6 bodies the hand-response model was not fitted on (2 of 64 is 3.1 in 100). The interval's excess it replaces: WELLNESS_GOAL_ATTAINMENT_2026-10-06.md section 2.2 (analysis_extra.json, shuffle_calibration).

rows.question: Do the two index fingers' own-minus-swapped readings of row investigate_motor_handle_reach_481800 hold under the exact sign-flip test over their 8 body means? The readings: index_L 0.16 and index_R 0.22, each the cosine of the predicted with the real change of the next proprioception token after a 20-degree turn of that finger's command, minus its mean cosine with the 25 other handles' real changes (0 = no better than another handle's consequence, 2 = its own and opposite to the others), each passed by a 95% interval from resampling the 8 bodies.
rows.why: The finger study (H84 first movement plan v3, section 4) studies both index fingers because they are 2 of the 7 handles whose predicted change points at their own real consequence. Register entry EIGHT_BODY_INTERVALS_FALSE_PASS measured that intervals from resampling 8 bodies excluded the null in 105 to 230 of 1,000 shuffles, against 50 for a correct interval, so the plan and its re-check (the first review's finding 5) require this exact re-read before the study cites 0.16 and 0.22. CONFIRMED keeps the index fingers among the handles whose prediction carries their own consequence; NOT CONFIRMED adds them to the 19 handles of PREDICTION_HANDLE_DIRECTION_LOST, and the study's question 3 then reads the main predictor's finger prediction as not shown to point at its own consequence.
rows.gof_link: Action causality: the planner can use a finger's predicted consequence only where the prediction points at that finger's own real consequence; this re-read decides whether the two index fingers are such handles at checkpoint 481,800.

rows.owner: finger study worker A (branch study/index-finger-2026-10-07)
rows.question: On checkpoint 481,800, at latched commands of the model's own behaviour in its 8 saved worlds, does raising (bend) or lowering (straighten) the raw goals of one index finger's knuckle, middle and distal joints by 15 degrees, carried through production's execution path (the joint limits and coupling tendons, the smoothing of 0.35 new and 0.65 previous, the 250 ms hold and the joint servo every 10 ms), move that index fingertip in its wrist's frame against the unchanged command run from the identical saved state; for the left index finger (the main record) and the right?
rows.why: The first link of the finger chain (plan v3 section 4, question 1): if a changed finger command does not move the fingertip, no prediction or planner reading of the finger can show use, and the break lies between command and joint. rows.title: Index finger: does proprioception's token carry the movement?
rows.owner: finger study worker A (branch study/index-finger-2026-10-07)
rows.question: Does the change of the raw proprioception token between question 1's arms (each arm minus unchanged, after the 250 ms hold) carry the index fingertip's change in its wrist's frame: does a ridge read-out, fitted on the replay ring's lived 250 ms changes of the 8 bodies and then frozen, read question 1's fingertip changes with R squared at least 0.25 while the body-shuffled control reads under 0.05?
rows.why: The second link of the finger chain (plan v3 section 4, question 2): the planner's goal distance and the main predictor's lessons are computed on tokens, so a fingertip movement the proprioception token does not carry cannot be predicted from it or steered toward a goal through it. PASS opens question 3 (worker B: is the movement predicted); FAIL marks the token box FAIL (the token loses the movement). It serves PLANNER_NO_REAL_GAIN through the same chain as question 1.
rows.gof_link: Sensing: a finger ability is learnable from the token only when the token carries the finger's change.
inputs: Question 1's folder D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/finger_study/q1_481800: ring_proprioception.npz (checkpoint 481,800's replay ring: per body and model step, up to 6,000 per body, the raw proprioception token, 192 numbers in float16 as stored, and the achieved pose of the 26 handles in float16, world position / 200 and x y z w; the proprioception validity flag, the episode number and the ring's write pointer), rows.jsonl and arms_<body>_<start>.npz (per arm the raw proprioception token after the hold, float32, and both index fingertips in their wrists' frames, cm), result.json (question 1's summary).
Saved files only: no checkpoint, model or world.
steps: Run docs/gain_of_function_v4/finger_study/q2_token_readout.py --q1 D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/finger_study/q1_481800 --out D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/finger_study/q2_481800 through production's test runner, after question 1's row reads its verdict.

Lived changes: per body, the ring in time sequence; every pair of model steps t and t + 5 (one hold) inside one episode with proprioception real at both: x = token(t + 5) - token(t), 192 numbers; y = the index fingertip's position in its wrist's frame at t + 5 minus at t, 3 numbers in cm; for each side.

The float16 floor: the ring's mean square change of x against twice the variance one float16 rounding adds per number ((grid step)^2 / 12 at each stored number); readable when the change is at least 10 times the floor.

The lived read-out's own check (the vestibular rows' rule): ridge with strength 1e-3 x the mean diagonal of x^T x and no intercept, fitted on the even-numbered bodies and scored on the odd ones, and the other way round; R squared.

The read-out: the same ridge fitted on every body's lived pairs, then frozen. The control: the same fit with every body's x paired with another body's y at the same index, for each of the 7 cyclic shifts of the 8 bodies; the control's reading is the mean of the 7 R squared values.

Applied to question 1: per clean start and per arm (L_bend, L_straighten, R_bend, R_straighten), x = the token difference arm - unchanged and y = that side's fingertip difference arm - unchanged; a side's read-out is scored on all four arms (the other side's arms test that a change of the other finger is not read as this one's).
Per side, the words by the pass line; the row's verdict is the left side's.
measures: R squared = 1 - (sum of squared errors) / (sum of squared fingertip differences): 1 = every fingertip difference predicted exactly from the token difference, 0 = no better than predicting no difference, below 0 = worse; per side pooled over the clean starts, per body beside.
The control's R squared (the mean over the 7 shifts and each shift's), the lived cross-body R squared, and the ring's change over its float16 floor (1 = at the floor).
rows.target_metric: R squared of the frozen read-out on question 1's left index fingertip differences.
rows.baseline: Row vestibular_token_stage_readouts used this read-out (ridge, fitted on some bodies and scored on the others) for head tilt (line 0.25; its control read -0.008 on the encoder's input). For proprioception and the fingertip no read-out has been run. Row investigate_motor_handle_reach_481800: a 20-degree turn of the index command changed the real proprioception token after one model step by 2 in 10,000 of its length (index_L 0.00020, index_R 0.00018), against a repeat floor of 0 (identical repeats).
rows.statistical_line: R squared pooled over the clean starts at least 0.25, with the mean of the 7 body-shuffled controls under 0.05; the per-body R squared values beside.
rows.material_gof_line: Not defined: how much of the fingertip a token must carry for prediction and planning to work is unmeasured; 0.25 is the vestibular rows' acceptance line A4 for a sensed quantity, the plan's choice.
rows.pass_line: Per side: PASS when R squared is at least 0.25 and the control's mean is under 0.05; FAIL when R squared is under 0.25 with the control under 0.05; INVALID when the control reads 0.05 or more, question 1's summary is INVALID or missing, or no fingertip difference can be scored; NOT TESTABLE when question 1 did not pass for that side, the ring's lived change is within 10 times its float16 floor, or fewer than 6 bodies have clean starts. The row's verdict is the left side's.
rows.pass_line_basis: 0.25 is the acceptance line A4 of the vestibular read-out rows (vestibular_token_stage_readouts), the plan's choice for this question; the control under 0.05 is that row's rule 1. The control is the mean over 7 cyclic body shifts because one shift's chance spread, measured on the study's test fixture, was -0.056 to +0.060 with 400 model steps per body and -0.042 to +0.013 with 2,000 (the ring holds up to 6,000). The float16 floor: the ring stores tokens in float16, whose rounding adds per number a variance of (grid step)^2 / 12 (8e-8 at 1.0); the fingertip's lived movement of 0.58 cm per hold has to move the token by more than that, checked as the ring's mean square change at least 10 times twice the floor. Reachability: the token changes with the index finger's command above its repeat floor (the 26-handle row: 2 in 10,000 of the token's length after one model step of a 20-degree command turn, repeats identical); whether a linear read-out reaches 0.25 is what this row measures.

cost.where: the processor, one process, saved files only (no model, no world, no graphics card); it can run beside any other job
cost.basis: The ring extract holds 8 x 6,000 x 192 float16 numbers (18 MB) and the achieved poses; the work is, per side, 10 ridge fits of 192 x 3 (the read-out, 7 controls and the 2 cross-body halves) on up to 48,000 pairs and their scores, each a solve of a 192 x 192 system.

rows.on_pass: The study's diagram box fingertip to token reads PASS for that side; question 3 (worker B) uses this frozen read-out to grade the main predictor's predicted tokens in centimetres.
rows.on_fail: The box reads FAIL: this read-out did not recover the movement from the token. A failed fit of this decoder class does not show that the token lacks the movement (corrected by the operator's additions of Oct 8, 2026 (received 7:53 AM PDT)). The lived cross-body R squared says whether the token carries the fingertip in lived changes at all (the encoder) or only not for question 1's small differences; the coordinator decides the next test; nothing is built here.

rows.title: Index finger goals: planner search against hand stage
rows.owner: finger study worker A (branch study/index-finger-2026-10-07)
rows.question: From identical saved worlds of checkpoint 481,800, given as its goal a pose the same body reached from that start with a recorded command (latent_body_compare.py's recorded_v2 goals for index_L and index_R), does production's planner search followed by the hand stage (chosen) end the index fingertip nearer that goal after the 250 ms hold than the same search with its updates left out and the hand stage after it (start_hand), and how do start_hand and the motor controller's command (reflex) compare on the frozen fit's training bodies 0 to 3 and test bodies 4 to 7? (The goals are whole recorded commands, the plan's design: the index finger is a small part of what the search aims at; a finger-only goal is not built.) Before any comparison each goal is classified as inside or outside the region the search and the hand stage may reach from that start within the 250 ms hold (the search's permitted command range, the reach clamp, the hand stage's 11-degree trust region). The result keeps a prediction or search failure on goals inside that region apart from goals the allowed action range excludes: plan v3 section 4 records that the latent-body comparison's goals lay outside the planners' search region, and a body having reached a pose before does not show that today's planner can reach it from the tested start. The probe does not run before its code makes that separation (added by the operator's additions of Oct 8, 2026 (received 7:53 AM PDT)).
rows.why: Plan v3 section 4, question 5, and section 6's decision on the frozen fit ('no change; question 5 measures whether it limits finger control'). R1 reads whether the search, which steers by the main predictor's predicted tokens, brings the fingertip nearer a reachable goal than the hand stage alone; R2 reads whether the hand stage, which steers by the frozen fit fitted on bodies 0 to 3, brings it nearer than the motor controller's command on the bodies the fit never saw. It serves PLANNER_NO_REAL_GAIN directly: R3 is the planner's command against the motor controller's on a reachable finger goal.
rows.gof_link: Planner: a goal reached by recorded experience must be reachable by the planner's command; a fixed calibration that limits the finger blocks finger control.
inputs: Checkpoint 481,800 of run H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41o_1431, its args.json and its episode companion, read only, built on the processor by the probe harness (as question 1).

The witness bank D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/latent_compare_design/split_h5/witness_bank.pt (latent_body_split --horizon-steps 5, Oct 1, 2026, from the seg41 recording): 7,992 recorded holds of the 8 bodies, each its start pose, its executed command and its pose 5 model steps later; its SHA-256 is written into the declaration and every row.

THE NEW CODE (decision D4), q5_witness_goal.py: production's search (LemLite._plan_chain) run from the saved decision with the witness's end as its goal: the goal tokens are the top-down-gated tokens of the witness's last model step (the form the goal ring stores) and decision['hand_goal'] (the hand stage's finger goal: pose, valid, horizon 250 ms, ring index -1) is the witness's achieved pose there.
Thread settings as question 1 (4, all four environment variables and torch), checked by the job and written into every row.
steps: Run docs/gain_of_function_v4/finger_study/q5_witness_goal.py --out D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/finger_study/q5_481800 --starts-per-body 4 --spacing 10 --witnesses 8 --threads 4 through production's test runner, only while no planner-gate job runs (decision D4; the job reads the process list at its start and refuses while a process names a planner_recovery job script or the attention cap's planner_qual_job.py); before it, a development pass on 1 body and 1 start with --dev (verdict INVALID; plumbing only).

Per body: a Session from the saved episode; live under the model's own behaviour (learning off) to its next planning event with a recorded plan (probe_planner_candidates.next_decision), at least 10 model steps after the previous start; snapshot.
Route check: production's search run again from the captured inputs with production's own goal returns production's chosen command number for number and the same raw hand goal, else the job stops.

Reflex: the motor controller's command through the decision's execution transform, smoother and hand smoothing (probe_planner_candidates.executed_candidate), run for the hold twice (the physical traces must match).

Witness candidates: the 8 recorded holds of the same body nearest in start (WitnessBank.nearest), each recorded command carried to the present pelvis (latent_body_compare.transplant: every handle's position and orientation; radius, strength and the eyes the motor controller's), projected to a feasible hand goal, executed as reflex is and run for the hold twice. Per goal (index_L, index_R, each the index handle in its wrist's frame), the first candidate whose end lies 0.30 cm or more from reflex's end is the goal; a start with none is recorded as not admitted.

Per admitted goal: start_hand = the search with 0 updates toward the witness's tokens and finger pose, then the hand stage (each joint goal within 11 degrees of the search's; 20 Adam updates scored by the frozen fit); chosen = the same with the search's own update count; each executed as reflex and run for the hold twice; the witness run again (its end must repeat, else the goal is not admitted).
Per arm: the goal's index fingertip's distance from the witness's end in its wrist's frame (cm), the world distance, and P on the raw tokens (proprioception plus vision) against the witness's.
summarise (q5_witness_goal.summarise): R1, R2 (with its two 4-body splits) and R3 per goal; the row's verdict is the left goal's R1.
measures: distance: the goal's index fingertip after the hold from the witness's end, in its wrist's frame, cm: 0 = at the goal (the witness reads 0 by construction); reflex reads 0.30 or more (the admission line).

R1 (use): start_hand minus chosen distance per body, cm (above 0 = the search's command ends nearer). R2 (the frozen fit): reflex minus start_hand per body, cm, over 8 bodies and split into bodies 0 to 3 and 4 to 7. R3 (overall): reflex minus chosen per body, cm.

Beside: the world distance (cm); P, per sense the mean over 192 numbers of the squared difference from the witness's raw token, summed over proprioception and vision (0 = the witness's senses); the hand stage's record (selected update, first and selected cost); admitted and not admitted starts with their separations.
rows.target_metric: Left goal: start_hand minus chosen fingertip distance (cm) per body, over the 8 bodies.
rows.baseline: The offline latent body comparison (checkpoint 455,800; plan v3 section 4): on left index goals the latent arm ended 0.31 cm from the goal against 0.62 and 0.59 cm for the two planner searches and 0.55 cm for the motor controller; every goal lay outside the region those searches could reach (physical goals on there). The hand stage moves each joint goal at most 11 degrees from the search's; through the smoothing (0.35) recorded holds predict a fingertip movement of 0.14 cm (median, left) for an 11-degree change of the 3 flexion joints (readings/bend_size.json, size 11), so start_hand can close about half of a 0.30 cm gap along a flexion. The search's joint goals are not bounded in H84's configuration, so chosen can reach the goal's joint configuration; whether the predicted tokens steer it there is what R1 measures. Admission: on recorded rows every start had a recorded neighbour beyond the separation line (latent_body_compare.py, goal_stand_in.py); here every candidate's separation is recorded. The exact test with 8 bodies can show a difference when 7 or 8 body means share its sign; the 4-body splits cannot meet a 5-in-100 line by the exact test and are read descriptively.

rows.title: HEAD_TILT_REPAIR merge: identity with the flag off
rows.question: Does the merge branch merge/head-tilt-repair-2026-10-07 at commit 865ece161, with --vestibular-input-path absent from the launch line, train a small learner bit for bit as production's commit 85d616e9e does: over 120 model steps from a fresh start, and over 40 model steps resumed from a checkpoint production's code saved at model step 30; and again with --motor-asked-change on --heads-all-slot-path on --vestibular-encoder-repair rescale_restart --agency-prior 0.0 --contact-control-wellness 2.0 added to both codes' launch lines (control run 2, the restart's base, launches with all five)? With each value of the flag, does training stay equal to the merge's run without the flag until the path can act: from a fresh start, under on_delayed_encoder_only every model step before the path's weight first reads above 0, and under on model step 0? At the switch on production's checkpoint (model step 30), does the load's check read the vestibular token unchanged for each value; is model step 30 equal to production's in every recorded field under on_delayed_encoder_only; and under on, does model step 30 differ from production's in nothing but the gradient norm and the state hash (what the update did: under on the delayed lesson's gradient into the vestibular encoder is cut from the switch's own model step), if at all?
rows.why: The repair has to be off by default and bit-identical when off: merging it must change nothing in production until the flag is set, and an old command must build the model it always built. The repair's own lockstep (row vestibular_input_path_lockstep) compared 470b6569c with production's 3f7b7e815 of Oct 4; production has changed since (the attention cap's lines in lem_model.py, train_mimo.py and four lem/model files, the watcher's M3 alert), and the merge resolved two files' conflicts by hand. The path's lines sit beside the lines of --motor-asked-change and --heads-all-slot-path in the learner's parameter list, the gradient clip groups and _side_modules (lem_model.py 1823-1831, 5486-5496 and 8020-8025 at 865ece161) and in load_checkpoint; the fixture's flags of Oct 1 build neither of those two paths, and control run 2 (H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41c_1433, args.json: motor_asked_change on, heads_all_slot_path on) runs with both, so the fifth comparison builds them in both codes (the independent check of Oct 8, its FIX line on the learner's flags). The decision that depends on it: whether the coordinator merges the branch into production with the flag off; the PASS is also evidence in the restart's training preflight record on the merged code. The coordinator added control run 2's three other non-default flags to the fifth comparison on Oct 8, 2026 (Oct 8, 2026 2:44 AM PDT; --vestibular-encoder-repair rescale_restart, --agency-prior 0.0, --contact-control-wellness 2.0, read from seg41c_1433's args.json by the lockstep fixer): rescale_restart acts on the vestibular lesson at every model step and at a load, beside the merged vestibular path, and the restart of D3 resumes with it on.
rows.gof_link: Training continuity for gain of function: the merge must leave every learned ability's training unchanged until HEAD_TILT_REPAIR is switched on at the restart.
rows.target_metric: The first model step at which any recorded field differs between production's code and the merge's code with --vestibular-input-path absent (none = every row equal), fresh and resumed, without and with --motor-asked-change on --heads-all-slot-path on --vestibular-encoder-repair rescale_restart --agency-prior 0.0 --contact-control-wellness 2.0.

rows.material_gof_line: Any difference with the flag absent fails, with or without the two neighbouring paths; at the switch, each value's rule of the pass line.

(4) The switch at that load, for each value: the load's switch record says exact at model step 30, the weight's largest absolute value 0.0, bit-identical in float32. rows.pass_line_basis: With the flag absent every statement the merge adds is skipped by a test on the flag's value or on an attribute that is not built (the independent check of Oct 8, 2026, section 2, by reading the code), so equality is what the code says, and the lockstep measures it on both codes, also with the two neighbouring paths built. rows.title: Index finger, link 4: does the proprioception token keep index_L's own movement? (lived data, checkpoint 481,800)
rows.owner: finger link4 worker (branch study/finger-link4-2026-10-08); run by the coordinator
rows.question: On the 8 bodies' lived model steps in checkpoint 481,800's replay ring: does a ridge read-out of the 192-number proprioception token's change over one model step (50 ms), fitted on 4 bodies and scored on the other 4, read index_L's own movement relative to the left hand (its displacement in cm and its turn in degrees, the hand's own turn removed) with a held-out R squared of at least 0.25, while the same read-out of another body's finger reads under 0.05?
rows.why: Link 4 of the joined record (docs/gain_of_function_v4/finger_investigation/JOINED_index_L_2026-10-08.md) is the first link on the learning path with no evidence. The main predictor's prediction of an index_L command's consequence explains -0.43 of the real change at 16 probe states of 481,800 (1 = exact, 0 = no better than predicting no change; row investigate_motor_handle_reach_481800). If the token does not keep the finger's own movement, nothing downstream of it can predict that movement and the repair lies in the input or the proprioception encoder; if it keeps it, link 5's failure lies in prediction or learning (findings F1, F4, F5, F6 of D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/finger_investigation/prediction_learning/REVIEW.md). The decision that depends on it: which side of the token a repair for the index finger's prediction is designed on. The queued row finger_q2_token_carries_fingertip_481800 answers this only after probe q1 restores worlds; this row reads saved data only.
rows.gof_link: Sensing for finger control: a finger ability can be learned through the main predictor only when the proprioception token keeps the finger's own movement; this row decides whether the index finger's failed prediction (link 5) is repaired in the input and encoder or in prediction and learning.

Self-check first: the summing-up runs on 11 built-in inputs (complete, incomplete and mixed: empty, a window missing, values None, text keys, NaN, a block incomplete, a failed data check, not a dict); a verdict other than the one the module text gives for any of them ends the job INVALID before the companion is read.

Read the companion without the model: forward through gzip three times; (A) to the end, keeping the last 64 MB and the SHA-256 of the compressed bytes, which must equal episode_state.json's; the end-of-archive record and the central directory give each record's offset and size; (B) data.pkl (3.4 MB) from the kept tail, unpickled with lazy tensors (storage key, dtype, shape, stride), the worlds left as unread byte records and an empty stand-in for any class outside torch, numpy and the standard library; (C) the ring's tokens, achieved, valid and episode records only. Pairs: per body the ring in time order (oldest slot = write pointer mod 6,000); every pair of model steps (t, t + k) with the same episode number, proprioception real at both, wrist_L and index_L active at both; k = 1 model step (50 ms, the main predictor's horizon) and k = 5 model steps (one hold of 250 ms).

Read-out features: the proprioception token's change token(t + k) - token(t), 192 numbers. Targets (positions = achieved x 200 cm): finger_position = R_w(t) [R_w(t + k)^T (p_i - p_w)(t + k) - R_w(t)^T (p_i - p_w)(t)] (index_L's displacement relative to the hand, written in world axes at t, cm); finger_turn = the rotation vector of q_rel(t + k) q_rel(t)^-1, q_rel = q_w^-1 q_i, written in world axes at t (degrees; the distal joint shows only here); reported beside: the same two in wrist_L's own axes, hand_turn = the rotation vector of q_w(t + k) q_w(t)^-1 (degrees, world axes), and index_L's input-row position change (p_i - p_w)(t + k) - (p_i - p_w)(t) (cm). R_w, q_w: wrist_L's achieved rotation; p_i, p_w: index_L's and wrist_L's achieved world positions.

Ridge read-out y = x W + b: fitted on the even-numbered bodies and scored on the odd-numbered ones, then the other way round. Strength lambda = s x mean(diag(Xc^T Xc)), s from 1e-8 to 10 in factors of 10, chosen per target group by leave-one-body-out inside the 4 fitting bodies only. R squared = 1 - sum of squared errors / sum of squared deviations from the held-out half's own mean, over the group's 3 numbers and both halves; a 95% interval from resampling the 8 held-out bodies (2,000 draws).

Controls: (1) hand_turn read from the token; (2) body-paired: each body's token change paired with the targets of another body of the same half at the same ring slot, shifts 1, 2 and 3, the mean of the 3 R squared values; (3) moving pairs: the share of pairs in which index_L moved 0.1 cm or more relative to the hand, and R squared over those pairs only; (4) input reference: the same read-out from the change of the 182 input numbers the achieved pose reconstructs (26 handles x world orientation and (position - wrist_L's position) / 200 cm); (5) hand-turn leak: the finger targets read from the hand's turn alone.

Noise: (a) float16 noise ceiling: the stored wrist_L and index_L numbers moved 4 times by a uniform error of +-half their float16 grid step, the targets recomputed; ceiling = 1 - (mean square change of the targets) / (their variance around each body's own mean); (b) the token change's mean square over twice the float16 rounding variance of the stored token numbers.

WINDOW, the coordinator's rule: every reading over the whole ring and over the newest 1,000 model steps per body (model steps 480,801 to 481,800), since the ring's tokens were encoded by the encoder weights of their own time, up to 6,000 model steps before 481,800. The whole ring decides, unless for a judged part the two 95% intervals do not overlap; then the newest 1,000 decide and the result's reason says so. Beside it, the same token read-out on each older block of 1,000 model steps (block j = the j-th 1,000 before the newest; fitted and scored on that block only), because the two windows also differ in how many rows the read-out is fitted on (about 24,000 against about 4,000): when the rule hands the verdict to the newest 1,000 while their interval lies inside the older blocks' range, the reason names it.
Write result.json (verdict, reason, hold_verdict, window_used, summary, window_readings, readings in the registry's reading form) and status.json after each window.
measures: R squared of each read-out on the held-out bodies: 1 = index_L's own movement over the interval predicted exactly from the token's change, 0 = no better than the held-out bodies' mean, below 0 = worse; per part (displacement, turn), interval length, window and held-out body, with its 95% body-resampling interval.

The controls' R squared on the same scale: hand_turn from the token (the token's input holds wrist_L's orientation directly; a FAIL needs it at 0.25 or more), the body-paired mean (expected 0: the bodies move independently), the input reference (what the same read-out gets from the input numbers themselves), the hand-turn leak.

The share of pairs with index_L moving 0.1 cm or more relative to the hand (0 = the finger never moved, 1 = it moved in every pair), and the finger's movement per pair in cm (median, 90th percentile, root mean square).

The float16 noise ceiling (1 = the stored numbers' rounding takes nothing from the target, 0 = the rounding is the whole target's variance) and the token change over its float16 floor (1 = the change equals the rounding; 10 or more is readable).

rows.pass_line: Per split, window and interval length, for index_L's row: PASS when min(R squared over all held-out pairs, R squared over the moving pairs) is 0.25 or more. FAIL when it is under 0.25 while, in the same split, the positive control (wrist_R's row) reads 0.25 or more from the token and the input reference reads 0.25 or more, the float16 noise ceiling is 0.5 or more and the token change is 10 or more times its float16 floor. INVALID when the body-paired control reads 0.05 or more, a held-out set has fewer than 200 moving pairs, a body has fewer than 100 pairs, a data check fails, a reading is missing or not finite, or a FAIL condition is unmet (the reasons are listed). The window by version 1's rule, per split. The interval length's verdict: the two splits' verdict when they agree; INVALID with the reason when they disagree. The row's verdict is the one-model-step interval's; the hold's (5 model steps) is written beside it.
rows.pass_line_basis: 0.25 is the acceptance line A4 of the vestibular read-out rows (vestibular_token_stage_readouts) and finger_q2's line; the body-paired control's 0.05 is that row's rule 1. Reachability: both row targets are exact straight-line functions of the encoder's input numbers (3 of them, x 200 cm), so the input reference reads 1.000 by construction (version 1 measured 1.000 for index_L's row on this ring), and the positive control is of the same kind: a token that keeps its input in a form a straight line reads gives both at 0.25 or more, and a FAIL is written only where the positive control shows the read-out can read a row from this token in the same split. The two splits ask two things of one read-out: the cross-body split, that it carries over to bodies it was not fitted on (version 1: hand-relative targets failed there even on the input numbers); the time split, that it carries over to later model steps of the same bodies; a verdict needs both, and a disagreement is reported as INVALID with its reason. The body-paired control reads 0 when nothing shared is read (version 1 on this ring, one model step, whole ring: -0.0002 to -0.0009; version 2's synthetic rings: -0.0002 to -0.00003); all 8 bodies share the ring slot, so shared timing such as the planner's latch every 10 model steps is what it tests. Measurement noise: the 95% interval from resampling the 8 bodies' held-out sums (version 1, index_L's row: -0.033 to 0.131 around 0.055); the float16 noise ceiling of index_L's row read 0.997 in version 1, and a FAIL needs 0.5 or more; the token change read 75,725 times its float16 floor in version 1, and a FAIL needs 10 or more. 200 moving pairs per held-out set is a chosen floor, not a measured one; the moving-pairs reading's own interval is written beside it. Kept from version 1: the moving-pairs reading inside the PASS line (stillness does not carry the fit), the window rule (the ring's tokens were encoded by the weights of their own time; the newest 1,000 model steps decide when their interval and the whole ring's do not overlap) and the one-model-step row verdict (link 5 failed at the main predictor's 50 ms horizon).

rows.title: Index finger, link 4: what linear and nonlinear decoders recover from the proprioception token on lived data (present state, movement, next movement; checkpoint 481,800)
rows.owner: finger link4 worker (branch study/finger-link4-2026-10-08); run by the coordinator
rows.question: On the 8 bodies' lived model steps 475,801 to 481,800 in checkpoint 481,800's replay ring, with training, validation and test blocks of 250 model steps alternating inside each body: how much of the held-out within-block variance does a linear decoder (ridge) and a nonlinear decoder (the ridge plus a network of 2 hidden layers of 128 fitted to its residuals, early stopping) recover, from the proprioception token and, matched, from the input numbers, for three separate questions: (Q-a) index_L's present state at model step t from the token at t; (Q-b) its movement from t to t + 1 from the observed tokens at t and t + 1; (Q-c) that movement from the tokens at t - 1 and t and the executed command from t to t + 1, with no observation after t?
rows.why: The operator's instruction received at 7:37 AM PDT on Oct 8, 2026 allows one bounded nonlinear comparison on the saved data, with what it tests stated first (docs/gain_of_function_v4/finger_investigation/LINK4_NONLINEAR_DESIGN.md, written at 7:43 AM PDT, amended at 8:00 AM PDT before any run on the model's data). Versions 1 and 2 of the straight-line read-out (rows finger_link4_token_readout_lived_481800 and _v2) read INVALID because their declared controls failed; they do not support the statement that the token loses information the input had, and a decoder that fails does not show the information is absent. Within bodies a ridge decoder fitted on the token scored 0.633 on index_L's row position and 0.117 on its change over one model step (version 2's forward split). This row keeps three questions apart: whether a decoder recovers the finger's present state from the token (Q-a), the movement that occurred from the two observed tokens (Q-b), and the next movement from what the predictor reads at t (Q-c), each beside the same decoders on the input numbers. The decision it informs: on link 5 (the main predictor's index_L prediction explains -0.43 of the real change at 16 probe states of 481,800), whether what a predictor needs is recoverable by these decoders from what UEMA's predictor reads at t. The probe states of 481,800, the shared episode near model step 483,800 (control run 1, about 2,000 updates later) and this ring are three separate bodies of evidence from different model states.
