Read the ring and check: 8 bodies, the 26 trunk_v1 handle names with wrist_R present, token width 192, the companion's trainer step 481,800, at least 2,000 slots filled; any failure gives INVALID.

Blocks: each body's ring, oldest model step first, cut into 24 blocks of 250 model steps labelled in turns train, train, validation, test (12, 6, 6 blocks; the newest block, 481,551 to 481,800, is a test block). A row is kept only when every model step it reads lies in one block, 10 or more model steps from its edges, with proprioception real, the same episode, wrist_L, index_L and wrist_R active and, for Q-c, has_executed set.

Targets (12 numbers in 4 groups): index_row = (p_i - p_w), cm, world axes; index_hand_position = R_w^T (p_i - p_w), cm, the left hand's own axes; index_hand_turn = the rotation vector (degrees) of the distal phalanx's orientation relative to the hand, Q-a from q_ref (the mean relative orientation of the training rows), Q-b and Q-c of q_rel(t + 1) q_rel(t)^-1; wrist_R_row = (p_wR - p_w), cm (the positive control). Q-a at t; Q-b and Q-c their change from t to t + 1.
Decoder inputs, token side | input side: Q-a x(t); Q-b [x(t), x(t + 1) - x(t)]; Q-c [x(t), x(t) - x(t - 1), the command numbers at t], and beside it the same without the command.

Decoders, both fitted and scored on within-block deviations (every target and prediction minus its mean in each body's block): LINEAR = ridge on the training rows' within-block deviations, inputs scaled by their within-block spread, strength s x mean(diag(X^T X)), s from 1e-8 to 10 in factors of 10, chosen per target group on the validation rows; NONLINEAR = the linear decoder plus a network (input -> 128 -> GELU -> 128 -> GELU -> 12) fitted to its within-block residuals of the training rows, AdamW (learning rate 0.001, weight decay 0.0001), batches of 256, at most 150 passes, output layer starting at zero, early stopping after 10 passes without a lower validation error, the lowest kept (the start, equal to the linear decoder, included); seed 0. One decoder per question and side, shared by the 8 bodies; both sides read the same rows.

Score: within-block R squared on the test rows (1 - sum of squared errors / sum of squared deviations from each body's test-block mean, over a group's numbers), the 95% interval from resampling the 8 bodies' test sums (2,000 draws), per body, per test block, and for movements over the pairs in which index_L's row moved 0.1 cm or more.

Controls: the matched input-number decoders; wrist_R_row; the body-paired control (each body's token inputs with the next body of its half's targets at the same ring slot, both decoders); the float16 noise ceiling of every target (the stored wrist_L, index_L and wrist_R numbers moved by +-half their float16 grid step, 4 draws) and the token's spread (Q-a) or one-model-step change (Q-b, Q-c) over its float16 rounding variance.
Local refit beside, deciding nothing: the token and input-number decoders on the newest 2,000 model steps (479,801 to 481,800) with blocks of 125 in the same turns.

Reading words per question, finger group and decoder (token side), and the row's verdict, by the pass line; write result.json (verdict, reason, words, summary, window_readings, readings in the registry's form) and status.json after each question.
measures: Within-block R squared of each decoder on the test rows: the share of the held-out within-block variance the decoder recovers (1 = all of it, 0 = none, below 0 = worse than the block means); per question, target group, side (token, input numbers), decoder, body and test block, with its 95% interval.

The controls on the same scale: wrist_R_row from the token; the body-paired control (0 = another body's target recovered no better than its block means); the matched input-number decoders; Q-c without the command.

The share of pairs in which index_L's row moved 0.1 cm or more (0 = never, 1 = every pair); the float16 noise ceiling (1 = the stored numbers' rounding takes nothing from the target, 0 = the rounding is its whole variance); the token's spread or change over its float16 rounding variance (1 = equal; 10 or more is readable).
For the nonlinear decoder: the passes run, the pass kept, and its validation error against the linear decoder's (the start).
rows.target_metric: Within-block R squared of the linear and the nonlinear decoder on the test blocks, token side beside input side, for index_L's present state (Q-a), its movement over one model step from the observed tokens (Q-b) and from the history at t with the command (Q-c).

rows.statistical_line: Per question, finger group and decoder, token side: within-block R squared at least 0.25 (for movements the lower of all pairs and moving pairs) with the body-paired control under 0.05 reads RECOVERED BY THIS DECODER; the 95% interval from resampling the 8 bodies' test sums is written beside each reading, and a reading is statistically clear when that interval lies entirely above or entirely below 0.25.
rows.material_gof_line: not yet defined: how much of the finger's state or movement a decoder must recover from the token for the main predictor to predict an index_L command's consequence is unmeasured; 0.25 is the plan's read-out line (the vestibular rows' acceptance line A4), not a gain-of-function line.
rows.pass_line: A measurement with declared reading words; it judges completeness, not the token. PASS when the measurement is complete: every question read by both decoders on the token and the input numbers, the data checks met, and every body-paired control (both decoders, all 4 target groups, all 3 questions) under 0.05. INVALID otherwise, with the reason. Reading words, token side, per question, finger group and decoder: RECOVERED BY THIS DECODER = the decoder recovers 0.25 or more of the held-out within-block variance (movements: the lower of all pairs and moving pairs), body-paired control under 0.05; NOT RECOVERED BY THIS DECODER = this decoder did not recover it (under 0.25) while the same decoder recovers 0.25 or more of that target from the input numbers and of wrist_R_row from the token, the body-paired control is under 0.05, the float16 noise ceiling is 0.5 or more and the token's spread or change is 10 or more times its float16 rounding; NOT JUDGED = any other case, with the reasons. A word reports what one decoder of a stated class, trained this way, recovered; NOT RECOVERED does not state that the token lacks the quantity.
rows.pass_line_basis: 0.25 is the acceptance line A4 of the vestibular read-out rows and the earlier finger read-outs' line; the body-paired control's 0.05 is the vestibular rows' rule 1. Within-block deviations: with alternating blocks a decoder that recognises when a token was recorded can place any slowly drifting quantity, including another body's (on the synthetic ring, scored against the pooled mean, the body-paired nonlinear control read 0.55 to 0.67 for Q-a; fitted and scored within blocks it read -0.010 at most), so only the variation inside each block of 250 model steps (12.5 s) is read. Alternating blocks also spread the training and test tokens over the same range of encoder weights (the ring's tokens come from the weights of their own model steps, about 6,000 updates); the per-test-block scores and the local refit on the newest 2,000 model steps show whether scores move along the ring. Reachability: the index_row and wrist_R_row targets are exact linear functions of the input numbers, so the input side's linear decoder recovers them up to float16 rounding; the hand-relative targets and the turns are nonlinear functions of the input numbers, which the nonlinear decoder is there to reach; the matched input-number decoder states, per target, what this decoder class recovers when the information is present by construction, and a NOT RECOVERED word needs it at 0.25 or more. The nonlinear decoder starts at the linear decoder and keeps the pass with the lowest validation error, so on the validation rows it is never worse than the linear one (synthetic: a network trained alone read 0.00 on Q-c from the input numbers where ridge read 0.96). Measurement noise: the 95% interval from resampling the 8 bodies' test sums; the float16 noise ceiling of every target; the token's float16 rounding against its spread or change (a NOT RECOVERED word needs 10 or more). The executed command is stored in float16 world cm (0.03 to 0.125 cm per number), the same for both sides of Q-c. One seed of the network; Q-c reads 2 model steps of history against the main predictor's 128.

decision.outcome_read: PASS: the measurement is complete (every question read by both decoders on both sides, every body-paired control under 0.05); PASS does not judge the token
decision.readings: Held-out within-block R squared (1 = all of the variance, 0 = none), token | input numbers, linear / nonlinear decoder. Q-a, present state: index_L's row in world axes relative to the left wrist 0.379 / 0.396 from the token (RECOVERED BY THIS DECODER) against 1.000 from the input numbers; its position in the hand's own axes 0.076 / 0.075 from the token against 0.321 / 0.882 from the input numbers, and its turn relative to the hand 0.109 / 0.111 against 0.290 / 0.928 (NOT RECOVERED BY THIS DECODER). Q-b, the movement that occurred: NOT JUDGED (wrist_R's control 0.192 / 0.236 from the token, under 0.25); the token side read 0.184 / 0.226 on the world-axes row and 0.038 to 0.051 on the hand-axes movement. Q-c, the next movement from two model steps of history and the command: the world-axes row 0.236 / 0.276 (RECOVERED BY THE NONLINEAR DECODER only) against 0.726 / 0.746 from the input numbers; the hand-axes position and turn 0.059 to 0.095 from the token against 0.327 to 0.687 from the input numbers (NOT RECOVERED BY THIS DECODER).
decision.meaning: From the token, these decoders recover the finger's row as the input gives it (world axes, relative to the left wrist, which mixes the hand's turn with the finger's own joints) at about 4 in 10 of its within-block variance, and they do not recover the finger's position or turn in the hand's own axes, which the same nonlinear decoder recovers from the raw input numbers at about 9 in 10. This reports what these decoders recovered; it does not show that the token lacks the hand-frame movement, that the transformer cannot use it, or that a later encoder would keep it.

rows.title: Finger joint servo on against off, real body
rows.owner: the coordinator (tool built on branch study/finger-servo-paired-trace-2026-10-08 at 27485a34c by an agent that has finished)
rows.question: From checkpoint 481,800's 8 saved worlds, with the same latched command and the same feasible hand joint goals in both arms (each body's latched goal, a hold goal equal to the start angles and 24 random goals drawn around the start angles), over one 250 ms hold (25 physics steps of 10 ms), does --finger-joint-servo on, against off: (1) never issue a finger hinge a command above 0.02 against its own goal while the command's gap term outweighs its speed term; (2) put on every finger hinge an actuator force and a joint torque with the command's sign at every 5 ms MuJoCo substep; (3) end nearer each hinge's goal than off on more than half of the bend pairs and of the extend pairs, per body over the 8 bodies; and how often does the whole-finger shared factor bind (below 1, below 0.5), which hinge sets it, and how often are the 6 finger_couple tendons at their limits?
rows.why: FINGER_JOINT_SERVO is REVIEWED (merged with the setting off at a56fd6ab3). The defect register's entry FINGER_JOINT_GOALS_SERVOED_AS_FINGERTIP_POSE (its next_action, commit e99634344) names this paired trace in the real body, under its own registry row, as the evidence toward QUALIFIED/OFF. The unit tests (row finger_joint_servo_on_check, 7 of 7) show each hinge's command sign at drawn states; they do not show what the body does over a hold: the passive forces, the coupling tendons, the fatigue gain and the motion each saved state carries into the hold. The operator's open question of Oct 8, 2026, whether the whole-finger scale stays: under it one hinge's command size depends on the other hinges' gaps; this row counts how often that happens in the real body and what share of the gap such hinges close. Before any switch-on the hand stage's fixed response is refit on holds executed with the setting on; this row states what such holds look like.
rows.gof_link: Control: a finger command can be learned as the cause of a finger movement only when the hinges move toward the goals the planner search and the hand stage chose; this row measures in the real body whether the on rule ends each hinge nearer its goal than the pose servo does.

rows.pass_line: verdict pass when B1, B2 and B3 hold. (B1) Under 'on', 0 readings at which the issued command exceeds 0.02 with the sign opposite to the hinge's goal - angle while 6 x |goal - angle| > 0.3 x |hinge speed|, over the 44 hinges, 26 goals and 8 bodies. (B2) In both arms, 0 substep readings whose actuator force or joint torque lacks the command's sign. rows.pass_line_basis: B1 is exact by the decoder's formula: under 'on' the command is f x strength x (6 x (goal - angle) - 0.3 x speed) with f and strength positive and the goals inside the hinge ranges, so it opposes the goal only when the speed term outweighs the gap term with the hinge turning toward its goal (braking); a gap-dominated reading against the goal would mean the world did not hand the decoder the latched goal. rows.title: Finger per-joint limit against on, real body
rows.owner: the coordinator (tool built on branch study/finger-per-joint-limit-2026-10-08 at 10a1f054c by an agent whose run ends with this draft)
rows.question: From checkpoint 481,800's 8 saved worlds, with the same latched command and the same feasible hand joint goals in both arms (each body's latched goal, a hold goal equal to the start angles and 24 random goals drawn around the start angles, the qualifying run's seed 20261008 and sigma 18.62 degrees), over one 250 ms hold (25 physics steps of 10 ms), does the finger joint servo with each finger hinge's command clipped to its own command range (on_per_joint) end the hinges nearer their goals than the tested on rule, whose commands one shared factor per finger chain scales down, on more than half of the bend pairs and of the extend pairs per body over the 8 bodies; and does it cost overshoot past the goal, goal crossings, hinge-speed sign changes or finger_couple tendon limit force?
rows.why: The operator's decision of Oct 8, 2026, about 1:10 PM PDT: build a per-joint limit (each finger hinge's command clipped to its own command range, no shared factor, tendons unchanged) and compare it with the tested on rule from the same starting positions and goals, reading closeness to goal, overshoot, shaking and tendon forces; the hand stage's fixed predictor is then fit to the rule that performs better. Per decision d = end hand shape error with the refit stage minus without it (below 0 = the stage's choice ended nearer; 0 = no difference); per body the mean of d; the same for admitted_forced minus without and refit minus admitted_forced (readings).

Finger position error (cm) and finger orientation error (degrees), means over the finger handles; the share of the start error closed in the hold, 1 - end / start (0 = as far as at the decision, 1 = arrived, below 0 = farther); the hand stage's own predicted cost before and after its 20 updates.

rows.why: The operator's decision received by 11:53 PM PDT, Oct 8, 2026: "Prepare the fresh matched comparison. Before launch, state the hand-performance measurements, success criteria, stop conditions and complete rollback checkpoint. Identify exactly which exceptions to gates 2, 3, 4 and 6 require my authorization. Keep code, starting worlds and other settings matched; vary only the finger-fix/calibration package. Stop after the declared comparison-no automatic continuation." SC2b compares the finger arm's end checkpoint with the control arm's; its margin comes from the old configuration's 14 rounds (pose servo, admitted fit, 8 decisions each: the spread of the difference of two independent 16-decision readings 3.6 in 100). Two equally trained checkpoints of production's configuration read the package's way measure the run-to-run part directly, before launch and without training (the style guide, No experiment launches on an unmeasured number).

rows.on_pass: The end checkpoint stands for row finger_comparison_verdict_484675, which runs next; the supervisor stays paused naming the run; nothing continues into normal training.
rows.on_fail: A stop of either arm, on any line, ends the comparison without a verdict: matched_comparison_verdict.py reads INVALID and the other arm is not launched. A finger-arm stop on the finger joint error line is in addition recorded as a finding against the package (the finger hinges ended farther from their goals than the line allows, the failure the package exists to remove); every other stop is recorded as readings only, neither a pass nor a fail of the package. The stopped arm's row reads FAIL: its run stopped; this record's one use is spent. The coordinator reports to the operator the stop's line, the stop fields' hour means and the stop's file (stop_reason.json, or the control file that holds it); a control-arm stop is recorded as readings only, neither a pass nor a fail of the package, and the finger arm's readings stand beside it as readings; the run's newest checkpoint is kept as evidence; the next launch resumes checkpoint 481,800, which no arm changes; any further run needs a new preflight record and the operator's new written authorization.

Arm own (the probe path, instrumented): per body, gof_probe_harness.Session restores body b from the companion; the start checks are recorded (the hash of MuJoCo's integration state, actuator gains and force ranges and the world's random stream against the same hash of the snapshot; the first frame's bytes; the world's dynamics fields); the trainer's own world recorder (observer_record.WorldRecorder) is attached to the world; then finger_switch_prediction_effect.run_body's loop at 601fbaf20 call for call: LemLite.step with learning off at every model step, its command latched on model steps that are multiples of 5 and sent for 5 physics steps with its eye command (the eyes drawn on the 5th), the babble bout schedule restored from the companion; recorded besides: the command, hinge goals and eye command handed at each burst, the author of each latch, the planning record of each planning event, the world records, and after the last body the arm's thread settings (the environment's thread variables, torch's thread counts, threadpoolctl's pools).

Arm replay (the operator's decisive split): the same restore, start checks and recorder; at each model step k the learner steps with learning off on the world's frames (its own command is not sent), and the world is handed control run 2's record k: the command in force (order_motor, 26 x 9 float32), its hinge goals (order_hand_goal, 44), its handle mask (order_mask) and that record's eye command (order_gaze), through the probe's own SingleEnvSource, for 5 physics steps with the eyes drawn on the 5th; the learner is told the command the world received, as the trainer tells it.

Arm k0bf16: the same restore and start checks, then one model step (481,800) with model.use_amp True and model.dtype bfloat16, every torch.amp.autocast('cuda') block of the trainer's code run as a processor autocast block with the same switch and type (probe_path_trace.card_precision_on_processor); its prediction errors, its proposed command and its planning record are recorded.

With the same restored state, a deterministic step gives the same state, and the records store qpos as whole multiples of 1 micrometre or 1 microradian, so equal states give equal records; one differing record is a different computation, not rounding. rows.pass_line_basis: Exact equality is reachable for model step 481,800 although control runs 1 and 2's records part from 481,807 (on bodies 1 and 5; the cause of that parting is not established): model step 481,800's input frame is the saved payload the companion restores (the restore check compares it byte for byte), no replay-ring update falls inside it (the ring updates after the burst on even model steps, train_mimo.py line 3660, read after step += 1), and both runs' planning records of 481,800 are equal in every field; arm on has the same code tree, launch command, saved state, random streams, device, precision and the supervisor's own environment. Should the step not repeat on the graphics card, arm on_again shows it, and the stage reads not judged, never not met: two arm-on runs that differ from each other mean training's step does not repeat, not that the replay is wrong. The six replaced values and the episode treatment build nothing physical: they name where files are written (the world row's world_settings stage tests the same claim for run_dir and caregiver_record_dir on the probe path), the tapes keep their events count, the latent body shadow is created after the command and draws from a private generator, and control runs 1 and 2 matched with different shadow states. Arm w1 is reported against arm on_current_code, as asked, without a line: its one body and the processor's arithmetic are expected to move the planner's result (PLANNER_SEARCH_UNSTABLE), and the command row's bfloat16 arm sizes that arithmetic.

rows.on_pass: The replay is training. If learning_off_command reads not met, the skipped learning by itself changes training's command at 481,800 (update_skipped beside it says whether the update or the training-only bookkeeping does it): the learning-off probe path cannot repeat training's command, the planner's jump stays its own defect, and probe_path_learning_off_match_481800 reads movement and sensors statistically, as the operator decided. A code_version_481800 not met adds the probe path's code to those candidates.
rows.on_fail: Not met: arms on and on_again agree with each other and both differ from control run 2's record, so the replay is not training: the result names the bodies and numbers that differ, and the readings beside it (the first world record, the model record and the planning record of 481,800) say whether the difference starts before the planner; the replay is repaired on the branch (its tests rerun, the row's draft amended) and runs again in a new folder before its other stages are read. rows.pass_line: verdict pass when computation_481800 (every sense's W at 481,800 at most 2 x its bfloat16 W) and goal_choice_481800 (8 of 8 bodies pick control run 2's goal) read met. fail when either reads not met, naming it. The command at 481,800, the first burst and the prediction at 481,801 are reported (result key reported), not judged: the replay row decides what the command's difference is. invalid when the own arm does not repeat the pilot's control arm number for number or ran another command file or thread count, a restored world differs from the saved one, a body or model step is missing, an arm ended in an error (the bfloat16 arm's error leaves the computation stage not judged), the parameters changed, or the records name more than one tool file, commit, trainer code hash, checkpoint file or loaded weights.
rows.pass_line_basis: The computation line is measured, not argued. bfloat16 keeps 8 significant bits, a rounding of up to 1 part in 256 of each number an autocast operation stores; for prediction numbers of size up to 1 that is up to 0.0039 per number, and a squared error per number of e x e changes by 2 x d / e of itself, so with body 0's vision error at 481,800 (0.0039 per number squared, e = 0.062) one number's squared error can move by up to 13 in 100; the pilot's W of 18 to 67 in 1,000 lies inside that bound, so the argument cannot tell arithmetic from another cause. The k0bf16 arm runs the same model step on the same state with the trainer's own autocast blocks in bfloat16, and W_bf16 is its distance from the 32-bit run; training's graphics-card kernels round other numbers than the processor's, so the line is 2 x W_bf16; the factor 2 is an allowance, not a measured ratio, and the k0bf16 arm does not reproduce TF32, which cuDNN may use on the graphics card for a 32-bit convolution outside an autocast block (torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 is True by default in torch 2.6.0, read in this checkout's environment; train_mimo's code sets neither it nor set_float32_matmul_precision; the encoders hold nn.Conv1d layers, lem/model/encoders/conv1d_stack.py). Reachability: with arithmetic the only difference, W and W_bf16 each measure one bfloat16 rounding of the same computation against its 32-bit result and are expected equal up to which numbers each machine rounds. The goal choice is discrete, from the same restored ring of 200 model steps: equal unless the ranking's inputs differ (the wellness evidence built against another body's command, SWITCH_EFFECT_REVIEW.md answer 5, or the training-only bookkeeping before the planner). The command is not judged: training's planner runs after the model step's optimizer update (lem_model.py, the update at lines 3930 to 3966 before the planner at line 4173), which the learning-off path cannot repeat, and the search turns a change of 1 part in 100,000 of its inputs into 23 degrees on the average handle (PLANNER_SEARCH_UNSTABLE, kept a separate defect by the operator's decision of 8:53 AM PDT); the replay row runs training's own path with learning off to decide that question.

rows.statistical_line: Each band is control run 2's average over the 16 windows plus and minus k x s_D / sqrt(n_eff). D = (the summary on control run 2) - (the same summary on control run 1) at every 100-step window both runs cover with full records, the first window left out (the two runs shared its first 7 model steps): 23 windows (482,300 to 484,500; control run 1's world and model copies start at 482,300) for the 45 summaries of the world and model records, 27 (481,900 to 484,500) for the 10 prediction ratios and no-change sums of the stats records; the slow change both runs share cancels in D. s_D = the root mean square of D; rho = D's correlation from one matched window to the next (0 where it reads below 0; 0.00 to 0.58 over the 55). n_eff = 16 / (1 + 2 x the sum over h = 1 to 15 of (1 - h / 16) x rho^h), the independent windows a 16-window average is worth when D correlates like an AR(1) series (12.19 for proprioception's no-change sum). k = the Student t quantile at 1 - 0.05 / (2 x 55) with n x (1 - rho) / (1 + rho) degrees of freedom, n the matched windows (3.726 to 5.952). If the probe path's windows are drawn like a training run's, its 16-window average minus control run 2's has the spread s_D / sqrt(n_eff), so each band is breached with a chance of about 0.05 / 55 and one of the 55 with a chance of about 5 in 100 at the measured correlations, whatever the summaries' dependence. Three approximations stand in that chance (the review of Oct 9, F8): the AR(1) shape of D's correlation, the effective degrees of freedom, and rho itself, a sample from 22 or 26 pairs of windows whose sampling error is carried into neither n_eff nor the degrees of freedom. L ran with the attention cap on: its 16-window averages are reported beside every band and form none.

rows.why: The operator's decision received by 5:42 PM PDT, Oct 9, 2026: "Choose 'Measure with learning on.' The learning-off test behaves differently from training, so it cannot reliably tell you when training should stop. Compare the finger fix off versus on, starting from identical checkpoint copies, with learning enabled in both. Set a short run length and emergency stop rules beforehand. Preserve the original checkpoint and save the test results. Use those results to distinguish normal variation from worsening predictions. Do not raise the stop limits just to let the finger fix pass. 'Alerts in both' would let training continue after those limits are crossed, leaving the end-of-run check to judge the damage afterward." The measurement row learning_on_stop_limits_481800 trains three arms of 1,000 model steps each; this run checks first the parts its 40 tests cannot reach without a checkpoint: train_mimo past one model step under the arm on a resumed episode with learning on (the one-update replay row ran the same launch for one model step), the finger configuration's launch probes and calibration replacement on a resume with learning on (unmeasured: the activation dry run's run B read fresh worlds, eval-only), the emergency rules against real processes, card readings and records, the priority and power-throttling settings on the arm's real processes, and the discard on real files. The development row runs 8 bodies and 100 model steps per arm, which the coordinator accepted (Oct 9) in place of the 2 bodies and few model steps first asked, for two reasons in the trainer's code: train_mimo refuses a resume whose continuation settings differ from the saved episode's (continuation_flags, n_envs among them: 'physical continuation configuration changed; explicit migration is required'), so every arm trains the saved 8 bodies; and the trainer writes a full stats record every 100 model steps (--report-every 100, train_mimo.py's test step % report_every == 0), so fewer than 100 model steps write no record for the emergency rules and the comparison to read. It decides no stage.
rows.gof_link: Measurement: the matched finger comparison's stop limits come from the learning-on measurement (learning_on_stop_limits_481800); this run checks its plumbing on real data before its arms are spent.

rows.title: Finger fix off against on with learning on: four senses' predictions against normal variation, 1,000 model steps
rows.owner: the coordinator
rows.question: Training from identical scratch copies of checkpoint 481,800 with learning on, 8 bodies, production's code (trainer code add5725e...) and the matched comparison's commands, for 1,000 model steps per arm (the full stats records of model steps 481,900 to 482,800): does the finger arm (the package: --finger-joint-servo on, the refit hand calibration, --replace-saved-hand-calibration naming its admission record) predict each of tactile (the skin's contact readings), proprioception (where each tracked body part is, how it is turned and how fast it moves), vision (the camera images the eyes receive) and audio (the sound spectrum the ears receive) no worse than the control arm (production's configuration) beyond normal variation, with the limits written before any arm runs from two training runs of production's configuration (control runs 1 and 2), and does it cross none of the emergency lines this row declares? Beside it: does a second control arm of the same session (control_again) differ from the first within normal variation, so that the declared basis describes this session?
rows.why: The operator's decision received by 5:42 PM PDT, Oct 9, 2026: "Choose 'Measure with learning on.' The learning-off test behaves differently from training, so it cannot reliably tell you when training should stop. Compare the finger fix off versus on, starting from identical checkpoint copies, with learning enabled in both. Set a short run length and emergency stop rules beforehand. Preserve the original checkpoint and save the test results. Use those results to distinguish normal variation from worsening predictions. Do not raise the stop limits just to let the finger fix pass. 'Alerts in both' would let training continue after those limits are crossed, leaving the end-of-run check to judge the damage afterward." The learning-off probe path does not stand in for training: its verification re-judgement read FAIL on a valid run (row probe_path_learning_off_match_rejudge_481800: with learning off over 1,600 model steps the probe path's movement and sensor readings lie outside training's bands, 7 of 12 and 34 of 43 inside), and the register entry FINGER_JOINT_GOALS_SERVOED_AS_FINGERTIP_POSE waits on this measurement ('The learning-on measurement's design, its review, its registry rows and its run.'). The matched comparison's stop list (stop_criteria_matched.json) stops either of its arms when an hour mean of a prediction ratio passes its line from run-hour 1.25; the package's rise in tactile and proprioception at the switch is unmeasured (the activation dry run's run B read fresh worlds), and a rise of tactile 57 (line 990 against 933), proprioception 185 (line 860 against 675), vision 262 (line 940 against 678), audio 62 (line 965 against 903) in 1,000 above the control configuration's highest window mean reaches the line. This row measures the rise in training itself, learning on in both arms, over the first 1,000 model steps after the switch, against limits fixed before any arm runs from normal variation, so that a worsening of the package's predictions is a finding before training continues past it; nothing in a run changes the limits, and they are never raised to let the finger fix pass. The limits come from the window the arms measure, model steps 481,900 to 482,800 (10 records). The limits file's history, every version written before any arm ran: (1) the whole run's 28 records, the arms measuring 8 records (sha256 71143d44..., Oct 9, 2026 6:06:25 PM PDT, kept as D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/finger_investigation/learning_on/limits_v1_whole_run_superseded.json): the first design; (2) the window the arms measured, 8 records (sha256 3e096bba..., Oct 9, 2026 7:10:20 PM PDT, kept as D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/finger_investigation/learning_on/limits_v2_window8_superseded.json): the coordinator's answer of Oct 9, "Normal variation from the same window as the measurement: compute the limits and the session bounds from C1 minus C2 over the records the arms will produce (the first 8 records, model steps 481,900 to 482,600), with the Student t quantile on that window's degrees of freedom (correlation counted as you do), not from the whole run's spread; ground: the arms measure that window, and C1 and C2 differ less there (tactile 8.9 against 21.1 later), so the whole-run spread would widen the limit beyond the window's own variation, against the operator's direction not to let the finger fix pass by a loose limit." (3) the window, 10 records (this file): the coordinator's decision of Oct 9 (after 7:26 PM PDT): under the window rule proprioception's rise caught in 95 of 100 at 8 records, 206.1 in 1,000, lay above its stop-list margin of 185, and 10 records is the shortest of the lengths computed (8, 10, 12, 14, 16 records; analysis/a3_window_lengths.json) at which all four lie under their margins. The window's numbers move with rho estimated from few records (vision's rho reads -0.60 at 10 records, 0.48 at 12 and 0.08 at 14 (counted as 0 when below 0), its degrees of freedom 10.00, 4.20 and 11.95, and its limit 35.2, 68.8 and 32.8 in 1,000), so the length was chosen as the shortest that passes, not by its neighbours' values. Against the whole run's spread at the same length the window's limits read tactile 13.8 against 16.3, proprioception 110.3 against 81.0, vision 35.2 against 58.2, audio 22.8 against 31.5 in 1,000: tighter in three senses, wider in proprioception, where C1 and C2 differ more inside the window (a root mean square of 94.7 against 81.5 over the whole run) and the window's 6.10 degrees of freedom raise the t quantile to 2.95 (2.47 over the whole run). The rise caught in 95 of 100 at 10 records lies under the stop margin in all four senses: tactile 23.0 against 57, proprioception 182.7 against 185, vision 59.4 against 262, audio 38.4 against 62. 1,000 model steps is 35 in 100 of the matched comparison's 2,875. control_again is kept (answer of Oct 9: "it measures run-to-run variation on today's code, which C1 and C2 (code 6525899f7) cannot").

rows.pass_line_basis: The operator's words: "Choose 'Measure with learning on.' The learning-off test behaves differently from training, so it cannot reliably tell you when training should stop. Compare the finger fix off versus on, starting from identical checkpoint copies, with learning enabled in both. Set a short run length and emergency stop rules beforehand. Preserve the original checkpoint and save the test results. Use those results to distinguish normal variation from worsening predictions. Do not raise the stop limits just to let the finger fix pass. 'Alerts in both' would let training continue after those limits are crossed, leaving the end-of-run check to judge the damage afterward." The limits come from normal variation only: the per-record differences of two training runs of production's configuration from one start (C1 and C2, read from their sha256-checked copies; L, the attention cap on, never enters them) over the window the arms measure, written into limits.json before any arm runs; the job refuses another file, nothing in a run changes them, the session pair decides validity only, and a later change would be a new row with a new limits file written before its run. The limits file's history, every version written before any arm ran: (1) the whole run's 28 records, the arms measuring 8 records (sha256 71143d44..., Oct 9, 2026 6:06:25 PM PDT, kept as D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/finger_investigation/learning_on/limits_v1_whole_run_superseded.json): the first design; (2) the window the arms measured, 8 records (sha256 3e096bba..., Oct 9, 2026 7:10:20 PM PDT, kept as D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/finger_investigation/learning_on/limits_v2_window8_superseded.json): the coordinator's answer of Oct 9, "Normal variation from the same window as the measurement: compute the limits and the session bounds from C1 minus C2 over the records the arms will produce (the first 8 records, model steps 481,900 to 482,600), with the Student t quantile on that window's degrees of freedom (correlation counted as you do), not from the whole run's spread; ground: the arms measure that window, and C1 and C2 differ less there (tactile 8.9 against 21.1 later), so the whole-run spread would widen the limit beyond the window's own variation, against the operator's direction not to let the finger fix pass by a loose limit." (3) the window, 10 records (this file): the coordinator's decision of Oct 9 (after 7:26 PM PDT): under the window rule proprioception's rise caught in 95 of 100 at 8 records, 206.1 in 1,000, lay above its stop-list margin of 185, and 10 records is the shortest of the lengths computed (8, 10, 12, 14, 16 records; analysis/a3_window_lengths.json) at which all four lie under their margins. The window's numbers move with rho estimated from few records (vision's rho reads -0.60 at 10 records, 0.48 at 12 and 0.08 at 14 (counted as 0 when below 0), its degrees of freedom 10.00, 4.20 and 11.95, and its limit 35.2, 68.8 and 32.8 in 1,000), so the length was chosen as the shortest that passes, not by its neighbours' values. A crossing by the finger arm is a finding against the package. Reachability: two runs of one configuration cross at least one of the four limits in about 5 in 100 measurements under the rule's own model, and in 8 to 14 in 100 if the records correlate as the whole run shows (11.5 in 100 against the whole run's spread; the independent review of Oct 9, FIX 1, D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/plan_review/learning_on_review/rule_calibration_output.txt); the basis pair itself, C1 minus C2 over the window, read tactile -4.2, proprioception +3.4, vision +37.7, audio +6.9 in 1,000: under the limit in tactile, proprioception, audio, and above it in vision (37.7 against 35.2, 107 in 100 of the limit: all 10 of its per-record differences are positive, a difference that persists between the two runs, which the rule counts as spread around zero; the coordinator's decision of Oct 9 keeps the rule and the limit as declared: a crossing reads fail, which sets only that the matched comparison is not launched until the operator decides, so a crossing normal variation could produce costs one operator decision and launches no training, while counting the persistent offset as spread would widen vision's limit from a single pair of runs against the operator's words; it would be shown wrong by the same-session pair, control_again minus control, crossing a sense's limit). When the finger arm crosses a sense's limit, the result names, beside the crossing, C1 minus C2 over the window and control_again minus control in the same sense (stage keys basis_pair_difference and session_pair_difference, and the crossing's text, which the verdict reason carries), and labels it, as declared here before any arm runs (the review's FIX 2, option (b), applied to all four senses; it changes no limit): 'not distinguished from normal variation' when the finger-minus-control difference is no larger than the larger of those two numbers (both read signed, as the result writes them), 'beyond both control pairs' otherwise; when control_again did not run, the label reads the basis pair alone and says the session pair was not measured. The verdict stays fail either way: the label explains a crossing and never turns it into a pass. The transient: the declared window is the switch's first 1,000 model steps, where a rise of the package would be largest; the lineage's one measured recovery after a change took 905 model steps (band to 1,617; MATCHED_COMPARISON_2026-10-09.md, SC3), so a rise that would recover later still reads as a finding here. rows.pass_line_basis: Exact equality between launches is made a property of the run, not assumed. (1) THE WINDOW AND THE MODE: the window stays model steps 481,800 to 481,805 (--max-steps 481,806; the bundle review's FIX-4). Without PyTorch's deterministic mode the card does not promise equal sums between launches: in row records_lockstep_2_481800 launches 1 and 2 repeated every command, world record and lane column, while launch 3 parted at the second transition, and A and B differed only in the self-state, whose spatial input is summed by index_add on the card (lem/model/spatial.py), an operation PyTorch 2.6.0 lists as normally nondeterministic on CUDA and runs deterministically under torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True). Under warn_only=True the memory-efficient attention's backward stays non-deterministic (PyTorch 2.6 sets one key split only when the mode is not warn-only), and warn_only=False is not usable because it raises on torch.cumsum of a floating CUDA tensor, NLLLoss on CUDA and median with indices on CUDA, which the trainer reaches; so the efficient, cuDNN and flash attention back ends are switched off and the attention takes its math path, its scores in bfloat16. The mode is the same in every arm, so it adds no difference between them. Operations with no deterministic implementation still run under warn_only=True and are named by their warnings in each arm's log; the repeat of A decides whether the configuration repeats, and a FAIL also needs B's repeat equal. Not measured before this run: the mode's cost in wall time, the math path's memory on the card (computed by the second reader of Oct 10 from the code's shapes: in bfloat16 within about 250 MiB of the stop line at the live step; learning_on's stop line of 8,100 of 8,188 MiB stays, a stop reads invalid with the stop named, and arm A runs first, so the series ends there), and whether every operation the trainer reaches has a deterministic implementation. (2) WHAT IS JUDGED (FIX-5): only what two launches of one code hold equal. On the processor two launches of the base differ only in the companion's 'worlds' part and in the world chunks' 'header' column, read with this job's own functions (D:/UEMA_Research/docs/gain_of_function_v4/comparison_records/evidence/lockstep_readers_cpu.json); those two are reported, not judged. Each arm's own folder in a text is read as <arm>, and the planner's decision record is compared on its parameter version counters, not on id() memory addresses. (3) The bundle's records are computed without gradient and without any random draw, from numbers the model step already computes (comparison_records.py; COMPARISON_RECORDS.md): on the processor the branch trained bit for bit as its base over 40 model steps and 15 replay passes, while a planted random draw in a record was caught at the first model step (D:/UEMA_Research/docs/gain_of_function_v4/comparison_records/evidence/cpu_lockstep_result.json). (4) The latent-body repair changes nothing under the Sep 30 configuration the control command names (LATENT_CONTRACT_REPAIR.md section 10: the restored transitions carry its own contract; the shadow draws from its own generator on the processor); this run therefore does not reach the repair's exclusion branch, whose evidence stays its unit tests and row latent_contract_check_2_481800 (the bundle review's NOTE-8). (5) The spike weights save does not run here: it fires only when one body's vision prediction error stays above 0.14 on 3 consecutive model steps, which on the recorded learning-on lane happened once, in the finger run, and never in either control run. Its evidence that it changes no training number is the processor's: train_mimo.main with a save forced at model step 6 (D:/UEMA_Research/docs/gain_of_function_v4/comparison_records/evidence/lockstep_readers_cpu.json, and the bundle review's probe_trainer_lockstep.py), and the fixture learner with 2 weights snapshots (D:/UEMA_Research/docs/gain_of_function_v4/comparison_records/evidence/cpu_lockstep_result.json). The equality is exact because any difference in a number training computes reaches the next command, the weights or the saved state; a tolerance would admit a defect of the kind the row exists to exclude. The repeat arm, run every time, shows within the same job that two launches of production's code agree; when they do not, the row reads invalid, never fail. (6) THE EMERGENCY LINES: the arms' only full stats record is the end record of model step 481,806, over 6 model steps; the learning-on limits file's gross lines (sha256 1720afbd...) are built on 100-model-step records and would stop production's own arm A there (audio 1361.7 in 1,000 against 1119.1, measured on the first attempt's record), so the row declares no prediction-ratio line and keeps every other stop (records_lockstep.LIMITS).

Run another test only where you identify a specific missing measurement." Normal training needs every target gate of record 4ba33dfc88ced223 judged again after its repair run (training_preflight's repair rule). Gate 5's failure at 481,800 had two parts (defect FINGER_JOINT_GOALS_SERVOED_AS_FINGERTIP_POSE): single joints driven against their goals, and the hand stage's fixed predictor missing the index joint angles by 36.1 degrees summed against 29.9 for predicting no movement. The decision that depends on this row: what gates 1, 5 and 7 of record 4ba33dfc88ced223 read for the finger and hand path, which the next bounded training plan cites.

rows.title: Whole-body capacity: hold hands-and-knees, rise there from belly-down, roll back to belly, learning off
rows.question: With learning off, on private copies of the 8 worlds of checkpoint 484,675, under the continuation's own body, decoder, force limits, fatigue, gravity, joint limits and floor contacts, can the body (i) hold a placed hands-and-knees posture for 10 s, (ii) reach it from belly-down, (iii) roll from its back to a supported belly-down position; and where a movement fails, is the cause the available force, the command route, the command itself, slip or a joint range?
rows.why: The whole-body decision at model step 489,350 (rhl_wholebody_decide_489350) reads supported rolling per opportunity. The 8 training bodies made 0 back-to-belly rolls, 0 partial trunk lifts and 0 crawl cycles in 731,356 body model steps (observer development record of model step 484,674), and the 20,000-step random-command baseline made 0 too. Those zeros cannot be read as a failure to learn until the movements are shown possible at training's limits, nor as weakness from failed sequences alone (the handback, item 2). No record holds per-joint delivered force at a failed transition; the Sep 23 roll search's raw report (116.75 degrees, fresh capacity) was deleted by the Oct 4 cleanup (the audit, section 1).
inputs: The episode file of 484,675, copied to scratch: D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_preserved/finger_repair_seg41j_1526_484675/episode_companion/ckpt_step_484675_9f0037bc4085471ea1d159a0e7adec72.pt.gz; each world rebuilt with env_kwargs_for from launch_command.json (kp 6, kd 0.3, damping x3, hinge armature 0.02, finger armature 0.0004, mechanical_v4, body function modulate, trunk_v1, 24 months, wrist_relative_v1 hand targets, finger joint servo on, action repeat 5, command hold 5, smoothing 0.35, strength limit 1.0).

No learner, no optimizer, no replay (learning off by construction). Outside forces removed: caregiver absent and its bodies parked 3 m away, toys and boxes parked, mobile and critters off; the start shows no body contact but the floor.

Capacity arms: (A) each world's own saved capacity vector, evolving under modulate; (B) capacity 1.0 at the start (the rested state training's fatigue model reaches: 0.90 after 10.7 s of rest). No other force change.
Strength channel 1.0 on all body handles (the ceiling the model can command); the hold repeats at 0.46, the recorded median.
Every command through the live route: LemLite.planned_execution, held 5 model steps, BridgeEnv.step (hand targets, decoder, chain and arm-group rescale, clip, modulate).
Seeds: the Sep 13 best roll sequence (Saved/mimo_bridge/developmental_integration/roll_reachability_20260913) and the observer's roll-synergy parts.

The tool: D:/UEMA_Research/docs/gain_of_function_v4/wholebody_capacity_check_2026-10-11/capacity_check.py at commit d1fc2d84aacef512a58c2fac78b09f38063b343f (branch build/wholebody-capacity-check-2026-10-11, merged), reviewed in CAPACITY_CHECK_REVIEW.md, CAPACITY_CHECK_RECHECK.md and CAPACITY_CHECK_RECHECK2.md (D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/wholebody_capacity_check_484675/reviews/); its declaration names every deviation from the specification (route differences: no hand_joint_goal, no exploration noise; pen walls non-colliding).
The specification: D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/remembered_hand_learning_2026-10-11/strength_audit/STRENGTH_AUDIT.md, section 4.
steps: Behind the guard: D:/UEMA_Research/.venv_mimo/Scripts/python.exe -m mimo_bridge.tools.commit_guard --need-gb 4 && D:/UEMA_Research/.venv_mimo/Scripts/python.exe -m mimo_bridge.tools.test_runner run wholebody_capacity_check_484675 --device cpu -- D:/UEMA_Research/.venv_mimo/Scripts/python.exe -B D:/UEMA_Research/docs/gain_of_function_v4/wholebody_capacity_check_2026-10-11/capacity_check.py run --out D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/wholebody_capacity_check_484675 --commit d1fc2d84aacef512a58c2fac78b09f38063b343f. The tool refuses a run whose file or any of its 13 live-route modules differs from the commit given, and refuses to overwrite an existing declaration.

1. Hold after placement, 40 trials: 8 bodies x capacity arm {A, B} x strength {1.0, 0.46}, plus one motors-off control per body. The posture is the audit's modelled one, solved per body inside every joint's range: thighs vertical with the knees under the hips, shanks on the floor, arms vertical with the elbows straight, palms flat (in the dev holds: left hip flexed 79.9 degrees, knee 90.0 degrees, trunk 8.1 degrees head-up, wrist at its 86.0-degree range end). Lowered until no contact penetrates over 2 mm, released at zero speed, each handle commanded to its own pose at release, run 10 s (200 model steps). Arm A's capacities evolve (a still hold recovers them); the end capacities are reported beside each result.

2. Rise from belly-down, 2 starts (body 2's own saved state; body 0 turned belly-down and rested 1 s with zero command): 16 candidates x 6 generations = 96 per start under arm B, half of each keyframe generation through the rail-respecting conversion (each joint moves toward its keyframe angle by at most its rail / (kp x strength) per model step), plus the Sep 23 grouped world-target family; each family's best replayed exactly, then under arm A, then once more rail-respecting under arms B and A.
3. Roll from the back, 1 start (body 0's saved state): the same budget and replays, seeded with the Sep 13 best sequence and the observer's roll-synergy parts.

Attribution per needed joint over the 250 ms before each failed transition, counted per stage (a primary reading only when the categories agree, else 'mixed' with the counts): force at its end (confirmed only by the same failure under arm B and in the second command family; in the hold, one family, 'force at its end, unconfirmed'), intended the wrong way, change too small, rescaled by another joint's over-rail demand, reversed with the body moved since the command was formed, reversed on a still body with the decoder's world error decreasing, world error increasing, slip (half the window and the failed step, with each supporting contact's travel), joint range. For every keyframe replay the tool decodes the latched joint targets afresh on the current state (no blend, no latch) and measures the decoder's weighted world-frame error for the handle group before and after that change (rotation rows and position rows at 8 per metre, each scaled by the handle's strength channel).
measures: Per 10 ms physics step of every hold trial and of each stage's best and failed candidates: the 26 x 9 command; per joint the decoder's demand before rescale, the rescale factor, the handed control, MuJoCo's control after MIMo's actuation, the delivered actuator force and joint torque, the force range now and the share left; the 10 capacities; joint angles, speeds, distance to each range end, joint-limit force, spring torque; per body-floor contact the normal and tangential force and |tangential| / (friction x normal); support shares of hands, knees, trunk, head and feet; chest and pelvis heights, trunk roll, centre of mass against the support polygon.

Hold: the share of the 10 s for which the line holds (0 = collapsed at once, 1 = held throughout). Rise and roll: the best candidate's reached state against the line, and the attribution of its failure.
rows.pass_line: Hold: for all 10 s chest and pelvis at 80% or more of their placed heights, no trunk or head floor contact, each hand and knee in floor contact on 95% or more of the 10 ms physics steps, each hand sliding 2 cm or less; the motors-off control must fail the same line. Rise: hands and knees carry 80% or more of the outside floor force, no trunk floor contact, chest at 80% or more of the placed hold's chest height, for 0.5 s, unassisted, replay exact. Roll: 150 degrees or more from the back, supported within 30 degrees of belly-down for 0.5 s, replay exact. THE VERDICT: pass only when every stage meets its line under arm A; fail when a stage misses its line (the per-stage readings carry why); invalid when the run could not measure.
rows.pass_line_basis: The 80% height line sits between the modelled servo sag (2 to 12 degrees at the hips, under 1 cm of pelvis height) and collapse (the lying trunk's centre about 5 cm up, about 30% of the placed 18.5 cm hip height); 10 s is 40 command holds and 20 times the roll goal's 0.5 s dwell; the motors-off control separates motor force from joint limits. The roll line is the Sep 13 and Sep 23 searches' goal, unchanged so the results compare (the audit, section 4).

rows.on_pass: All three stages pass under arm A: the movements are possible at training's limits, and the zero counts become a learning and goal-selection question for the 489,350 whole-body decision (the declared next test: the rolling learning comparison of ROLLING_LEARNING_EXPERIMENT_2026-09-23.json). A stage passing under arm B only: fatigue limits it; rest is the learning question, and any change to fatigue rates or the effort formula is the operator's (a change to the world the body lives in).
rows.on_fail: Per stage, from the counts of the needed joints' readings. Force at its end under arm B, confirmed: the 24-month body's actuators cannot make that transition by the tested families; reported to the operator as a world-semantics decision with the per-joint deficit; no force increase to obtain a pass. Intended the wrong way, change too small or rescaled by another joint's over-rail demand: the candidates' search coverage, not the body and not the decoder. Command interface (the rail-respecting replay of each start's keyframe best): reported to the operator as a measured property of the command interface, in these words: "the decoder's joint change had the opposite sign to the keyframe's intended change on X% of joint-physics-steps of the rail-respecting replay, Y% of them on steps where the root and trunk had turned under 2 degrees and no joint of the group had moved more than its asked step since the command was formed; on those steps the decoder's weighted world-frame error for the handle group fell on Z% and grew on W%". It is not a defect and not a repair trigger. A decoder defect, handled by the preserve, repair and verify rules, is read only where the fresh decode on the current state moves the group of a needed joint away from its own command: its joint change, applied by forward kinematics, raises the decoder's weighted world-frame error for that group (rotation rows and position rows at 8 per metre, each scaled by the handle's strength channel), at a physics step whose asked steps sit inside their rails, and the exact replay repeats it. Slip: a contact-geometry finding for the operator. Mixed: the counts are reported as they stand. A motors-off control that also held: the hold says nothing about motor force for that body, reported as such.

rows.baseline: Nothing passed before: no hold or rise demonstration in the records; partial rolls only, 105.4 degrees (Sep 13, kp 2, no force scaling) and 116.75 degrees (Sep 23, fresh capacity, raw report deleted); the audit's lever-arm estimate (hold feasible at every recorded capacity with straight arms; the push onto straight arms at the elbow's limit fresh and short at training's capacities).
rows.statistical_line: Each stage's best candidate is replayed exactly (identical physics on the processor), so a pass is a demonstration, not a rate; the 8 bodies' holds are reported one by one.
rows.material_gof_line: A pass under arm A shows the movement is within the body at training's limits, the precondition for reading the 489,350 whole-body decision's zero counts as a learning question.

coordinator_reading.verdict_meaning: PASS means every (start, rest, version) was measured validly and both T = 0 controls reproduced the registered arm-A record bit for bit; it says nothing about the movements, which follow.
coordinator_reading.rise: Body 0 turned belly-down, the rested joint-keyframe command, chest height as a share of the placed hold's (line 80% held 0.5 s), in place / posture kept: after 0 s 64% / 64% (lowest set 43% of rested force); after 10 s 73% / 76% (65%); after 30 s 81% / 83%, above the line only 0.12 s / 0.47 s (87%); after 60 s 88% / 89%, held 0.54 s / 1.71 s: MET in both versions (97%). Met after 60 s of the supplied rest and not after 30 s; only 0, 10, 30 and 60 s were measured, so 60 s is not a measured minimum (the handback correction of Oct 11).
coordinator_reading.roll: Body 0 on its back, the rested world-target command, largest turn (line 150 degrees, 0.5 s supported), in place / posture kept: after 0 s 29.7 / 29.7 degrees; 10 s 27.8 / 26.4; 30 s 25.0 / 25.6; 60 s 28.6 / 41.4 (lowest set 97% of rested force): met in NEITHER at any rest. With every capacity set to 1.0 the same command turned 179.97 degrees; it failed at every recovered vector tested, the 60 s one at about 0.970 to 0.992 over its 10 sets. No cutoff between that vector and full capacity was measured: sensitivity of this tested sequence, not a universal strength requirement or an impossibility of rolling (the handback correction of Oct 11).
coordinator_reading.limits: The rest is the measurement's supplied command, not training's rest: a success shows rest can restore what the rise needs, not that UEMA has learned when or how to rest. The supplied rest let the body drift (up to 65 degrees at the left toes); the posture-kept version removes that and the outcomes agree. The recovery follows the fatigue formula exactly (recovery 0.05 per second, drain 0.02 per unit effort, residual 6e-15); that checks the arithmetic and the recorded effort, not biological fatigue.

rows.title: Proprioception encoder, start (484,675) against end (489,350) and the repair's frozen encoder, on the same saved rows: body 1's posture information and body 3's joint information (PASS = measured validly; the answers are in status.json summary)
rows.question: (1) Body 1: on the same unchanged saved input rows, does the end encoder hold less decodable posture than the start encoder and the repair's frozen older encoder, consistently across the windows' parts, or within their part-to-part spread? (2) Body 3: with heading removed from what is scored (87 joint-relative hinge angles from the observer records), how much joint information does its proprioception token carry, against the other bodies, a 9-shift null and the input rows' own ceiling, for both encoders?
rows.why: During the continuation body 1's proprioception response dipped repeatedly (to 1.09, 1.29 and 1.21 per unit of posture movement) with the repair engaged, and body 3's token stayed quiet while its joints moved; the warning review asks whether these are a learning defect before any exclusion or repair changes, measured on saved checkpoints, never beside a trainer (the handback, Oct 11, 2026).

rows.pass_line: PASS means only that every check of validity held: strict load, the repeat, the cross-path identity, the reproduction of the trainer's own ratios, windows, alignment, interior or flagged bests, and the AGREEMENT GATE: at all 11 shared penalties the float64 curve equals proprio_token.posture_content's own algorithm run in float64 within 5.0e-4 (the comparison with production's float32 score is recorded beside it, not gated: at 0.0030518 production's float32 Cholesky rounding differs by up to 8.4e-4). INVALID otherwise. The answers are in status.json summary, never in the verdict.
rows.pass_line_basis: A measurement, not a demonstration (the handback's builder guard; the review's F5). The 5.0e-4 tolerance: the float64 curve and the float64 copy of production's algorithm agree within 7.9e-13 on the dev rows (the assessment), so 5.0e-4 sits nine orders of magnitude above that agreement, and 28 times under the smallest paired difference the question-1 rule read on the dev parts (0.014).

rows.title: Body 1 posture content through the lineage, against the lesson's dose
rows.question: On fixed saved input rows, does body 1's decodable posture fall between two saved encoders when, and only when, the proprioception token repair lesson pushed body 1 between them; and do the other bodies' contents fall during their own pushed stretches?
rows.why: The repair of body 1's lost posture information (row proprio_encoder_check_484675_489350, 'later encoder lower') depends on which lesson removes it. If the loss follows the repair lesson's push on body 1, the repair changes that lesson; if the loss comes without the push, the cause is another lesson or the input.

Load each encoder strictly into the production EncoderRegistry (encoder_check.build_registry), learning off (eval mode, no gradient, no optimizer), float32 on the processor at 2 threads; the frozen encoders through torch.func.functional_call (encoder_check.snapshot_encoder).

For every encoder and every fixed window: the tokens of the real rows, of production's posture-only rows (velocity fields 7-9 and capacity field 10 held at their window mean) and of velocity-only rows (posture fields 0-6 and capacity held at their window mean); per body the content score's best over the penalty grid (encoder_check.FoldSolver) for the world posture, whole window and its four 300-sample parts, and on the posture-only tokens; the response ratio on real and posture-only rows; the velocity-only response over the real response.

Order the encoders by model step. For each pair of consecutive encoders and each body: the content change (later minus earlier, mean over the 7 windows) and the lesson's dose on that body between them from the trainer's records (records with the body pushed / records; the log shortfall times the model steps to the next record, summed; the change of the lesson's attributed lift).

Per body: Spearman's rho between dose (log shortfall x model steps) and content change over the pairs at least 30 model steps apart, one-sided permutation p over 10,000 permutations; the content change per 1,000 model steps over the pairs where the body was pushed in at least 30 in 100 of the records and over those under 10 in 100, with its standard error; the noise floor: the content change between encoders under 30 model steps apart.

Checks: strict load; one encoder twice on the same rows (largest token difference 0); every model encoder whose run recorded a repair reading at its own checkpoint step reproduces that recorded ratio and posture spread (encoder_check.reproduction_check), at least 3; the agreement gate at all 11 shared penalties on two readings; the registered encoder check's full-window body-1 bests reproduced within 1e-4.
measures: Content score's best (1 - squared reconstruction error / squared error of predicting the window's mean posture; 0 = no better than the mean, 1 = exact, below 0 = worse) per encoder, window, part and body, on real and on posture-only tokens.

Response ratio: the token's standard deviation over the window per number (mean over 192) / the posture's (mean over 182); 0 = the token does not move with the posture; the repair's lines are DEAF 2.87 and LINE 3.77.
Velocity share: the token's response on velocity-only rows / its response on real rows; 0 = the token ignores the limb velocities, 1 = they alone move it as much as everything.

Dose per body and interval: pushed share (0 = never pushed, 1 = pushed at every record), log shortfall x model steps (0 = no push), attributed change (the lesson's own first-order change of ln ratio, summed).
Spearman's rho (-1 = more dose always with more loss, 0 = no relation, +1 = more dose with more gain) and its one-sided permutation p (0 to 1).
rows.pass_line: PASS means only that the measurement was valid: every encoder loaded strictly, the repeat held, at least 3 model encoders reproduced their run's recorded ratio (|ln ours / recorded| <= 0.02, posture spread within 1e-3 relative) and none failed, the agreement gate held at all 11 shared penalties within 5.0e-4, and the registered check's body-1 bests were reproduced within 1e-4. INVALID otherwise. The answers are in status.json tests, intervals and noise_close_pairs, judged by the statistical line.
rows.pass_line_basis: The validity checks are encoder_check.py's own, with their measured bases (reproduction 0.0027 at most on 484,675; agreement 7.9e-13 on the dev rows). The 1e-4 reproduction of the registered bests: both runs use the same code path, float32 at 2 threads; the registered values carry 5 significant digits (rounding at most 5e-6).

rows.on_pass: Read the tests against the statistical line. If body 1's content falls with the lesson's dose and not without it, the next read-only step is the first-order direction test of the lesson's step on body 1's content at saved checkpoints (its own row), then the repair is named from both. If content falls without the dose, the lesson is not singled out and the other lessons' directions are measured next.
rows.on_fail: INVALID: read the invalid reasons; repair the probe or its inputs and measure again under this row.
rows.owner: the body-1 mechanism investigation (read-only agent of Oct 11, 2026)
rows.gof_link: The proprioception token carries each body's posture to the core, the planner and the predictors; body 1 lost part of it, and the lesson that removes it decides the repair.
rows.target_metric: Body 1's change of content-score best per pair of saved encoders against the repair lesson's dose.
rows.baseline: Registered check (row proprio_encoder_check_484675_489350): body 1's full-window bests, start window / end window: frozen 481,100 encoder 0.837 / 0.830, 484,675 encoder 0.808 / 0.772, 489,350 encoder 0.790 / 0.727; the other 7 bodies within the spread or higher.
rows.statistical_line: The candidate (the lesson's push removes body 1's posture) is SUPPORTED when, for body 1, rho < 0 with one-sided permutation p < 0.05, AND the content change per 1,000 model steps over the high-dose pairs (pushed in >= 30 in 100 records) is below 0 by more than 2 standard errors, AND over the low-dose pairs (pushed in < 10 in 100) it lies within 2 standard errors of 0. It is NOT SUPPORTED when rho >= 0 or p >= 0.05, or when the low-dose rate is below 0 by more than 2 standard errors (the loss happens without the push). The other bodies are read by the same line.
rows.material_gof_line: not yet defined: this measures which lesson removes the information; the repair's own line is body 1's content back at the frozen 481,100 encoder's level on the same rows (0.837 / 0.830).

rows.why: A dose-response relation between the lesson and body 1's loss (row body1_posture_trajectory_415075_489350) cannot by itself separate the lesson from what else changes when body 1's ratio falls under DEAF. At each checkpoint, per body k: the content with the gain removed, S~_k = posture_content's own algorithm in float64 (10 blocks, 10 samples removed each side, ridge) on the tokens divided by their response, at the penalty of body k's curve best divided by the response squared (equal to the curve best at the checkpoint; unchanged by a pure gain): every body on the checkpoint's own window and on the fixed 489,350 window, body 1 on the fixed 479,350 and 484,675 windows and the 489,350 window's third part; its gradient with respect to the encoder's weights (no optimizer, no step). The update directions: the lesson's push on body b alone (minus the gradient of ln of the posture-only response, rescaled per tensor to 0.02 x the root mean square of the tensor's running gradient size, divided by that size, times the learning rate: proprio_token.WithinBody.apply); production's AdamW update from the saved running averages; VICReg's proprioception share over 256 window samples and the residual-path proxy (consecutive window samples, 5 model steps apart) over 256 pairs, each times the clip factor and divided by the running size.

Per direction and body: the first-order change per update of S~_k (each target), of ln ratio (real rows), of ln posture-only ratio, of ln velocity-only response and of body 1's ln response on each trajectory window. Beside it, in a temporary copy of the weights: S~_1, the ratio and the curve best at +-25 updates (the finite-difference check) and at 500 and 2,000 updates along the lesson's body-1 update held fixed.

The continuation account: body 1's pushed updates in each interval (pushed share of the records x model steps) x the mean per-update change of S~_1 along the lesson's body-1 update on each fixed target, summed, against the measured change of body 1's curve best there (trajectory/status.json); production's update x model steps beside it.

Checks: the saved running averages name and shape every encoder tensor with equal step counts; production's update from the earlier checkpoint's saved running averages points along the weights' actual change (cosine > 0.5) on at least 3 of the 4 close pairs; first order and finite difference agree within 25 in 100 wherever the change exceeds 1e-7 per update.
measures: S~_k change per update along each direction: content-score units (1 - squared error / squared error of the window's mean posture; 0 = no better than the mean, 1 = exact) per update; negative = the update removes decodable posture with the gain removed.
ln ratio change per update (0 = no change; +0.01 = the token's movement per unit of posture movement rises by 1 in 100).
Counts: checkpoints at which the lesson's body-1 update lowers S~_1, of 16; the same for production's update.
The continuation account: predicted and measured change of body 1's curve best on the fixed window, content-score units.
Close-pair cosine (-1 to 1; 1 = production's saved update points exactly along the weights' actual change).
rows.pass_line: PASS means only that the measurement was valid: every checkpoint's saved running averages mapped by name, shape and step count; production's update pointed along the actual weight change with cosine above 0.5 on at least 3 of 4 close pairs; first order and finite difference agreed within 25 in 100 wherever judged. INVALID otherwise. The answers are in status.json points, continuation_account and the counts, judged by the statistical line.
rows.pass_line_basis: The cosine line: over 10 to 25 updates Adam's running average of the gradient (beta1 0.9) and of its square (beta2 0.999) change little, so a correctly mapped saved update points along the actual change; a misaligned mapping pairs unrelated tensors and reads near 0. The 25 in 100 agreement allows the curvature over 25 updates; a sign or scale error in the derivative fails it.

rows.title: How fragile is body 1's posture reading
rows.question: On the saved rows where body 1's posture content fell (its lower trunk at headings -144 to -166 degrees, and the turn from -77 to -134 degrees in window 479,350), does a weight change as small as 25 lesson updates in a random direction move the encoder's reading of body 1's posture as much as the lesson's own direction does, far more than on body 1's earlier rows and on the other bodies' rows, since when, and what do the encoder's LayerNorms receive on those rows?
rows.why: Row body1_posture_trajectory_415075_489350 found body 1's content on those rows swinging by up to 0.3 between checkpoints about 1,000 model steps apart, without following the lesson's dose; row body1_posture_direction_first_order found up to 0.39 for +-25 lesson updates. If any small update moves it as much, the repair has to make those rows' reading stable, not only change the lesson; the LayerNorm inputs say where the instability sits.

Fixed saved windows (8 bodies x 1,200 samples x 312 numbers, one sample every 5th model step) of model steps 421,461 and 450,425 (body 1's lower trunk at -12 and -78 degrees) and 479,350, 484,675 and 489,350 and the 489,350 window's third 300-sample part (-96 turning, -154, -153 and -147 degrees: the rows where its content fell), read unchanged.

At each checkpoint: per body and window, the curve best (the ridge decoder's best content score for the world posture over the penalty grid) and the ratio, at the saved weights.

The displacement size: 25 x the lesson's body-1 update (the repair lesson's push on body 1 alone as WithinBody.apply applies it, from the checkpoint's own window and saved running averages), per tensor root mean square. Directions of that size per tensor: the lesson's update itself; 6 random directions (Gaussian per weight, seed 20261012); production's saved AdamW update. Each applied with + and -, the curve bests read, the weights restored and their sha256 checked.
Fragility per body, window and direction: |curve best at +D - curve best at -D| / 2; curvature: their mean minus the base. For random directions the median over the 6.

At the saved weights, per body and window, at each of the encoder's three hidden LayerNorms and the output LayerNorm: the median over rows of the entering vector's standard deviation across its 192 numbers (the divisor) and its constant share (the squared size of its window mean over its mean squared size).
measures: Fragility: content-score units (0 = the reading does not move; 1 = the whole range from no better than the mean posture to exact).
Curvature: content-score units; negative = both directions lower the reading.
Divisor: the LayerNorm's input spread across its numbers, in the layer's units (larger = the normalisation divides by more, a weight change moves the output less).
Constant share: 0 to 1 (1 = the vector entering the LayerNorm never changes over the window).

rows.title: Body 1: lost posture information or non-linear code
rows.question: On the same saved rows where a linear decoder reads less of body 1's posture from its proprioception token with the 489,350 encoder than with the 481,800 encoder (every 300-sample part of windows 484,675 and 489,350, lower trunk at -142 to -166 degrees), does a non-linear decoder (RBF kernel ridge) on the same folds read the same loss (the token no longer holds the information), no loss (a non-linear code), or a loss only in the trunk's heading?
rows.why: The independent review of the mechanism write-up (D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/body1_posture_mechanism/reviews/MECHANISM_REVIEW.md, computation 2) and the coordinator's amendment to rows body1_posture_trajectory_415075_489350 and body1_posture_fragility_and_normalisation: the loss is measured with a linear decoder only, and the core's attention and MLP layers can read a non-linear code. Lost information is a defect to repair, whose cause the separating training run from 481,800 (the review's computation 3) decides; a non-linear code is no information defect, and that run is not needed for one.
inputs: Encoders, proprioception tensors only, loaded strictly by encoder_check.py's readers (commit 3a53248bc): the frozen 481,100 encoder saved in D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_preserved/finger_repair_seg41j_1526_484675/run/checkpoints/ckpt_step_484675 (runtime_state.pt, proprio_token_repair snapshot, through functional_call); the model encoders of Saved/mimo_bridge/experiments/H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41o_1431/checkpoints/ckpt_step_481800, of that 484,675 checkpoint, and of D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_preserved/remembered_hand_learning_continuation_end/run/checkpoints/ckpt_step_489350; each one's weights must hash to the trajectory row's record of it.

Three saved repair windows read unchanged (8 bodies x 1,200 samples x 312 numbers, one sample every 5th model step, 300 s): those of the checkpoints at model steps 479,350 (Saved/.../H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41m_0402), 484,675 and 489,350; whole and in 4 parts of 300 samples.

Targets per body from the same rows: the world posture (fields 0-6 of the 26 rows, 182 numbers, the registered check's target); the same 182 fields with every row turned about the world vertical by minus the lower trunk's heading (mimo_bridge/proprio_heading.py heading_free: psi = 2 atan2(q_z, q_w) of the lower trunk's world quaternion); the heading alone (cos psi, sin psi).
