Planted cases on synthetic data: the kernel solver with the linear kernel equals encoder_check.FoldSolver at the 11 shared penalties within 1e-6; a planted non-linear code reads at least 0.85 with the kernel decoder and at least 0.30 above the linear decoder; planted lost information reads no more than the share the token holds + 0.05 under either decoder.

Each encoder reads each window through the production path (encoder, then the output LayerNorm), learning off, float32, 2 threads. Per encoder, window part (whole, 4 parts), body and target: the LINEAR decoder, FoldSolver's curve best (ridge over lam = 0 and 200 x 4^k, k = -24..2, unchanged); the KERNEL decoder, RBF kernel ridge on the same 10 blocks with 10 samples removed each side of the withheld block, centred on the fitted part, k(z, z') = exp(-|z - z'|^2 / (2 sigma^2)), sigma = c x the fold's median distance between fitted tokens, c = 2^k for k = -6..6, lam = 4^k for k = -16..4, its best cross-validated score over that grid.

Beside, deciding nothing but the clock clause: on the 300-sample parts the same decoders on the tokens rolled by 150 samples against the target; on every part the encoder-free CLOCK FLOOR, the kernel decoder reading each sample's time index instead of the token.

Checks: strict load; weights hash to the trajectory row's; no checkpoint turned its rows; one encoder twice gives the same tokens; the linear curve bests (world posture, whole and parts, 8 bodies) equal the trajectory row's within 1e-4 for all 4 encoders on all 3 windows; the linear-kernel identity within 1e-6 on the 489,350 encoder's readings of window 489,350 (whole and parts, 8 bodies, 3 targets); weights unchanged after.
The rule (statistical line), written into declaration.json before any reading, on the 7 ruled parts.
measures: Content score: 1 - squared reconstruction error / squared deviation of the part's target about its mean (0 = no better than the part's mean target, 1 = exact, below 0 = worse), per encoder, part, body, target and decoder.
Paired difference: later encoder's score minus the earlier encoder's on the same part (-1 to +1 score units; 0 = no change, negative = the later encoder holds less that the decoder can read).
Reference band: the lowest and highest of bodies 2-8's mean paired differences over the same parts.
Clock floor: the kernel decoder's score from the samples' time index alone, same scale (0 = time gives nothing, 1 = time interpolation alone rebuilds the target).
rows.pass_line: PASS means only that the measurement was valid: the planted cases held, every encoder loaded strictly and hashed to the trajectory row's record, the repeat held, the linear curve bests reproduced the trajectory row's within 1e-4, the linear-kernel identity held within 1e-6, and the weights were unchanged after. INVALID otherwise. The answer is status.json summary.primary_reading, judged by the statistical line.
rows.pass_line_basis: The reproduction reads the trajectory row's own code path and rows (float32 rounding, 5-digit records: 1e-4). The identity: the dual and primal ridge solves are the same algebra; on planted rows they agree within 7.0e-10 (dev run, file time Oct 12, 2026 1:10 AM PDT, planted.json in info_vs_linear/dev_planted), so 1e-6 sits three orders above float64 rounding. The planted lines: the dev run read 0.97 and 1.00 kernel against -0.00 and 0.12 linear on the planted code, and 0.50 and 0.52 against held shares 0.52 and 0.54 on the planted loss.

rows.statistical_line: Body 1 reads LOWER under a decoder and target when encoder_check's question-1 rule on its 7 paired differences reads 'later encoder lower' (lower on at least 6 of 7 and the 97.5% upper bound of the mean, t with 6 degrees of freedom, below 0) AND its mean paired difference is below the lowest of bodies 2-8's. Primary pair: 489,350 against 481,800. PREMISE: linear LOWER on the world posture, else 'premise not reproduced'. LOST INFORMATION: kernel LOWER on the world posture; then kernel LOWER on the heading-free posture = lost posture information, else kernel LOWER on the heading = lost heading, else not attributed. NON-LINEAR CODE: kernel not LOWER on the world posture AND the 489,350 encoder's kernel score above the clock floor on at least 6 of the 7 parts; NOT DECIDED BY THE TOKEN when that clock clause fails. UNREADABLE: a ruled part's best at a grid end (linear: either end of its penalty grid; kernel: either end of lam or the smallest c). The same rule against the frozen 481,100 and the 484,675 encoders is read beside.
rows.material_gof_line: not yet defined: this decides whether a defect exists; the repair's line, if one does, is body 1's kernel and linear scores on these parts back within bodies 2-8's band of the 481,800 encoder's.

Kernel decoder, world posture: body 1 lower on 7 of 7 parts, mean paired difference -0.168, 97.5% upper bound -0.083; bodies 2-8's means -0.025 to +0.013. Kernel decoder, heading-free posture: -0.158, 7 of 7, bound -0.074; bodies 2-8 -0.032 to +0.014. Kernel decoder, heading alone: -0.049, lower on 4 of 7, within the spread across parts. The premise held: linear decoder, world posture -0.177, 7 of 7, bound -0.077; bodies 2-8 -0.027 to +0.019. Clock clause held: body 1's kernel score above the time-index floor on 7 of 7 parts (floor -0.075 to +0.198).
findings: The non-linear decoder does not recover the loss. Body 1's kernel scores on the 7 parts: 0.317 to 0.637 with the 489,350 encoder against 0.663 to 0.755 with the 481,800 encoder; the linear scores 0.269 to 0.649 against 0.665 to 0.756. On every part the kernel decoder's best sat at its smoothest setting (c = 64 x the fold's median token distance, the end nearest a low-order polynomial ridge): every more local, more non-linear setting of the 13 read less. Limit: this excludes codes an RBF kernel ridge reads from about 250 fitted samples per fold, not every possible code.

The loss is in the body's configuration, not its heading: turned to the heading-free frame, body 1's posture loses -0.158 against -0.168 in the world frame; the heading alone -0.049 (4 of 7 parts lower, within the spread).

Against the 484,675 encoder the same reading: kernel -0.067, 7 of 7, bound -0.040; bodies 2-8 -0.019 to +0.011. Against the frozen 481,100 encoder UNREADABLE by the declared grid rule (the frozen encoder's kernel best on window 484,675 part 3 at the lowest penalty, 2.3e-10); its numbers: kernel -0.160, 7 of 7, bound -0.072; bodies 2-8 -0.007 to +0.033.

Timing of the loss, beside: 481,800 to 484,675 the kernel decoder reads body 1 LOWER (-0.101, 7 of 7, bound -0.003; bodies 2-8 -0.019 to +0.008) while the linear decoder reads within the spread (bound +0.028); frozen 481,100 to 481,800: +0.008, no loss. By 484,675, 2,875 model steps after 481,800, the kernel decoder reads 60 in 100 of the loss measured at 489,350 (-0.101 of -0.168).

Turn window 479,350, whole (beside): with the 489,350 encoder the kernel decoder reads 0.537 where the linear reads 0.217; the 481,800 encoder reads 0.757 kernel, 0.754 linear. A non-linear decoder recovers part of the single map across the 57-degree turn, not all of it. Its 4 parts read 0.639 to 0.808 (kernel, 489,350) against 0.657 to 0.776 (481,800).

Controls: the tokens shifted 150 samples against the posture read -0.149 to -0.005 (both decoders, both encoders, body 1); the encoder-free time-index floor -0.075 to +0.198. The scores are the token's, not temporal interpolation.
investigation_reading.consequence: The row's on_pass: lost information is a defect to repair. Its cause is not decided here; the separating training arm from 481,800 (the review's computation 3) decides it under its own row and preflight, and row body1_posture_equal_size_gradient_directions runs first to narrow the candidates (the push; the other lessons on the new heading; the 481,800 configuration change).

rows.title: Near-half-turn decoder turns in the seg41j, seg41u and seg41r commands
rows.question: In the saved commands of seg41j_1526 (model steps 481,800 to 484,675, finger joint servo on), seg41u_1718 (same span, servo off) and seg41r_1539 (484,675 to 489,350, servo on), how many of the decoder's turn calculations (mimo_bridge/action_decoder.py rotmat_log) fell in its near-180-degree branch, and by how many degrees did the old calculation's turn differ from the repaired one (commit 2148378cf) on those calls?
rows.why: ADOPTION.txt item 1 of the code sanity review (Oct 12): before admitting the repaired decoder, identify the affected near-half-turn commands; that audit did not count how often they occurred, so the fault is not yet assigned any part of the stall. Decision that depends on it: whether a run on repaired source can be compared with seg41j and seg41r (made on the old source) as the same turn calculation on recorded commands, or whether the listed calls must be carried into the coordinator's saved-state control comparison first.
inputs: Saved/mimo_bridge/experiments/H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41j_1526, Saved/mimo_bridge/experiments/H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41u_1718, Saved/mimo_bridge/experiments/H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41r_1539: args.json, and observer/world/b0..b7 chunk files (29, 29 and 47 per body, 100 model steps each, one process per body, no gaps file) with the one saved compiled world model observer/world/models/5aff7b57135ab6431aae071e6a4a6680.mjb.gz.

Per record (one per body per model step, written after the burst, the 5 physics steps of 10 ms of one model step): qpos (146 numbers, every joint, stored as whole multiples of 1e-6 rad, 1e-6 m or 1e-7), the command handed at the burst's first physics step (26 body handles x 9 numbers: target position xyz in cm, orientation quaternion x y z w, radius, strength 0-1; float32), the handle mask, the 44-number hand joint goal (rad), the author code, world episode, simulated time and frame counter.

Old function: rotmat_log imported from main's Source/Python/mimo_bridge/action_decoder.py (equal to base 362702f9b and to HEAD; last changed by c93d30a31, Oct 8 8:15 AM PDT, before the three runs began). Repaired function: rotmat_log's source text from commit 2148378cf, executed into an isolated module; main is not edited and nothing is cherry-picked.

Code reused: reader.load_world_lane of docs/gain_of_function_v4/remembered_hand_learning_2026-10-11/reader.py (observer_record.orders_in_force); main's ActionDecoder (body_layout trunk_v1) and HandTargetControl built on the saved model; observer_record.load_world_model; MuJoCo mj_kinematics.
steps: Check the two functions: main's action_decoder.py equals 362702f9b's and HEAD's; 2148378cf's parent is 362702f9b and it changes the file only inside rotmat_log. Function control: on the review's example R = [[-1,0,0],[0,0,-1],[0,-1,0]] (a half-turn about (0,1,-1)/sqrt(2)) the old and repaired turn vectors must be 90 degrees apart and the repaired one must rebuild R within 1e-9 per element.

Per run and body, read the world lane with reader.load_world_lane, and from the same chunks with the same live mask the handle mask, rest flag, command-recorded flag, simulated time and frame counter, joined by model step.

Burst t is examined when record t-1 is model step t-1 of the same episode and process, 0.05 s and 5 frames earlier, and record t carries a recorded command; every other record is counted under its reason (first record of the lane, scheduled rest hold whose command is not recorded, reset or restore).

For the decoder's first call of each examined burst, form its input as decode() does (env.step hands the same command on all 5 physics steps): for every handle with hinge joints, not masked and with strength above 0 (arm members wrist, lowerarm, upperarm: raw strength > 0; others: strength clipped to 0-1 > 0), skipping the 10 finger handles when finger_joint_servo is on: R_t = quat_xyzw_to_mat of the command's quaternion, or for a finger row with the servo off the quaternion HandTargetControl.execute gives on record t-1's qpos and the joint goal; R_c = the handle body's xmat from mj_kinematics of record t-1's qpos; R = R_t R_c^T.

Call the old and the repaired rotmat_log on the same R. Record the distance from a half-turn (pi minus the turn angle arccos((trace R - 1)/2)), whether the branch ran (distance below 1e-6 rad), |w_old - w_new|, and for differing calls the angle between the two turn vectors, the angle between the orientations the two turns end at, and how far each turn misses R.

Bracket the 4 unrecorded calls of each burst: the distance from a half-turn at record t's state with burst t's command, and the handle body's own turn from record t-1 to record t (and over the previous burst).

Planted control: on 9 real calls per body per run (216; 2 of each 9 with a half-turn axis whose x is exactly 0, the review's failing class), replace the command quaternion by the one that makes R an exact half-turn; every planted call must fall in the branch and the repaired turn must rebuild the half-turn within 1e-6 rad.

Write D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/near_half_turn_count/result.json: per run and handle group the counts, degrees, author counts (planner; self_choice; reflex = motor network output; reflex_noise = motor network output plus babble noise) and the bodies, handles and model steps of differing calls and of the 50 calls nearest a half-turn.
rows.measures: Per run and handle group (arm: wrist, lowerarm, upperarm; finger: thumb, index, middle, ring, pinky, turned only with the servo off; head; leg: thigh, calf, foot; trunk: lower_trunk, chest; gaze is never turned, its chain is empty): (1) decoder calls examined; (2) calls in the branch; (3) calls whose turns differ by more than 1e-9 rad, as a count and a share of calls examined (0 = the old calculation gave the repaired turn on every call, 1 = on none); (4) among them, the angle between the old and repaired turn vectors in degrees (0 = identical, 180 = opposite) and between the orientations they end at (0 = same end orientation reached by turning the other way, 180 = ends a half-turn apart); (5) every call's distance from a half-turn in degrees (0 = exact half-turn requested, the branch covers only the first 0.0000573 degrees; 180 = no turn requested), its minimum and a histogram; (6) the bracket for the unrecorded calls; (7) author counts of the examined and of the differing calls.
rows.pass_line: The measurement is valid (verdict pass) when every check holds: (a) main's action_decoder.py equals 362702f9b's and HEAD's, 2148378cf changes it only inside rotmat_log, and the imported old function is main's; (b) the function control gives 90 degrees (within 1e-6) and the repaired turn rebuilds the example within 1e-9; (c) all 8 bodies of all 3 runs read with no refusal, the added fields join load_world_lane's model steps exactly, and every record is counted as examined or excluded with a reason; (d) the decoder built on the saved model has the header's 26 handle names and body ids and only gaze lacks hinge joints; (e) on every call outside the branch the old and repaired outputs are bitwise equal; (f) at least 200 planted half-turns, each caught in the branch and rebuilt by the repaired turn within 1e-6 rad; (g) with the servo off, every finger target was formed by HandTargetControl.execute without error. Any count of differing calls, 0 or many, is a finding, not a failure.
rows.pass_line_basis: The checks are the conditions under which the counts measure the decoder's own two calculations on the decoder's own inputs: the right two functions (a, b, e), the right records, model and handles (c, d, g), and a pipeline shown to place a real half-turn into the branch (f). The 1e-9 rad tolerance: outside the branch both versions run the same arithmetic; inside it both return a unit axis times the same angle, so one axis agrees to float64 rounding (about 4e-16 x pi); 1e-9 rad is about a million times that rounding and a thousand times below the branch's own 1e-6 rad width, so a difference above it is another axis or sign, never rounding. Same end orientation below 1e-4 rad: a reversed turn inside the branch ends at most 2e-6 rad from the other, 50 times under that line, while the axis fault ends 90 to 180 degrees away. The stated limit: R_c from a recorded qpos is one 5 ms MuJoCo substep later than the decoder's data.xmat (mj_step leaves xmat at its last substep, env.py) and qpos is stored to 1e-6 rad, so a reconstructed call within a few times that substep's turn of the branch cannot be assigned to it or away from it; the result lists the nearest calls with the handle's turn per burst beside them.

rows.title: Would a per-hinge refit of the hand stage's forecast have forecast the measured hold ends better? (saved holds of four windows, no training)
rows.question: Row hand_goal_attribution_489350 found the hand stage's forecast gap (summed measured hold-end hand-shape error minus summed forecast error for the selected finger goal, over summed start distance) at 0.12 to 0.15 in all four windows, against measured pooled closure of 0.04 to 0.07. On those saved holds, would the adjustable predictor's declared per-hinge lesson (branch build/adaptive-hand-predictor-2026-10-11: three features per hinge, penalty 0.01 toward the admitted coefficients), the same lesson without the penalty, or the same lesson plus the command's finger strength have forecast the measured hold-end hand shape better than the admitted fixed fit, on planning steps held out of the fit and on a later window than the fit's?
rows.why: proxy decision asks for one concrete command or predictor repair and for reconciling the adjustable predictor's pending physical-choice comparison. Whether its lesson can remove the forecast gap on these windows' own holds, and whether its declared penalty or a missing strength input limits it, decides which repair is proposed and what its decision test must contain; it is measurable on saved records before any physical test or training.
inputs: The same four readings, world lanes and calibration as row hand_goal_attribution_489350 (its inputs field), plus the command's 26 x 9 handle numbers for each finger handle's strength (motor[handle, 8], 0 to 1).

THE PROGRAM: D:\UEMA_Research\external\D\UEMA_scratch\hand_goal_attribution_20261013\refit_check.py (sha256 588c60cec11d508f...), which imports attribution.py (D:\UEMA_Research\external\D\UEMA_scratch\hand_goal_attribution_20261013\attribution.py (sha256 c157249a08a57710...)) for the readings' paths.
steps: Per decision and hinge: angle at the decision q0 (world record t-1), speed (q0 - angle at t-2) / 0.05 s, the command's joint goal g (record t), the angle at the hold's end q5 (t+4), the hinge's range r, the finger handle's strength s.

Forecasts of the hold-end angle, each through the hand geometry's own joint/tendon projection: ADM the admitted coefficients; A3 per hinge argmin mean((x.c - y)^2) + 0.01 sum((c - c_adm)^2), x = [1, (g-q0)/r, 0.25 x speed/r], y = (q5-q0)/r; U3 the same without the penalty; S4 x plus s x (g-q0)/r; NC no change.

Within each window: fit on the even planning steps, test on the odd ones, and the reverse. Forward: fit on B1LO's start window, test on B1E's end window; seg41j start to seg41r end; seg41r end to B1E end.

Hand-shape error of each forecast pose against the remembered finger pose with the lines of CalibratedHandResponse.local_goal_cost; started after commit_guard --need-gb 4 allows it; CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES empty.
measures: Forecast gap on test decisions: (summed measured - summed forecast hand-shape error) / summed start distance; 0 = the forecast's pooled closure equals the measured one, the admitted fit reads 0.12 to 0.15.

Mean absolute difference between measured and forecast hand-shape error per decision (the useful-movement investigation's 0.669 for the fixed fit at seg41r's end window), and mean absolute hold-end angle error over hinges in degrees, beside no change.
How far each refit's coefficients move from the admitted ones (mean |c - c_adm| per feature).
rows.pass_line: VALIDITY, not which forecast is better (verdict key of refit_check.json): pass when this program's hand-shape error for the ADM forecast equals CalibratedHandResponse.local_goal_cost on the same inputs within 1e-9 on every decision. THE READING'S OWN LINE for proposing the adjustable predictor's lesson as the repair: A3's forecast gap on held-out and forward tests at most half the admitted fit's, with its mean absolute hand-shape difference lower; if U3 meets that line and A3 does not, the declared penalty is the limit; if S4 lowers the held-out gap below U3's by more than the spread between the two folds, strength is a missing input.
rows.pass_line_basis: The equality check proves the hand-shape forecast is computed by the trainer's own lines. Half of the admitted gap is the smallest change that would move the forecast's pooled closure from about three times the measured one to under twice it; held-out planning steps and a later window keep a fit from being graded on the holds it learned. This reading cannot say whether the hand stage would choose better commands with a refit forecast: those commands were not executed, which is the paired physical comparison's question.

COMMAND: the wrist position target (motor[wrist, 0:3]) against the palm and the object; the action decoder's arm-group step evaluated on the recorded pose (stacked damped least squares, lambda 0.001, of the wrist, lower-arm and upper-arm orientation rows and the wrist position row weighted 8, each times its handle's strength; each hinge's step clipped to its range), iterated to its fixed point from the pose at t-1 (at most 200 iterations, at most 0.10 rad per hinge per iteration, stop below 1e-5 rad) with trunk, root and the other arm held; again without the range clip; again with the chest and lower-trunk chains moved by their own handles' steps. The palm at each fixed point against the object.

5. PREDICTED: the efference body head's tenure expectation for the wrist handle (expected_cm, formed when the command began its hold), added to the palm at t-1; its record is matched to the hold by the offset whose recorded achieved palm change equals the forward-kinematics change.

6. ACTUAL: the palm at t+4; the palm change split by forward kinematics into the arm hinges' part (the hold-end arm angles on the start pose), then the trunk hinges' part, then the free root's part; the arm hinges' change projected on the fixed point's change (execution share).

7. EXECUTION LIMITS: arm hinges within 1 degree of a range end at t-1 and t+4 and at the fixed point; hold records whose recorded arm actuator commands (ctrl) reach 99.5% of the largest recorded in that direction; hold records with a contact of the arm or hand against the focus object, other objects, the caregiver, the own body or a surface (floor, crib, wall).

8. Medians and counts per run, body and writer: all holds, holds inside the 45 cm nearby-object filter (the object visible and collidable, root within 45 cm of the palm at t-1), holds overlapping an R01 reach act toward the focus object, planner holds whose goal ring entry touched the focus object; make_summary.py condenses them into summary.json with B1E minus seg41r. Direction cosines toward the object and toward the goal displacement (1 = straight at it, 0 = sideways, -1 = straight away) for the wrist target, the decoder's first palm step, the fixed point, the prediction and the actual change.
Execution share: the arm hinges' change over the hold projected on the fixed point's hinge change (0 = no movement along the command, 1 = the commanded configuration reached in 250 ms).
Counts: holds with any arm hinge at a range end, hold records at the actuator rails, hold records with each contact kind; the palm change's parts made by arm hinges, trunk hinges and the free root.

The alignment line rejects a mismatch of efference records to holds: a one-record shift moves the palm by about a fifth of a hold's change, far above 10%. The sign line: the recorded ctrl is taken one 10 ms physics step before the record's pose and the damping term uses a 50 ms finite-difference speed (the records hold no joint speeds), so exact equality cannot be demanded; a sign agreement of 80% or more shows the replica evaluates the decoder's own rows, while a wrong joint sequence or a wrong frame gives about 50%.

rows.pass_line: verdict pass when every input file is read and body 1 receives a label by the declared rule, with rT = body 1's mean motor token spread over CUR divided by its mean over PRE and rX the same for X_hand: (a) quieter inputs when rX <= rT + 0.05 and X_joint's ratio <= rT + 0.05; (b) changed encoder response when rX >= 0.95 and rT <= 0.90; (c) unresolved otherwise, or when X_hand covers under 80 of every 100 commands of either span's windows. Verdict invalid when a file cannot be read, no reading's window lies inside the raw records, or available memory is under 3 GB at the start.
rows.pass_line_basis: The rule compares the token's change with the change of the input block the code shows the live motor token reads (the handles' achieved world positions), with X_joint as the joint-space check, since per-handle orientations are not saved. The 0.05 allowance and the 0.95 and 0.90 lines are chosen, not measured: no saved measurement gives the motor encoder's response curve, and the token's spread need not move in proportion with its input (a LayerNorm output bounded at 1; four pooling heads that each put 99.75 to 99.97 of every 100 parts of their weight on one handle, lem/model/motor_asked_change.py, measured Oct 3, 2026). So an input fall at least as large as the token's is read as input-driven, an unchanged input under a fallen token as a changed response, and the band between as unresolved. Coverage 0.8: below it the rebuilt positions come from short stretches and understate the spread.

replacement.paired_output_difference_rms: Per body, sqrt(mean over the 200 samples and the 192 numbers of (end-encoder token - start-encoder token)^2) on the same input rows. 0 = identical tokens; larger = further apart. No upper bound and no quality scale is claimed. For two outputs of root mean square 1 its square is 2 - 2 x mean(end x start), so about 1.41 (sqrt 2) is only the reference for a zero average product of the two outputs, not a maximum; outputs of opposite sign give 2. Calling 1.41 'unrelated' would need the centring and unit-root-mean-square assumptions stated, and it would still not test statistical independence.
replacement.token_spread: Per body, the mean over the 192 numbers of each number's standard deviation over the 200 samples (correction 1). 0 = no variation over the samples; larger = more variation. A reading of 1 does not show unrelated or independent tokens: the spread ignores the samples' order and can be large for deterministic, highly structured sequences.

rows.title: Explainer output fence: --no-run-copy writes only the requested page, reaches the watcher's child builder, and leaves the input run folder's bytes unchanged
rows.question: With build_explainer --no-run-copy, does a rebuild write only the requested page and no <run>/explainer.html; does the watcher's fresh child builder receive the option; is an output inside the run folder or the --stats-from run folder refused under every spelling (absolute, relative, '..', letter case, the folder itself, the \\?\ extended-length prefix, the administrative and loopback shares), on drive C: and on drive D:; does main() refuse before making its lock file when the input run cannot be chosen; and does the old mode (no option) still write both of its declared targets?
rows.why: The explainer watcher started at 9:49 AM PDT on Oct 15, 2026 read the completed B1K run and, because build_explainer.build() always wrote <run>/explainer.html beside the requested page, rewrote D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/b1_continue_492800/run/B1K_skip13_492800/explainer.html at 10:23:31 AM inside a protected predecessor folder during the arm run's before/after fence; that run's reading names it an external-write defect. the decision arm1-failure-reconciled-output-fence-20261015 authorizes the repair and requires this check before the watcher is restarted and before another protected-run experiment.
inputs: Fixture runs built in a temporary folder by tests/test_build_explainer.py _fixture_run (the render tests' own fixture: args, receipt, stats and snapshot JSON; no model weights, no world, no checkpoint file).
The code under test: Source/Python/mimo_bridge/tools/build_explainer.py, Source/Python/mimo_bridge/explainer/refresh.py, Source/Python/mimo_bridge/tests/test_explainer_refresh.py.
The check program D:/UEMA_Research/docs/explainer_output_fence_2026-10-15/output_fence_check.py.
steps: Run: cd D:/UEMA_Research/Source/Python && D:/UEMA_Research/.venv_mimo/Scripts/python.exe -m mimo_bridge.tools.commit_guard --need-gb 2 && D:/UEMA_Research/.venv_mimo/Scripts/python.exe -m mimo_bridge.tools.test_runner run explainer_output_fence_check_20261015 --device cpu --threads 2 --cwd D:/UEMA_Research --log D:/UEMA_Research/docs/explainer_output_fence_2026-10-15/registered/runner.log -- D:/UEMA_Research/.venv_mimo/Scripts/python.exe -B D:/UEMA_Research/docs/explainer_output_fence_2026-10-15/output_fence_check.py --out D:/UEMA_Research/docs/explainer_output_fence_2026-10-15/registered.

A: the old mode. build() without the option, and one real --watch-child rebuild through refresh_loop without it: both write <run>/explainer.html and the requested page; the child's command line has no --no-run-copy.
B: the new mode. build(run_copy=False) writes only the requested page; every file of the run folder is listed with its size and sha256 before and after, and the lists are compared.

C: an output inside the run under eight spellings (absolute, relative, '..', upper case, the run folder itself, the \\?\ extended-length prefix, the \\localhost\C$ administrative share and the \\127.0.0.1\C$ loopback share) is refused by build() (ValueError) and by build_explainer.main (exit 2); the run folder's list is compared again.

D: refresh_loop with no_run_copy runs the guard and one real fresh child builder: its command line carries --no-run-copy, it writes the requested page and no run copy, the run folder's list is unchanged, and the refresh receipt names the run and its one destination.

E: on drive D: (Paragon's HFS+ driver, where the B1K run lives), in a scratch folder the program makes and removes under D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch (never the B1K folder): the plain, prefix and two share spellings of an output inside a fixture run are found inside, a sibling folder's outputs (plain, prefix, shares) are not, build() refuses each inside spelling, and the run keeps its bytes; the two folders' file identities (st_dev, st_ino) are recorded.

F: an output inside the --stats-from run is refused by build(), main() and refresh_loop (no command run, the chart run's bytes unchanged); main() --watch --no-run-copy with the production record made unreadable exits 2 and makes no lock file.
The program writes result.json with the verdict, each check, the child command lines and the process tree's peak memory.
measures: Per check, held or not held (14 checks: A1, A2, B1, B2, C1, C2, D1 to D4, E1, E2, F1, F2); for the run folders, the number of files, their bytes and the paths whose size or sha256 changed (0 changed is the requirement); the process tree's peak resident memory in MB; the seconds taken.
rows.pass_line: PASS: all 14 checks held and both child builds completed (receipt state 'built'). FAIL: a check was taken and did not hold. INVALID: a check could not be taken (the memory guard refused a child, a child timed out, a fixture could not be built).
rows.pass_line_basis: the overseer's four required demonstrations (the old mode keeps its declared targets; the new mode changes only the allowed output; the run folder's files and bytes stay unchanged across a child rebuild; the child receives the option), the spelling refusals of the coordinator's terms, and the independent recheck's three findings (A-M1: the prefix and share spellings, on C: and on D:; A-m1: no lock file before the run is judged; A-m2: the --stats-from run); each is a deterministic file comparison, so one failed comparison is a FAIL.

rows.title: Serialization diagnostic: one processor-only load and save of Baseline A's end runtime_state.pt
rows.question: Inside Baseline A attempt 4's trainer, torch.save of runtime_state.pt took 47 to 49 s (D: keeps whole-second file times: the file was created at 04:10:33 AM PDT and last written at 04:11:21 AM PDT on Oct 14, 2026, and torch.save opens the file before it pickles). How many seconds does torch.save of the same 489,337,072-byte state take from processor memory to the same disk outside the trainer, and how many processor seconds does it use (user plus system time of all its threads, which is not the complement of disk waiting)? And how long does torch.load of it take?
rows.why: The whole-process 10x lines (287.74 and 288.76 ms per model step) need the fixed per-process costs (startup 59.6 s, end save 73.5 s in A) to fall by 90.0% on the 200-model-step diagnostic (budget v5, verdict 6). Of the 48 s between optimizer.pt's last write and runtime_state.pt's last write, D:'s file times put 47 to 49 s inside torch.save itself and under 1 s in building rt (every tensor copied to the processor) and the space walk. This re-save tells apart two causes: torch.save of this state on this disk (then the saved form is the place to work: fewer, larger tensors; one copy of the histories) and the conditions inside the trainer's process or on the machine during its save (then the trainer-side timers are the next reading).

replaced.on_pass: the result, with its scope fields, goes to the overseer for an actual-result decision: a scoped PASS clears neither the whole-loop timing comparison (the NET effect of the per-use casts and the captures together) nor the flag's adoption or training use while POLICY numerical and imagination off numerical read NOT QUALIFIED and the hold reads its own status; before any flag-on training or adoption decision, either the hold's path is qualified, or reviewed per-call handling prevents an unqualified hold update and preserves or stops for qualification (the hold neither disabled nor its state cleared silently; a stats report every 100 model steps is not enough)
replaced.on_fail: each FAIL entry names its pair, model step, point or lesson, tensor, both statuses and values or the relative difference and the line; the result is preserved; a confirmed fault is repaired and reviewed again; no automatic retry
replaced.on_invalid: each INVALID entry is named: an arm that did not complete with its error and the model steps done; a required comparison not made or its measured basis missing; a 'not qualified' breach with its line; the observer changing a total, a start state, an activity or a site count; a forward replay that differed or a state change after the last replay; an unresolved zero against nonzero in a capture comparison with its relative difference and values; a coverage gap (the declared risk: the within-body gauge kind needs a push at 492,800 itself; the attempt is then spent, its records kept); the sensitivity not shown; a reader check that did not hold; a stop, a cleanup not verified or a missing supervision record follows the CLEANUP PROTOCOL of step 6; nothing is retried. A refusal at admission (exit 7) is not the attempt (step 7)
replaced.target_metric: the program's verdict; lost lesson contributions and lost totals (0 required)
replaced.baseline: the flag-off learner from the same start, same inputs (OFF), its repeat (OFF2), and the flag-on learner with every capture refused (REF) and its repeat (REF2)
replaced.statistical_line: declared lines (pass_line): the CAPTURE line a stated function of the measured same-step repeat difference and the gradient's own bf16 step, a prospective engineering screen, not a statistical confidence bound; no statistical test

rows.why: the overseer's d2-review-reject-a-prime-correction-before-execution-20261016 () chose A-prime and rejected option B. Neither existing option is a decision at index 494,025: the model plans when its step index is a multiple of --intention-every 10 (lem_model.py at 641c931a6 line 4250, the index read before the step count is incremented, lines 2543 and 4058; the harness passes step_index = the step count, gof_probe_harness.py line 893; a load sets the step count to 494,025, lem_model.py line 9516), so the first planning event after the restore is at 494,030. A-prime's input is produced by the weights saved at 494,025, the same weights the controls replay. Its scope: a frozen, one-body, processor continuation from the saved start (learning off for the 5 model steps; each body alone; the babble noise drawn from the batch's processor generator for one body, lem_model.py line 1974; the companion's card random stream dropped by the harness, gof_probe_harness.py line 464); comparable to the prior one-body mechanism readings; not the trainer's next batched or card decision and not an uninterrupted-learning event at 494,030. 'From the saved state' is true of the start, not of the decision reached. Exploration noise (the d1-d2-rereview-decisions-conditional-execution-20261016, D2 item 3; exploration_noise = 0.05 is the frozen A-prime intervention, and the trainer's bout scheduler is not emulated): All six isolated-body observes from 494,025 through 494,030 carry constant exploration_noise=0.05. The five intervening policy_act calls execute commands held from their preceding observes; the captured 494,030 command is not executed. The training run used --babble-bouts real and --rest-control choice, so it could use 0.05 during a bout and 0 during a rest. A-prime neither restores nor advances that saved trainer scheduler. This difference can change the physical state and planning input at 494,030. The result is therefore conditional on the frozen one-body A-prime inputs and is not the trainer's counterfactual next batched event. This keeps the causal live-versus-held comparison valid because all four control modes replay the same captured input, weights and random state. Restoring only the bout scheduler would still omit training, batching, card random state and batch context, so it would not reconstruct the trainer event.

rows.question: On the 8 A-prime decisions (from 494,025, event 494,030: the checkpoint-494025-derived first planning event at 494030, frozen-learning one-body CPU probe): of the change of production's selected command (Adam, learning rate 0.1, 20 updates; the hand stage left out) when the five senses' present tokens change by Gaussian noise of 0.00001 per number (4 fixed-seed draws against the unchanged row 0), how much is left when the attention weights are held at their values at the search's starting command: the motor encoder's modules (motor), those and the forward model's 4 blocks' modules (motor_core), and every attention module of the predictor's route (all)? And are the two native side paths beside the motor encoder's pool present, and what share of the motor token and of its gradient does each carry, both staying live under every hold?
rows.why: the overseer's d2-review-reject-a-prime-correction-before-execution-20261016 () keeps all four modes in one run: 4 modes x 8 decisions = 32 searches, against 16 for live and all alone. The old finding (row planner_search_mechanism_controls, Oct 5, 2026: all held left 0.0015 of the live change on 479,350 and 0.00012 on 481,800) is evidence about older weights and code. The failed attention cap stays off (args.json attention_cap off, bound null).

Per planner arm against the same arm at 494,025: the mean over bodies of the goal-averaged difference (below 0 = nearer here, 0 = no change), its paired 95 percent interval, the bodies nearer and farther (0 to 8), the same per goal, and the hand joint and wrist error differences with their intervals.

rows.title: PLANNER_SEARCH_REPAIR outcome spread of gradient descent in the command's own units (sgd) on 481,800, under the frozen line L
rows.owner: the H84 coordinator (the row was prepared by the planner search agent of Oct 20, 2026, branch planner/search-sgd-spread-2026-10-20)
rows.question: On the same 16 saved planning decisions of checkpoint 481,800 that row planner_search_outcome_spread_481800 used (the first 2 of each of the 8 bodies), executed for the 5-model-step hold from the same restored state: how far apart do the real outcomes P of the sgd search's command and of the same search's command after Gaussian noise of 0.00001 on the present tokens (draw 1) end, against the frozen line L = 0.0039 and beside production's Adam's 0.0252; and, beside it, how far does sgd's command as the body receives it lie from the motor controller's command, and where does its P end against reflex and against chosen?
rows.why: The operator's decision of Oct 20, 2026 (the coordinator's brief): read the outcome spread of the one search form whose gain over Adam a 16-cluster held-out trial can show, before any trial is considered. PLANNER_JUMPING_2026-10-19.md section 4: sgd's gain over Adam on row v3 (0.028 over 64 decisions of 481,800) has a between-body spread of 0.008, so a trial shows it from 0.014 with 32 decisions per body (s4's between-body spread 0.047 needs 0.039); its outcome spread Q was never read. The decision that depends on the answer: within the line, sgd is named to the coordinator as a candidate for a held-out trial; above it, sgd is recorded as outside the outcome line. Nothing is deployed either way.
rows.gof_link: A planner command serves gain of function when what the body reaches with it does not depend on rounding of the inputs and ends nearer the goal than today's search.
inputs: Production checkpoint D:/UEMA_Research/Saved/mimo_bridge/experiments/H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41o_1431/checkpoints/ckpt_step_481800 (read only) and its saved eight-world episode; per body the first 2 planning decisions (k = 0 and k = 1, 10 model steps apart; body 0's first is model step 481,800, its second 481,820), the decisions of row planner_search_outcome_spread_481800 (its rows D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/planner_search/design_arms_481800_v8a/rows.jsonl and _v8b/rows.jsonl). Each body's first decision is the same saved state as on Oct 5; its second is reached by the main line after the first, which the other arms of a job can change (row planner_search_design_arms_481800_v7's decision), so arms are compared inside this job only and Adam's Q is read from the Oct 5 rows.

Arms (docs/gain_of_function_v4/planner_recovery/design_arms_sgd_spread.json at the pinned commit; arms_probe.py parses them): reflex = the motor controller's command (26 body handles x 9 numbers: target position xyz in units of 200 cm, orientation as 4 numbers, radius, strength); chosen = the command production's Adam selected at the decision; sgd = search_lib.Variant kind sgd, 20 updates from the motor controller's command, each update p <- p - scale x gradient of the objective (per real sense the mean over 192 numbers of (predicted next token - goal token)^2, summed, plus the effort term), the scale fixed at the first update so that the largest searched number moves 0.1 of its unit and every other number 0.1 x its gradient / the largest gradient, no trust region, the evaluated command of lowest objective kept; sgd@1 = the same search from the present tokens plus Gaussian noise of 0.00001 per number on the five real senses (search_lib.token_noise, draw 1; draw 0 = no noise). Every command is executed from the identical restored snapshot for the 5-model-step hold; reflex and chosen are executed twice and their physical traces must be bit-identical.

P = the real goal distance in proprioception plus vision after the hold on raw encoder tokens: for each of the two senses the mean over the token's 192 numbers of (the raw token after the hold - the goal's token)^2, summed (0 = the senses equal the goal's; the motor controller's command's own P is about 0.40 on 481,800).

rows.question: At commit e3f48551bfd38dfab2d1377df9c8ee298546330a of branch repair/whole-body-request-2026-10-21 (the whole-body request repair of the whole-body-request-repair-handoff-20261021: the planner's twin of the world's arm projection, arm_reach.py and its wiring through limb_target_control.py, env.py, train_mimo.py and lem_model.py; the movement viewer's render v17, pose_geometry.py, api.py and the page), run by the package's one test entry point run_package_tests.py one after another and stopping at the first group that does not pass, do the tests pass: (1) the 24 synthetic tests of test_arm_reach.py and test_movement_viewer_geometry.py; (2) the 46 tests of test_arm_reach_world.py (the twin's arm rows against the rows the world's own projection records, on MIMo's saved model and recorded poses), test_movement_viewer_geometry_world.py (the viewer's arm geometry against the world's; the screenshot command's four measured contradictions, its corrected command and its pose inside every joint range; its remembered goal; its whole drawing) and test_limb_target_control.py (every test, the two crib worlds' end-to-end tests among them, and the check that one restored crib-world state renders the same eye-image bytes twice in one process, which the comparison's repeat and bare arms need under --vision on); (3) the 8 drawing tests of test_movement_viewer.py named in run_package_tests.py's VIEWER_TESTS?
rows.why: the decision d1-pilot-closed-whole-body-next-20261021 authorized the repair's implementation and allowed only synthetic tests behind the commit guard; every test that loads a saved model, builds a world or draws a picture runs only inside a registered row after the runtime decision. Those tests are the only checks that the planner's twin forms the arm rows the world records (the equality the handoff, item 3, asks to be measured before any planner qualification under --reach-projection arms), that the viewer's corrected command reproduces the diagnostic numbers on the screenshot command, and that the repaired drawing draws. The comparison row whole_body_request_comparison_483120 draws its before and after pictures with the same drawing code. The eye-image test shows before the comparison runs whether its repeat and bare arms can repeat their physics under --vision on (the independent review of Oct 21, 2026, MINOR 3).
rows.gof_link: Gain of function needs the body to execute and approach the commands the planner selects; the planner's twin and the viewer's corrected command only serve that if they equal what the world executes, which these tests compare on MIMo's saved model.

rows.statistical_line: No statistical judgement: each test passes or fails.
rows.pass_line: PASS when result.json reads verdict pass: every group exits 0 with exactly its expected count (24 fast, 46 model, 8 viewer, as pytest --collect-only counted them at the commit), 0 failures, 0 errors and 0 skipped. FAIL when a group's pytest exits 1 with failed tests named. INVALID otherwise: a refusal (the identity check), a memory or time stop, a skipped test, a count other than the expected one, pytest exiting 2 to 5, a missing result.
rows.pass_line_basis: The planner twin's equality with the world's projection and the viewer's reproduction of the diagnostic are the claims the repair makes, and the in-process eye-image repeat is what the comparison's repeat and bare arms need; one failing or skipped test means one of them is unshown. A skip is not a pass because the model tests skip when their saved data is missing. The counts are pytest's at the commit: 24 fast (the JUnit file of the 1:39 PM PDT run), 46 model and 8 of 30 viewer tests with 22 deselected (collected at 12:38 PM PDT; the model and viewer files' test counts unchanged since).

rows.title: Whole-body request: corrected against run mapping, saved start
rows.owner: the coordinator runs the row; the whole-body repair builder (the builder subagent of session 358a210a) owns the package
rows.question: The operator's screenshot command: body 5 of recording f642891fa3cd (run H84_fresh_drivers_20260918_seg41j_1526), the command the planner's search selected and the trainer latched at model step 483,120, whose requested lower-leg and forearm directions lie 23.02 (left knee), 64.90 (right knee), 16.17 (left elbow) and 40.76 (right elbow) degrees from every direction the knee or elbow can give them on the requested thigh and upper-arm directions. From one replayed saved state of body 5 that reproduces record 483,119 (the binding: the 15 scored parts within a mean 1.554 degrees of the record's orientations, the record's contact pairs, every saved contact place within 0.0924 cm), with the same command and eye commands, does the corrected mapping (limb_target_control.py: each calf row replaced by its knee's goal on the requested thigh row, the arm rows by the arm projection with the chest where it is) turn the 15 powered body parts further toward the ORIGINAL requested directions in 250 ms than the mapping the run used (the requested rows sent as they are), without ending farther from the remembered goal (observer record 483,016) by more than E's tie band; and what do the 1,000 ms hold, the run's own following commands, the achievable-target control, the contacts and the four attribution readings show? AMENDED by the decision of Oct 21, 2026 1:10 PM PDT (whole-body-matched-comparison-decision-20261021, a prospective decision, not an operator quotation): a replayed start that differs from record 483,119 is retained, and the pass line's word on it is judged and labelled as from that differing start; this is a paired reconstruction experiment, not a claim to reproduce the historical screenshot exactly.
rows.why: the decision d1-pilot-closed-whole-body-next-20261021: 'The next decision is the repair's physical result followed by the bounded learning route if the repaired control path passes.' The geometry (the handoff whole-body-request-repair-handoff-20261021) removes the four contradictions on paper (at most 0.000002 degrees left) but moves the requested wrist places 18.35 cm (left) and 8.73 cm (right); whether the body then approaches the original request and goal better is unmeasured, and the run's own record shows the body turning its parts a mean 15.54 degrees while their distance to the requested directions went only from 29.24 to 26.03 degrees.
rows.gof_link: Gain of function needs commands the body can execute to move it toward what the planner selected; this comparison reads whether making the requested rows consistent moves the body nearer the original request and the remembered goal, or only changes the request.

rows.title: The s4 experiment's automatic saved end reading: forecast error, score tradeoff and physical outcome
rows.question: From the two arms' saved files only, per arm and side by side: (1) for each captured planner command, how far was the body from the selected earlier pose at the actual start, one model step later and at the hold end (both wrists and the 15 scored handles, cm and degrees), and in how many commands do sensory match and physical reaching disagree; (2) how large is each sense's forecast error (vector MSE and the signed error in predicted distance-to-goal), the raw route and the acting route apart, with frozen proprioception; (3) how much of each search's objective fall from the first proposal to the selected command came from the strength part rather than the goal part; (4) did the repair arm's s4 search stay inside its trust region at every decision?
rows.why: the overseer's overnight-learning-and-reach-assignment-20261021 item 3: 'automatic end reading that explains forecast error versus score tradeoff and physical outcome. Include meaningful progress versus the actual start, not only selected versus initial proposal'; overnight-measurement-minimal-approved-20261021: 'Prefer reading the in-training captures' and the 900 s cumulative limit per question across both arms; exact-command-selection-score-20261021: keep predicted and actual per-sense match to the same selected memory beside physical wrist progress, the reading that separates prediction error from a score that accepts poor reaching. The re-measurement row of the repair arm's target gates 4 and 7 (remeasure). The readings are descriptions of each run (overnight-item1-scope-accepted-20261022).

measures: PHYSICAL OUTCOME per captured command and body: distance to the selected earlier pose at the actual start, one model step later and the hold end (cm for both wrists and the 15-handle mean, degrees for the 15-handle orientation; the chest's displacement beside it); progress = start minus hold end (above 0 = nearer at the hold end); exact means, medians, quartiles; nearer, farther and unchanged counts; start-gap and goal-age distributions; per-body counts and rates; contacts during the hold (yes, no, unknown).

DISAGREEMENT COUNTS: captured sensory match (summed live raw distance, and frozen proprioception) nearer or farther against physical nearer or farther; the predicted improvement against physical progress.

FORECAST ERROR per sense: every planner command, body-averaged (learning route one model step later and at the hold end, each over persistence: 0 = exact, 1 = no better than 'nothing changes'; the acting route's depth-one forecast); the capture per body: vector MSE of the selected prediction against the raw actual tokens (and, for proprioception, against the frozen encoder's tokens), and the signed error in predicted distance-to-goal (raw and acting routes apart; the full-hold forecast at the hold end).

SCORE TRADEOFF per decision and body: selected minus first proposal for the objective, the goal part and the strength part; the strength share of each fall; counts of falls with the goal part rising and of falls more than half from the strength part.
GATE 4 IN RUN (repair arm): trust_region_used per body (count above 1.0001; missing), selected_fraction counts. INCOMPLETE ITEMS: counts per reason (identity, timing, source, execution validity).
rows.pass_line: DECLARED BEFORE LAUNCH. COMPLETE when both arms' results and repair_minus_control.json are written within the 900 s total with every section's counts of valid, invalid and incomplete items; INCOMPLETE when an arm's reading stops at the budget or an arm has no preserved end state (never an outcome); the repair arm is INVALID when any saved s4 reading exceeds 1.0001 or is missing. No ability label: the results are exact descriptive means and counts of each run, side by side, with no interval and no verdict.
rows.pass_line_basis: the overseer's overnight-reader-drop-invalid-intervals-20261022: sequential commands share bodies, weights and trajectories, so an interval over them is not justified; overnight-item1-scope-accepted-20261022: live samples with different goals and start states describe each run and explain individual failures, and a lower average alone cannot establish learned reaching improvement. The 1.0001 line is s4's own construction (planner_search.py used_of). The frozen same-start ability comparison is not part of this package; 2,500 model steps did not resolve this lineage's only measured learned change (483,411 against 494,025: -0.0214 to +0.0671).

cost.where: the processor, after each arm, never beside a trainer; saved files only (no learner, no torch checkpoint, no environment, zero physics steps); the saved MuJoCo world model loaded for forward kinematics and offscreen pictures
cost.time_limit_basis: 900 s cumulative per question across both arms with every retry. The timing pass on ARM2's real saved files with a synthetic capture at every planning decision (1,992 commands per arm): both arms and the comparison 11.29 s of wall time, forward kinematics 1.355 s and 1.407 s, pictures 1.816 s and 1.092 s; peak commit charge 1,636,659,200 bytes per process (timing_pass_arm2/). The final reader (version s4_end_reading_v3, the capture layout of 1d321ad22) with its model-free stand-in for forward kinematics on ARM2's files plus a capture line at every planning decision (1,992 commands per arm): both arms and the comparison 13.97 s, the observer index 9.42 s on cold files, peak commit charge 916,103,168 bytes.

rows.on_pass: COMPLETE: both arms' results, the pictures and the side-by-side descriptions go to the overseer; the next repair is chosen from the measured reason (prediction error, a score that accepts poor reaching, or execution), and a focused same-state check is proposed from the preserved identities only if the result calls for it; nothing is launched automatically.
rows.on_fail: INCOMPLETE or INVALID: the cause traced from budget.json, the result's invalid and incomplete counts and the arm's files; no outcome is reported from a partial reading; no retry past the 900 s total. After an EARLY STOP the stopped arm's per-arm result (descriptions of that arm's saved records, with owner_end.json's state and reason) and the stop's cause go to the overseer; no repair-minus-control comparison is written.
rows.gof_link: Whether a learned forward model and its planner search turn a remembered pose into a command that brings the body nearer that pose, measured on the body, with the prediction error and the score tradeoff that explain each miss.
rows.target_metric: 15-handle mean distance to the selected earlier pose at the actual start and at the hold end, cm, per captured command, described per arm
rows.baseline: each command's actual start; the control arm (today's search, the same span, start and capture) beside it
rows.statistical_line: none: exact descriptive means and counts; no interval over sequential commands

rows.title: Research release: a clone in another folder continues training from model step 494,025
rows.question: Does a fresh clone of the private research release (github.com/bhartsb/UEMA_Research), in a folder other than D:/UEMA_Research, continue training from the saved state at model step 494,025 through resume.py, with the trainer and its eight world processes opening, listing or checking no file outside the clone?
rows.why: Reviewers under NDA will clone the private repository and must be able to load the weights and train. On Oct 22, 2026 three defects that would have stopped them were repaired in the release: the hand calibration copy had paths rewritten inside it (the trainer checks its content hash and the file fingerprint the checkpoint saved), the resume command named 12 paths of this machine, and Git converted line endings on checkout. This run checks those repairs end to end. The operator's yes of Oct 22, 2026 to 'Test it once: clone into a fresh folder at a different path and run a short resume' authorizes it.
inputs: the clone D:/UEMA_review_test/clone2 at release commit 95e2654 (git status clean; the six Git LFS weight files checked out; setup_checkout.py run: 4,982 file times restored). Attempt a2 at 33960a2: the trainer loaded model step 494,025, then stopped at 'speech extension requires legacy-to-responsive-exchange libraries' (the command named the clone's speech library, the saved state its development-repository path). Attempt a3 at 4dcf32f: numpy failed to import (the new re-rooting also redirected the Python environment, which on this machine sits inside the development repository). 72740a7 keeps the recorded names and never re-roots the Python environment. Attempt a4 at 72740a7: past the speech library and the eight worlds' construction, stopped at 'exact continuation requires the saved execution device': the test runner hides the graphics card (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1) unless started with --device gpu, which a4's start lacked; a5 passes it. Attempt a4 also showed the worlds writing their scene files to D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/protected_memory_8body_20260929/start/scenes (40 files written there at 10:41-10:42 AM: 24 new files named by process id, 16 shared scene files that production regenerates at each resume); 9be0214 re-roots the D: data folders into the clone's external/D. Attempt a5 at 9be0214 (with --device gpu): resumed at model step 494,025 on the graphics card, then the trainer's own preflight probe stopped the launch: scipy could not create its temporary file (the runner sets the temporary folder inside D:/UEMA_Research/external/D/UEMA_scratch/h84, which the new re-rooting redirected into the clone). 95e2654 never re-roots the process's temporary and output folders and re-roots a saved world's folder where the world is built. Attempt a6 at 95e2654: the trainer resumed at model step 494,025, ran to 494,125 and saved its end checkpoint (summary ok=True after 6.2 min), but the test wrapper crashed reading its trace log (eight processes appended to one file and 100 of 10,277 lines interleaved), so the runner judged FAIL from the wrapper's exit code 1. a7 repeats it with one trace file per process and the reading rule revised below.

the saved state weights/b1_continue_B1K_skip13_492800 inside the clone (model step 494,025; model.safetensors 73,119,988 bytes, optimizer.pt, runtime_state.pt, episode_state.pt.gz, latent_body/latest.pt)
the interpreter D:/UEMA_Research/.venv_mimo/Scripts/python.exe (Python 3.13.3)
100 model steps (stop step 494,125; one model step = 50 ms of each of the eight bodies' simulated time)
steps: 1. The commit guard allows 25 GB, checked as its own step before the runner starts.

2. The runner, started with --device gpu, starts release_resume_test.py, which runs `python resume.py --out D:/UEMA_review_test/clone2/_resume_test --steps 100` from the clone with the tracer folder on PYTHONPATH, so the trainer and every world process append each file access outside the clone to foreign_resume.jsonl; it samples Windows' committed memory every 2 s.

3. After the trainer exits, the wrapper reads _resume_test/run/trainer.log (the line 'resumed from ... at step N') and _resume_test/run/replay_training_stats.jsonl (step, next-frame loss, model steps per second, peak graphics-card memory) and writes the result file.
measures: the trainer's exit code (0 = it reached its stop step; any other value = it stopped early)
the model step the log says it resumed at (494,025 = the saved state; any other = another state loaded)
the last model step in the stats (494,125 = all 100 model steps ran)

file accesses outside the clone by the trainer and its world processes (0 = a reviewer's machine without this machine's folders runs the same; each access names a file a reviewer would lack). Revised before attempt a7, after reading a6's saved trace: NOT counted are Python's import machinery (installed software a reviewer has: the environment, the DLL search over PATH), the installed MIMo package's own folder (the README has the reviewer install it), named pipes (process links, not files), and the folders that contain the clone with the files directly in them (a path lookup walks up through them). Under this rule the 10,177 readable lines of a6's trace held 0 counted accesses (its other 100 lines were unreadable; 36 MIMo package files, 4 upward lookups of an optional .checkpoint_retention.json, 8 pipes).

reported beside the line, not judged: the next-frame loss of the run's training records against the saved run's last 13 records (0.05721 to 0.07594), model steps per second (the saved run: 0.4444 to 0.4868), peak graphics-card memory in MB (the saved run: 4,213 to 4,291), peak committed memory in GB
rows.pass_line: exit code 0, resumed at model step 494,025, last model step 494,125, and 0 file accesses outside the clone
rows.pass_line_basis: each part is a yes-or-no condition of 'a reviewer can continue training from the clone': a different exit code, start step or end step means the resume did not happen as stated, and an outside access names a file a reviewer's machine lacks. The loss and the speed are reported, not judged: no measured line exists for what 100 model steps after a correct load read. Revised before attempt a7: the outside-access count excludes installed software a reviewer has by the README (Python's import machinery, the MIMo package) and non-file links (named pipes, the folders above the clone), named in the measures.
